-- The typecheck stage: Hindley-Milner inference, interface/impl constraint solving,
-- and dict-passing elaboration.  Architecture doc, including the component model this
-- file is being decomposed towards: `compiler/TYPECHECK-TARGET-ARCHITECTURE.md`.
--
-- The HM core is monotypes over Ref-based union-find tyvars, level-based
-- generalization, unification (occurs-check + level adjust), and instantiation.  On
-- top of it, and NOT deferred elsewhere, this file also carries: interfaces, impls,
-- superclasses and coherence; constraint solving and the dict-passing elaboration the
-- backends consume; effect rows; records; explicit signatures; and operator inference.
-- Exhaustiveness is the one part that lives elsewhere and is still called from here --
-- `checkMatchExhaustive` (`compiler/frontend/exhaust.mdk`), once per `EMatch`
-- ([P-EXHAUST-IN-TYPECHECK]).
--
-- ONE GRAPH DRIVER, TWO OUTPUT SELECTIONS.  `driveGraphK` is the single whole-graph
-- driver: `GOutDiags` (per-module diagnostics and schemes) is what `medaka check`,
-- `check --json`, the LSP, MCP, the playground and `medaka test`'s gate consume, and
-- `GOutTrees` (the same diagnostics plus the elaborated, dict-passed trees, the
-- residual and the evidence table) is what `run`, `build`'s child, `medaka test`'s
-- phases and the emit entries consume.  They share one preamble, one per-module
-- worker and one graph-end drain, so a module is checked against the same universe,
-- the same seed and the same mark sets on both.  Every whole-graph entry point in this
-- file is a projection of that function.  A keyed diagnostics drive
-- (`checkModulesDiagsChain (Some …)`) hands the one fold a serve policy (`diagsServe`),
-- which serves each unchanged module before the entry from its recorded interface
-- (`types/module_interface.mdk`) instead of checking it.
--
-- One thing the selections still differ on by construction, and it is observable:
-- `GOutTrees` promotes (inferred-constraint user fns join the dict-name set).  So
-- acceptance under one selection is still not proof about the other for a program that
-- promotes an inferred-constraint fn across modules; its consequence for the gate over
-- this compiler's own source is #1811.  `renameAliasedMethods` is NOT a second such
-- difference: it runs on both selections, because half (b) of it decides which
-- declaration a bare method name binds to, so skipping it on one selection would make
-- that selection typecheck a different program
-- (`test/run_check_agreement_fixtures/reject_1812_alias_import_order.mdk` and its
-- permuted accepting twin).
--
-- Single-file consumers are one-module projections of the same graph driver. There
-- is no second checking mode or second stamper order; `checkOne*` and `elaborateOne`
-- supply the one-module entry surface.
--
-- History: this began as a prelude-less HM engine validated against the (since removed)
-- OCaml reference compiler.  Both that reference and its `dev/tc_probe.exe` harness are
-- gone; native is the sole compiler.  The remaining probe is
-- `compiler/entries/selfproc_tc_probe.mdk`.

-- ── v2 Stage 3: the `IO` widening union alias (design §3.2) ─────────────────
-- `IO` is the coarse security alias: in a BOUND/annotation row it stands for
-- the join of the narrow security labels the selected profile grants, every one
-- at ⊤ when none is selected.  `hostLabels` lists them (every minted security
-- label EXCEPT IO itself); internal labels (Mut/Panic) are NOT members, so they
-- are tracked independently of IO.
-- NOTE: `FFI` is deliberately NOT a member. #2071/#2070 (epic, Layer 1, R1):
-- an `<IO>` bound must NOT subsume an `<FFI>`-performing body — FFI crosses a
-- trust boundary the IO alias is not meant to paper over. Do not "complete"
-- this list by adding FFI.

-- What `IO` joins in this drive: the selected profile's grants of the alias
-- labels, each at the parameter granted, in `hostLabels` order.  With no
-- profile that is all eleven at their tops.  Every module of the program is
-- judged against the one join, the shipped stdlib included.
export
ioJoinAtoms : List (String, Param) -> List (String, EffParamTy) -> List Atom
ioJoinAtoms domains grants =
  filterMap
    (l =>
      map
        (granted =>
          atomWith
            (builtinLabel l)
            (writtenParam (dtopIn domains (builtinLabel l)) granted))
        (lookupAssoc l grants))
    hostLabels

-- ── global inference state ────────────────────────────────────────────────

-- sorted + deduplicated string set (canonical effect-label order, matching the
-- OCaml `List.sort_uniq String.compare` so multi-label rows render identically)
-- sortUniqS / sortUniqSGo / sortInsertS moved to support/util.mdk (imported above).

-- ── effect propagation (Phase 79) ─────────────────────────────────────────
-- the latent effect of the function body currently being inferred: application
-- arms widen it; entering a lambda saves+reopens it, and the accumulated row
-- becomes the lambda's arrow effect. The accumulator begins at the empty row;
-- a closed row is an effect value, never a switch for discarding effects.

-- Close a local binding scope over [members]: whether each generalizes, and
-- its type.  Joins recorded in the scope are decided first when a member
-- generalizes, since its type must not generalize over an undecided join;
-- otherwise they belong to the enclosing scope, where later uses of the
-- alternatives can still shape them.  Everything the close reads (roots,
-- quantifiable authorities) is taken after that.
finishValueEffectsKeeping : DynCtx ->
  List (Bool, Mono) ->
  List (Int, AuthResidual)
finishValueEffectsKeeping dyn generalizing =
  let members =
    map ((generalizes, mono) => (localRole generalizes, mono)) generalizing
  let level = dyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentLevel.value
  if anyList fst generalizing then
    settlePendingJoins dyn level
  else
    postponePendingJoins dyn.dcModule level
  let monos = map snd members
  finishEffectSummaryScopeKeeping
    dyn.dcModule
    (scopeRolesOf members)
    (fold (acc mono => effectRoots mono acc) Tip monos)
    (fold (acc mono => borrowedEffectCells dyn.dcModule mono acc) Tip monos)

-- #822 (graded interfaces): an instance head must have the KIND the interface's
-- corresponding type parameter has.  A graded interface binds the whole row-indexed
-- FAMILY — `impl GThenable Async`, never a fixed row like `impl GThenable (Async e)`
-- (EFFECTS-SEMANTICS §6, DICT-SEMANTICS §3) — so the head's REMAINING parameter
-- kinds (its declared kinds minus the ones the head already applied) must equal the
-- interface slot's kinds.
--
-- This is a soundness guard, not polish.  A kind-mismatched head elaborates the
-- method type's KRow slot to a `TEff` row while the constructor's own scheme has a
-- plain tyvar in that position, and `unify` binds a tyvar to a TEff without
-- complaint: the impl would be ACCEPTED and its grade would mean nothing — every
-- index a caller reads off the result would be a fabrication.
--
-- Only interfaces that actually HAVE a graded slot are JUDGED — the `anyKRow want`
-- guard below is what does that, not the table: every slot of every interface is
-- recorded (it always was, and `ceRowParamKinds` keeps doing so), and an all-`KType`
-- row falls into the same `_ => ()` arm an outright miss does.  ⚠️ This paragraph
-- read *"only interfaces that actually HAVE a graded slot are inspected
-- (ifaceParamKindsRef records nothing else)"* until #1557 A-3.5c, and the
-- parenthetical was false of the retired table too.  Runs on BOTH whole-program
-- paths: its one call site is in checkBodyImpl, shared by Flat and Module,
-- immediately after `dataEnv` has populated the head-constructor kind table.
--
-- 🚨 #1557 A-3.5c: IT STILL ITERATES `prog`, AND THAT IS THE UNIT'S DEFINING
-- CONDITION, not an implementation detail.  The owner ruling that split A-3.5c
-- out of the A-3b lane (issue #1557, 2026-08-12) is CONDITIONAL: this check
-- qualifies as CE-only *"only if the graded impl-head kind check keeps
-- iterating `prog` rather than `IE.ieRows`"*.  The impl HEADS come from the
-- decl list; only the interface's declared slot kinds come from stage K's `CE`.
-- Whoever re-points this walk at `IE.ieRows` has re-classified the unit as A-3b
-- by construction — that is a routing decision, not a refactor.
checkGradedImplHeads : ModuleCtx -> ClassEnv -> Int -> List Decl -> Unit
checkGradedImplHeads mctx _ _ [] = ()
checkGradedImplHeads mctx ce cur (d :: rest) =
  checkGradedImplHeadDecl mctx ce cur d
  checkGradedImplHeads mctx ce cur rest

-- OCCURRENCE MINT (#1110/#1111 A-2.4): `implOrigin` is the identity the
-- interface NAME in `impl <iface> …` acquired at resolve — read off the same record
-- pattern as the name itself so the two cannot drift apart, exactly as A-2.3 reads
-- `tyConOrigin` beside `tyConName`.
checkGradedImplHeadDecl : ModuleCtx -> ClassEnv -> Int -> Decl -> Unit
checkGradedImplHeadDecl mctx ce cur (DAttrib _ d) =
  checkGradedImplHeadDecl mctx ce cur d
checkGradedImplHeadDecl mctx ce cur (DImpl { iface, tys, implOrigin = o, ... }) =
  checkGradedImplTys mctx ce cur o iface 0 tys
checkGradedImplHeadDecl mctx _ _ _ = ()

-- The `CE` lookup via `ceSlotKindsAt` uses ordinal filtering — the key is a RegKey
-- (`ifaceTabKey o iface` + slot position), identity-based not bare-name, preserving
-- the identity mint from A-2.4. Ordinals are assigned in dependency-first order,
-- matching the order the accumulator is grown in, so ordinal filtering and the
-- previous marshalled population agree. See
-- compiler/TYPECHECK-TARGET-ARCHITECTURE.md § "5. Decisions reopened, and decisions
-- deliberately kept" (A-3.5c) for the prior bare-name table this replaced and the
-- #1257 defect class it drains.
checkGradedImplTys : ModuleCtx ->
  ClassEnv ->
  Int ->
  TyConOrigin ->
  String ->
  Int ->
  List Ty ->
  Unit
checkGradedImplTys mctx _ _ _ _ _ [] = ()
checkGradedImplTys mctx ce cur o iface i (t :: rest) =
  match ceSlotKindsAt (regKeyOfTab (ifaceTabKey o iface)) cur i ce
    Some want if anyKRow want => checkGradedImplHead mctx iface t want
    _ => ()
  checkGradedImplTys mctx ce cur o iface (i + 1) rest

-- [want] is the interface slot's kind list.
--
-- Only a head whose kind is actually KNOWN is judged, and the two ways it can be
-- unknown are BOTH deliberate abstentions, not oversights:
--   * a type ALIAS head lives in aliasTableRef, never in dataParamKindsRef, and its
--     saturation is already policed by T-ALIAS-ARITY — a kind complaint here would be
--     a second, worse-worded report of the same defect;
--   * a head absent from dataParamKindsRef entirely — a builtin like `Int`, whose kinds
--     this compiler records nowhere.  Abstaining costs nothing real: a genuinely wrong
--     head still fails on its method bodies, where the mismatch is concrete and located.
--     ⚠️ An ABSTRACTLY-exported data type (`export data Asy e a`) USED to land here too,
--     cross-module, and the abstention was load-bearing for it: judging it reported a
--     correct program rejected and told the author to add a `Row` parameter the type
--     ALREADY HAD.  #804/#1028 fixed that at the source — an opaque type's kinds are
--     published cross-module (`kindPublicDataDecl`'s `VisAbstract` arm; it was
--     `registerOpaqueParamKinds` until A-3.2b retired the kind universe) — so an
--     abstract head is now judged on its REAL kinds like any other, and this arm no
--     longer covers for it.
-- A head that is not a TyCon spine at all is judged where it can be: a saturated
-- TUPLE is kind `Type`, which is never a graded slot's kind, so it is reported; a bare
-- tyvar head carries no kind and is left to the checks that already reject it.
checkGradedImplHead : ModuleCtx -> String -> Ty -> List Kind -> Unit
checkGradedImplHead mctx iface t want = match tyAppSpine t
  (TyCon { tyConName = n, tyConLoc = loc, tyConOrigin = o }, applied) =>
    checkGradedImplHeadCon mctx iface o n loc (listLen applied) want
  -- A saturated tuple is kind `Type`, which is never a graded slot's kind.  It gets its
  -- OWN remedy: the generic "give it a Row parameter" advice is nonsense for a tuple —
  -- you cannot add one.  ⚠️ The span is best-effort: `TyTuple` carries no loc of its own
  -- and `TyVar` carries none either, so `impl I (a, b)` genuinely has no span to point at
  -- and reports unlocated.  Fabricating a nearby one would be worse than saying nothing.
  (TyTuple ts, _) =>
    pushTypeErrorOncePerSite
      mctx
      "T-IMPL-KIND-MISMATCH"
      (firstTyLocList ts)
      (implTupleHeadKindMsg iface (listLen ts) want)
  _ => ()

checkGradedImplHeadCon : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  TyConOrigin ->
  String ->
  Option Loc ->
  Int ->
  List Kind ->
  Unit
checkGradedImplHeadCon mctx iface o n loc nApplied want =
  match headRemainingKinds mctx o n nApplied
    None => ()
    Some got => checkGradedImplHeadKinds mctx iface n loc nApplied want got

-- The head constructor's declared parameter kinds MINUS the ones the head already
-- applies (`impl I (Async e)` supplies one).  `None` = "this head's kind is not
-- knowable here" (an alias or a builtin), which the caller treats as an abstention.
-- ⚠️ An abstractly-exported type was in that bucket until #804/#1028 and is NOT any
-- more — `kindPublicDataDecl`'s `VisAbstract` arm gives it a real `dataParamKindsRef`
-- entry (via `declEnvSeedChain`), so it returns `Some` and is judged exactly like
-- a `public export` one.
-- `key` is minted ONCE and shared by both guard arms via the `where` (#1111
-- A-2.3 follow-up): the first guard ALWAYS evaluates it (Medaka is strict, and
-- a `where` scoping over guard arms lowers to `ELetGroup (..key..) (EGuards
-- arms)`, so the binding runs once before either arm is tested), so hoisting
-- adds nothing on the alias arm and removes the previously-redundant second
-- mint on the common `otherwise` arm.  A redundant-allocation removal, not a
-- measured perf win (`test/bench.sh` doesn't run on this box, #1187; the
-- perf-scaling gate grades a growth ratio, blind to a constant factor).
headRemainingKinds : ModuleCtx ->
  TyConOrigin ->
  String ->
  Int ->
  Option (List Kind)
headRemainingKinds mctx o n nApplied
  | isSome (lookupTab key mctx.mcCells.aliasTableRef.value) = None
  | otherwise =
    map (drop nApplied) (lookupTab key mctx.mcCells.dataParamKindsRef.value)
  where
    key = tyTabKey o n

checkGradedImplHeadKinds : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  String ->
  Option Loc ->
  Int ->
  List Kind ->
  List Kind ->
  Unit
checkGradedImplHeadKinds mctx iface n loc nApplied want got
  | kindsEq got want = ()
  | otherwise =
    pushTypeErrorOncePerSite
      mctx
      "T-IMPL-KIND-MISMATCH"
      loc
      (implKindMismatchMsg iface n nApplied want got)

-- Closure construction is pure; only the source body's final application runs it.
arrowsWithLastEffect : List Mono -> EffRow -> Mono -> Mono
arrowsWithLastEffect params eff result = bodyArrows params eff result

-- Keyed indices — so the hot per-field-access read paths never walk a linear registry
-- (issue #149).  #415 item 3: `registerRecordInfoKeyed` is the sole REGISTRATION writer of
-- both; they are cleared together by `freshModuleCtx`; and the cross-module record floor is
-- loaded by `loadDataUniverse` from `universeRecordPop`.
--
-- 🚨 THE LOCKSTEP WAS "STRUCTURAL, NOT AN OBLIGATION" UNTIL #1111 A-2.12 (#1319 unit 2),
-- AND IT IS NOW AN OBLIGATION.  `applyRecordScopeOverrides` re-points `recordByNameRef`
-- for a collided key and does NOT touch `fieldOwnersRef`, so the two are no longer written
-- only in pairs and nothing enforces that they agree.  Re-pointing key `K` cannot change
-- which KEYS own a field name, but it does change which FIELDS `K` declares — so with two
-- same-named records having DISJOINT field sets, `fieldOwnersRef` can name `K` as the owner
-- of a field the newly-selected `K` does not declare.
-- ⚠️ THAT IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL AND AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS NOTE SAID IT WAS.  It called the
-- divergence "an obligation with no observed consequence" on the strength of one probe that
-- kept every projection inside the module which NAMED the record — where the overlay and the
-- floor agree by construction, so the probe could not have shown anything.  **#1377 was the
-- consequence**: a module naming one `Cfg` and holding a value of the other was refused.
-- 🚨 #1319 UNIT 3 DRAINED #1377, AND THE OBLIGATION SURVIVES IT.  Unit 3 did not reconcile
-- the two tables; it stopped ASKING the overlay a question the overlay could not answer —
-- `resolveFieldRecord`'s arm (a) now selects by the receiver's identity (see
-- `lookupRecordForReceiver`).  So the one observed consequence is gone and the write
-- asymmetry is not.  ⚠️ Do NOT restate this as "no observed consequence today": that exact
-- sentence has now been wrong twice here, and what is true is narrower — the consequence
-- that was found has been removed, and nobody has established that it was the only one.
-- Anything added here must state which of the two it writes and why the other is safe.
--   recordByNameRef : registry KEY → RecordInfo.  omInsert is last-write-wins and
--     the register site inserts in registration order, so it reproduces the old
--     prepend-list first-match (latest-registered wins) for lookupRecordByName.
--   fieldOwnersRef  : field name → the registry keys whose RecordInfo declares it
--     (a multimap).  fieldOwnerNames still `sortUniqS`es this so the owner-list
--     order that feeds ambiguousFieldMsg/head stays byte-identical.

-- Transparent type aliases (`type Foo = Int`, `type Pair a = (a, a)`).  Keyed by
-- alias name → (params, RHS surface type).  Populated in a pre-pass by
-- `registerData`'s DTypeAlias arm (mirrors `dataParamKindsRef`); consulted
-- on-demand at the `Ty→Mono` seam (`fromAstTypeE`) to expand an alias to its RHS.
-- The param list is stored even though stage 2 only expands the zero-param case,
-- so parameterized expansion (stage 3) can extend this without reshaping the table.

-- Names of record/named-field types exported ABSTRACTLY (`export data`/`export
-- record` without `public`).  Seeded ONCE (over EVERY module's decls, prelude
-- included) by the multi-module check drivers, BEFORE per-module checking, and
-- deliberately NOT cleared by `freshModuleCtx` — it is whole-program metadata, not a
-- per-module accumulator.  An abstract export brings the type NAME into scope but
-- never registers its fields (publicDataDecls drops VisAbstract decls, so they never
-- reach the record registry in an importer — its PARAM KINDS do travel, since #804/#1028, via
-- kindPublicDataDecl's VisAbstract arm, but a kind is not a field).  A dot-access on
-- such a type therefore lands at resolveFieldRecord's `head known but no record
-- info` branch with the type name still recoverable as the receiver's head tycon;
-- membership here distinguishes that case (clear abstract-export diagnostic) from a
-- genuinely-unknown field on an unbound receiver (the `<unknown>` message).  This
-- mirrors resolve's destructure-side AbstractFieldAccess signal (env.types ∋ owner
-- ∧ owner owns no field) without threading anything new through the import seed.

-- collect the names of all VisAbstract record-shaped (a DData whose variants
-- carry named fields) decls across the given decl list.  Only
-- record-shaped abstract types can be a dot-access receiver, but harvesting any
-- abstract DData name too is harmless (a positional ADT can't reach the abstract
-- branch with a field access — its fields never exist).
collectAbstractRecordTypes : List Decl -> List String
collectAbstractRecordTypes [] = []
collectAbstractRecordTypes ((DData { dataVis = VisAbstract, dataName = n }) :: rest) =
  n :: collectAbstractRecordTypes rest
collectAbstractRecordTypes (_ :: rest) = collectAbstractRecordTypes rest

-- seed abstractRecordTypesRef from every module's decls (the per-module progs plus
-- the prelude/core decls), once, before checking begins.  Keyed by the type
-- word (`typeTagOf`), so a program's own type that shares an abstract export's
-- name is not mistaken for it.
seedAbstractRecordTypes : GraphCtx ->
  List Decl ->
  List (String, List Decl) ->
  Unit
seedAbstractRecordTypes gctx coreDecls modules =
  let abstracts =
    collectAbstractRecordTypes coreDecls
      ++ flatMap (m => abstractTypeWords (fst m) (snd m)) modules
  gctx.abstractRecordTypesRef := namesToSet abstracts omEmpty

abstractTypeWords : String -> List Decl -> List String
abstractTypeWords mid decls =
  map (n => typeTagOf (OriginModule mid) n) (collectAbstractRecordTypes decls)

-- return-position method sites discovered during inference: (method name, the
-- EMethodAt route ref to fill, the EMethodAt impl-dicts ref to fill, the method's
-- result mono).  After the whole program is inferred, each result mono's head
-- tycon is the concrete impl tag the site dispatches to (RKey) — or, when it is a
-- constrained function's constraint variable, that function's dict parameter
-- (RDict).  The impl-dicts ref is filled (single-module elaborate path only) when
-- the route is a parametric impl with a `requires` — one route per requires.
-- #156 S3a: entries are `PendingEntry`s of kind `SKReturn`.

-- Phase 151 / Gap G: comparison/equality OPERATOR sites discovered during
-- inference: (method name, the EBinOp route ref to fill, the operand mono).
-- After inference resolveBinopSites stamps each ref with the resolved Eq/Ord impl
-- route (RKey) — but ONLY when the operand grounds to a NON-primitive type; the
-- structural-builtin EBinOp eval path handles primitive / ungroundable operands
-- (so `eq a b = a == b` on Int never recurses).  dictPass then rewrites the
-- stamped node into the method application.
-- (method, route ref, operand mono, inImpl-flag, enclosing-fn name).  The 5th
-- field is currentFn at record time: for a TOP-LEVEL constrained fn an operator on
-- its own constraint var routes RDict $dict_<encl>_<slot> (via enclDictVarOf), the
-- operator analogue of the direct `eq x y` arg-stamp path.
-- #156 S3a: entries are `PendingEntry`s of kind `SKOp`.

-- Roadmap #18c: the EUnOp analogue of pendingBinopSites — `-` (Num's `negate`)
-- sites discovered during inference.  Same tuple shape/fields, same resolve/
-- rewrite seam (resolveUnopSites / rewriteUnopExpr), one operand instead of two.

-- Arithmetic EBinOp sites whose operand type may ground to a concrete primitive.
-- Recorded during inference (operand Mono + the node's route ref);
-- resolveArithSites reads each solved Mono after the whole module is inferred and
-- stamps its supported scalar tag so lowering carries the result type into
-- CBinPrim and the native emitter need not recover it from operand structure. A still-
-- polymorphic (Num a) operand never grounds → stays RNone → today's dict path
-- (mirrors resolveBinopSite's grounded-only guard, so dict-routed arithmetic is
-- untouched).

-- Error-path BLOCKER B4 (audit finding D3): missing-impl dispatch obligations.
-- `methodEntryHere` maps each interface method NAME → (iface, the iface's typarams,
-- the method's declared AST type), as the reading module's scope resolves it
-- (`methodScopeAt`).  At each EVar/EMethodAt occurrence of a
-- registered method, recordImplObligation captures the OCCURRENCE mono so that,
-- after inference, checkImplObligations can read what the interface params
-- resolved to (parallel-walking the declared type against the normalized
-- occurrence mono) and reject the call when those concrete head types have NO
-- matching impl in the program (the `No impl of … for …` reject).  Skips while a param is still a
-- polymorphic tyvar (deferred to the caller).
-- A bare-name collision between two unrelated interfaces is decided by the reading
-- module's scope, never by registration order (#1092) — see `MethodEnv`.

-- C5 (TYPECHECK-AUDIT / Phase 112): names that are BOTH an interface method AND a
-- cross-module-imported standalone top-level function (e.g. box's `toList`/`isEmpty`
-- shadowing Foldable's).  Populated per module by elabModuleStamp from the full graph
-- (a top-level funDef name that is also a method name and is NOT defined in the
-- current module).  resolveSite consults it: a method site at a concrete receiver
-- with NO impl, whose name is here, routes RLocal (eval reads the standalone) instead
-- of RKey<head> (which would panic with no impl).
-- `freshModuleCtx` starts it empty; `checkBodyImpl` rebuilds it per module.

-- DEFINER-shadow names (facet 2): the names THIS module declares as a top-level
-- funDef that ALSO name an interface method (buildDefinerShadows) — e.g. a user
-- `eq : List Int -> List Int -> Bool`.  A DIRECT call `eq [1] [2]` in user code
-- must resolve to the user's OWN definition (RLocal), NOT to a method impl, even
-- when the receiver's head HAS an impl of the interface (`List` has `Eq`).  The
-- arg-stamp pass would otherwise stamp `RKey:List` (the impl), making the eval path
-- dispatch to the prelude `Eq (List a)` impl (`[1] ≠ [2]` → False) instead of the
-- user's fn (True) — a run≠build divergence (the EMIT path already routes to the
-- user's def).  resolveRLocalSite stamps these RLocal unconditionally.  Populated
-- per-module in checkModuleFullImpl from buildDefinerShadows; reset by `freshModuleCtx`.

-- P0-19: the declared top-level SIGNATURES of definer-shadow standalones
-- (`size : Int -> Int`), keyed by name.  When a definer-shadow occurrence resolves
-- to the STANDALONE (no visible impl for the grounded receiver, or an ungrounded
-- receiver), inferDefinerShadowApp enforces this declared domain against the actual
-- argument — closing the S2/S5 "must then type against the standalone's domain" hole
-- that let `size "hi"` / a poly wrapper `useIt x = size x; useIt (Box 3)` type against
-- the permissive method scheme and reach codegen as garbage.  Set per-path from
-- `sigsOf prog`; empty for an unsignatured standalone (no domain to enforce → the old
-- permissive behavior, unchanged).

-- P0-19 d4b (S4): True while inferring the HEAD of a definer-shadow APPLICATION
-- (`size (Box 3)`) — set around the head-infer call in inferDefinerShadowVarApp /
-- inferDefinerShadowApp.  A shadow occurrence reaches inferVar / inferMethodAt in
-- two shapes: as an application head (dispatch-vs-standalone decided per-receiver by
-- the surrounding shadow-app machinery, so the head must keep the permissive METHOD
-- scheme `a -> Int`) OR in bare VALUE position (`map size xs`, `let f = size`), which
-- S4 says ALWAYS denotes the standalone.  This flag distinguishes the two so only the
-- value-position occurrence is pinned to the standalone scheme.  Default/reset False.

-- P0-18 (EMIT path only): the mangler (`mangleUnits`) renames a definer-shadow
-- standalone def + its call sites to `<mid>__name` BEFORE marking, but (correctly)
-- leaves the interface method name bare — so the mark pass's NAME-based shadow
-- detector (buildStandaloneShadowsGraph / buildDefinerShadows, keyed on
-- funDef-name ∩ iface-method-name) no longer sees a shadow and the occurrence never
-- becomes an `EMethodAt` dispatch site (→ a silent direct call to the standalone =
-- the build miscompile).  elaborateModules recovers the shadow post-mangle by
-- forward-constructing `mangledName mid method` for every (module, iface-method)
-- pair and checking it against the module's actual funDef names; each hit is a
-- `(mangledSymbol ↦ bareMethod)` entry recorded here.  The mark pass then (a) marks
-- the mangled occurrence `EMethodAt` with the BARE dispatch name (so `implFor` finds
-- the impl for a receiver that HAS one) and (b) carries the mangled symbol in the
-- route's `RLocal <symbol>` fallback for a receiver that does NOT.
-- #2809 RETIRED THE "EMPTY OFF THE EMIT PATH" INVARIANT.  Mangling now runs AFTER
-- elaboration, so NO path reaches this map with mangled funDefs and the rows every path
-- gets are the BARE ones `unitMangledShadows` adds: `(name ↦ name)` for a definer
-- shadow, in every module of the graph.  Both spellings are still recorded there, so
-- (a) and (b) above read the same way; what changed is that the SYMBOL half is now the
-- bare standalone name and the rename that moves it runs later.  A consumer must no
-- longer treat a non-empty map as "this is the emit path".
-- Set once at the top of elaborateModules;
-- deliberately NOT cleared by `freshModuleCtx` (checkModuleFullImpl's per-module `freshModuleCtx`
-- must not wipe it mid-graph) — the forward-construction membership check makes a
-- stale value inert (no funDef matches → no entry).

-- one entry per occurrence of a registered interface method: (iface, typarams,
-- declared method Ty, the occurrence's instantiated mono).  Resolved post-inference.
-- B.10.2c: the 5th element is the enclosing construct's span (`mcLoc`) snapshotted
-- at the RECORD site (during inference, when the construct is live), so the post-HM
-- obligation check (checkImplObligations) can pair a `No impl of …` reject with
-- the offending expression's range — captured at record time
-- rather than reading the stale global at the post-HM raise.

-- PERF: the obligation list's length, in O(1).  That list grows with every
-- constrained occurrence in the program and is NEVER trimmed, yet each top-level
-- group brackets its inference with a length-before / length-after pair to recover
-- the obligations IT added (they are consed on the front, so `wWindow` recovers
-- them).  Measuring that length by walking the list was O(N) over an O(N) list once
-- per group — O(N²), and the single hottest symbol in the typecheck stage on a large
-- file.  #841 ports this channel onto `Windowed` (see `implObls` below): `wPush`,
-- the per-module `ModuleCtx` mint, and `wRestore` (checkMethodBodyAgainst's error
-- rollback) are its only mutators, so the list and its length can no longer drift.

-- PLAN.md #11: one entry per source integer literal (ENumLit):
-- (litVar, fref, n, dref).  [litVar] is the literal's fresh Num-obligated type var;
-- [fref] is the node's own Option Float cell; [n] the int value; [dref] is the
-- node's `fromInt`-route cell (filled by resolveSites — the literal is modelled as a
-- `fromInt n` method occurrence).  After defaulting + grounding, the post-HM pass
-- setNumlitFloats decides the runtime rep: litVar ground Float ⇒ fref Some, dref cleared ⇒ ELit (LFloat f);
-- litVar ground Int ⇒ both cleared ⇒ ELit (LInt n); litVar still polymorphic `Num a`
-- (the soundness case — `1` in `inc x = x + 1`) ⇒ dref KEPT (RDictFwd onto the
-- enclosing Num dict) ⇒ dictPass emits `EApp (EMethodAt "fromInt" …) (ELit (LInt n))`.

-- Chunk A (error framing): the union-find root ids of every type var that took
-- part in a unification failure (`typeMismatch`).  Consulted ONLY by
-- `undeterminedGoalExempt` to SUPPRESS a secondary `ambiguous instance`
-- cascade on a var the primary mismatch already explained — never read on the
-- inference path, so a well-typed program (no mismatch) never poisons anything
-- and behaves identically.

-- Chunk D (Num mis-framing): (litVar, loc) for every numeric literal whose var
-- carried a Num obligation — captured at inferNumLit/inferNumLitBare record time
-- while the var is still unbound.  Lets checkOneImplObligation reframe a purely
-- literal Num obligation forced to a concrete non-Num type (`Type mismatch: Int vs
-- T`) while an OPERATOR-sourced one (`x + 1`) keeps `No impl of Num for T`.  Storing
-- the VAR (not just the loc) lets the operator-taint pass below share a root through
-- `normalize`, so `1 + x` and `x + 1` are both recognised as operator-sourced
-- regardless of unify direction.  Error-path only; reset per run.

-- PERF: the literals that are NOT YET operator-tainted.  `markNumlitOpTaint` scans
-- THIS instead of the full `numlitVarLocs` (which is never trimmed).  Sound because
-- tainting is idempotent: it appends a loc to `numlitOpLocs`, whose only reader
-- (`numlitReframeLoc`) does a membership test — so re-tainting an already-tainted
-- literal cannot change any outcome, and a tainted literal may leave the worklist.
-- Scanning EVERY literal ever recorded on EVERY arithmetic operand was O(N²), and
-- after the allocation fix (see `rootIdOf`) it was still the typecheck stage's
-- dominant remaining cost on a large file.
--
-- `numlitVarLocs` itself keeps every literal — `numlitReframeLoc` and
-- `tagLitLocsWithRoot` both still need the complete list.

-- Chunk D: locs of literals whose var was ALSO an operand of an arithmetic op
-- (recordIfaceObligation).  Such a literal keeps the Num message — the operator is the
-- real culprit — so the reframe skips it (it reframes `litLocs \ opLocs`).

-- Chunk D: (literalLoc, contextKind) recorded when inferIf / inferListLit / consOp
-- is about to force a still-unbound literal var against a concrete sibling type —
-- lets the reframe pick site-specific wording (if-branches / list elements / cons
-- head-vs-element) over the bare `Type mismatch: Int vs T`.

-- Every local binding (let-bound name, lambda param, function-clause param,
-- match-arm binder) flows through inferPat's PVar/PAs arms, which capture
-- (name, mono var) here.  The mono var is union-find-solved by the time inference
-- ends; the module checker then generalizes each into `localSchemesOut`, and
-- `captureEntryTables` freezes them into the drive's `PartialAnalysis`.  The seed
-- (runtime.mdk externs: putStrLn, readLine, …) stays in scope for inference but
-- is excluded from the returned env, so `seedSchemesOut` is frozen the same way.
-- Neither enters the returned env.

-- #1114 (DICT-SEMANTICS §4.2 D1): would `checkOneCallObligation` reach a VERDICT on this
-- recorded predicate right now?  That — not groundness — is the question the D1-preserving
-- window in `inferUserImplBodies` has to ask, and getting it wrong is silent by
-- construction (see the warning at the end of this comment).
--
-- The gate decides a goal now exactly when every argument has a constructed head
-- (`allConcreteHeads`), and that verdict cannot change later: grounding is monotone, so
-- a constructed head (a type constructor, a rigid, or an arrow) never becomes a variable.
-- A predicate this filter drops while the gate would decide it vanishes with no verdict
-- from any channel (D4 exempts the impl channel from D3), which is #792's three-verdict
-- signature (`check` 0 / `run` `intToString: not an Int` / `build` `arg-tag dispatch on
-- impl type that owns no constructors`).
-- `numUnimplementableHead`'s `TApp` arm (a spine head that is an unbound tyvar) is NOT
-- kept: that head can still bind, so its verdict is not stable and the predicate belongs
-- to D2's deferred population.  An EMPTY argument vector is inert at the gate
-- (`if isEmptyL args then ()`), so dropping it loses no verdict.
--
-- The set is closed, enumerated from the type rather than sampled.  `Mono` has six
-- constructors and `headMonoNode` peels `TApp`, so a head is one of `TVar`, `TCon`,
-- `TRigid`, `TFun`, `TEff`.  `TCon`/`TRigid`/`TFun` are the constructed heads
-- `headTyconMono` answers, so `allConcreteHeads` keeps them; `TVar` can still bind, so
-- gate and filter agree to defer it; and `TEff` is decided by neither (the gate reaches
-- its own `allConcreteHeads` arm and defers).  A vector mixing a constructed head with a
-- variable defers in both, whatever the constructed head is.
--
-- ⚠️ NO GATE CAN CATCH A REGRESSION HERE.  A predicate this filter drops is one no channel
-- ever reports, so it produces silence, and silence is what every golden in the corpus
-- already records for a program the compiler accepts.  If you narrow this predicate, the
-- suite stays green.  The obligation is on the reader: any arm added to
-- `checkOneCallObligation` ABOVE its `allConcreteHeads` test must be mirrored here, or it
-- becomes unreachable for every parametric impl body in the language.
uOblIsDecidableNow : GraphCtx -> UObligation -> Bool
uOblIsDecidableNow gctx o =
  let args = map normalize (uOblArgs gctx o)
  isNonEmptyL args && allConcreteHeads args

-- the top-level fn whose body is currently being inferred ("" = none); captured
-- into a deferred RecDictApp so its recursive calls forward the right dict param.

-- G4: True while inferring an impl method BODY (set around inferImplMethod).  A
-- comparison/equality OPERATOR site records this flag so resolveBinopSite consults
-- `activeDictVarOf` (→ route the impl's threaded element dict, RDict) ONLY for sites
-- genuinely inside an impl body.  A TOP-LEVEL `<=`/`==` must NOT — its operand could
-- normalize to an unsolved tyvar whose id collides with a stale activeDictVars entry
-- left by a previously-inferred impl, spuriously routing it RDict (which flipped the
-- repl's String-keyed `:browse` sort).  activeDictVars is global + uncleared, so the
-- flag is the scope gate the id-lookup alone cannot provide.

-- INFERRED (unsignatured) `=>`-constraint promotion (the reference's two-pass
-- Elaborate / Phase 83/84/115).  An unsignatured fn whose body uses a
-- return-position method — or calls a constrained fn — at one of its OWN
-- generalized tyvars carries a constraint only AFTER inference.  We discover this
-- by recording, per occurrence, the enclosing fn (currentFn) and the live mono,
-- then (post-generalization) intersecting with the fn's quantified ids.
--   methodSiteFns : (enclosing fn, a return-position method site's result mono)
--   dictAppFns    : (enclosing fn, a constrained-fn call's instantiated constraint
--                   monos) — propagates a constraint to an unsignatured CALLER
--   promotedRef   : fns discovered THIS pass to carry an inferred constraint; read
--                   by the retired promotion fixpoint to grow the dict-passed set
--   dictEligibleRef: the USER fn names eligible for promotion (the prelude's
--                   constrained fns stay arg-tag/RKey — out of scope).  Set by
--                   the old elaborator; NOT cleared by `freshModuleCtx` (constant per run).
--
-- PERF: both are INDEXED BY ENCLOSING FN rather than kept as flat (fn, mono) assoc
-- lists.  Their sole reader, `inferredConstraintIds`, selects the entries of ONE fn,
-- and it runs once per member of every top-level group — so scanning a flat list that
-- accumulates a site for every constrained occurrence in the whole file was O(N²).
-- Each key's list is built by consing, exactly like the flat lists were, so a fn's
-- sites keep the same most-recent-first order the old scan produced.

-- The graph's promoted names so far, in load order.  `freshModuleCtx` clears
-- `promotedRef` per module, so `graphModuleWorker`'s `GOutTrees` arm unions each
-- module's `promotedRef.value` into here right after that module's check (before
-- the next module's `freshModuleCtx` wipes it).  Its reader is `beginModuleMarking`: a
-- module's dict-name set is the bare set plus THIS list, which is what lets one
-- sweep mark a promoted callee's cross-module call sites (ARCH §E).  Cleared at
-- every Module-arm driver entry (`elaborateModules`, `checkModulesPreambleK`) so an
-- earlier elaboration in the process cannot leak promoted names into a later mark
-- set; NOT touched by `freshModuleCtx`.  `elaborateModules` reads it once more at the
-- end, for the set `dictPass` prepends dict params over (`markDictNames`).

-- O(log n) membership index of dictEligibleRef.  #415 item 3: DERIVED from the list by
-- `setDictEligible`, the single writer of both — not mirrored at each set site, so the
-- two cannot drift.  maybeInferConstraint tests it per SCC member per discovery pass —
-- an O(members × eligible) scan over the whole program when it was a list.

-- Whether the retired single-program checker also inferred each parametric impl's
-- method bodies (instance-`requires` dict-passing, Phase 83/84 single-level).  ON
-- only for the old elaborate/dict path; off for the
-- `=== TYPES ===` golden path (checkProgram) and the multi-module path
-- (elaborateModules) so their scheme output stays byte-identical.  Deliberately
-- NOT reset by `freshModuleCtx` — the entrypoint that owns the path sets it.

-- ── D0.5 arg-position dispatch MEASUREMENT (probe-only) ─────────────────────
-- Classify every ARGUMENT-position interface-method occurrence (the bare-EVar
-- arg-tag population D0 counted, upper bound 1065) by the inferred type of its
-- DISCRIMINATING argument: concrete-primitive / concrete-ADT / type-variable.
-- Mirrors recordSite/resolveSites (which stamp RETURN-position sites) but for
-- arg-position sites it MEASURES, never stamps.  An arg-position method is exactly
-- one that reached inferVar (return-position + method-constrained methods were
-- already rewritten to EMethodAt/EDictAt by prePassDict, so they never arrive there).

-- method name → 0-based index of its first argument mentioning the interface
-- typaram (its dispatch position).  Set by the probe before elaboration; absence
-- of a name means "not an arg-position interface method" → not measured.

-- ── D3a arg-position dispatch STAMPING (Native backend, ALL elaboration paths) ──
-- The action analog of the D0.5 measurement: instead of classifying each
-- ARGUMENT-position interface-method occurrence, STAMP a static `RKey <head>` for
-- every one whose discriminating-argument type resolves to a concrete head (the
-- 903 concrete sites = 25 primitive + 878 ADT).  Type-variable occurrences (the
-- 110 D3b sites) stay RNone → the emitter falls back to runtime arg-tag dispatch.
-- Stamping is UNCONDITIONAL: emit, eval, and the `=== TYPES ===` / Core-IR golden +
-- ceval-oracle drivers all elaborate identically — one single elaboration mode
-- (#157).  Measured byte-identical across the 204/204 fixtures, so the unification
-- is representation-neutral, not a behaviour change.

-- the route refs awaiting an arg-position stamp + their discriminating-argument
-- mono (captured during inference, resolved by resolveArgStamps while the tyvar
-- cells are still bound).  Recorded as `GKArgStamp` goals on `GraphRun.goals`,
-- drained per module like the return-position sites.
-- D3b-1: also carries the method name + the EMethodAt impl-dicts ref, so a
-- concrete site whose head names a parametric `requires` impl can thread the
-- element dict (resolveArgStamp → argImplDictRoutesForEncl), exactly as the
-- return-position sites carry implRef for resolveSite.
-- #156 S3a: entries are `PendingEntry`s of kind `SKArg`.

-- Native Gap C (parametric default-method dict-synthesis, 2026-06-12): a BY-NAME
-- relational method (`lt`/`gt`/…) at a parametric Ord head (tuple/`List a`/`Box a`)
-- has NO own impl, so its element `requires` dicts must be keyed off the inner
-- `compare` (whose impl carries them).  emitDefaultDefine eta-prepends matching
-- dict params; emitDefaultRKey forwards these words.  Concrete head / a method
-- with its own impl ⇒ same key as before (empty for non-parametric), unchanged.

-- ── type-error accumulator ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Unification failures record diagnostics here instead of panicking, so
-- ill-typed programs emit matching `TYPE ERROR: …` lines.  occursCheckFailed
-- is a per-bindVar flag: occursAdjustUnbound sets it so bindVar can skip the
-- actual link (preventing a cyclic union-find entry).
-- Each accumulated error carries the span of the construct around its push site
-- (the record's `mcLoc`, see `mctxAt`) unless the push names one.  severity = 1.
--
-- issue 1146 — THE CHANNEL IS SPLIT BY ROLE.  "Which diagnostics are REPORTED"
-- is OUTPUT and lives in `ModuleCells.mcCells.typeErrors`, a `Windowed TcDiag` like its
-- obligation-channel siblings (see `Windowed` above — `wPush`/`wRestore` are
-- its sole WRITERS, so its list and its count cannot drift apart).  "An error
-- OCCURRED" is CONTROL and lives in `ModuleCells.mcCells.errorsDetected`, a monotone-per-module
-- occurrence counter that is not a diagnostics channel at all.
--
-- The counter counts errors DETECTED, not errors STORED (PR2).  The three dedup
-- helpers below still read the list by CONTENT to decide whether to store, but a
-- short-circuit bumps the counter anyway (`noteTypeErrorDetected`), so "was an error
-- detected here" and "is this diagnostic worth printing" are now independent
-- judgments.  That is the property the whole split exists for: NO diagnostics
-- decision — dedup key, rendering, ordering, loc selection, code selection — can
-- reach a control decision, because the only thing control reads is a count of
-- detections and none of those choices changes whether a detection happened.
--
-- PR1 stopped short of this: it bumped only on a real store, so the counter's delta
-- equalled `listLen typeErrors`'s delta exactly (which is what let PR1 land without
-- moving a golden), and a deduped push therefore answered `erredDuring` False and let
-- a gated `unify` run that a non-deduped push would have suppressed.  PR2 gives that
-- equality up on purpose; it is no longer an invariant and must not be restored.
--
-- See `recordTypeError` / `noteTypeErrorDetected` (the counter's sole writers) and
-- `erredDuring` (its sole reader) below.

-- G1 (SOUNDNESS): `GraphCtx.typeErrorsSticky` is a sticky mirror of typeErrors that
-- `freshModuleCtx` does not clear.  The multi-module elaborate path
-- (elaborateModules → checkModuleFullImpl) calls `freshModuleCtx` at the start of each
-- module, wiping `typeErrors`, so after the whole graph only the last module's errors
-- survive there.  build/run must abort on a type error in any module, so
-- `pushTypeError` also records into this accumulator, which the drive's mint
-- starts `False`.  Read via `hadTypeErrors` to gate the CLI exit code before
-- emit/eval.
--
-- #2089 / #2544 (M4): `GraphCtx.typeErrorsStickyDiags` holds the diagnostics behind
-- the flag, newest first, across every module of the graph.  `ModuleCells.mcCells.typeErrors` is
-- wiped per module, so this is the only place a caller with no per-module hook can
-- read what armed the sticky flag rather than merely that it was armed — it is what
-- `elaborateModules` returns as its residual, each entry with its own `Loc`.  Written
-- only by `recordTypeError`, started empty by the drive's mint, and rolled back
-- wherever the flag is (`checkGraphFinish`) — the same pairing obligation the
-- detection counter states.  Both are the drive's own.

-- #2544 (M4): every diagnostic that armed the sticky gate in the drive, each tagged
-- with the module it was recorded in, in push order, deduplicated PER GOAL —
-- module, code, location and text together — never by text alone (a text key would
-- re-introduce the suppressed-check shape OD5 forbids: two goals at two sites with
-- the same rendering are two findings).
export
stickyTypeErrorDiags : DriveOutputs -> List (String, TcDiag)
stickyTypeErrorDiags o = stickyDiagsInPushOrder o.doStickyDiags

-- True iff the drive recorded a type error, as the drive left it.
export
hadTypeErrors : DriveOutputs -> Bool
hadTypeErrors o = o.doHadTypeErrors

-- Whether the `main` binding recorded obligations remains inference-private; the
-- publication module receives its Boolean answer rather than this side table.
mainHasObligations : ModuleCtx -> Bool
mainHasObligations mctx =
  let id = optionOr 0 (omLookup "main" mctx.mcCells.schemeDefIdsRef.value)
  match lookupSchemeObls "main" id mctx.mcCells.schemeObligationsRef.value
    Some (_ :: _) => True
    _ => False

-- ── non-exhaustive-match warning accumulator (the type-aware `check_match`) ──
-- `inferMatch` pushes a warning here for every `match` whose non-guarded arms
-- don't cover the scrutinee's type.  `matchOracle` is the ctor oracle the matrix
-- recursion consults; `checkOneMatchToLines` seeds it from the program's
-- data decls (so it sees the same user + builtin ctors check_match does) before
-- inference runs.  `freshModuleCtx` installs both from the `CheckRunSeed` and the driver
-- reads `matchWarnings` after the typecheck pass; runs that ignore match warnings
-- (the schemes/selfproc paths) simply never read it.
-- #159: element type is now `TcDiag` (severity 2), carrying the span (formerly the
-- parallel `matchWarningLocs`) and the actionable-fix help (formerly the message-
-- keyed `matchWarningHelp`) INLINE — no parallel lists, no lookup-by-message.  The
-- `TcDiag.msg` holds the FULL "Warning: …"-prefixed string exactly as the old
-- `List String` did, so the text-rendering paths (`checkOneMatchToLines`,
-- checkToLinesWithRuntime, checkModulesEntryReport) stay byte-identical; only the
-- prefix strip happens on the driver/diagnostics.mdk side.
--
-- ⚠️ THE `W-*` CODE IS AUTHORED AT THE PUSH SITE — write it into the `TcDiag`, never
-- leave it `""` for a downstream reader to guess.  `driver/diagnostics.mdk`'s
-- `diagOfTypeWarning` carries whatever code it finds here straight through to
-- `--json`; it used to re-derive one by prefix-matching this message text, which
-- silently relabelled any third warning `W-NONEXHAUSTIVE` (see that function's own
-- note, and DIAGNOSTIC-CODES-DESIGN.md — "*No chokepoint can infer these*").
-- Register the code in DIAGNOSTIC-CODES-DESIGN.md's warning table in the same change.
--
-- ⚠️ THE `W-` PREFIX IS LOAD-BEARING, not a naming convention.  The JSON `kind` is
-- DERIVED from the code's prefix (`codeKind`), so the code you write here decides
-- how every consumer classifies the diagnostic.  A demoted error that KEEPS its
-- `T-*` code is the trap: it reads as a type error to anything filtering the
-- per-stage taxonomy.  `diagKind` now stops that from rendering an incoherent
-- `{"kind":"type","severity":2}`, but it deliberately does NOT rewrite your code —
-- inventing `W-FOO` from `T-FOO` would be the same derive-identity-from-spelling
-- mistake in the other direction.  Author a `W-*` code; do not reuse the error's.
--
-- This is THE channel for a typecheck-stage warning — including one that used to be
-- an error.  Do NOT demote an error by pushing a severity-2 `TcDiag` through
-- `recordTypeError` instead: it arms `typeErrorsSticky` (aborts `build`/`run`) and
-- bumps `errorsDetected` (steers `erredDuring`-gated inference, issue 1146)
-- UNCONDITIONALLY, without reading severity at all — so the "warning" keeps both of
-- an error's side effects.  It does not even RENDER as a warning: `diagOfTypeError`
-- binds the severity field to `_` and prints severity 1.  (Removing that hardcode
-- would not rescue the idea — it would print severity 2 and still abort the build.
-- The side effects are the reason, not the rendering.)  `matchWarnings` has neither.

-- True iff the last typecheck pass pushed any match warning.  Read by the snapshot
-- runner (`tools/snapshot.mdk`) to decide whether a rendered `# TYPES` section carries
-- diagnostic prose — a `W-*` warning is graded by `compiler/ERROR-QUALITY.md` exactly
-- like an error is, so a `# TYPES` section holding one is NOT `--bless`-able.  Keyed on
-- the accumulator rather than sniffing the rendered text: the renderer must not have to
-- guess which of its own lines are diagnostics.
export
hadMatchWarnings : DriveOutputs -> Bool
hadMatchWarnings o = o.doHadMatchWarnings

-- `hadMatchWarnings` of the last module checked: the only read of a drive that returns no
-- outputs (the projections).
export
matchWarningsNow : ModuleCtx -> Bool
matchWarningsNow mctx = match mctx.mcCells.matchWarnings.value
  [] => False
  _ => True

-- The drive inputs of a driver that loads no stdlib ownership and selects no
-- profile: no module stdlib-owned, the flat entry not stdlib, every trace off, and
-- the `IO` join of no profile.  A pure value (it holds no `Ref`).
--
-- No ownership means every `extern` is stamped (#2072, `ffiStampModeOwned`), and that
-- direction is the safe one on purpose: a driver that passes no ownership suppresses
-- nothing, so the worst it can do is render an `FFI` atom on the stdlib catalog when
-- someone points it at stdlib source.  The inverse default would leave #2072's hole
-- (a user `extern f : Int -> <> Int` typing pure) open on every such path, which is
-- a soundness hole rather than a cosmetic one.
export
defaultDriveInputs : DriveInputs
defaultDriveInputs = DriveInputs {
  diExecutedMainDriver = None,
  diManifestRequests = [],
  diStdlibOwned = omEmpty,
  diFlatEntryIsStdlib = False,
  diTrace = None,
  diIoJoinGrants = ioJoinGrants None,
  diProfileName = "",
  diPreludeKey = None,
}

-- The drive inputs a driver builds from the profile it selected and the loader's
-- owning-root fact (`stdlibOwnership`, `driver/loader.mdk`): whether the flat entry
-- is a stdlib module, and the stdlib-owned module ids.  That fact is read by
-- `ffiStampMode`, which decides whether an `extern` DECLARATION in the program
-- under check is the stdlib's extern catalog (never stamped) or a user's FFI
-- declaration (always stamped).
--
-- Two ownership fields because graph checks carry different amounts of identity.
-- `Module mid _ _` has a module id, so the Module arm asks "is THIS module
-- stdlib-owned" of the set.  `Flat _` has no id at all (the flat driver has already
-- flattened the program into one anonymous decl list), so the entry's ownership
-- arrives as its own Bool.
--
-- NOT `projectTrustedMods` (`driver/loader.mdk`): that predicate answers a different
-- question (may module M *reference* an internal-only extern?) and is opt-in-able
-- from any `medaka.toml` via `allow-internal` (#1713).  Routing this through it would
-- let a user exempt their own externs from the stamp by writing one manifest line.
export
driveInputsFor : Option TargetProfile -> Bool -> List String -> DriveInputs
driveInputsFor profile flatEntry mods = { defaultDriveInputs |
  diStdlibOwned = namesToSet mods omEmpty,
  diFlatEntryIsStdlib = flatEntry,
  diIoJoinGrants = ioJoinGrants profile,
  diProfileName = match profile
    None => ""
    Some p => profileName p,
}

-- Every route a goal carries, in slot order — one for a site, one per slot for
-- a dictionary application.
obligationRoutes : Obligation -> List Route
obligationRoutes o = match o.oDest
  EvRoute r => [r.value]
  EvRoutes rs => rs.value

-- The predicate mono behind each slot, aligned by position with
-- `obligationRoutes`'s answer for the SAME obligation. `GKMethodDict`'s slots
-- carry an `IfaceRef`/`PredicateSlotArgs` pair rather than a `Mono` (#8251), so
-- it answers `None` per slot rather than reconstructing one.
obligationPredicateMonos : Obligation -> List (Option Mono)
obligationPredicateMonos o = match o.oPayload
  GPSite _ m _ => [Some m]
  GPArith m => [Some m]
  GPDictApp app => map Some app.pdaMonos
  GPMethodDict pmd => map (_ => None) pmd.pmdSlots
  GPRecDictApp (RecDictApp _ _ _ m _ _) => [Some m]

routeOutcomeKind : Route -> EvidenceOutcomeKind
routeOutcomeKind RNone = EOKNone
routeOutcomeKind (RKey _ _ _) = EOKInstance
routeOutcomeKind (RDict _) = EOKGiven
routeOutcomeKind (RDictFwd _) = EOKGiven
routeOutcomeKind (RLocal _ _) = EOKLocal
routeOutcomeKind (RScalar _) = EOKScalar
routeOutcomeKind (RProj r _) = routeOutcomeKind r

routeGivenBinder : Route -> Option String
routeGivenBinder (RDict n) = Some n
routeGivenBinder (RDictFwd n) = Some n
routeGivenBinder (RProj r _) = routeGivenBinder r
routeGivenBinder _ = None

routeInstanceKey : Route -> Option String
routeInstanceKey (RKey k _ _) = Some k
routeInstanceKey _ = None

-- The nested route list an `RKey`/`RLocal` packs at this slot: the packed
-- `requires`, exactly as `entailInst` produces them.
routePrerequisiteRoutes : Route -> List Route
routePrerequisiteRoutes (RKey _ rs _) = rs
routePrerequisiteRoutes (RLocal _ rs) = rs
routePrerequisiteRoutes _ = []

renderRouteIdentity : Route -> String
renderRouteIdentity RNone = "RNone"
renderRouteIdentity (RKey k _ _) = "RKey " ++ k
renderRouteIdentity (RDict n) = "RDict " ++ n
renderRouteIdentity (RDictFwd n) = "RDictFwd " ++ n
renderRouteIdentity (RLocal n _) = "RLocal " ++ n
renderRouteIdentity (RScalar n) = "RScalar " ++ n
renderRouteIdentity (RProj r path) =
  "RProj (\{renderRouteIdentity r}) \{joinWith "." (map intToString path)}"

noteEvidenceObservation : GraphCtx -> Obligation -> Unit
noteEvidenceObservation gctx o = match gctx.trace
  Some sink =>
    if sink.tsEvidenceObservationEnabled then
      let routes = obligationRoutes o
      let predicates = obligationPredicateMonos o
      let arity = listLen routes
      sink.tsEvidenceObservationEntries :=
        evidenceObservationEntriesGo o routes predicates arity 0
          ++ sink.tsEvidenceObservationEntries.value
  None => ()

evidenceObservationEntriesGo : Obligation ->
  List Route ->
  List (Option Mono) ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  List EvidenceObservationEntry
evidenceObservationEntriesGo _ [] _ _ _ = []
evidenceObservationEntriesGo o (r :: rs) preds arity slot =
  let (predHere, predsRest) = match preds
    p :: ptail => (p, ptail)
    [] => (None, [])
  EvidenceObservationEntry {
      eoeEv = o.oEv,
      eoeGoalKind = goalKindName o.oKind,
      eoeSlot = slot,
      eoeArity = arity,
      eoePredicate = map ppMono predHere,
      eoeOutcome = routeOutcomeKind r,
      eoeGivenBinder = routeGivenBinder r,
      eoeInstanceKey = routeInstanceKey r,
      eoePrerequisites = map renderRouteIdentity (routePrerequisiteRoutes r),
      eoeScope = o.oScope,
    }
    :: evidenceObservationEntriesGo o rs predsRest arity (slot + 1)

closeScope : ModuleCtx -> Unit -> Unit
closeScope mctx _ =
  mctx.mcCells.currentScope :=
    Scopes.closeScopeCursor
      (currentScopeStore mctx.mcGraph ())
      mctx.mcCells.currentScope.value

-- The `dictPass` mints: a node constructed AFTER the drain, from a route another
-- node already solved, so its cells start at their final values.  The entry is
-- recorded in [pe] as well: the index the pass reads was taken before the node
-- existed.
mintMethodCellWith : ModuleCtx ->
  PassEvidence ->
  String ->
  Int ->
  Route ->
  List Route ->
  EvId
mintMethodCellWith mctx (PassEvidence _ minted) iface arity tag impls =
  let ev = mintMethodCellRaw mctx iface (Some arity) tag impls
  minted :=
    omInsert
      (intToString (evOrdinal ev))
      (EvMethod iface arity tag impls [])
      minted.value
  ev

-- The whole evidence table of this graph: one entry per method occurrence and per
-- minted site, plus the per-goal entries the drain recorded and the entries of the
-- modules a tree drive served (`applyModuleTrees`).
drivenEvidence : GraphCtx -> Unit -> EvTable
drivenEvidence gctx _ =
  cellEntriesFrom gctx.graphRun gctx.graphRun.evBase
    ++ gctx.graphRun.evTable.value

-- Each channel's length as this module begins.
graphMarksNow : GraphCtx -> Unit -> GraphMarks
graphMarksNow gctx _ = GraphMarks {
  mGoals = gctx.graphRun.goalsN.value,
  mNumlit = gctx.graphRun.numlitN.value,
}

recordModuleStart : GraphCtx -> String -> Unit
recordModuleStart gctx mid =
  gctx.graphRun.moduleRanges :=
    (mid, graphMarksNow gctx ()) :: gctx.graphRun.moduleRanges.value

-- The summary's operations over the view of the entry the drive [o] checked.  The
-- field instantiation runs in a graph record of its own, whose effect-variable
-- counter continues from the drive's (`doEffvarNext`).
export
lastInvocationOps : DriveOutputs -> InvocationOps
lastInvocationOps o = match o.doInvocationView
  InvocationView ctors pols kinds =>
    let byHead = ctorsByHead invocationHeadKey ctors
    let gctx = initialGraphCtx builtinCtors (freshGraphRun ())
    gctx.graphRun.effvarCounter := o.doEffvarNext
    InvocationOps {
      headVariances =
        h => match headTyconMono h
          Some (HkDecl key) =>
            slotVariances (paramPolaritiesIn pols key) (lookupTab key kinds)
          _ => None,
      appliedFields =
        applied =>
          let (h, args) = spineParts applied
          flatMap
            (c => instantiateFields gctx args c)
            (optionOr [] (omLookup (invocationHeadKey h) byHead)),
      headKey = invocationHeadKey,
    }

-- Generalize each captured local binding's (now-solved) mono into a Scheme for
-- the LSP hover fallback (see localBindRefs).  Runs at the end of inference when
-- currentLevel is back at the top, so a still-free local var quantifies cleanly
-- to `a`; a ground var (e.g. a `let` bound to a String) renders concretely.
mapLocalSchemes : ModuleCtx ->
  List (String, Option Loc, Mono) ->
  List (String, Option Loc, Scheme)
mapLocalSchemes mctx [] = []
mapLocalSchemes mctx ((n, l, m) :: rest) =
  (n, l, generalize mctx m) :: mapLocalSchemes mctx rest

-- The context the module last checked recorded for its binding [n].
ownContext : ModuleCtx -> String -> List VecObl
ownContext mctx n =
  -- #837: key the obligation lookup by (name, binding-id), exactly as the check-path
  -- reader does — recovering the id from schemeDefIdsRef (top-level binders of the
  -- module last checked).  With the leak-guard windows retired this is what stops a
  -- where-helper `g`'s obligation rendering on an unrelated top-level `g`; a binder
  -- absent from schemeDefIdsRef (id 0) falls to the bare-name scan (today's path).
  let id = optionOr 0 (omLookup n mctx.mcCells.schemeDefIdsRef.value)
  optionOr [] (lookupSchemeObls n id mctx.mcCells.schemeObligationsRef.value)

-- A module's own schemes, each with its context, taken when the module closes:
-- [mctx] still holds that module's tables, and the next module's check
-- mints its own record.
publishOwn : ModuleCtx -> List (String, Scheme) -> List (String, PubScheme)
publishOwn mctx = publishWithContexts (ownContext mctx)

-- Core's own obligations, keyed by bare name (#837: the binding-id half of each
-- key is dropped, as every cross-module reader looks a prelude name up by name).
-- Read right after the core pass, from the record [mctx] core was checked in.
coreOwnContexts : ModuleCtx -> OrdMap (List VecObl)
coreOwnContexts mctx =
  omFromPairs
    (map (kv => (fst (fst kv), snd kv)) mctx.mcCells.schemeObligationsRef.value)
    omEmpty

-- The context a seed name renders with, by three steps in order.  A name the
-- module last checked BINDS takes that module's own context, or none, and never
-- reaches the prelude store, so a buffer's own `isEven x = "s"` cannot pick up the
-- prelude `isEven`'s context (#2054's shape).  The prelude's contexts are consulted
-- ONLY for a name this module does not bind and whose per-run table has no entry
-- at all: on the module arm each module gets its own `freshModuleCtx`, so the
-- prelude's obligations are not in [mctx], and a prelude scheme would otherwise
-- render without its `=>`.
-- The third step reads [coreContexts], the prelude's contexts keyed by bare name.
seedContext : ModuleCtx -> OrdMap (List VecObl) -> String -> List VecObl
seedContext mctx coreContexts n =
  match omLookup n mctx.mcCells.schemeDefIdsRef.value
    Some _ => ownContext mctx n
    None => match lookupSchemeObls n 0 mctx.mcCells.schemeObligationsRef.value
      Some obs => obs
      None => optionOr [] (omLookup n coreContexts)

-- The last module of [modules], checked in [mctx]: its locals and its import seed,
-- frozen with their contexts.  The seed's prelude contexts come from
-- [coreContexts], `graphPreamble`'s snapshot.
captureEntryTables : ModuleCtx ->
  OrdMap (List VecObl) ->
  List (String, List Decl) ->
  EntryTables
captureEntryTables mctx coreContexts modules = match last modules
  None => noEntryTables
  Some (mid, _) => EntryTables {
    etModule = mid,
    etLocals =
      map
        ((n, loc, s) => (n, freezePub s (ownContext mctx n), loc))
        mctx.mcCells.localSchemesOut.value,
    etSeed =
      map
        (b => (
          fst b,
          freezePub (snd b) (seedContext mctx coreContexts (fst b)),
        ))
        mctx.mcCells.seedSchemesOut.value,
  }

-- bind the field pattern vars with fresh types (no field-type info) so the
-- arm body still typechecks; the oracle fails fast on the unknown record, we
-- accumulate, so dropping the bindings would raise spurious unbound-var errors

-- bind the field's pattern vars against a fresh type so the arm body still
-- typechecks (the oracle fails fast on the unknown field; we accumulate, so
-- skipping the binding would raise spurious downstream unbound-variable errors)

-- The module's inference is complete: every deferred literal pattern takes the
-- type its scrutinee finally got, or `Int`.
settleDeferredPatLits : ModuleCtx -> Unit -> Unit
settleDeferredPatLits mctx _ =
  let deferred = mctx.mcCells.patLitDeferred.value
  mctx.mcCells.patLitDeferred := []
  settlePatLitsGo (dynFor mctx) True deferred

-- still infer the sub-patterns so their bindings reach the arm body
-- (else the continued path raises spurious unbound-variable errors the
-- oracle never reaches — it fails fast on the unknown constructor)

-- ── expression inference ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
infer : TcEnv -> Expr -> Mono
infer env (ELit l) = litType l
-- PLAN.md #11: a source integer literal is `Num a` for a fresh `a`.  With the
-- prelude loaded (Num registered + `fromInt` in scope), model the literal exactly
-- as `fromInt n`.  inferMethodAt
-- "fromInt" records the Num impl obligation AND a pendingSite keyed on [dref] (the
-- node's route cell), so resolveSites later stamps [dref]: RKey when the literal's
-- type grounds to a concrete Num head, RDictFwd onto the enclosing `Num a` dict when
-- it stays polymorphic (the soundness case, `1` in `inc x = x + 1` — exactly the
-- route `fromInt 0` in `sum` gets).  Apply the `Int -> a` method type to an Int arg
-- (mirror OCaml's `unify from_int_ty (TFun t_int … a)`) to recover the result var
-- [a], and stash (a, fref, n, dref) in numlitRefs so the post-HM setNumlitFloats can
-- decide concrete-Float / concrete-Int / still-poly.  Recording the obligation here
-- AND (when under `+`) in numArithOp is harmless: both unify the same var, both
-- demand `Num`.  Without the prelude (bare-HM oracle, `builtinClassPresent BNum` False)
-- `fromInt` is unbound: fall back to a plain fresh var, dref stays RNone (⇒ Int).
infer env (ENumLit n ev _) = inferNumLit env n ev
infer env (EWideLit hi lo ev lx) = inferWideLit env hi lo ev lx
infer env (EVar x) = inferVar env x
-- #837: EVarId carries the resolve-minted binding id; thread it to
-- instantiateVarTracked so obligation lookup keys by (name, id).
infer env (EVarId x id) = inferVarId env x id
infer env (EApp f x) = inferAppExpr env f x
infer env (ELam pats body) = inferLam env pats body
infer env (ELet _ isFun pat e1 e2) = inferLet env isFun pat e1 e2
infer env (ELetGroup binds body) = inferLetGroup env binds body
infer env (EIf c t e) = inferIf env c t e
infer env (EMatch scrut arms) = inferMatch env (infer env scrut) arms
infer env (ETuple es) = tupleMono (inferEach env es)
infer env (EListLit es) = inferListLit env es
infer env (EAnnot e ty) = inferAnnot env e ty
infer env (EBinOp op l r ev) =
  inferBinopE env op l r (siteRouteCell env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph ev)
-- An operator or a field access the parser leaves unwrapped names its own span
-- (its operand's: the operator and the field name carry none).
infer env (EUnOp op e ev) =
  inferUnopE
    (envAtIfSome (exprSpanLoc e) env)
    op
    e
    (siteRouteCell env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph ev)
infer env (EInfix op l r) = inferInfix env op l r
infer env (ERecordCreate name fields) = inferRecordCreate env name fields
infer env (EFieldAccess e fname ev) =
  inferFieldAccess (envAtIfSome (exprSpanLoc e) env) e fname ev
infer env (ERecordUpdate base fields ev) = inferRecordUpdate env base fields ev
infer env (EVariantUpdate cname base fields) =
  inferVariantUpdate env cname base fields
infer env (EBlock stmts) = inferBlock env stmts
infer env (EMethodAt name _ ev) =
  inferMethodAtCell env name (methodCellOf env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph ev)
infer env (EDictAt name ev) = inferGrantedAt env name ev
infer env (EArrayLit es) = inferArrayLit env es
infer env (ERangeList lo hi _) = inferIntRange env lo hi (tconBuiltin "List")
infer env (ERangeArray lo hi _) = inferIntRange env lo hi (tconBuiltin "Array")
-- EIndex is desugared to an `index` method call before typecheck (Phase #16b);
-- the built-in index-inference path is retired, so no `EIndex` arm here.  ESlice
-- is likewise desugared to a `slice` method call before typecheck (#670), so
-- no `ESlice` arm here -- a surviving one is a desugar-ordering bug and hits the
-- loud "unsupported expression" catch-all, and a non-container receiver becomes a
-- "no impl of Slice" constraint error via normal method dispatch.
infer env (EHeadAnnot e ty) = inferHeadAnnot env e ty
-- ELoc is transparent: the wrapped expression and every check inside it are
-- located at this span, until a nested construct names its own.
infer env (ELoc l e) = infer (envAt (Some l) env) e
-- Phase 150: a do-lowered chain.  Record the do-block loc so a monad-shape
-- mismatch during inference is retargeted to the tailored "do requires a monad"
-- error (see typeMismatch).  The chain's walk gets its own context; an inline
-- nested `do` block (`a <- (do ...)`) mints another, so its first report never
-- un-blames a LATER statement of the outer chain (#894 review finding 2).
infer env (EDoOrigin l e) =
  -- #824: the lowered chain's synthesized callee names the herald
  -- (`deferThen` for a `defer` block), so the "requires a monad" reframe can
  -- name the right interface.
  let doCtx = DoCtx {
    doLoc = l,
    doDeferred = doChainIsDeferred e,
    doReported = Ref False,
  }
  infer { env | teDyn = { env.teDyn | dcDo = Some doCtx } } e

infer env _ = panic "typecheck: unsupported expression"

-- is this lowered do-chain a `defer` block?  Its head callee is the tagged
-- `deferThen` (see `callAndThen` in desugar.mdk).
doChainIsDeferred : Expr -> Bool
doChainIsDeferred (EApp f _) = doChainIsDeferred f
doChainIsDeferred (ELoc _ e) = doChainIsDeferred e
doChainIsDeferred (EDoOrigin _ (EVar "deferThen")) = True
doChainIsDeferred (EDoOrigin _ (EVarId "deferThen" _)) = True
doChainIsDeferred _ = False

inferArrayLit : TcEnv -> List Expr -> Mono
inferArrayLit env es =
  let elem = joinValueTypes env.teDyn JoinArray (inferProduced env es)
  TApp (tconBuiltin "Array") elem

-- [lo..hi] : List Int, [|lo..hi|] : Array Int
inferIntRange : TcEnv -> Expr -> Expr -> Mono -> Mono
inferIntRange env lo hi container =
  unifyIn env.teDyn (infer env lo) (tconBuiltin "Int")
  unifyIn env.teDyn (infer env hi) (tconBuiltin "Int")
  TApp container (tconBuiltin "Int")

-- (ESlice's `inferSlice`/`indexKind` were retired with #670: `a.[lo..hi]` now
-- desugars to a `slice` method call before typecheck, so slicing infers
-- through normal interface dispatch on `Slice`, not a bespoke arm here.)

-- C5: if [name] is a standalone-shadow method, record its discriminating-arg
-- mono cell UNGATED so resolveRLocalSites can route RLocal when the receiver
-- grounds to a no-impl head (the arg-stamp path would otherwise leave it RNone
-- → arg-tag panic on a receiver with no impl).

-- Cause-A prerequisite: ALSO record the discriminating-arg mono into
-- methodSiteFns keyed by currentFn (mirroring recordSite, which only fires
-- for return-position).  Without this, an unsignatured fn whose body
-- dispatches a method in ARGUMENT position (`f s = display s`) never
-- surfaces its inferred constraint to inferredConstraintIds → never gets
-- promoted → no leading dict param on the build path → dict word 0 (SIGSEGV/
-- silent).  Inert unless promotion (`registerInferredConstraints`, whose result the
-- schedule marks with) consumes it.

localAbsFor : GraphCtx -> String -> Option LocalAbs
localAbsFor gctx name =
  match omLookup name gctx.graphRun.localAbs.lasBinders.value
    Some found => found
    None => None

-- Forget what a previous inference of the same binder left, before any member of
-- its group is inferred (a group member's body records its siblings' uses): an
-- earlier inference in this drive, or a check of the module id in an earlier one.
forgetLocalAbs : GraphCtx -> String -> Unit
forgetLocalAbs gctx name =
  forgetLocalRows gctx.graphRun.localAbs gctx.graphRun.grants name

-- Enter a candidate local binder's own scope before its right-hand side is
-- inferred.
openLocalScope : ModuleCtx -> String -> ScopeId
openLocalScope mctx name =
  let parent = captureScope mctx ()
  let sid =
    Scopes.freshScope
      (currentScopeStore mctx.mcGraph ())
      (Some parent)
      mctx.mcCells.currentLevel.value
      (Scopes.scopeFrame (currentScopeStore mctx.mcGraph ()) parent).sfModuleId
      (LocalBindingOwner name)
  openScope mctx sid
  sid

-- The candidate local's scope, opened when the binder is a candidate.
openLocalScopeIf : ModuleCtx -> String -> Option ScopeId
openLocalScopeIf mctx name
  | isLocalAbsName name =
    forgetLocalAbs mctx.mcGraph name
    Some (openLocalScope mctx name)
  | otherwise = None

closeLocalScope : ModuleCtx -> Option ScopeId -> Unit
closeLocalScope mctx (Some _) = closeScope mctx ()
closeLocalScope mctx None = ()

-- An occurrence of a candidate local.  Once its binder has generalized with
-- predicates the occurrence instantiates them; before that (a recursive use) it is
-- recorded for `registerLocalAbs`.
inferLocalDictAt : TcEnv -> String -> EvId -> Mono
inferLocalDictAt env name ev =
  match (omLookup
    name
    env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph.graphRun.localAbs.lasBinders.value)
    Some (Some la) => match lookupVar env name
      Some s =>
        let inst = instantiateVarTrackedWithSubst env name 0 s
        pushLocalDictApp
          env.teDyn.dcModule
          name
          ev
          la
          inst.mtiSubstitution.misTypeSubst
          (captureScope env.teDyn.dcModule ())
        inst.mtiBody
      None => unboundVarFresh env.teDyn.dcModule name
    Some None => inferVarId env name 0
    None =>
      recordLocalRecOcc env.teDyn.dcModule name ev
      inferVarId env name 0

recordLocalRecOcc : ModuleCtx -> String -> EvId -> Unit
recordLocalRecOcc mctx name ev =
  let st = mctx.mcGraph.graphRun.localAbs
  let occs =
    (ev, captureScope mctx ())
      :: optionOr [] (omLookup name st.lasRecOccs.value)
  st.lasRecOccs := omInsert name occs st.lasRecOccs.value

-- dict_pass for locals: an abstracted binder takes its dictionary parameters, and an
-- occurrence of a binder that abstracted nothing is a plain variable again.
rewriteLocalDictExpr : GraphCtx -> Expr -> Expr
rewriteLocalDictExpr gctx (EDictAt n ev)
  | isLocalAbsName n = match localAbsFor gctx n
    Some _ => EDictAt n ev
    None => EVar n
  | otherwise = EDictAt n ev
rewriteLocalDictExpr gctx (ELet m r (PVar x xloc bid) e1 e2) =
  match localAbsFor gctx x
    Some la => ELet m r (PVar x xloc bid) (prependLocalDicts la.laParams e1) e2
    None => ELet m r (PVar x xloc bid) e1 e2
rewriteLocalDictExpr gctx (ELetGroup binds body) =
  ELetGroup (map (rewriteLocalLetBind gctx) binds) body
rewriteLocalDictExpr gctx (EBlock stmts) =
  EBlock (map (rewriteLocalDoStmt gctx) stmts)
rewriteLocalDictExpr gctx e = e

rewriteLocalLetBind : GraphCtx -> LetBind -> LetBind
rewriteLocalLetBind gctx (LetBind n clauses site bid) = match localAbsFor gctx n
  Some la =>
    LetBind n (map (prependLocalDictClause la.laParams) clauses) site bid
  None => LetBind n clauses site bid

prependLocalDictClause : List String -> FunClause -> FunClause
prependLocalDictClause params (FunClause pats body) =
  FunClause (map localDictPat params ++ pats) body

rewriteLocalDoStmt : GraphCtx -> DoStmt -> DoStmt
rewriteLocalDoStmt gctx (DoLet m r (PVar x xloc bid) e site) =
  match localAbsFor gctx x
    Some la =>
      DoLet m r (PVar x xloc bid) (prependLocalDicts la.laParams e) site
    None => DoLet m r (PVar x xloc bid) e site
rewriteLocalDoStmt gctx stmt = stmt

prependLocalDicts : List String -> Expr -> Expr
prependLocalDicts params (ELoc l e) = ELoc l (prependLocalDicts params e)
prependLocalDicts params (ELam pats body) =
  ELam (map localDictPat params ++ pats) body
prependLocalDicts params e = ELam (map localDictPat params) e

localDictPat : String -> Pat
localDictPat n = PVar n (Loc "" 0 0 0 0) noBinderId

inferDictAt : TcEnv -> String -> EvId -> Mono
inferDictAt env name ev
  | isLocalAbsName name = inferLocalDictAt env name ev
  | otherwise = inferGlobalDictAt env name ev

inferGlobalDictAt : TcEnv -> String -> EvId -> Mono
inferGlobalDictAt env name ev = match lookupVar env name
  None => panic ("unbound constrained fn: " ++ name)
  Some scheme =>
    let inst = instantiateValueTracked env.teDyn.dcModule name scheme
    let occurrence = (inst.mtiBody, inst.mtiSubstitution.misTypeSubst)
    match bindingDeclaredAt env name inst
      Some dc => inferDeclaredDictAt env.teDyn.dcModule name ev dc occurrence
      None => inferDictAtFound env.teDyn.dcModule name ev occurrence

-- A program lowered without elaboration (the prelude-free emitter probes) has no
-- inference to solve a grant from: each file extern it names is granted the
-- whole domain, and saturated as elaboration saturates it.  The parameter names
-- come from the process's grant counter (the interners' lineage), which the next
-- drive continues.
export
grantWholeDomain : List Decl -> List Decl
grantWholeDomain prog =
  map (mapDeclBodies (wholeDomainExpr interners.value.lineage.lnGrants)) prog

wholeDomainExpr : GrantState -> Expr -> Expr
wholeDomainExpr st (e@(EApp _ _)) = match grantSpine e []
  (EVar n, args) => match omLookup n fileGrantExterns
    Some (arity, paths) =>
      saturateGrants
        st
        (EVar n)
        arity
        (replicate paths (EListLit []))
        (map (wholeDomainExpr st) args)
    None => mapChildren (wholeDomainExpr st) e
  _ => mapChildren (wholeDomainExpr st) e
wholeDomainExpr st (EVar n) = match omLookup n fileGrantExterns
  Some (arity, paths) =>
    saturateGrants st (EVar n) arity (replicate paths (EListLit [])) []
  None => EVar n
-- every other node: its children, through the one traversal every pass shares
wholeDomainExpr st e = mapChildren (wholeDomainExpr st) e

-- Apply [f] once to the root of every expression a declaration holds.
export
mapDeclBodies : (Expr -> Expr) -> Decl -> Decl
mapDeclBodies f (DFunDef pub n ps e site bid) = DFunDef pub n ps (f e) site bid
mapDeclBodies f (DLetGroup pub binds) =
  DLetGroup
    pub
    (map
      (b => match b
        LetBind n clauses site bid =>
          LetBind
            n
            (map
              (c => match c
                FunClause ps e => FunClause ps (f e))
              clauses)
            site
            bid)
      binds)
mapDeclBodies f (d@(DInterface { methods, ... })) = DInterface { d |
  methods =
    map
      (m => match m
        IfaceMethod n ty def mloc =>
          IfaceMethod
            n
            ty
            (map
              (dm => match dm
                MethodDefault ps e => MethodDefault ps (f e))
              def)
            mloc)
      methods,
}
mapDeclBodies f (d@(DImpl { methods, ... })) = DImpl { d |
  methods =
    map
      (m => match m
        ImplMethod n ps e => ImplMethod n ps (f e))
      methods,
}
mapDeclBodies f (DProp pub name params body) = DProp pub name params (f body)
mapDeclBodies f (DTest pub name body) = DTest pub name (f body)
mapDeclBodies f (DAttrib attrs d) = DAttrib attrs (mapDeclBodies f d)
-- a declaration with no expression body (data, signatures, imports, externs)
mapDeclBodies _ d = d

-- How many grants a top-level binding with this scheme takes ahead of its value
-- arguments.
export
bindingGrantArity : DriveOutputs -> String -> Scheme -> Int
bindingGrantArity o _ sch =
  if o.doGrantsEnabled then listLen (grantOrder sch) else 0

-- An `EDictAt` use: a dictionary application, a grant-only use, or both.  The
-- instantiation inference makes for it is recorded for its grants; a grant-only
-- use is inferred exactly as the stamped variable it stands for.
