  -- Located at the right-hand side, as `inferLetSimple`.
  let env = envAtIfSome (exprSpanLoc e1) outer
  checkRecBindNonFunction env.teDyn.dcModule x e1  -- #799
  enterLevel env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  let oblN0 = wMark env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.implObls
  let callN0 = wMark env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.obls
  let dictN0 = goalsMark env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph ()
  let lscope = openLocalScopeIf env.teDyn.dcModule x
  let (t1, residuals) = inferRecursiveValue env x e1
  closeLocalScope env.teDyn.dcModule lscope
  exitLevel env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  let addedObls = wWindow env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.implObls oblN0
  let _ = improveLocalGoals env.teDyn addedObls callN0
  let _ = finalizeNumBoundary env.teDyn NumBoundary {
    nbDisposition =
      NumBoundaryOwnedMember
        (env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentLevel.value + 1),
    nbMembers = [t1],
    nbSurvivingIds = memberTiedSurvivors env.teDyn.dcModule t1 addedObls callN0,
    nbDefaultObls = addedObls,
    nbAmbiguityObls = addedObls,
    nbGuard = localNumGuard env.teDyn.dcModule addedObls callN0,
  }  -- PLAN.md #11 / RETPOS soundness
  recordLocalBind env.teDyn.dcModule x xloc bid t1  -- LSP hover (recursive PVar let bypasses inferPat)
  let sch =
    genBindingRestricted env.teDyn Tip (residualsOf 0 residuals) True pureRow t1  -- #866
  registerLocalScheme env.teDyn.dcModule x sch oblN0 callN0 dictN0
  registerLocalAbsIf env.teDyn.dcModule x lscope sch oblN0 callN0
  infer
    (envAt
      outer.teDyn.dcModule.mcLoc
      (seedAlphaLets (extendLocalVar env x sch) x e1))
    e2  -- WS-2: α scope-seed

-- Recursive local bindings are strict. Their initializer is charged here;
-- recursive occurrences read only the value, never a lazy forcing descriptor.
-- A recursive local is a function, so it generalizes, and its scope keeps
-- residuals over its own quantified authorities.
inferRecursiveValue : TcEnv ->
  String ->
  Expr ->
  (Mono, List (Int, AuthResidual))
inferRecursiveValue env name expr =
  beginEffectSummaryScope env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  let arity = sourceBindingArity expr
  let owned =
    newBindingSummary
      arity
      (freshVar env.teDyn.dcModule)
      (freshEffectSummary env.teDyn.dcModule)
  let envSelf = extendLocalVar env name (monoScheme owned.bsRecursiveValue)
  let (actual, immediate) = captureEffects
    env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.curEffect
    (joinCellOf env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph)
    (_ => infer envSelf expr)
  unifySourceDomains env.teDyn arity owned.bsValue actual
  publishProducedResults env.teDyn owned [(exprLoc expr, actual)]
  recordEffectBody env.teDyn.dcModule owned.bsBody (if arity == 0 then
    immediate
  else
    bodyRowAt arity actual)
  checkRecursiveValue env.teDyn owned
  let residuals = finishValueEffectsKeeping env.teDyn [(True, owned.bsValue)]
  performEffect
    env.teDyn.dcModule
    env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.curEffect
    immediate
  (owned.bsValue, residuals)

-- Source arity is the count of syntactic lambda parameters under the transparent
-- wrappers; every other expression is a computation that yields its value when
-- forced, so it has arity 0 even when that value turns out to be a function
-- (a conditional between two lambdas is a thunk producing a closure). The
-- catch-all is that rule, not a set of unhandled constructors.
sourceBindingArity : Expr -> Int
sourceBindingArity (ELoc _ expr) = sourceBindingArity expr
sourceBindingArity (EDoOrigin _ expr) = sourceBindingArity expr
sourceBindingArity (EAnnot expr _) = sourceBindingArity expr
sourceBindingArity (EHeadAnnot expr _) = sourceBindingArity expr
sourceBindingArity (ELetGroup _ expr) = sourceBindingArity expr
sourceBindingArity (ELam pats _) = listLen pats
sourceBindingArity _ = 0

-- Round-2 adversarial break "let-alias evasion" (#816): register a LOCAL
-- binding's generalized scheme obligations exactly as processSCC does for
-- top-level members, so a later use re-instantiates them into the
-- call-obligation window every checker reads.  Before this, `let f = hh`
-- (re-generalizing `hh : Num x => x -> x`) registered NOTHING: the RHS
-- occurrence's obligation stayed on a var generalization then orphaned, Int
-- defaulting satisfied it quietly, and `f x` at a method-scheme var sailed
-- through check into an eval panic / native SEGFAULT.  Name collisions across
-- bodies are safe: obligations are keyed by the scheme's own quantified ids,
-- and substMonos skips ids a different scheme's instantiation does not map.
--
-- A local binding whose scheme keeps class predicates is dictionary-abstracted
-- (`registerLocalAbs`): each use applies it to dictionaries solved at the use, so its
-- constrained vars generalize and defer exactly as described above.
registerLocalScheme : ModuleCtx -> String -> Scheme -> Int -> Int -> Int -> Unit
registerLocalScheme mctx x sch oblN0 callN0 dictN0 =
  declareQuantified mctx sch
  -- Obligations registered universally (#827/#838 I2); do not gate to IMPL/DEFAULT
  -- bodies only. See docs/spec/DICT-SEMANTICS.md § "4.1 `gen` at a local binder".
  let addedObls = wWindow mctx.mcCells.implObls oblN0
  let callOblsDelta = callOblsWindow mctx callN0
  -- #838 I5: the dict-slot's forwarded obligation is ALREADY in callOblsDelta as the
  -- mirroring PCallSlot obligation recorded at inferDictAtFound (recordCallObligations,
  -- beside pushDictApp), reaching schemeOblsForMember via forwardedVecObls; the old
  -- `allDictObls` re-derivation was a redundant second source (deduped away). Retired.
  registerSchemeObligations mctx omEmpty [] callOblsDelta addedObls [(x, sch)]

-- A generalized local's quantified variables are its uses' to choose, as a
-- signature's are its callers' (DICT-SEMANTICS §3), so they are declared before
-- its context is read off its goals: an instance that answers a goal only by
-- binding one does not discharge it, the goal stays in the scheme, and each use
-- poses it at its own instantiation to the binder enclosing that use.
declareQuantified : ModuleCtx -> Scheme -> Unit
declareQuantified mctx sch =
  declareRigidVars mctx (map intToString (schemeIds sch))

inferLetSimple : TcEnv -> Pat -> Expr -> Expr -> Mono
inferLetSimple outer pat e1 e2 =
  -- The binding's own checks are located at its right-hand side; the body is
  -- the enclosing construct's.
  let env = envAtIfSome (exprSpanLoc e1) outer
  enterLevel env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  beginEffectSummaryScope env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  let oblN0 = wMark env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.implObls
  let callN0 = wMark env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.obls
  let dictN0 = goalsMark env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph ()
  let lscope = match pat
    PVar x _ _ => openLocalScopeIf env.teDyn.dcModule x
    _ => None
  let t1 = infer env e1
  closeLocalScope env.teDyn.dcModule lscope
  let residuals = finishValueEffectsKeeping env.teDyn [
    (patIsVar pat && isNonexpansive env e1, t1),
  ]
  exitLevel env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  -- PLAN.md #11 / D4: ground an ambiguous Num-only var owned by this inner let
  -- before it generalizes, so `let z = 2 in y + z` (y:Float) is a clean type
  -- error and never leaks an unbound Num var.  Scoped to this binding's new obligations.
  let addedObls = wWindow env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.implObls oblN0
  improveLocalGoals env.teDyn addedObls callN0
  let _ = finalizeNumBoundary env.teDyn NumBoundary {
    nbDisposition =
      NumBoundaryOwnedMember
        (env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentLevel.value + 1),
    nbMembers = [t1],
    nbSurvivingIds = memberTiedSurvivors env.teDyn.dcModule t1 addedObls callN0,
    nbDefaultObls = addedObls,
    nbAmbiguityObls = addedObls,
    nbGuard = localNumGuard env.teDyn.dcModule addedObls callN0,
  }
  inferLetBody
    env
    outer.teDyn.dcModule.mcLoc
    pat
    t1
    residuals
    e1
    e2
    oblN0
    callN0
    dictN0
    lscope

-- [env] is located at the binding, [bodyLoc] is the span the body is inferred at.
inferLetBody : TcEnv ->
  Option Loc ->
  Pat ->
  Mono ->
  List (Int, AuthResidual) ->
  Expr ->
  Expr ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  Option ScopeId ->
  Mono
inferLetBody env bodyLoc (PVar x xloc bid) t1 residuals e1 e2 oblN0 callN0 dictN0 lscope =
  recordLocalBind env.teDyn.dcModule x (Some xloc) bid t1  -- LSP hover (PVar let bypasses inferPat)
  let sch =
    genBindingRestricted
      env.teDyn
      Tip
      (residualsOf 0 residuals)
      (isNonexpansive env e1)
      pureRow
      t1  -- #866
  registerLocalScheme env.teDyn.dcModule x sch oblN0 callN0 dictN0
  registerLocalAbsIf env.teDyn.dcModule x lscope sch oblN0 callN0
  infer (envAt bodyLoc (seedAlphaLets (extendLocalVar env x sch) x e1)) e2  -- WS-2: α scope-seed
inferLetBody env bodyLoc pat t1 _ _ e2 _ _ _ _ =
  let lits = takePatLits env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  let pr = inferPat env pat
  unifyIn env.teDyn (fst pr) t1
  settlePatLits env.teDyn lits
  checkBinderPat env (fst pr) pat
  infer (envAt bodyLoc (extendLocalVars env (snd pr))) e2

inferIf : TcEnv -> Expr -> Expr -> Expr -> Mono
inferIf env c t e =
  -- A condition that is not a `Bool` is reported at the condition.
  unifyIn
    (dynAtIfSome (exprSpanLoc c) env.teDyn)
    (infer env c)
    (tconBuiltin "Bool")
  let tt = infer env t
  let ee = infer env e
  let context = if isOmittedElse e then JoinElselessIf else JoinIf
  joinValueTypes env.teDyn context [(exprLoc t, tt), (exprLoc e, ee)]

-- The parser builds an omitted `else` as a bare unit literal (`elseBranch`,
-- `compiler/frontend/parser.mdk`) and wraps every atom it reads in `ELoc`, a
-- written `()` included, so only an omitted branch arrives unwrapped.  The
-- final clause is a deliberate catch-all: the question is whether the branch is
-- exactly that one parser-built shape, and every other constructor, including
-- one added to `Expr` later, is a written branch.
isOmittedElse : Expr -> Bool
isOmittedElse (ELit LUnit) = True
isOmittedElse _ = False

publishProducedResults : DynCtx ->
  BindingSummary ->
  List (Option Loc, Mono) ->
  Unit
publishProducedResults dyn owned values =
  let results = map (clauseResult owned.bsArity) values
  let produced =
    optionOrFresh
      dyn.dcModule
      (joinProducedEnvelope
        (valueJoinOps dyn JoinClause (_ => collectProducedSummary dyn.dcModule))
        results)
  let _ =
    map
      ((loc, lower) => recordFileValueFlow dyn.dcModule loc produced lower)
      results
  match resultAfterArrows owned.bsArity owned.bsValue
    Some expected => bindFrom dyn expected produced
    None => panic "binding source arity differs from its allocated shape"

clauseResult : Int -> (Option Loc, Mono) -> (Option Loc, Mono)
clauseResult arity (loc, value) = match resultAfterArrows arity value
  Some result => (loc, result)
  None => (loc, value)

inferProduced : TcEnv -> List Expr -> List (Option Loc, Mono)
inferProduced env [] = []
inferProduced env (e :: es) =
  let value = infer env e
  (exprLoc e, value) :: inferProduced env es

inferEach : TcEnv -> List Expr -> List Mono
inferEach env [] = []
inferEach env (e :: es) =
  let t = infer env e
  t :: inferEach env es

inferListLit : TcEnv -> List Expr -> Mono
inferListLit env es =
  let elem = joinValueTypes env.teDyn JoinList (inferProduced env es)
  TApp (tconBuiltin "List") elem

inferAnnot : TcEnv -> Expr -> Ty -> Mono
inferAnnot env e ty =
  let oblN0 = wMark env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.implObls
  let callN0 = wMark env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.obls
  let t = infer env e
  let pair = astTypeFreshTbl env.teDyn.dcModule ty
  let annot = fst pair
  -- The annotated expression flows into the written type as an argument
  -- into its parameter: a qualified annotation bounds its abstraction.
  argumentIntoOrd True env (Some e) annot t
  checkAnnotTooGeneral env.teDyn.dcModule ty (map snd (snd pair))
  -- The written variables are declared for the annotated expression's goals.
  -- Past it they are not: an annotated local that generalizes declares them as
  -- its quantified variables, and one that does not leaves them to its binder.
  let annotation = [("", ty, snd pair)]
  let declared = sccProtectedSignatureIds annotation
  if omSize declared == 0 then
    ()
  else
    checkSigVarGoals
      env.teDyn.dcModule
      DeclaredByAnnotation
      declared
      annotation
      (wWindow env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.implObls oblN0
        ++ callUOblsWindow env.teDyn.dcModule callN0)
  annot

-- Phase 108 head-pin (`:~`, EHeadAnnot): like inferAnnot but WITHOUT the
-- checkAnnotTooGeneral skolemization guard — the pin's type variables are MEANT
-- to ground (the container literal's element types).  Fixes `e`'s head tycon to
-- the named container so `fromEntries`'s return-position dispatch resolves to
-- that container's impl.
--
-- Phase 114 (was wrongly dropped here): ignore the *arity* the lowering happened
-- to supply and apply the head tycon to its *declared* arity of fresh vars.  The
-- parser can't tell empty `Map { }` from `Set { }` — both have no entries, so
-- classifyBrace falls through to `ESetLit name []` and the desugar pins a UNARY
-- `Map _a`, the wrong arity for `Map k v` (→ `Map vs Map …`).  Looking the arity
-- up by the head tycon makes empty literals work regardless of the lowering's
-- guess; element vars stay free and ground via inference as before.
inferHeadAnnot : TcEnv -> Expr -> Ty -> Mono
inferHeadAnnot env e ty =
  let t = infer env e
  let annot = headAnnotTy env.teDyn.dcModule ty
  unifyIn env.teDyn t annot
  t

-- The head-pin's target type: if the annotation's head is a TyCon with a known
-- declared arity (from `dataParamKindsRef`), rebuild it at that arity with fresh
-- vars (so an empty literal's wrong-arity pin is corrected); otherwise fall back
-- to the literal annotation type.
headAnnotTy : ModuleCtx -> Ty -> Mono
headAnnotTy mctx ty = match tyAppSpine ty
  -- OCCURRENCE MINT (#1110): same source as `fromAstTypeE`'s — the identity of
  -- the annotation head being rebuilt at its declared arity.
  (TyCon { tyConName = n, tyConOrigin = o }, _) =>
    match lookupTab (tyTabKey o n) mctx.mcCells.dataParamKindsRef.value
      Some kinds => applyParams (tconFrom o n) (freshVars mctx (listLen kinds))
      None => fst (astTypeFreshTbl mctx ty)
  _ => fst (astTypeFreshTbl mctx ty)

inferMatch : TcEnv -> Mono -> List Arm -> Mono
inferMatch env scrutTy arms =
  let result = joinValueTypes env.teDyn JoinMatch (inferArms env scrutTy arms)
  scheduleMatchChecks
    env
    scrutTy
    arms
    (matchWarningLoc env.teDyn.dcModule.mcLoc arms)
  result

scheduleMatchChecks : TcEnv -> Mono -> List Arm -> Option Loc -> Unit
scheduleMatchChecks env scrutTy arms loc = match normalize scrutTy
  TVar _ =>
    env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.matchChecksDeferred :=
      (scrutTy, arms, loc)
        :: env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.matchChecksDeferred.value
  _ => checkMatchChecks (mctxAt loc env.teDyn.dcModule) scrutTy arms

-- A `let` pattern or lambda parameter is judged as the single arm of a match
-- on its own type, at the binding.  The parameters of one binding are judged as
-- one tuple pattern, so a binding with several refutable parameters warns once,
-- not once per parameter.
checkBinderPats : TcEnv -> List Mono -> List Pat -> Unit
checkBinderPats env [t] [p] = checkBinderPat env t p
checkBinderPats env ts ps
  | allList patIsVar ps = ()
  | otherwise = checkBinderPat env (tupleMono ts) (PTuple ps)

-- The variable that is the body of a binder's one arm: it marks the check as a binder's, whose
-- warning is worded for a pattern with no match to add an arm to.
binderMarker : String
binderMarker = "<binder>"

isBinderArms : List Arm -> Bool
isBinderArms [Arm _ [] (EVar n)] = n == binderMarker
isBinderArms _ = False

checkBinderPat : TcEnv -> Mono -> Pat -> Unit
checkBinderPat env ty pat =
  if patIsVar pat then
    ()
  else
    scheduleMatchChecks
      env
      ty
      [Arm pat [] (EVar binderMarker)]
      env.teDyn.dcModule.mcLoc

-- A match's warnings are located at the match through its last arm.  The
-- match's own span runs on over any comment or blank line that follows, on the
-- last arm's line or after it, so it is cut at the end of the last arm.  On
-- that arm's own line the cut takes the body's own span (its `ELoc`): the
-- parts of an unwrapped body do not reach its end (a field access's name has
-- no span).
matchWarningLoc : Option Loc -> List Arm -> Option Loc
matchWarningLoc (Some (Loc f sl sc el ec)) arms = match last arms
  Some (Arm _ _ body) => match exprSpanLoc body
    Some (Loc _ _ _ bel bec) if bel < el => Some (Loc f sl sc bel bec)
    _ => match exprLoc body
      Some (Loc _ _ _ bel bec) if bel == el && bec < ec =>
        Some (Loc f sl sc bel bec)
      _ => Some (Loc f sl sc el ec)
  None => Some (Loc f sl sc el ec)
matchWarningLoc None _ = None

-- A scrutinee whose type is still unknown after its arms (only literal, variable
-- and wildcard patterns, e.g. a lambda's parameter matched against integer
-- literals) is checked at the module's end instead, once `settleDeferredPatLits`
-- has given it its type, so the warning names it (`non-exhaustive match on U8`).
checkMatchChecks : ModuleCtx -> Mono -> List Arm -> Unit
checkMatchChecks mctx scrutTy arms =
  checkMatchExhaustive mctx scrutTy arms
  checkMatchRedundant mctx scrutTy arms

checkDeferredMatches : ModuleCtx -> List (Mono, List Arm, Option Loc) -> Unit
checkDeferredMatches mctx [] = ()
checkDeferredMatches mctx ((scrutTy, arms, loc) :: rest) =
  checkMatchChecks (mctxAt loc mctx) scrutTy arms
  checkDeferredMatches mctx rest
-- Type-aware exhaustiveness (`check_match`): run AFTER the arms have unified
-- the scrutinee type, so `scrutTy` is fully resolved when we read its head.

-- Warn if an all-wildcard query is still useful against the matrix of the
-- non-guarded arms — i.e. some scrutinee value escapes every arm.  Guarded arms
-- are excluded (their guard may fail at runtime), matching the reference.
checkMatchExhaustive : ModuleCtx -> Mono -> List Arm -> Unit
checkMatchExhaustive mctx scrutTy arms =
  let rows = nonGuardedRows mctx arms
  if useful
    mctx.mcCells.matchOracle.value
    (matchCol0Type scrutTy)
    rows
    [PWild] then
    let binder = isBinderArms arms
    let (msg, help) = nonExhaustiveMsg mctx scrutTy rows binder
    -- A let-bound function is nested one-parameter lambdas that share the
    -- binding's location; the first refutable parameter's warning is the one.
    if binder
      && anyList (warnedAt mctx.mcLoc) mctx.mcCells.matchWarnings.value then
      ()
    else
      mctx.mcCells.matchWarnings :=
        writtenDiag (TcDiag "W-NONEXHAUSTIVE" 2 mctx.mcLoc msg help None)
          :: mctx.mcCells.matchWarnings.value

warnedAt : Option Loc -> TcDiag -> Bool
warnedAt loc (TcDiag code _ at _ _ _) =
  code == "W-NONEXHAUSTIVE" && locKey loc /= "" && locKey at == locKey loc

checkMatchRedundant : ModuleCtx -> Mono -> List Arm -> Unit
checkMatchRedundant mctx scrutTy arms =
  checkRedundantGo mctx (matchCol0Type scrutTy) [] omEmpty False arms

-- PERF: `prec` accumulates the preceding arms' patterns and is PREPENDED to, so
-- it holds them in REVERSE arm order.  It used to be built with `prec ++ [[dp]]`,
-- which copies the whole accumulator once per arm — O(N²) allocation on a match
-- with many arms, and the dominant allocation source in the redundancy check.
--
-- Reversing the rows is sound because `useful` is a PREDICATE OVER THE SET of
-- matrix rows ("does some value match the query and no row?"): `specializeCon` /
-- `specializeLit` / `defaultMatrix` are row-wise filters, and the only decision
-- that reads rows in order is `columnCtors`, which just needs SOME column-0
-- constructor to name the column's type — and it is consulted only when `col0`
-- is `None`, i.e. when the scrutinee type has no concrete head, in which case no
-- arm carries a constructor pattern and there is no head constructor to find in
-- either order.
checkRedundantGo : ModuleCtx ->
  Option TabKey ->
  List (List Pat) ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  Bool ->
  List Arm ->
  Unit
checkRedundantGo mctx _ _ _ _ [] = ()
checkRedundantGo mctx col0 prec heads offCol ((Arm pat gs body) :: rest) =
  let dp = desugarPat mctx.mcCells.matchOracle.value pat
  if armUnreachable mctx col0 prec heads offCol dp then
    mctx.mcCells.matchWarnings :=
      TcDiag
          "W-UNREACHABLE-ARM"
          2
          (orElseLoc (exprLoc body) mctx.mcLoc)
          unreachableArmWarning
          None
          None
        :: mctx.mcCells.matchWarnings.value
  -- Only UNGUARDED, range-free arms contribute to the covered set: a guarded arm
  -- may not fire, and a range collapses to a wildcard that over-states coverage
  -- (patHasRange) — either would produce a false "redundant" on a later arm.
  let contributes = armIsUnguarded gs && not (patHasRange pat)
  let prec2 = if contributes then [dp] :: prec else prec
  let heads2 = if contributes then noteHeadCtor dp heads else heads
  let offCol2 = offCol || contributes && not (isConPat dp)
  checkRedundantGo mctx col0 prec2 heads2 offCol2 rest

-- PERF fast path.  `patUnreachable` runs the full Maranget `useful` recursion, which
-- re-scans EVERY preceding row — so the fold as a whole is O(arms²) on a wide match.
-- But a constructor arm `C …` can only be unreachable if some preceding row could
-- match a `C` value, and the only rows that can are (a) rows headed by `C` itself and
-- (b) rows with a WILDCARD head, which match anything.  When neither exists,
-- `specializeCon C` yields the EMPTY matrix and `useful _ _ [] _` is `True` by
-- definition — the arm is reachable — so the recursion is guaranteed to say
-- "reachable" and we can skip it outright.
--
-- `heads` is the set of head constructors of the preceding contributing rows and
-- `offCol` records whether any of them has a NON-constructor head.  `offCol` is a
-- deliberate over-approximation of "has a wildcard head" (it also trips on a literal
-- head, which `specializeCon` would in fact discard): erring towards `True` only ever
-- costs us the fast path and falls back to the exact check, never an answer.
armUnreachable : ModuleCtx ->
  Option TabKey ->
  List (List Pat) ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  Bool ->
  Pat ->
  Bool
armUnreachable mctx col0 prec heads offCol (PCon c args)
  | not offCol && not (omHasKey c heads) = False
  | otherwise =
    patUnreachable mctx.mcCells.matchOracle.value col0 prec (PCon c args)
armUnreachable mctx col0 prec _ _ dp =
  patUnreachable mctx.mcCells.matchOracle.value col0 prec dp

noteHeadCtor : Pat -> OrdMap Unit -> OrdMap Unit
noteHeadCtor (PCon c _) heads = omInsert c () heads
noteHeadCtor _ heads = heads

-- Only UNGUARDED arms contribute to the covered set (a guarded arm may not fire).
armIsUnguarded : List Guard -> Bool
armIsUnguarded [] = True
armIsUnguarded (_ :: _) = False

-- Build the specialised warning: recover a concrete uncovered pattern (the
-- Maranget witness) and name it, plus the scrutinee type when it has a real
-- head name.  Falls back to the generic wording if no witness is recoverable
-- (keeps the warning firing whenever `useful` should, never naming a wrong
-- constructor).  Actionable-fix hint (F dimension): when a witness IS
-- recoverable, append a concrete-edit suggestion using the witness string
-- VERBATIM (so `Triangle _` reads as `Triangle _`, not `Triangle`) and return it
-- as the `Some` help so `--json`'s `help` field carries it too.  #159: returns
-- `(message, Option help)` so the caller can stash both in the warning's TcDiag —
-- no more message-keyed `matchWarningHelp` side channel.
nonExhaustiveMsg : ModuleCtx ->
  Mono ->
  List (List Pat) ->
  Bool ->
  (String, Option String)
nonExhaustiveMsg mctx scrutTy rows binder =
  match (usefulWitness
    mctx.mcCells.matchOracle.value
    (matchCol0Type scrutTy)
    rows
    1)
    Some (w :: _) =>
      let witnessStr = renderWitness w
      if binder then
        let (msg, hint) =
          binderNonExhaustiveMsg (matchCol0Type scrutTy) witnessStr
        (msg, Some hint)
      else
        let hint =
          if witnessStr == "_" then
            "add a `_ => ...` arm"
          else
            "add a `\{witnessStr} => ...` arm or a `_` wildcard"
        let msg =
          "Warning: non-exhaustive match\{tyOfMsg (matchCol0Type scrutTy)}: missing `\{witnessStr}`; \{hint}"
        (msg, Some hint)
    _ => (nonExhaustiveMatchWarning, None)

-- one single-column matrix row per non-guarded arm (its desugared pattern)
nonGuardedRows : ModuleCtx -> List Arm -> List (List Pat)
nonGuardedRows mctx [] = []
nonGuardedRows mctx ((Arm pat [] _) :: rest) =
  [desugarPat mctx.mcCells.matchOracle.value pat] :: nonGuardedRows mctx rest
nonGuardedRows mctx ((Arm _ _ _) :: rest) = nonGuardedRows mctx rest

inferArms : TcEnv -> Mono -> List Arm -> List (Option Loc, Mono)
inferArms env _ [] = []
inferArms env scrutTy ((Arm pat gs body) :: rest) =
  let value = inferArm env scrutTy pat gs body
  (exprLoc body, value) :: inferArms env scrutTy rest

inferArm : TcEnv -> Mono -> Pat -> List Guard -> Expr -> Mono
inferArm env scrutTy pat gs body
  | env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph.graphRun.anyExistentialsRef.value
    && patOpensExistentials env pat = inferArmOpening env scrutTy pat gs body
  | otherwise =
    let lits = takePatLits env.teDyn.dcModule ()
    let pr = inferPat env pat
    bindFrom env.teDyn (fst pr) scrutTy
    settlePatLits env.teDyn lits
    let envBody = inferArmGuards (extendLocalVars env (snd pr)) gs
    infer envBody body

-- An arm whose pattern opened existential authorities (§4.1) is their scope.
-- The body runs one level deeper, so a cell bound into anything the arm did
-- not create is lowered by the ordinary level discipline and found at the
-- end; a cell in the arm's own value type is found there.  Either is an
-- escape (`T-AUTHORITY-ESCAPE`): the arm's value cannot carry an authority
-- nothing outside it can name.  A row the arm performs at the authority is
-- checked against the enclosing declaration as any row is (rigid: only the
-- label bare admits it), and an inferred row publishes it as the domain's
-- top (`defaultSourcelessAuthorities`).
inferArmOpening : TcEnv -> Mono -> Pat -> List Guard -> Expr -> Mono
inferArmOpening env scrutTy pat gs body =
  let lits = takePatLits env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  let pr = inferPat env pat
  bindFrom env.teDyn (fst pr) scrutTy
  let scope =
    openExistentialScope
      env.teDyn.dcModule
      (takeOpenedExistentials env.teDyn.dcModule ())
  settlePatLits env.teDyn lits
  let envBody = inferArmGuards (extendLocalVars env (snd pr)) gs
  let t = infer envBody body
  closeExistentialScope env.teDyn.dcModule scope t (exprLoc body)
  t

-- Thread an arm's guard qualifiers left-to-right: a `GBool` must be `Bool` and leaves the env unchanged; a
-- `GBind p e` infers `e`, binds `p` against it, and extends the env so the bound
-- vars are in scope for LATER qualifiers and the arm body.  A qualifier's own
-- check is located at its expression.
inferArmGuards : TcEnv -> List Guard -> TcEnv
inferArmGuards env [] = env
inferArmGuards env ((GBool g) :: rest) =
  unifyIn
    (dynAtIfSome (exprSpanLoc g) env.teDyn)
    (infer env g)
    (tconBuiltin "Bool")
  inferArmGuards env rest
inferArmGuards env ((GBind p e) :: rest) =
  let te = infer env e
  let at = envAtIfSome (exprSpanLoc e) env
  let lits = takePatLits at.teDyn.dcModule ()
  let pr = inferPat at p
  bindFrom at.teDyn (fst pr) te
  settlePatLits at.teDyn lits
  inferArmGuards (extendLocalVars env (snd pr)) rest

inferLetGroup : TcEnv -> List LetBind -> Expr -> Mono
inferLetGroup env binds body =
  checkLetGroupBindsLocated env.teDyn.dcModule binds  -- #799
  let env2 = fold processLetGroup env (letGroupComponents binds)
  infer env2 body

-- instantiate a record's quantified params with fresh vars.  Rebuilds ALL fields —
-- used by the record-CREATE and record-PATTERN paths, which must see every declared
-- field (missing-field check / binding each pattern field).  The single-field access
-- and record-update paths use `instantiateRecordShared` + the field index instead so
-- they never rebuild all N fields per access (issue #980).

-- Instantiate ONLY the result type, returning the shared param substitution so the
-- caller can instantiate individual fields on demand (via the field index).  The
-- fresh-var allocation is identical to `instantiateRecordOpening` (both call `freshSubst
-- paramIds`); only the per-field `substMono` trees for UNACCESSED fields are skipped,
-- and those allocate no fresh tyvars, so tyvar numbering is byte-identical.
instantiateRecordShared : ModuleCtx -> RecordInfo -> (RecordSubst, Mono)
instantiateRecordShared mctx (RecordInfo paramIds authIds result fields _) =
  let subst = freshSubst mctx paramIds
  let cells = recordAuthCells authIds result fields
  let asub =
    map (id => (id, sharedAuthority mctx id (IdMap.get id cells))) authIds
  (RecordSubst subst asub, substMono mctx.mcGraph subst [] asub result)

-- An update repacks a field under an existential binder only where it
-- replaces every field that mentions the binder: the value's index is then
-- the replacement's own.  Replacing some of them would leave one binder
-- naming two values at different authorities, so that is refused.  A binder
-- none of the assigned fields mentions is untouched and, as at a read,
-- recovers the top.
instantiateRecordUpdate : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  RecordInfo ->
  List String ->
  (RecordSubst, Mono)
instantiateRecordUpdate mctx rname (RecordInfo paramIds authIds result fields _) assigned =
  let subst = freshSubst mctx paramIds
  let cells = recordAuthCells authIds result fields
  let asub =
    map
      (id => (
        id,
        updateAuthority mctx rname fields assigned id (IdMap.get id cells),
      ))
      authIds
  (RecordSubst subst asub, substMono mctx.mcGraph subst [] asub result)

updateAuthority : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  List String ->
  Int ->
  Option (Ref Authvar) ->
  Authority
updateAuthority mctx rname fields assigned id source
  | IdMap.has id mctx.mcGraph.graphRun.ctorExistentialsRef.value =
    let mentioning =
      map fst (filterList (f => IdMap.has id (authCellsIn (snd f) Tip)) fields)
    let replaced = filterList (n => contains n assigned) mentioning
    if isEmptyL replaced then
      sharedAuthority mctx id source
    else if listLen replaced == listLen mentioning then
      AVar (freshInferenceAuthvar mctx id source)
    else
      pushTypeError
        mctx
        "T-AUTHORITY-EXISTENTIAL-SCOPE"
        (partialExistentialUpdateMsg rname mentioning)
      AVar (freshInferenceAuthvar mctx id source)
  | otherwise = AVar (freshInferenceAuthvar mctx id source)

-- A universal freshens flexible, as at any use.  An existential binder is
-- opened only by a pattern; a field read or update sees the value without
-- opening it, so what it recovers is the domain's top: the value proves
-- nothing about an authority the read cannot name.
sharedAuthority : ModuleCtx -> Int -> Option (Ref Authvar) -> Authority
sharedAuthority mctx id source
  | IdMap.has id mctx.mcGraph.graphRun.ctorExistentialsRef.value = match source
    Some cell => authTop (authvarDomain cell)
    None => authTop PUnit
  | otherwise = AVar (freshInferenceAuthvar mctx id source)

substRecordField : GraphCtx -> RecordSubst -> Mono -> Mono
substRecordField gctx (RecordSubst subst asub) fm =
  substMono gctx subst [] asub fm

recordFieldMap : RecordInfo -> OrdMap Mono
recordFieldMap (RecordInfo _ _ _ _ idx) = idx

recordFieldNames : RecordInfo -> List String
recordFieldNames (RecordInfo _ _ _ fields _) = map fst fields

-- Publish every top-level function clause and top-level let-group member under
-- the scheme its group generalized to, mirroring the decl shapes `funDefs`
-- flattens.  Each clause of a multi-clause function has its own id and records
-- the one scheme, and whether the module declares a signature for its name.
recordTopBinderTypes : GraphCtx -> OrdMap Scheme -> List Decl -> Unit
recordTopBinderTypes gctx schemes decls =
  let signed = signedTopNames decls omEmpty
  fold (_ d => recordTopDeclBinderTypes gctx schemes signed d) () decls

-- The names a top-level type signature declares, an annotated one included.
signedTopNames : List Decl -> OrdMap Unit -> OrdMap Unit
signedTopNames [] acc = acc
signedTopNames ((DTypeSig _ n _ _) :: rest) acc =
  signedTopNames rest (omInsert n () acc)
signedTopNames ((DAttrib _ d) :: rest) acc = signedTopNames (d :: rest) acc
signedTopNames (_ :: rest) acc = signedTopNames rest acc

recordTopDeclBinderTypes : GraphCtx ->
  OrdMap Scheme ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  Decl ->
  Unit
recordTopDeclBinderTypes gctx schemes signed (DFunDef _ n ps _ _ bid) =
  recordTopFunBinderType gctx schemes signed n bid (listLen ps)
recordTopDeclBinderTypes gctx schemes signed (DLetGroup _ binds) =
  fold
    (_ b => match b
      LetBind n clauses _ bid => match clauses
        (FunClause ps _) :: _ =>
          recordTopFunBinderType gctx schemes signed n bid (listLen ps)
        [] => recordTopFunBinderType gctx schemes signed n bid 0)
    ()
    binds
recordTopDeclBinderTypes gctx schemes signed (DAttrib _ d) =
  recordTopDeclBinderTypes gctx schemes signed d
recordTopDeclBinderTypes gctx _ _ _ = ()

recordTopFunBinderType : GraphCtx ->
  OrdMap Scheme ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  String ->
  BinderId ->
  Int ->
  Unit
recordTopFunBinderType gctx schemes signed n bid arity =
  match omLookup n schemes
    Some sch =>
      recordBinderType
        gctx
        bid
        n
        (schemeMono sch)
        (Some arity)
        (omHasKey n signed)
    None => ()

-- #799: the guard above (checkLetRecDecls/checkLetBind) only walks TOP-LEVEL
-- DLetGroup declarations. BLOCK-level (`let rec x = v` as a DoStmt) and
-- EXPRESSION-level (`let rec x = v in e2`, an ELetGroup) `let rec` reach
-- blockRecLet/inferRecLet/inferLetGroup directly, with no non-function check at
-- all — a non-function binding (e.g. `let rec loop = loop`) silently pre-binds
-- the name to a placeholder Ref and evaluates to it, never erroring.

-- process one dependency component of a where block: bind names, infer,
-- generalize
processLetGroup : TcEnv -> List LetBind -> TcEnv
processLetGroup env binds =
  enterLevel env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  beginEffectSummaryScope env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  let oblN0 = wMark env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.implObls
  let callN0 = wMark env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.obls
  let dictN0 = goalsMark env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph ()
  let summaries = map (localBindingSummary env.teDyn.dcModule) binds
  fold
    (_ entry => recordLetBindType env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph entry)
    ()
    (zipL binds summaries)
  let placeholders = map (p => (fst p, monoScheme (snd p).bsValue)) summaries
  let recursive =
    map (p => (fst p, monoScheme (snd p).bsRecursiveValue)) summaries
  let env2 = extendLocalVars env recursive
  fold
    (_ bind => forgetLocalAbs env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph (letBindName bind))
    ()
    binds
  let lscopes = inferLetBinds env2 (zipL binds summaries)
  fold (_ entry => checkRecursiveValue env.teDyn (snd entry)) () summaries
  let residuals =
    finishValueEffectsKeeping
      env.teDyn
      (map (letBindGeneralizes env) (zipL binds summaries))
  flushPendingEscapes env.teDyn.dcModule env.teDyn.dcGroup
  exitLevel env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  -- PLAN.md #11 / D4, as a where block narrows it (#3487): ground the Num-only
  -- vars owned by this just-exited component that no member's type mentions
  -- (nothing can generalize them).  One a member's type does mention, even in
  -- return position, generalizes with its constraint, so a sibling or the
  -- enclosing body instantiates it (`two _ = 2` beside `go y = y / two ()`);
  -- the enclosing binding's boundary decides what its uses leave ambiguous.
  -- Scoped to this group's newly added obligations.
  let addedObls = wWindow env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.implObls oblN0
  improveLocalGoals env.teDyn addedObls callN0
  let memberMonos = map (p => schemeMono (snd p)) placeholders
  let _ = finalizeNumBoundary env.teDyn NumBoundary {
    nbDisposition =
      NumBoundaryOwnedGroup (env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentLevel.value + 1),
    nbMembers = memberMonos,
    nbSurvivingIds = omEmpty,
    nbDefaultObls = addedObls,
    nbAmbiguityObls = addedObls,
    nbGuard = localNumGuard env.teDyn.dcModule addedObls callN0,
  }  -- RETPOS soundness
  let genv = generalizeGroup env residuals 0 (zipL binds placeholders)
  -- Round-2 adversarial break "let-alias evasion" (#816): a LOCAL constrained
  -- binding (`let f = hh` re-generalizing `hh : Num x => x -> x`) previously
  -- registered NOTHING in schemeObligationsRef — only top-level SCCs did — so a
  -- later use `f x` instantiated no obligation at all: the one recorded at the
  -- RHS occurrence stayed on a var the generalization then orphaned, Int
  -- defaulting quietly satisfied it, and a scheme-var instantiation sailed
  -- through check into an eval panic / native SEGFAULT.  Register the group
  -- exactly as processSCC does; instantiateVarTracked's per-use re-recording
  -- then feeds the same call-obligation window every checker reads.  Name
  -- collisions across bodies are safe: the obligation ids are the scheme's own
  -- quantified ids, and substMonos skips entries whose ids a different scheme's
  -- instantiation does not map.
  let callOblsDelta = callOblsWindow env.teDyn.dcModule callN0
  let schemes = groupSchemesOf genv binds
  fold (_ p => declareQuantified env.teDyn.dcModule (snd p)) () schemes
  -- #827/#838 I2: register EVERYWHERE, not only inside a method body.  The
  -- uniform deferral (`undeterminedGoalExempt`'s OD2 test) makes a generalizable
  -- where/let var defer into the enclosing scheme rather than trip an ambiguity
  -- reject, closing the orphaned-local-constraint S0 (#827).  See registerLocalScheme.
  -- #838 I5: dict-slot forwarding rides callOblsDelta's PCallSlot obligations (see
  -- registerLocalScheme); the redundant `allDictObls` re-derivation is retired.
  registerSchemeObligations
    env.teDyn.dcModule
    omEmpty
    []
    callOblsDelta
    addedObls
    schemes
  registerLocalGroupAbs genv oblN0 callN0 (zipL binds lscopes)
  genv

-- the generalized (name, scheme) pairs of a just-closed local group
groupSchemesOf : TcEnv -> List LetBind -> List (String, Scheme)
groupSchemesOf env [] = []
groupSchemesOf genv ((LetBind name _ _ _) :: rest) = match lookupVar genv name
  Some sch => (name, sch) :: groupSchemesOf genv rest
  None => groupSchemesOf genv rest

inferLetBinds : TcEnv ->
  List (LetBind, (String, BindingSummary)) ->
  List (Option ScopeId)
inferLetBinds env [] = []
inferLetBinds env ((bind@(LetBind name clauses _ _), (_, owned)) :: rest) =
  let pairs = map funClausePair clauses
  let lscope =
    if isLocalAbsName name then
      Some (openLocalScope env.teDyn.dcModule name)
    else
      None
  let _ = inferMemberClauses env None owned pairs
  closeLocalScope env.teDyn.dcModule lscope
  match pairs
    [([], _)] =>
      performEffect
        env.teDyn.dcModule
        env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.curEffect
        owned.bsForce
    _ => ()
  lscope :: inferLetBinds env rest

-- The D3 channel rule is an identity intersection, not whole-type reachability:
-- only roots constrained by this boundary's own Num obligations can survive, and
-- only when the supplied head/dictionary channels carry that exact live root.
numChannelRootSet : List UObligation -> List Mono -> OrdMap Unit
numChannelRootSet obls channels =
  let channelIds = monoRootIdSet channels
  omFromNames
    (filterList
      (name => omHasKey name channelIds)
      (map intToString (dedupI (numConstrainedIds obls))))
    omEmpty

-- ── elaboration: resolve return-position method dispatch (RKey) ────────────
-- Rewrite each return-position method occurrence to EMethodAt (with a fresh route
-- ref), type-check (recording the sites), then stamp each site's route from its
-- now-resolved result type.  Returns the SAME tree (refs filled) for eval.
-- There is no flat elaboration driver left: every caller goes through the
-- 1-module `elaborateOne` (the typed/dict tree of the degenerate 1-module multi
-- path).

-- ── 1-module wrapper over the multi-module path ────────────────────────────
-- elaborateOne runs the SINGLE program [prog] (the user's decls, the live prelude
-- ALREADY shadow-dropped by the caller) through elaborateModules as the degenerate
-- 1-module list [(rootId, prog)], returning the flat shape its callers consume:
-- core2 (dict-passed core) ++ the dict-passed module's decls.
--
-- The 1-module case automatically satisfies that shape's invariants — one
-- `freshModuleCtx` (one module ⇒ one checkModuleFullImpl), zero imports ⇒ the full
-- constraint set, and elaborateModules runs the eval-dict layer unconditionally
-- (ARGSTAMP-UNIFY Phase 4), so the return-position constrained-fn dict layer is
-- present here too.
--
-- The dict-name set is the module path's own: elaborateModules computes it via
-- `moduleDictNames` (the prelude's constrained names followed by the module graph's
-- FULL `constrainedSigNames`), rather than taking an externally built list.  This
-- wrapper therefore takes `coreDecls` SEPARATE (not pre-flattened into prog),
-- exactly as elaborateModules expects.  The grader for the Flat-vs-Module relation
-- is test/diff_compiler_flat_vs_onemodule.sh (ARCH B-2.1-a): it now pins the
-- own acceptance and diagnostics, and grades the relation only through a clause
-- true on both sides of the #1564 fix — every arm that ACCEPTS must compute the
-- same value.  Read its header before changing either arm.
export
elaborateOne : DriveInputs ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  (String, List Decl) ->
  List Decl
elaborateOne inputs runtimeDecls coreDecls prog =
  fst (elaborateOneFacts inputs runtimeDecls coreDecls prog)

-- `elaborateOne` with the `ProgramFacts` value its elaboration built, for a caller that lowers
-- the flat decls.
export
elaborateOneFacts : DriveInputs ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  (String, List Decl) ->
  (List Decl, ProgramFacts)
elaborateOneFacts inputs runtimeDecls coreDecls (rootId, prog) =
  let elab = elaborateModules inputs runtimeDecls coreDecls [(rootId, prog)]
  let (coreD, modules, _, _, _, _, _) = elab
  (coreD ++ flatMap snd modules, factsOfElab elab)

-- #415 item 3: the ONLY writer of dictEligibleRef / dictEligibleSetRef.  The set is
-- DERIVED from the list here rather than mirrored at each set site, so the two cannot
-- drift: there is no longer a second side for a future edit to be absent from.  (Both
-- former sites hand-wrote `namesToSet <names> omEmpty` next to the list store; the
-- module site additionally recomputed `moduleUserFnNames modules` for the mirror.)
setDictEligible : GraphCtx -> List String -> Unit
setDictEligible gctx names =
  gctx.dictEligibleRef := names
  gctx.dictEligibleSetRef := namesToSet names omEmpty

-- the USER modules' top-level fn names (NOT core/prelude) — the promotion-eligible
-- set on the build path. Mirrors the retired elaborator's user-function eligibility.
moduleUserFnNames : List (String, List Decl) -> List String
moduleUserFnNames modules =
  dedup (flatMap (p => map fst (funDefs (snd p))) modules)

-- The PRELUDE's own `=>`-constrained fns that must ALSO be dict-passed: those
-- whose body uses a return-position method (`when`/`unless` use `pure`), so
-- arg-tag dispatch can't resolve it at a constraint variable's type.  Every OTHER
-- constrained prelude fn (sum/any/elem/clamp/…) uses only arg-position methods —
-- arg-tag already resolves those, and the goldens type-check with them on RKey, so
-- they stay OUT.  [allDecls] supplies the interface set for returnPosMethodNames;
-- bodies come from [preludeDecls] (the shadow-dropped prelude).
export
preludeReturnPosDictNames : List Decl -> List Decl -> List String
preludeReturnPosDictNames preludeDecls allDecls =
  let rpNames = returnPosMethodNames allDecls
  filterList
    (n => anyMember (declBodyVars n preludeDecls) rpNames)
    (constrainedSigNames preludeDecls)

-- D3b-2: the PRELUDE's `=>`-constrained fns that dispatch a method in ARGUMENT
-- position (the ~23 helpers: neq/elem/any/all/find/count/sum/product/maximum/
-- minimum/clamp/flatMap/flat/debugListItems/displayListItems/hashListItems/print/
-- println).  These stay OUT of the eval/golden dict set — arg-tag resolves them in
-- ceval (tagged values) and the goldens type-check with them on RKey — but the
-- NATIVE emit path MUST dict-pass them: arg-tag cannot dispatch on a PRIMITIVE
-- element (an `Int`/`String` immediate carries no cell tag).  The arg-position
-- analogue of preludeReturnPosDictNames: every constrained prelude fn that is NOT
-- already return-position.  Wired (alongside preludeReturnPosDictNames) into the
-- emit + dict_pp-oracle drivers ONLY (llvm_emit_typed_main / core_ir_dict_pp_main),
-- which no golden driver shares — so module/`=== TYPES ===`/eval goldens stay
-- byte-identical; the body sites route RDict $dict_<method>_<slot> through the same
-- activeDictVars layer registerConstraintRegs already builds for return-position.
export
preludeArgPosDictNames : List Decl -> List Decl -> List String
preludeArgPosDictNames preludeDecls allDecls =
  let rpSet = preludeReturnPosDictNames preludeDecls allDecls
  filterList (n => not (contains n rpSet)) (constrainedSigNames preludeDecls)

-- the EVars referenced anywhere in [n]'s definition body (multi-clause: union)
declBodyVars : String -> List Decl -> List String
declBodyVars n decls = flatMap (declBodyVarsOf n) decls

declBodyVarsOf : String -> Decl -> List String
declBodyVarsOf n (DFunDef _ m _ body _ _)
  | n == m = allEVars body
  | otherwise = []
declBodyVarsOf _ _ = []

resolveSites : SiteCtx -> OrdMap Unit -> List PendingEntry -> Unit
resolveSites sx _ [] = ()
resolveSites sx rpNames ((PendingEntry name tagRef resultMono encl kind loc scope _) :: rest) =
  let sx = { sx | sxSite = loc }
  match kind
    SKReturn implRef fullMono =>
      resolveSite
        sx
        rpNames
        name
        tagRef
        implRef
        resultMono
        fullMono
        encl
        loc
        scope
    SKAdmittedReturn ifaceRef implRef fullMono =>
      resolveAdmittedSite sx name ifaceRef tagRef implRef fullMono encl scope
    SKExactReturn implRef request =>
      resolveExactReturnSite
        sx
        rpNames
        name
        tagRef
        implRef
        resultMono
        request
        encl
        loc
        scope
    SKNumReturn predicate fullMono =>
      resolveNumLitSite
        sx
        rpNames
        name
        tagRef
        resultMono
        fullMono
        predicate
        encl
        loc
        scope
    _ => ()
  resolveSites sx rpNames rest

-- C5: stamp RLocal on each recorded standalone-shadow arg-position site whose
-- receiver mono now grounds to a concrete head tycon with NO impl of the method.
-- The receiver HAS an impl (the genuine-method case, e.g. `toList (Some 7)`) → leave
-- the route untouched (RNone → eval arg-tag-dispatches to the real impl).  An
-- ungrounded receiver (still a tyvar) → leave it (polymorphic, deferred).
-- RLocal only when no impl exists.
-- S-1: the stamp calls routesOfMonosTop — a PURE
-- function of the (union-find-solved) constraint monos — to fill the standalone's own
-- dict routes IN PLACE.  Deliberately NOT routed through pendingDictApps: that list is
-- resolved by resolveDictApps, which runs AFTER this in `moduleStampOrder`, so the stamp
-- would read `[]`.  Resolving inside the stamp is ordering-immune.  An unconstrained
-- standalone has no monos ⇒ routesOfMonosTop returns [] immediately (it cannot even
-- reach its AmbiguousImpl arm) ⇒ `RLocal sym []` ⇒ byte-identical to the pre-S1 stamp.
-- #156 S3d — resolveRLocalSites is DELIBERATELY NOT routed through `entail`, and DICT-
-- SEMANTICS §3 conformance REQUIRES that, rather than merely permitting it.  This pass
-- implements §4 `(var)`'s FIRST premise — binding selection: does this occurrence denote the
-- module's own standalone `sym` or a shadowed interface method?  (Keyed on the solved receiver
-- mono, which is why it runs post-inference.)  That decision reads shadow facts — isDefinerShadow,
-- definerShadowNamesRef — that are NOT components of entailment's domain `(IE, CE, P, π)` (§3
-- resolution-determinism); they are facts about Γ.  Folding them into the one entailment function
-- would make it depend on inputs outside its spec-given domain — violating the very law a merge
-- would invoke.  The tell: the `Some tag` arm treats "a live impl exists" as DO-NOTHING (the name
-- is a genuine method, dispatched elsewhere) and emits RLocal for the NO-impl case — the inverse of
-- `entailInst`'s success condition.  "No π to discharge; the name denotes another binding" is not an
-- evidence statement.  §4 `(var)`'s SECOND premise — the chosen standalone's actual entailment
-- obligations — IS routed through the one engine: every RLocal payload is filled by routesOfMonosTop
-- → entail (EKNestedTop).  So the single-entailment-function law holds at 4-of-5 BY CONSTRUCTION; what
-- stays out is exactly the binding-selection axis §3 never claimed (cf. §8 I1: identity keyed by
-- binding, not bare name).  "Does an impl exist" and "which impl entails" must agree on ONE
-- impl table — a drift between them would be a real dispatch bug.  #415 item 2: that
-- agreement is STRUCTURAL, not a standing obligation.
-- Arch B-2.1-g rebased both reads, together, onto `ModuleCells.mcCells.bodyImplEnvRef`, and the
-- sentence that stood here — "There is no second table in scope to drift TO" — WAS ALREADY
-- FALSE and is what licensed a bad scoping.  `bodyImplEnvRef` has been a second impl table,
-- in scope from anywhere, since B-2.1-a2, and B-2.1-b2 moved three SELECTION legs onto it
-- while this site's two reads stayed on the threaded prefix `[keyTable]`.  `B-2.1-c` then
-- moved the sibling SHADOW existence reads and deferred this one, which produced exactly the
-- drift this block claimed was unreachable: existence answered True off the whole graph while
-- `routesOfMonosTop … keyTable`, one line below, had no row to select — a located reject
-- became exit 0 printing a garbage pointer.  So the agreement is restored the only way it can
-- be, by moving BOTH: `ieImplExistsForHead …bodyImplEnvRef…` directly, and `keyForSite` (also
-- repointed onto `bodyImplEnvRef`) via routesOfMonosTop → routeOf → entail (EKNestedTop) →
-- entailInst.  ⚠️ THE INVARIANT IS UNCHANGED AND IS STILL THE ONE THAT MATTERS: these two
-- reads must name ONE population.  It is no longer enforced by a shared parameter, so it is
-- now enforced by a shared REF — and the check on any future edit here is "does the thing I
-- am reading answer over the same population `keyForSite` selects from?", not "am I using
-- [keyTable]?".  No impl list is threaded through this signature or through
-- `routesOfMonosTop`'s subtree any more.
-- (The inference-time existence reads in `inferShadowApp` / `definerReceiverDispatches` are
-- the same decision at an earlier PHASE and are now on the same ref for the same reason —
-- B-2.1-c's measurement is that a phase split of one decision is as fatal as a table split.
-- ⚠️ Do not re-derive the retired defence "GLOBAL by design — local ∪ imported ∪ prelude":
-- `SHADOW-SEMANTICS.md:242-245` retires that phrase as a false synonym for graph-global, and
-- `shadowKeyTableRef` was in fact the cumulative topological PREFIX on the Module arm.)
resolveRLocalSites : SiteCtx -> List PendingEntry -> Unit
resolveRLocalSites sx [] = ()
resolveRLocalSites sx ((PendingEntry name tagRef am encl kind loc scope _) :: rest) =
  let sx = { sx | sxSite = loc }
  match kind
    SKRLocal sym forceLocal monos ifaces argVecs =>
      if forceLocal then
        tagRef :=
          RLocal sym (routesOfMonosTopV sx encl scope monos ifaces argVecs)
      else
        resolveRLocalSite sx name tagRef am encl scope sym monos ifaces argVecs
    _ => ()
  resolveRLocalSites sx rest

-- After the module is inferred, classify each recorded arithmetic operand mono and
-- stamp the supported concrete scalar tag on the node's route. Grounded-only,
-- exactly like resolveBinopSite: a still-
-- polymorphic operand (headTyconMono None) is left untouched (RNone → dict path),
-- so polymorphic-Num arithmetic keeps routing through the runtime Num dict. Never
-- overwrite a route another pass already set (a comparison op has a different
-- node/ref; an arithmetic route starts RNone).
resolveArithSites : List (Ref Route, Mono) -> Unit
resolveArithSites [] = ()
resolveArithSites ((dref, m) :: rest) =
  resolveArithSite dref m
  resolveArithSites rest

-- EBinOp and EUnOp share ONE dict-route resolution family
-- (resolveOpSites/resolveOpSite/stampOpRouteVal/opDictVarOf), selected by an `isBinop`
-- flag (Roadmap #18c collapsed the binop/unop mirror pair — unopMethodApp already
-- reused binopRouteSplit, proving the shapes unify).  The two paths differ in exactly
-- two flag-keyed places: the dict-var-of policy (opDictVarOf) and the RKey stamp
-- (stampOpRouteVal — its builtin-head guard and Ord-style innerDefaultMethod reduction).
-- #156 S3c: resolveOpSite is now a thin adapter over `entail` (EKOp kind); the inst
-- route is stampOpRouteVal, a pure Route-returning extraction of the old stampOpRoute.
resolveOpSites : SiteCtx -> Bool -> List PendingEntry -> Unit
resolveOpSites sx _ [] = ()
resolveOpSites sx isBinop ((PendingEntry method tagRef operandMono encl kind loc scope _) :: rest) =
  let sx = { sx | sxSite = loc }
  match kind
    SKOp inImpl =>
      resolveOpSite sx isBinop method tagRef operandMono inImpl encl scope
    SKPredicateOp inImpl predicate =>
      resolvePredicateOpSite
        sx
        isBinop
        method
        tagRef
        operandMono
        inImpl
        predicate
        encl
        scope
    _ => ()
  resolveOpSites sx isBinop rest

-- Gap #21 (CLOSED): element reqs are now forwarded unconditionally on both eval and
-- emit paths.  The impl method `eq`/`compare` carries leading `$dict_*` params
-- (resolveArgStamps runs on both paths); emitter applies them; eval's methodAtNarrow
-- forwards dict reqs (like RDictFwd) truncated to the matched impl's reqCount.

-- ── coherence check (TYPECHECK-AUDIT S3) ───────────────────────────────────
-- Phase 68: reject incoherent USER
-- impl sets at declaration time.  Two impls of the SAME interface whose head
-- types can match the same concrete type (impls_overlap) are unresolvable unless
-- one strictly specializes the other (most-specific-wins).  Genuinely incoherent:
--   • two overlapping impls that are NOT a strict specialization → OverlappingImpls.
-- (Named impls + `@Name` selection + `default impl` were removed 2026-07-11; the
-- newtype-wrapper approach is the answer for a second instance.)
-- Prelude/seeded impls are excluded entirely (the driver passes USER decls only):
-- user impls are meant to override prelude impls (e.g. single-file `impl Ord Int`),
-- so they must not pair with a prelude `impl Ord Int`.  At most ONE error is
-- emitted (mirrors the oracle raising Type_error on the first conflict).

-- 🪦 RETIRED 2026-08-12 (#1559 A-3.7 bite 3.7-9): `cohImplsOf` / `cohImplsOfMid` —
-- the decl-walking adapters that built `CohImpl`s straight off `DImpl` nodes, and
-- `cohCollectImpls` / `cohCollectModuleImpls`, their two list drivers.  Coherence's
-- input is now a projection of `IE`'s rows (`cohImplOfRow`), so both sweeps read the
-- registry the rest of stage K reads instead of re-walking decls.  Zero tree-wide
-- callers at deletion time (`grep -rn 'cohCollectImpls\|cohCollectModuleImpls\|
-- cohImplsOf' --include=*.mdk .` → definitions and comments only).  The `#414` span
-- derivation they carried is preserved below, because `cohImplOfRow` still calls
-- `firstTyLocList` on the row's head and inherits every word of it.
--
-- #414: the span to blame for an impl comes from its head types, via
-- `firstTyLocList` (`frontend/ast.mdk`), which folds `firstTyLoc` — that inner
-- walk is the one shared with resolve (`dupSigOf`); resolve does not call
-- `firstTyLocList` itself (issue 480).
-- A `DImpl` has no `Loc` of its own (`DUse` is the only `Decl` variant
-- carrying one inline) — but the parser stamps every `TyCon` leaf with its span
-- (`parser.mdk`'s parseTyAtom: `tyConUnresolved c (Some (locOfSpan s q))`), so the head's
-- own tycon IS the impl's location.  Pre-order, so `impl C (Pair a Int)` blames
-- `Pair` — the head — not the argument.  An alias head's expansion is located at
-- the alias occurrence (`locateTyAt`), so `impl C LB` still blames `LB`.
--
-- ⚠️ RESIDUAL (#414): only `TyCon` leaves carry spans, so a head with NO tycon —
-- the fully-parametric `impl Foo a` — still yields `None` and falls back to the
-- file-start caret.  That is the degenerate overlap case (`test/
-- typecheck_error_fixtures/overlapping_impls.mdk`).  Closing it needs a span on
-- `TyVar` (an ast.mdk change rippling through every `Ty` consumer) or the parser's
-- `DeclPos` side-table threaded into typecheck; both are out of proportion to an
-- S3 diagnostic-quality fix.  Every head naming a CONCRETE type is covered.
--
-- #1559 A-3.7 OCCURRENCE MINT, and the retirement above is the reason it worked:
-- the deleted adapter destructured `implOrigin` in the SAME record pattern as `iface`
-- and built the `IfaceRef` from that pair on the spot, using the identical expression
-- `implDeclFact` uses to build `ImplRow`'s interface half.  Because the two
-- constructions could not drift, replacing the adapter with a projection of `IE`'s
-- rows yields the same interface half by construction rather than by assertion.
--
-- the impl's head args → monos under ONE shared fresh-var map (so a var reused
-- across args, e.g. `Conv a a`, is the SAME fresh tyvar — the oracle shares one
-- tbl across the whole impl head; distinct impls get distinct ids).
cohFreshTys : ModuleCtx -> List Ty -> List Mono
cohFreshTys mctx tys = snd (implHeadMonos mctx tys)

-- An impl head's variables under their declared kinds: a name in an
-- `Authority`-kinded slot (`impl Eq (Handle p)`) is an authority binder, as
-- in a signature; every other bare name is a type variable.  One map is
-- shared across the head's arguments, so a name reused across them is one
-- variable.
implHeadMonos : ModuleCtx -> List Ty -> (List (String, Mono), List Mono)
implHeadMonos mctx tys =
  fold (_ ty => checkImplHeadIndices mctx ty) () tys
  let auths = dedupBinders (flatMap (authArgBindersIn mctx) tys) []
  let pats = flatMap (patternSlotNamesIn mctx) tys
  let tvMap =
    freshTvMap
      mctx
      (removeAllS (map fst auths) (dedup (flatMap tyVarNames tys)))
  let etbl =
    sigVarsWithAuths
      (map (b => freshAuthBinderRanged mctx (contains (fst b) pats) b) auths)
      emptySigVars
  (tvMap, map (fromAstTypeE mctx etbl tvMap) tys)

-- An instance is chosen by its head's type constructor and the index is
-- erased, so an impl covers every index of the head: an `Authority` slot of
-- an impl head takes a name, never a written term.
checkImplHeadIndices : ModuleCtx -> Ty -> Unit
checkImplHeadIndices mctx (TyApp a b) = match tyAppSpine (TyApp a b)
  (TyCon { tyConName = n, tyConOrigin = o }, args) =>
    match lookupTab (tyTabKey o n) mctx.mcCells.dataParamKindsRef.value
      Some kinds if listLen kinds == listLen args =>
        fold
          (_ ka => match ka
            (KAuth _ _, TyAuth ps loc) =>
              pushTypeErrorOncePerSite
                mctx
                "T-AUTHORITY-KIND"
                loc
                (implHeadIndexMsg n (ppTy (TyAuth ps loc)))
            _ => ())
          ()
          (zipL kinds args)
      _ => ()
  _ => ()
checkImplHeadIndices mctx _ = ()

-- #1559 A-3.7: THE `IE`→`CohImpl` ADAPTER — coherence's input, relocated off the decl
-- walk.  Every one of the four things coherence judges on comes out of the row:
--   * the interface half is `ieRowTriple`'s `IfaceRef` — the SAME value
--     `cohImplsOfMid` built by hand from `iface`+`implOrigin`, because `implDeclFact`
--     builds it with the identical expression.  That is why this relocation is not an
--     acceptance change: `cohSameIface` (3.7-4) sees the same pair of `IfaceRef`s.
--   * the head is `cohFreshTys` of the row's `List Ty`, the same call the decl
--     adapter made.  Effectful (fresh tyvars), exactly as the decl adapter was.
--     The head is already in alias normal form (`stampGraphDecls`), so
--     coherence compares the head selection reads, and `fromAstTypeE` finds no
--     alias left on it to expand with the checked module's alias table (the
--     wrong table for another module's head).
--   * the owner module id is `instRefMid` of the row's `InstRef` — this is where
--     `InstRef` acquires its FIRST judgment reader in this tree.
--   * the blame span is `firstTyLocList` of that same head.
-- ⚠️ `ieLoc` IS NOT OWED FOR THIS.  `ImplRow`'s "no location field" note argues from
-- `Decl` carrying no `Loc`, which is true and beside the point: the row carries the
-- head's `List Ty`, and the parser stamps every `TyCon` leaf with its span, so the span
-- coherence uses today is recoverable with no new field and no `DImpl` change.
cohImplOfRow : ModuleCtx -> ImplRow -> CohImpl
cohImplOfRow mctx r = match ieRowTriple r
  (ir, tys, _) =>
    CohImpl
      ir
      (cohFreshTys mctx tys)
      (instRefMid (ieRowInst r))
      (orElseLoc (firstTyLocList tys) (ieRowLoc r))

-- The prelude is ordinal 0 on the Module arm, structurally: `buildDeclEnvs` builds
-- `declEnvModulesFrom 0 (("core", coreDecls)::modules)`, so nothing else can be.
-- Coherence compares a program's impls with the prelude's (DICT-SEMANTICS §6.1), but
-- never the prelude's with itself: the prelude is trusted and cannot be edited.
cohPreludeOrd : Int
cohPreludeOrd = 0

-- the prelude's own rows: the second population of the per-module sweep.
cohPreludeRows : ImplEnv -> List ImplRow
cohPreludeRows env = ieRowsOwnedBy cohPreludeOrd env

-- every USER module's rows, for the whole-graph sweep.  The prelude is absent here
-- because a program-vs-prelude pair is owned by the per-module sweep (which sees the
-- prelude and reports with the impl's own span); the whole-graph sweep would report
-- the same pair a second time, span-less.
cohRowsOf : ImplEnv -> List ImplRow
cohRowsOf env = filterList (r => ieRowOrd r /= cohPreludeOrd) (ieRowsAll env)

-- the per-module sweep's own population.  The prelude module itself checks nothing:
-- its rows are the second population, never the first.
cohRowsOwnedBy : Int -> ImplEnv -> List ImplRow
cohRowsOwnedBy cur env
  | cur == cohPreludeOrd = []
  | otherwise = ieRowsOwnedBy cur env

-- subsumes ~general ~specific: is [specific] an instance of [general]?  Only the
-- general side's vars bind (consistently: a var bound twice must see structurally
-- equal types); the specific side's vars are rigid (match only the same id).
cohSubsumes : List Mono -> List Mono -> Bool
cohSubsumes general specific
  | listLen general == listLen specific =
    isSome (matchOneSided cohStep eqInt cohEqMono (zipL general specific) [])
  | otherwise = False

-- Mono-space step: normalize BOTH sides (chasing links), then classify the general
-- node.  Effect rows are row-blind (TEff/TEff ⇒ MOk; TFun's row slot ignored).
cohStep : Mono -> Mono -> MStep Int Mono Mono
cohStep g0 s0 =
  let g = peelQual (normalize g0)
  let s = peelQual (normalize s0)
  match g
    TVar c => MVar (tyvarId c)
    -- #1111 A-2.10 on the `TCon`/`TCon` pairing only (`sameTyConHead`); the
    -- cross-population arms stay name-only for the reason `cohGoR` gives.
    -- ⚠️ The cross-population ones are NOT SEPARATELY PROBED — armed
    -- because the pre-split arm answered them, and because a rigid and a real
    -- head CAN both spell `__tupleN__` (see `Mono.TRigid`).  Measured instances
    -- of that forgery: `unifyN`, `matchStep` (§8 I6.2(b), OWED-#1243).
    TCon a oa => match s
      TCon b ob => if sameTyConHead a oa b ob then MOk else MFail
      TRigid b => if a == b then MOk else MFail
      _ => MFail
    TRigid a => match s
      TRigid b => if a == b then MOk else MFail
      TCon b _ => if a == b then MOk else MFail
      _ => MFail
    TApp f1 a1 => match s
      TApp f2 a2 => MKids [(f1, f2), (a1, a2)]
      _ => MFail
    TFun a1 _ b1 => match s
      TFun a2 _ b2 => MKids [(a1, a2), (b1, b2)]
      _ => MFail
    TEff _ => match s
      TEff _ => MOk
      _ => MFail
    TAuth _ => match s
      TAuth _ => MOk
      _ => MFail

eqInt : Int -> Int -> Bool
eqInt a b = a == b

-- [a] strictly more specific than [b]: b subsumes a but not a subsumes b
cohStrictlyMoreSpecific : List Mono -> List Mono -> Bool
cohStrictlyMoreSpecific a b = cohSubsumes b a && not (cohSubsumes a b)

-- [impls] are paired with each other; each is also paired with every one of [fixed]
-- (the prelude's impls), which are never paired with one another.
cohScan : CohSweep -> List CohImpl -> List CohImpl -> CohScan
cohScan sweep impls fixed = cohScanOuter sweep impls fixed (CohScan None None)

cohScanOuter : CohSweep -> List CohImpl -> List CohImpl -> CohScan -> CohScan
cohScanOuter _ [] _ acc = acc
cohScanOuter sweep (e :: rest) fixed acc
  | cohScanDone acc = acc
  | otherwise =
    cohScanOuter
      sweep
      rest
      fixed
      (cohScanInner sweep e fixed (cohScanInner sweep e rest acc))

-- both classes already witnessed ⇒ nothing later can change what is reported.
cohScanDone : CohScan -> Bool
cohScanDone (CohScan (Some _) (Some _)) = True
cohScanDone _ = False

-- #1559 A-3.7: DO TWO IMPL OCCURRENCES NAME THE SAME INTERFACE?
--
-- 🚨 `sameTyConHead`, NEVER `ifaceIdMatches`, AND THE TWO ARE EXACT INVERSES.  This
-- is the whole substance of the bite, so the derivation is here rather than in a
-- ledger:
--   * `sameTyConHead n1 o1 n2 o2 = n1 == n2 && not (tyConIdsConflict o1 o2)`
--     (`frontend/ast.mdk`) — name equality, and an ABSENT origin makes NO CLAIM, so
--     it matches anything.
--   * `ifaceIdMatches a b = a /= "" && a == b` (`frontend/ast.mdk`) — absence NEVER
--     matches, not even itself.
-- `recordCandIsType`'s header states which to use when, and the rule is about the
-- QUESTION being asked, not about the table: `sameTyConHead` belongs where a false
-- REJECT would refuse a valid program (an ACCEPTANCE question); `ifaceIdMatches`
-- belongs where a false HIT is silent wrongness (a LOOKUP).
--
-- Coherence is an ACCEPTANCE question — it decides whether to reject a program — so
-- `sameTyConHead` is correct, and it is also the FAIL-LOUD direction here: an impl
-- whose `implOrigin` is still `OriginUnresolved` compares by name exactly as it did
-- before this unit, so no live rejection can silently vanish.  `ifaceIdMatches` in
-- this position would turn every unstamped-origin conflict into a SILENT ACCEPT,
-- which is a severity INCREASE and one no fixture in the tree would catch.
--
-- ⚠️ NOT a re-keying of the HEAD half.  Coherence's head comparison already routes
-- through `sameTyConHead` (`cohGoR`'s `TCon` arm, A-2.10) and is untouched, so the
-- #1317 T1 rule and closed S0 #1277 are not in scope for this unit.
cohSameIface : IfaceRef -> IfaceRef -> Bool
cohSameIface a b = sameTyConHead a.irName a.irOrigin b.irName b.irOrigin

cohScanInner : CohSweep -> CohImpl -> List CohImpl -> CohScan -> CohScan
cohScanInner _ _ [] acc = acc
cohScanInner sweep (e1@(CohImpl if1 xs mid1 _)) ((CohImpl if2 ys mid2 _) :: rest) acc
  | cohScanDone acc = acc
  | cohSameIface if1 if2 && cohOverlap xs ys =
    cohScanInner sweep e1 rest (cohClassify sweep e1 xs ys mid1 mid2 acc)
  | otherwise = cohScanInner sweep e1 rest acc

-- classify ONE overlapping pair.  A strict specialization either way is coherent
-- (most-specific-wins ranks it) and contributes nothing.  The remaining two cases
-- are exhaustive and disjoint: `cohStrictlyMoreSpecific a b = cohSubsumes b a && not
-- (cohSubsumes a b)`, so if neither direction is strict then `cohSubsumes` holds
-- BOTH ways (mutual ⇒ HARD) or NEITHER way (incomparable ⇒ SOFT).
-- Keep-first per class mirrors the old "first conflict wins" reporting.
--
-- ⚠️ WHY THE HARD ARM CANNOT SIMPLY MOVE TO THE GOAL SITE, stated because "then fix
-- it there" is the obvious review question and the answer is not "we didn't try".
-- The root is one level up from `entryCovers`: `entryCoversAllOthers` /
-- `findMostSpecificEntry` test for a ⊑-MINIMUM, where §6 C1 requires **at most one
-- ⊑-MINIMAL element**.  In a preorder that is not antisymmetric those two coincide
-- everywhere EXCEPT at α-equal heads — precisely this arm's class.  (`entryCovers`
-- itself is fine: with `S = tySubsumesV`, `tyHeadEqV a b || S b a` is exactly ⊑;
-- it does not conflate ⊒ with =.)  Tightening `entryCoversAllOthers` to demand
-- STRICT specificity was built and measured: it finds 6 true positives and then
-- breaks `stdlib/core.mdk`, which stops typechecking with "the goal `Num Int`
-- matches `impl Num Int` and `impl Num Int`" — checking core as a user program
-- registers the same instance twice, and deduping needs INSTANCE IDENTITY this tree
-- does not have (`bucketKeyEntriesFrom` restarts its numbering at 0 per module, so
-- two distinct impls in different modules share an index).  That is L2 / A-3 / B-2
-- work.  Until it exists, the declaration site is the only place this class is
-- caught at all.
--
-- A program impl α-equal to a PRELUDE impl is this arm's class too: the per-module
-- sweep pairs each program impl with the prelude's impls (DICT-SEMANTICS §6.1), so a
-- user `impl Display String` is rejected at the program's impl.  A strictly more
-- specific program impl is coherent and wins on every engine.
cohClassify : CohSweep ->
  CohImpl ->
  List Mono ->
  List Mono ->
  String ->
  String ->
  CohScan ->
  CohScan
cohClassify sweep e1 xs ys mid1 mid2 (CohScan hard soft)
  | cohStrictlyMoreSpecific xs ys = CohScan hard soft
  | cohStrictlyMoreSpecific ys xs = CohScan hard soft
  | cohMutuallySubsumes xs ys && cohHardInScope sweep mid1 mid2 =
    CohScan
      (cohKeepFirst hard (Some (cohHardMsg e1 xs ys mid1 mid2, cohImplLoc e1)))
      soft
  -- A mutually-subsuming pair the sweep does NOT own contributes nothing at all --
  -- it must not fall through to the soft arm below, because HARD and SOFT are
  -- disjoint classes (mutual subsumption is the exact complement of
  -- ⊑-incomparability here), and reporting it as `W-INCOMPARABLE-IMPLS`
  -- would be a wrong classification, not a quieter one.
  | cohMutuallySubsumes xs ys = CohScan hard soft
  | not (cohSoftInScope sweep mid1 mid2) = CohScan hard soft
  | otherwise =
    CohScan
      hard
      (cohKeepFirst
        soft
        (Some (
          cohIncomparableMsg (cohImplIfaceName e1) xs ys mid1 mid2,
          cohImplLoc e1,
        )))

-- Which sweep OWNS a soft (⊑-incomparable) pair.  Two sweeps run over overlapping
-- inputs: `checkCoherence` over ONE module's own impls and `globalCoherenceConflict`
-- over every user module's impls (real mids).  A pair
-- whose two impls live in the SAME module is seen by BOTH — the per-module one with a
-- real span, the global one span-less (#414) — so recording it in both makes
-- `run`/`build` print it TWICE where `check` prints it once.  The global sweep's
-- unique contribution is the pair that SPANS two modules, which no per-module sweep
-- can see; that is the only soft pair it should claim.
--
-- ⚠️ Scoped to the SOFT class deliberately.  The HARD class double-reports the same
-- way, and that is PRE-EXISTING — it did so as a `T-CONFLICTING-IMPL` error before
-- F-3d, on these same two paths — so narrowing it here would be an unrelated
-- behaviour change riding this one, and one that moves error goldens.
-- 🚨 #1559 A-3.7: SWEEP-SCOPED, NOT MID-SHAPE-SCOPED, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS A
-- LOUD→SILENT REGRESSION THIS FUNCTION USED TO BE ONE COMMIT AWAY FROM.
-- The body was:
--     cohSoftInScope "" ""   = True
--     cohSoftInScope m1 m2   = cohIsCrossModule m1 m2
-- i.e. it asked "are both mids empty?" as a stand-in for "am I the per-module
-- sweep?".  That proxy held only because the per-module sweep's input came from
-- `cohImplsOf`, which had no module id to stamp and so stamped `""`.  Pointing that
-- sweep at `IE` gives every row a REAL id (`instRefMid`), so an intra-module pair
-- arrives as `(m, m)` with `m /= ""` — the first arm stops matching, `cohIsCrossModule
-- m m` is `False`, and EVERY intra-module `W-INCOMPARABLE-IMPLS` silently stops being
-- reported.  Diagnostic-only, so no value golden in this tree could see it.
--
-- The sweep tag says outright what the mid shapes were being read to infer:
--   * `CohSweepOwn` — the per-module sweep.  Its input is ONE module's own rows, so
--     every pair it sees is intra-module BY CONSTRUCTION and it owns all of them.
--     Answering `True` unconditionally is exactly what the old `"" ""` arm did for
--     the only input that sweep ever had.
--   * `CohSweepGlobal` — the whole-graph sweep.  It owns only the pair that SPANS two
--     modules; the intra-module ones already belong to the sweep above.  The `"" ""`
--     arm is retained HERE (and only here) because it is behaviour-preserving for a
--     degenerate global input in which both ids are blank — a shape this function
--     answered `True` for before A-3.7, and one this bite deliberately does not
--     re-adjudicate.
cohSoftInScope : CohSweep -> String -> String -> Bool
cohSoftInScope CohSweepOwn _ _ = True
cohSoftInScope CohSweepGlobal "" "" = True
cohSoftInScope CohSweepGlobal mid1 mid2 = cohIsCrossModule mid1 mid2

-- Which sweep OWNS a HARD (mutually-subsuming) pair.  #1449 / F8: the SAME rule as
-- `cohSoftInScope`, and it is a delegation rather than a copy so the two classes can
-- never drift apart silently.
--
-- 🚨 THIS IS THE NARROWING `cohSoftInScope`'s header DECLINED TO MAKE, now made
-- deliberately.  That header said, of the hard class: "The HARD class double-reports
-- the same way, and that is PRE-EXISTING … so narrowing it here would be an unrelated
-- behaviour change riding this one, and one that moves error goldens."  It is no
-- longer unrelated: the double report IS #1449's shape, and it is user-visible on the
-- most ordinary program there is.  Measured before this change, on a single file with
-- two `impl Foo Int`, `medaka check --json` emitted the identical
-- `T-CONFLICTING-IMPL` message TWICE — once with the declaration's real span (from the
-- per-module sweep, `checkCoherence` / `CohSweepOwn`) and once span-less (from this
-- whole-graph sweep, prepended by `attachCoherenceConflict`, which `driveGraphK` and
-- the keyed arm of `checkModulesDiagsChain` both call.  An IMPORT-BEARING two-module
-- program whose overlap is entry-module-local double-reports identically, so the
-- double report is not specific to one module.  Per-module sweep and whole-graph
-- sweep each report the pair: one with the declaration span, one without it.
--
-- ⚠️ NOT loud→silent, and here is why that is a claim and not a hope.  The pair this
-- now declines is INTRA-module, and the per-module sweep's population
-- (`cohRowsOwnedBy cur`) contains every one of that module's own rows by
-- construction, with `foldModules` running the worker for EVERY module in the graph.
-- So the union of the per-module sweeps already covers every intra-module pair the
-- whole-graph sweep could see, WITH a span, which is strictly the better diagnostic.
-- The whole-graph sweep's unique contribution -- the pair that SPANS two modules, which
-- no per-module sweep can see -- is exactly what this predicate keeps.  Control
-- measured across the change: two modules each declaring `impl Foo Int` for a third
-- module's interface still reports `Conflicting `impl Foo`. Defined in amod and main`,
-- once.
--
-- The one residual hole is `runFinalChecks`' documented `-1` ordinal sentinel, at which
-- `checkCoherence` sweeps no rows: an intra-module hard pair would then be reported by
-- NEITHER sweep.  That path is unreachable today and `ordinalSentinelGuard` already
-- pushes a loud `T-INTERNAL-ORDINAL` error when it is taken, so the failure announces
-- itself rather than accepting silently.
cohHardInScope : CohSweep -> String -> String -> Bool
cohHardInScope sweep mid1 mid2 = cohSoftInScope sweep mid1 mid2

-- each head matches the other, i.e. they are α-equal up to renaming (`cohSubsumes`
-- is one-sided matching, so mutual matching means each is an instance of the other).
cohMutuallySubsumes : List Mono -> List Mono -> Bool
cohMutuallySubsumes xs ys = cohSubsumes xs ys && cohSubsumes ys xs

cohKeepFirst : Option a -> Option a -> Option a
cohKeepFirst (Some x) _ = Some x
cohKeepFirst None y = y

-- HARD wording.  When the two impls come from DIFFERENT modules (mid1 /= mid2, both
-- non-empty), the message names BOTH owning modules (the cross-module global-
-- coherence case, D3/WS-2 — which is exactly the duplicate-instance class).
cohHardMsg : CohImpl -> List Mono -> List Mono -> String -> String -> String
cohHardMsg e1 xs ys mid1 mid2
  | cohPairsPrelude mid1 mid2 = cohPreludeOverlapMsg (cohImplIfaceName e1) xs ys
  | cohIsCrossModule mid1 mid2 =
    cohCrossModuleMsg (cohImplIfaceName e1) mid1 mid2
  | otherwise = cohOverlapMsg (cohImplIfaceName e1) xs ys

-- the prelude's module id in `buildDeclEnvs`' module list.
cohPreludeMid : String
cohPreludeMid = "core"

-- Whether one impl of the pair is the prelude's.  The per-module sweep pairs a
-- module's own rows (first) with the prelude's (second), so the prelude's is [mid2].
cohPairsPrelude : String -> String -> Bool
cohPairsPrelude mid1 mid2 = mid1 == cohPreludeMid || mid2 == cohPreludeMid

cohIsCrossModule : String -> String -> Bool
cohIsCrossModule mid1 mid2 = mid1 /= "" && mid2 /= "" && mid1 /= mid2

-- SOFT wording (`W-INCOMPARABLE-IMPLS`).  Carries the "Warning: " prefix the
-- `matchWarnings` channel's text renderers expect and `stripWarnPrefix` removes for
-- the structured `--json` form.  ERROR-QUALITY: it states the rule that was violated
-- in the user's own vocabulary (these two heads, this interface), says the acceptance
-- consequence rather than asserting the program is wrong — because under (c) it may
-- not be — and puts the SPEC's remedy first.  The old error's advice ("make them
-- disjoint, or wrap one type in a newtype") is #614's S2: it is the wrong fix here
-- and, as that issue's own control shows, adding the ranking impl changed nothing.
-- A pair with the prelude names the prelude's impl as such rather than by module id,
-- as `cohPreludeOverlapMsg` does: the program's own module id differs between verbs.
cohIncomparableMsg : String ->
  List Mono ->
  List Mono ->
  String ->
  String ->
  String
cohIncomparableMsg iface xs ys mid1 mid2 = match cohPpPair xs ys
  (s1, s2) =>
    if cohPairsPrelude mid1 mid2 then
      "Warning: overlapping impls of \{iface}: neither \{s1} nor the prelude's \{s2} is more specific than the other, so a goal matching both has no impl to pick"
    else
      "Warning: overlapping impls of \{iface}\{cohWhereSuffix mid1 mid2}: neither \{s1} nor \{s2} is more specific than the other, so a goal matching both has no impl to pick"

cohWhereSuffix : String -> String -> String
cohWhereSuffix mid1 mid2
  | cohIsCrossModule mid1 mid2 = " (defined in `\{mid2}` and `\{mid1}`)"
  | otherwise = ""

cohImplIface : CohImpl -> IfaceRef
cohImplIface (CohImpl i _ _ _) = i

-- #1559 A-3.7: the SPELLING, for the message renderers alone.  Every `coh*Msg`
-- below keeps its `String` parameter deliberately — the rendered wording is pinned
-- byte-for-byte by error goldens, and this unit moves no diagnostic text.  Reading
-- `.irName` through a named projection rather than at each call site keeps the
-- "identity decides, spelling only prints" split visible.
cohImplIfaceName : CohImpl -> String
cohImplIfaceName e = (cohImplIface e).irName
