cohImplLoc : CohImpl -> Option Loc
cohImplLoc (CohImpl _ _ _ l) = l

-- push the SOFT (condition-(a)-only) coherence finding onto the typecheck WARNING
-- channel.  ⚠️ `matchWarnings`, NOT `recordTypeError` with severity 2 — see
-- `matchWarnings`' own note: `recordTypeError` arms `typeErrorsSticky` (aborts
-- build/run) and bumps `errorsDetected` (steers `erredDuring`-gated inference)
-- unconditionally, without reading severity, so a severity-2 push there keeps BOTH of
-- an error's side effects and still renders as severity 1.  A demotion has to change
-- channel, not just the number.
pushCoherenceWarning : ModuleCtx -> Option Loc -> String -> Unit
pushCoherenceWarning mctx loc msg =
  let warning =
    TcDiag
      "W-INCOMPARABLE-IMPLS"
      2
      (orElseLoc loc mctx.mcLoc)
      msg
      (Some cohIncomparableHelp)
      None
  mctx.mcCells.matchWarnings := warning :: mctx.mcCells.matchWarnings.value

-- run coherence over USER decls; push at most one HARD conflict into typeErrors and
-- at most one SOFT one onto the warning channel.  The impls are scanned in REVERSE
-- declaration order to mirror the oracle, whose env.impls is built by prepending each
-- entry (`entry :: !(env.impls)`) — so the conflict message names the later-declared
-- impl as the first head, byte-identical.
-- #1559 A-3.7: the input is `IE`'s rows for THIS module, not a decl list.
-- [cur] is the reading module's ordinal.  Its own rows are paired with each other and
-- with the prelude's rows (`cohPreludeRows`), never prelude with prelude.
--
-- POPULATION EQUALITY, derived rather than assumed (it is the one thing that could
-- silently change what gets checked).  The Module caller used to pass `prog`, the
-- module's own desugared decls as `foldModules` holds them.  `ieRowsOwnedBy ordHere`
-- returns the rows `implRowsOf` built from `demDecls` at that ordinal.  Those are the
-- same list VALUE: `driveGraphK` stamps once (`stampGraphDecls`) and hands
-- the SAME `modules` to `graphPreamble` → `buildDeclEnvs` and to `foldModules`,
-- and `foldModules` passes each `(mid, prog)` pair's `prog` to the worker verbatim —
-- no transform on either side.  Harvest equality holds too: `implDeclFact` and the
-- retired `cohImplsOfMid` match arm-for-arm (unwrap `DAttrib`, take `DImpl`, drop
-- everything else) and both are a `flatMap` in decl order.
checkCoherence : ModuleCtx -> ImplEnv -> Int -> Unit
checkCoherence mctx env cur =
  match (cohScan
    CohSweepOwn
    (reverseL (map (cohImplOfRow mctx) (cohRowsOwnedBy cur env)))
    (map (cohImplOfRow mctx) (cohPreludeRows env)))
    CohScan hard soft =>
      cohPushHard mctx hard
      cohPushSoft mctx soft

cohPushHard : ModuleCtx -> Option (String, Option Loc) -> Unit
cohPushHard mctx None = ()
cohPushHard mctx (Some (msg, loc)) =
  pushTypeErrorAt mctx "T-CONFLICTING-IMPL" loc msg

cohPushSoft : ModuleCtx -> Option (String, Option Loc) -> Unit
cohPushSoft mctx None = ()
cohPushSoft mctx (Some (msg, loc)) = pushCoherenceWarning mctx loc msg

-- ── the superinterface rule for impl declarations (DICT-SEMANTICS §3 W-super) ──
-- Checks each impl in [userDecls] against every direct super of its interface; see
-- `checkImplSuperContexts`.  The supers come from `CE` at the reading ordinal [cur],
-- keyed by the impl's `implOrigin`.  Existence of a super impl is asked of every
-- `IE` row in the graph (`ieRowsVisibleAt` reads `ieCandidacyVisibleAt`, the
-- predicate instance candidacy reads), so a super impl declared in a later module
-- counts, as it does for dispatch; a row counts only when its own interface identity
-- is the super's `superOrigin`, never a same-spelled interface.
--
-- The row list is bound here, once: it is O(rows), and the existence test runs per
-- (impl x super).
checkSuperImpls : ModuleCtx -> List Decl -> ClassEnv -> ImplEnv -> Int -> Unit
checkSuperImpls mctx userDecls ce ie cur =
  let rows = ieRowsVisibleAt cur ie
  foreachUnit (checkImplSuperContexts mctx userDecls ce cur rows) userDecls

-- DICT-SEMANTICS §3, the declaration rule for supers: a dictionary for `C ts` carries
-- one for each direct super `D` of `C` at the same arguments, built by the instance
-- `D ts` selects, so that instance's `requires` is part of what `C ts` owes.  The impl
-- must entail it from its own `requires` (with their supers), at its head with the
-- head variables rigid, or every binder that reduces `C ts` drops it.  A goal of the
-- selected instance's context is reduced through the instances as W3-inst's are; a
-- leaf that is no given is reported at the impl.  A super goal no given answers and
-- no impl row covers (`superRowExists`) is a missing super impl, reported at the impl
-- whether its head is concrete or parametric.  Direct supers suffice because every
-- impl is checked, the super's own impl included.
--
-- A parsed `impl` always records its interface token's span; a derived one records
-- none, so it is reported at the `data`/`newtype` declaration that produced it, and
-- its remedies are a `deriving` clause or a hand-written impl, since a `deriving`
-- clause takes no `requires`.
checkImplSuperContexts : ModuleCtx ->
  List Decl ->
  ClassEnv ->
  Int ->
  List ImplRow ->
  Decl ->
  Unit
checkImplSuperContexts mctx decls ce cur rows (DAttrib _ d) =
  checkImplSuperContexts mctx decls ce cur rows d
checkImplSuperContexts mctx decls ce cur rows (DImpl { iface, tys, reqs, implOrigin = o, implIfaceLoc = ifaceLoc, ... }) =
  let derived = isNone ifaceLoc
  let loc = if derived then derivedImplDeclLoc decls tys else ifaceLoc
  match ceLookupAt (regKeyOfTab (ifaceTabKey o iface)) cur ce
    Some r if listLen (ceRowTyparams r) == listLen tys =>
      let (implTvMap, headMonos) = implHeadMonos mctx tys
      let roots = implHeadTypeVarRoots implTvMap
      let headIds = omFromNames (map (p => intToString (snd p)) roots) omEmpty
      let declared = map (requirePredicateSlot mctx implTvMap) reqs
      let givens =
        declared
          ++ flatMap
            (s => map fst (predicateSlotKnownSupers mctx.mcGraph s))
            declared
      let subject = "impl \{iface} \{joinWith " " (map ppTyAtom tys)}"
      let subst = zipL (ceRowTyparams r) tys
      let argsOf =
        sup =>
          mapAll
            (p => lookupPos p (ceRowTyparams r) headMonos)
            (superParamsOf sup)
      fold
        (_ sup => match argsOf sup
          Some supArgs => checkSuperInstanceContext
            mctx
            subject
            roots
            headIds
            givens
            loc
            derived
            (superIfaceRef sup)
            supArgs
            (_ => superRowExists rows subst sup)
          None => ())
        ()
        (ceRowSupers r)
    _ => ()
checkImplSuperContexts mctx _ _ _ _ _ = ()

-- The span of the `data`/`newtype` declaration a derived impl's head names.
derivedImplDeclLoc : List Decl -> List Ty -> Option Loc
derivedImplDeclLoc decls tys = match flatMap tyConNamesInTy tys
  [n] => match flatMap (declNameLocs n) decls
    l :: _ => Some l
    [] => None
  _ => None

declNameLocs : String -> Decl -> List Loc
declNameLocs n (DAttrib _ d) = declNameLocs n d
declNameLocs n (DData { dataName, dataNameLoc = (Some l), ... })
  | dataName == n = [l]
declNameLocs n (DNewtype { newtypeName, newtypeNameLoc = (Some l), ... })
  | newtypeName == n = [l]
declNameLocs _ _ = []

checkSuperInstanceContext : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  List (String, Int) ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  List PredicateSlot ->
  Option Loc ->
  Bool ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  (Unit -> Bool) ->
  Unit
checkSuperInstanceContext mctx subject roots headIds givens loc derived sup supArgs covered
  | anyList (givenAnswers sup supArgs) givens = ()
  | otherwise =
    match rigidHeadInstanceContext (siteFor mctx) headIds sup supArgs
      None =>
        if not (covered ()) then
          reportMissingSuperImpl mctx subject roots loc derived sup supArgs
      Some ctx =>
        let walk = reqWalkStart ()
        let leaves =
          flatMap
            (g =>
              superContextLeaves mctx walk headIds givens loc (fst g) (snd g))
            ctx
        fold
          (_ leaf =>
            reportSuperContextLeaf
              mctx
              subject
              roots
              loc
              derived
              sup
              supArgs
              leaf)
          ()
          leaves

-- Whether some impl row of the super covers the super goal at the impl's head
-- (`superHeadCovers`).  Rows are graph-wide, so a super impl declared downstream
-- counts.
superRowExists : List ImplRow -> List (String, Ty) -> Super -> Bool
superRowExists rows subst (Super { superHead = n, superParams = ps, superOrigin = so }) =
  let tys = substParams ps subst
  listLen tys /= listLen ps || superImplExists rows (ifaceTabKey so n) n tys

-- The super is named by its spelling, as the checked impl's own interface is, so
-- the text is the same on every verb and at every head.  A derived impl's remedy is
-- the `deriving` clause when the super is derivable, else the hand-written impl.
reportMissingSuperImpl : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  List (String, Int) ->
  Option Loc ->
  Bool ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  Unit
reportMissingSuperImpl mctx subject roots loc derived sup supArgs =
  let named = Ref (map (p => (snd p, fst p)) roots)
  let goal = "\{sup.irName} \{joinWith " " (ppEach named (Ref 0) 3 supArgs)}"
  let missing = "requires the superinterface `\{goal}`, which no impl covers"
  pushTypeErrorOnceAt mctx "T-MISSING-SUPER-IMPL" loc (if not derived then
    "`\{subject}` \{missing}; add an `impl \{goal}` covering it, or add `requires \{goal}` to the impl"
  else if derivableIface sup.irName then
    "`\{subject}` (derived) \{missing}; add `\{sup.irName}` to the type's `deriving` clause, or add an `impl \{goal}`"
  else
    "`\{subject}` (derived) \{missing}; add an `impl \{goal}`")

-- The goals below [iface] [args] that no given answers: a goal over variables alone,
-- or one no instance selects with the head variables rigid.  Bounded by the shared
-- `requires` measure, a cycle or a runaway chain reported at [loc].  Each goal is
-- solved once per walk (`solvedOnWalk`); [headIds], [givens] and [loc] are fixed for
-- the walk `checkSuperInstanceContext` starts.
superContextLeaves : ModuleCtx ->
  ReqWalk ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  List PredicateSlot ->
  Option Loc ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  List (IfaceRef, List Mono)
superContextLeaves mctx walk headIds givens loc iface args
  | anyList (givenAnswers iface args) givens = []
  | not (anyConcreteHead args) = [(iface, args)]
  | otherwise = match reqWalkReported mctx loc (reqWalkEnter walk iface args)
    None => []
    Some next => solvedOnWalk
      mctx
      next
      iface
      args
      (_ => match rigidHeadInstanceContext (siteFor mctx) headIds iface args
        None => [(iface, args)]
        Some ctx =>
          flatMap
            (g =>
              superContextLeaves mctx next headIds givens loc (fst g) (snd g))
            ctx)

-- A leaf over head variables names the `requires` to add; a ground one names the
-- missing instance.  A leaf mentioning a variable the head does not bind has no
-- `requires` to name and is left to the goal's use.
reportSuperContextLeaf : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  List (String, Int) ->
  Option Loc ->
  Bool ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List Mono ->
  (IfaceRef, List Mono) ->
  Unit
reportSuperContextLeaf mctx subject roots loc derived sup supArgs (iface, args) =
  let ids = flatMap monoUnboundIds args
  let named = Ref (map (p => (snd p, fst p)) roots)
  let argsText = joinWith " " (ppEach named (Ref 0) 3 args)
  let superGoal =
    "\{qualifiedIfaceLabel sup} \{joinWith " " (ppEach named (Ref 0) 3 supArgs)}"
  let pred = "\{qualifiedIfaceLabel iface} \{argsText}"
  let predBare = "\{iface.irName} \{argsText}"
  if isEmptyL ids then
    pushTypeErrorOnceAt
      mctx
      "T-NO-IMPL"
      loc
      (superContextNoImplMsg subject derived superGoal pred predBare)
  else if allList (i => containsI i (map snd roots)) ids then
    pushTypeErrorOnceAt
      mctx
      "T-IMPL-MISSING-REQUIRES"
      loc
      (superContextUndeclaredMsg subject derived superGoal pred predBare)

foreachUnit : (a -> Unit) -> List a -> Unit
foreachUnit _ [] = ()
foreachUnit f (x :: xs) =
  f x
  foreachUnit f xs

-- ── P0-17: impl-completeness check ─────────────────────────────────────────
-- Beta finding P0-17 (qa-beta-2026-07-07): an `impl Iface Ty…` that defines only
-- SOME of the interface's methods used to `check` clean, then PANIC at runtime
-- (`E-PANIC: unbound identifier: <method>`) when a missing method is dispatched —
-- a run≠check hole.  For each impl, verify every REQUIRED interface method (one
-- declared WITHOUT a default body) is defined by the impl body; each missing one
-- is a located `T-INCOMPLETE-IMPL` error, so check/run/build all reject instead of
-- deferring to a runtime panic.
--
-- Runs POST-desugar (from the typecheck cores), which is the ONLY stage where both
-- sets are cleanly visible with defaults distinguishable:
--   • desugar's mergeIfaceDefaults has coalesced each interface method's split
--     signature-entry (`lt : …`, default None) and body-entry (`lt x y = …`,
--     default Some) into ONE `IfaceMethod` carrying the merged Option MethodDefault.
--     PRE-merge the sig-only `None` entry would make every defaulted method (Ord's
--     lt/gt/…) look REQUIRED → hundreds of false positives across core/stdlib.
--   • an impl's defined set is exactly what it writes: a method it leaves to its
--     interface's default is a disposition row, not a clause, so the defined set
--     cannot mask a genuinely-missing required method.
-- The interface decl is resolved out of stage K's `CE` at the reading module's
-- ordinal (`ceRequiredAt`), so an IMPORTED interface resolves exactly as a local one
-- does; [iterDecls] (this module's own decls) are the impls to check.  Unknown
-- interface (not in scope) → skip (a distinct error is reported elsewhere), as
-- `checkImplSuperContexts` skips one.
--
-- #1557 A-3.5a: there is now ONE checker for both driver modes.  There used to be
-- two — `checkImplCompleteness`, whose retired arm looked the interface up by a bare
-- first-match scan over the decl list, and `checkImplCompletenessMap` below.  The
-- retired arm's deletion was the unit's only genuine re-key (owner ruling on #1557 owed
-- 1, 2026-08-12: re-key, accept the acceptance delta, no bare-spelling compatibility
-- leg on CE).  Its one observable consequence: on a flat program where a USER
-- interface shadows a prelude one by spelling, the bare scan walked
-- `coreProg ++ userProg` head-first and returned the PRELUDE's required set for a
-- user impl; under identity the impl's own `implOrigin` decides, which is the
-- correct answer.
pushIncompleteImpl : ModuleCtx -> (Option Loc, String) -> Unit
pushIncompleteImpl mctx (loc, msg) =
  pushTypeErrorOnceAt mctx "T-INCOMPLETE-IMPL" loc msg

-- The span a missing-method error is attributed to: the first impl method's
-- body, read from its parsed AST whether or not the body was ever inferred.
-- `exprLoc` sees only an outermost `ELoc`/`EDoOrigin` wrapper, and a body shaped
-- `f x` (an application) has none, so `appArgLoc` gives its argument's span, a
-- location inside the impl block.  `None` for an impl with no method body or a
-- body neither form locates; the caller then reports at the impl's interface
-- name (`implIfaceLoc`).
firstImplMethodLoc : List ImplMethod -> Option Loc
firstImplMethodLoc [] = None
firstImplMethodLoc ((ImplMethod _ _ body) :: _) =
  orElseLoc (exprLoc body) (appArgLoc body)

-- The `Map` suffix is retained because it is cited from
-- compiler/frontend/resolve.mdk, compiler/TYPECHECK-TARGET-ARCHITECTURE.md, and
-- other comments in this file (see TYPECHECK-TARGET-ARCHITECTURE.md § "9.6 The
-- subsumption enumeration — derived by SHAPE, not by prefix", the
-- `implCompletenessMsgsOf` row, for the #1258 bug and the #1111/#1557 migration
-- history). Since A-3.5a there is no non-`Map` sibling; this is the ONE
-- impl-completeness checker, for both driver modes.
--
-- Required-ness is prePass-INVARIANT: `requiredMethodNames` reads only the presence
-- of `IfaceMethod`'s third position, and the prePass rewrite touches only a
-- `Some (…, e)` arm's body, so building `CE` from raw `demDecls` cannot change the
-- required-ness.
checkImplCompletenessMap : ModuleCtx -> ClassEnv -> Int -> List Decl -> Unit
checkImplCompletenessMap mctx ce cur iterDecls =
  foreachUnit
    (pushIncompleteImpl mctx)
    (flatMap (implCompletenessMsgsOfMap ce cur) iterDecls)

-- OCCURRENCE MINT (#1110/#1111 A-2.4): `implOrigin` beside `iface` in the same
-- record pattern, so the identity and the name it qualifies cannot drift apart.
implCompletenessMsgsOfMap : ClassEnv -> Int -> Decl -> List (Option Loc, String)
implCompletenessMsgsOfMap ce cur (DAttrib _ d) =
  implCompletenessMsgsOfMap ce cur d
implCompletenessMsgsOfMap ce cur (DImpl { iface, tys, methods, implOrigin = o, implIfaceLoc = ifaceLoc, ... }) =
  match ceRequiredAt (regKeyOfTab (ifaceTabKey o iface)) cur ce
    None => []  -- unknown interface (reported elsewhere) → skip
    Some required =>
      let defined = map implMethodName methods
      -- An impl with no method body of its own is located at its interface name.
      let loc = orElseLoc (firstImplMethodLoc methods) ifaceLoc
      map
        (m => (loc, missingImplMethodMsg iface tys m))
        (filter (m => not (contains m defined)) required)
implCompletenessMsgsOfMap _ _ _ = []

-- `insertIfaceRequired`, the retired writer of `universeIfaceRequiredRef` (see that
-- cell's tombstone in `CrossRun`), is superseded by `classEnvRowsOf`, which mints the
-- SAME key from the SAME `ifaceOrigin` and stores the SAME `requiredMethodNames
-- methods` value on `CeRow`; its DAttrib-unwrapping is preserved by
-- `classEnvDeclFact`, which unwraps `DAttrib` on the way into `CE`.

-- ── #1111 Stage A-2 unit A-2.11 (#1319 unit 1): the CONSTRUCTOR-namespace peer ──
--
-- Everything from here to `ctorExportsInto` (in `tc_decls`) is the constructor twin of the METHOD
-- method machinery (`MethodEnv` … `exportsIdentFor`).  It is a
-- deliberate near-copy and it is NAMED SCAFFOLDING, not an oversight:
--
--   * the METHOD index is already, by its own admission, a THIRD implementation of a
--     fact `resolve.mdk` derives, with **#1288** named as the absorbing stage that
--     deletes it.  This makes a FOURTH.  #1288's scope names the constructor peer, so
--     the deleter is real rather than asserted;
--   * B2 (resolve owns the fact and typecheck consumes it) is the target-conformant
--     answer under L2's identity-at-resolve law, and was REJECTED FOR NOW for a stated
--     reason: resolve's only delivery channel to typecheck is the AST, so B2 implies a
--     decl-adjacent carrier whose cost across printer / sexp / fmt / lower / mangle was
--     never costed.  See #1319's adjudication comment.
--
-- ⚠️ MIRROR DISCIPLINE IS LIVE between the two families until #1288 lands: a fix to the
-- scope ladder, the witness, or the export index on ONE side is silently absent from the
-- other.  They are kept together on purpose (this file and `tc_decls`).
--
-- ── WHAT THIS FIXES, AND WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT ──────────────────────
-- The ctor floor (`universeCtorPop`'s `spFloor`) is keyed by the BARE constructor name and is
-- last-write-wins, so when two unrelated modules each declare a `Dup` the whole loaded
-- program has ONE entry for `Dup` and load order picks the winner.  #1111 A-2.6 attacked
-- that with an import-scoped DECL overlay (`importedCtorTypeDecls`), and the boundary
-- moved one hop out twice: a member reached through a RE-EXPORT is not identity-matched
-- (#1283), and a ride-along SIBLING constructor of an overlaid decl out-ranks a ctor the
-- unit imports BY NAME from an earlier clause (#1284).
--
-- This unit keeps the overlay (unit 4 retires it) and adds the A-2.5-shaped answer on
-- top: an identity-keyed COMPANION of the bare map, plus a per-module SCOPE DECISION for
-- the colliding names only.  The overlay's unit is the DECL; a scope decision's unit is
-- the NAME, which is why a ride-along sibling cannot win here.
--
-- 🚨 IT MUST NOT RE-DECIDE AMBIGUITY.  Constructor-name ambiguity is provenance-based
-- (`ctorAmbiguousSet` → `keepAmbiguous` in `frontend/resolve.mdk`: ≥2 distinct
-- declarations in scope), and that rule is deliberately ONE rule across the value / type /
-- interface / ctor namespaces — resolve's own note says a change there must change all
-- four at once.  This is a different question on the same data: "which declaration does
-- this module mean" is asked only where resolve has already ACCEPTED the program.  Two
-- witnesses decline to the floor here rather than picking one, so a genuinely ambiguous
-- import is still resolve's to reject and nothing here can quietly accept it.
--
-- ⚠️ MODULE-PATH-ONLY, exactly as A-2.5: a flat/single-file declaration carries
-- `OriginUnresolved`, `mkIdent` refuses it, no candidate is recorded, and the override
-- site is on the `Module` arm alone.
--
-- No prelude rung, unlike the method ladder's `methodUndecided` — and that asymmetry is measured, not
-- assumed.  A module that declares OR imports a constructor spelled like a prelude
-- constructor is rejected outright (`Duplicate constructor: Lt`), so `core` can never be
-- one of two candidates for one ctor name and there is no rung for it to be.

-- The two tables `registerRecordInfoKeyed` writes in lockstep — `recordByNameRef`
-- (registry key → RecordInfo) and `fieldOwnersRef` (field name → owning registry keys) —
-- are the constructor namespace's other half; a record literal / record pattern /
-- `.field` access never reads the constructor scheme env, so
-- `applyCtorScopeOverrides` cannot reach them. Only `recordByNameRef` is fixed here: an
-- identity-keyed COMPANION plus a per-module SCOPE DECISION for the collided keys.
-- `fieldOwnersRef` stays a graph-global multimap, open on #1070 / #1319 — its value (the
-- candidate owner set) needs a REACHABILITY predicate (can a value of this record type
-- be obtained here at all, including transitively), not a constructor-witness test; a
-- prior attempt at the witness-predicate shape was reverted for producing accept→reject
-- regressions on legitimate value-only imports, a quadratic memory cost, and
-- non-monotonic ambiguity decisions — do not re-attempt that shape here.
--
-- The witness half is deliberately NOT re-implemented here: `declaresCtorNamed` and
-- `anyUsePathBindsCtor` are SHARED with unit 1, because a record's name IS its
-- constructor and a named-field variant is keyed by its constructor; only the candidate
-- ROW type differs (RecordInfo instead of Scheme), so only the two projections below are
-- new. It must not re-decide ambiguity, for the same reason as unit 1: two witnesses
-- decline to the floor rather than picking one, so a genuinely ambiguous import stays
-- resolve's to reject. Scaffolding with a named deleter, same as unit 1: this is a
-- further implementation of a fact `resolve.mdk` derives; #1288 owns the consolidation.
--
-- A DECL-level scope decision is the right instrument and no node carrier is needed:
-- neither an interface-default specialization's copied body nor another module's impl
-- body re-resolves a record occurrence in the importer's own record scope, so the
-- occurrence is decided once, at the declaration, not per node. This is falsifiable by a
-- future change: a driver that hands `desugar` a concatenation of modules would reopen
-- it.

-- ── WS-5: phantom interface method detection ──────────────────────────────
-- A method whose declared type mentions NONE of the interface's type parameters
-- (neither in argument position nor in the result) cannot be dispatched: there
-- is no argument or return type to select an impl from.  Reject at check time
-- so the silent mis-dispatch at runtime is caught early.
--
-- Examples:
--   interface Phantom a where
--     name : String          -- PHANTOM: `a` appears nowhere in the type
--   interface Show a where
--     show : a -> String     -- OK: `a` appears in argument position
--   interface Pure f where
--     pure : a -> f a        -- OK: `f` appears in result position
--
-- The check uses the full method type (args AND result via tyVarNames), so
-- return-position methods like `pure : a -> f a` or `minBound : a` are NOT
-- flagged.  Multi-param interfaces: phantom iff ALL params absent.

-- #1557 A-3.5c: relocated onto stage K's `CE`.  The row set is
-- `ceRowsOwnedBy` — the READING module's OWN interfaces, which is exactly the
-- decl list this check was handed before (`prog` on the Module arm, the
-- driver-staged USER decls on Flat), NOT the visible prefix: an imported
-- interface's phantom method is reported once, at the module that declares it,
-- not once per importer.  See `ceRowsVisibleAt`/`ceRowsOwnedBy` for why the two
-- populations are kept apart.
--
-- Reading `CE` rather than re-destructuring `DInterface` also drops the
-- `DAttrib` unwrapping this check used to open with: `classEnvDeclFact` already
-- peels it, so an attributed interface reaches `CE` as a row like any other.
checkPhantomMethods : ModuleCtx -> ClassEnv -> Int -> Unit
checkPhantomMethods mctx ce cur =
  foreachUnit
    ((loc, msg) => pushTypeError (mctxAtIfSome loc mctx) "T-PHANTOM-METHOD" msg)
    (flatMap phantomMethodMsgs (ceRowsOwnedBy cur ce))

-- Each message with the span of the method's declared type it is about, or of
-- the interface's name when that type carries none (a default with no signature).
phantomMethodMsgs : CeRow -> List (Option Loc, String)
phantomMethodMsgs r =
  map
    (m => (orElseLoc (fst m) (ceRowLoc r), snd m))
    (flatMap
      (phantomMethodMsg (ceRowIfaceName r) (ceRowTyparams r))
      (ceRowMethods r))

phantomMethodMsg : String ->
  List String ->
  (String, Ty, List (String, List Kind)) ->
  List (Option Loc, String)
phantomMethodMsg ifaceName typarams (mname, mty, _) =
  if isEmptyL typarams then
    []
  else if anyMember (tyVarNames mty) typarams then
    []
  else
    let noun = if listLen typarams == 1 then "parameter" else "parameters"
    [
      (
        firstTyLoc mty,
        "method `\{mname}` of interface `\{ifaceName}` does not mention the interface \{noun} \{joinWith ", " (map (t => "'" ++ backticked t ++ "'") typarams)}, so it cannot be dispatched",
      ),
    ]

-- ── WS-4a: cyclic superinterface detection ────────────────────────────────
-- A cyclic `interface A requires B; interface B requires A` is ill-formed: no
-- impl can ever be constructed (each demands the other) and the transitive
-- evidence resolver would diverge.  DFS over the `requires` graph; if any node
-- is re-encountered on the current DFS stack, report the cycle.
-- Runs over ALL interfaces in scope (prelude + user) — a prelude cycle would
-- be equally ill-formed.  The `done` ref tracks fully-explored nodes to avoid
-- redundant traversal and re-reporting multi-root cycles.
-- 🚨 #1557 A-3.5c: relocated onto stage K's `CE`, AND RE-KEYED — this is the
-- unit's #1258-class acceptance delta, the one the owner ruling of 2026-08-12
-- accepts by name (*"re-keying a bare-name table does not create wrongness, it
-- creates VISIBILITY"*).
--
-- WAS: `collectIfaceNames allDecls` for the roots and `ifaceSupersOf allDecls
-- <name>` for every edge — BOTH bare-name scans of a decl list, so a superinterface
-- edge resolved to whichever same-spelled interface appeared FIRST in
-- the concatenation of every module's decls.  Two unrelated modules each declaring `Same` collapsed
-- into one node: `mod_a.Same requires mod_b.Same` could be reported as a self-cycle it
-- is not, and a genuine cycle could be masked by the other module's row winning the
-- scan.  Import order selected the symptom, exactly as it did for `#1257`'s kind rows.
--
-- NOW: nodes are `CeRow`s and an edge is followed by IDENTITY —
-- `ceLookupAt (regKeyOfTab (ifaceTabKey superOrigin superHead))`.  `Super` has carried
-- `superOrigin` since #1110 Stage A-1 and `resolve.mdk` stamps it through the SAME
-- `mapSuperOcc`/`tyOriginScope` walk that stamps a `DImpl`'s `implOrigin`, so the
-- occurrence and the `DInterface`'s `ifaceOrigin` declaration layer meet for the same
-- reason `ifaceTabKey`'s header argues for the impl-head key.  The `done` set and the
-- DFS `path` are keyed on `regKeyRender` rather than the bare name for the identical
-- reason.
--
-- ⚠️ THE MISS ARM IS AN ABSTENTION, AND IT IS THE ONE PLACE THIS COULD GO
-- LOUD→SILENT.  An edge whose target is not in `CE` at this ordinal yields `None` and
-- the walk stops — the same disposition `ifaceSupersOf`'s `None` arm already had
-- ("unknown interface, reported elsewhere"), and resolve rejects an interface naming
-- an unknown superinterface before typecheck runs.  What is NEW is that a super whose
-- identity failed to resolve would now MISS where a bare name used to hit.  That is
-- why the abstention arm needs a POSITIVE control -- a shape whose edge MUST still be
-- followed -- rather than only a negative one.
--
-- Cite fixtures that exist, and check what actually consumes them.  The gate
-- for this arm is `test/diff_compiler_fmt_test.mdk`'s `typecheckErrorFailures`,
-- which walks its fixture directory RECURSIVELY via `fixtureFiles` -- so a
-- directory-nested fixture IS discovered and consumed.  No gate catches a wrong
-- citation here: `make docs-links` and `make agent-doc-symbols` do not scan
-- compiler comments.  It matters more than a typo because this is the one
-- sentence answering "is the abstention arm covered?", and a citation like
-- that gets relayed into the next unit's design as an established fact.  The
-- real controls, both verified to reject on this binary:
--   * MULTI-MODULE: `test/analyze_project_fixtures/1557_a35c_cycle_masked_by_samespelled/`
--     (consumed by `test/diff_compiler_fmt_test.mdk`'s `analyzeProjectFixtureFailures`)
--     -- its edge must resolve BY IDENTITY for the fixture to pass at all, so
--     an abstention that swallowed a real edge reds it.
--   * FLAT: `test/dict_fixtures/s3-w1-cyclic-superinterface-rejected.mdk` (no imports)
--     and `test/typecheck_error_fixtures/cyclic_superinterface.mdk`.
-- The negative direction -- an edge that must NOT be followed -- is
-- `1557_a35c_samespelled_iface_bystander/`.  The set is the assertion; no member is.
--
-- ROOTS are `ceRowsVisibleAt` — the reading module's whole ordinal prefix: {prelude} ∪
-- {every earlier module in full} ∪ {this module}, members and order.  `accAll` is
-- seeded with the WHOLE `coreDecls` and grown `accAll ++ prog` (not `publicDataDecls
-- prog`; only `accData` is public-filtered) and every Module-arm driver runs
-- `AccumulateBoth`, so the prefix is the full set.  `CE` at this ordinal is that set in
-- ordinal order.
--
-- ⚠️ AN EARLIER CUT OF THIS COMMENT CLAIMED A DELIBERATE WIDENING HERE — *"`accAll`/
-- `accData` carry only `publicDataDecls`, so a PRIVATE interface of an earlier module
-- was never a root"* — and it was simply WRONG about `accAll`, so the widening it
-- conceded does not exist.  Measured on two binaries rather than argued: a module
-- declaring a PRIVATE cyclic interface pair has that cycle reported in a sibling
-- module with NO import path to it, on the pre-relocation arm too, byte-identical.
-- Do not reinstate the hedge; the relocation is root-set-preserving.
checkInterfaceCycles : ModuleCtx -> List Decl -> ClassEnv -> Int -> Unit
checkInterfaceCycles mctx prog ce cur =
  -- #973: `done` is an OrdMap-backed SET (omHasKey/omInsert), NOT a growing `List` scanned
  -- by `contains`.  The membership test ran once per interface over the fully-explored
  -- set, which grows to the interface count → O(interfaces^2), the flat-path
  -- `manyifaces:typecheck` op-count quadratic (independent of use sites — it surfaces on a
  -- file of N cycle-free interfaces).  Keyed into a set it is O(log n): `done` only prunes
  -- already-explored nodes (set membership is order-insensitive), and the DFS order +
  -- cycle messages are driven by `path`/the root list.  A-3.5c keeps the shape and only
  -- changes the KEY from a bare name to `regKeyRender`.
  let done = Ref omEmpty
  foreachUnit
    (checkOneIfaceCycle mctx prog ce cur done)
    (ceRowsVisibleAt cur ce)

-- #152: the whole-program final-checks tail, shared by all five entry points
-- (the `checkOne*` projections and `checkModuleFullDiags`). [cohDecls] feeds coherence and
-- checkSuperImpls's impl-iteration argument.
-- ⚠️ trap #5: coherence must see USER decls only, so
-- this helper has NO access to `prog` — the caller decides [cohDecls] explicitly
-- (never a `prog` fallback).  Call ORDER is load-bearing (all push into typeErrors).
--
-- #1557 A-3.5c: two of the four members now read stage K's `CE` instead of a decl
-- list.  [ownCe]/[cycCe] are the class environments the caller is entitled to read
-- and [cur] is the READING module's ordinal — Module passes the whole-graph
-- `deIfaces` twice with its own ordinal; Flat passes two single-module envs built
-- from the very lists it used to hand `checkPhantomMethods`/`checkInterfaceCycles`,
-- at ordinal 0 in the standalone-list compatibility helper; reading a graph envelope there
-- would switch both checks silently OFF.
--
-- ⚠️ CALL ORDER IS UNCHANGED AND THAT IS DELIBERATE.  A-3.5c moves two members'
-- SOURCE, not their position: coherence still runs first, then cycles, then phantom,
-- then super-impls, so no diagnostic changes rank against another family.  Whichever
-- unit lands A-3.5a/A-3.5b inherits this constraint — pulling a member OUT of this
-- sequence re-orders every accumulated diagnostic after it.
-- #1557 A-3.5b: the super-impl check reads stage K, taking [cycCe] and [cycIe] at the
-- same ordinal.  Both envs must be built over the same population: the whole-graph
-- `deImpls` with the reader's own ordinal on the Module arm, `flatImplEnvOf` of the
-- one list the Flat callers hand `cycCe`'s peer.
-- #1559 A-3.7: coherence reads stage K too, so this helper carries TWO `IE`s for
-- the same reason A-3.5c gave it two `CE`s — [cohIe] is the env over the population
-- [cohDecls] names (the USER boundary, trap #5) and [cycIe] is built over the
-- whole-graph population.  They are the same env only on the paths where those two
-- populations were already the same.  [cohIe] must contain the prelude at
-- ordinal 0, since coherence pairs the module's own rows with the prelude's.
--
-- 🚨 SA-6 (sprint repair round): THE `-1` SENTINEL IS FAIL-CLOSED HERE, AND IT HAS TO BE
-- ANNOUNCED AT THIS READER.  [cur] is `declEnvsOrdOf mid` on the Module arm, whose miss
-- value is `0 - 1` (see that function: a miss is documented fail-CLOSED, and it says in
-- so many words that the remedy for a stray id is at the READER — "abstain loudly / fail
-- the pass" — never a sentinel that means "everything").  All four members below take
-- [cur], and at `-1` they abstain in OPPOSITE directions: `checkCoherence` takes
-- `cohRowsOwnedBy -1` → no rows → **it checks nothing, silently**, where pre-A-3.7 it
-- walked the decl list unconditionally; `checkInterfaceCycles`/`checkPhantomMethods` take
-- `ceRowsVisibleAt -1`/`ceRowsOwnedBy -1` → likewise nothing; and `checkSuperImpls`,
-- whose row read SA-3 just widened to `ieCandidacyVisibleAt`, still finds no SUPERS
-- (`ceLookupAt … -1`) and so also reports nothing.  So the whole tail degrades to a
-- SILENT ACCEPT — a loud→silent transition, which this repo ranks as a severity increase
-- even while unreachable.
-- ⚠️ UNREACHABLE TODAY, AND THE GUARD IS STILL RIGHT.  The three drivers pass either a
-- literal `0` (both Flat entries) or `declEnvsOrdOf mid` over the very list
-- `buildDeclEnvs` indexed, so no live path can arrive at `-1`; a fourth Module-mode
-- driver, or any path stamping a mid `buildDeclEnvs` did not index, makes it live.  It
-- cannot fire spuriously, because `cur < 0` is exactly and only the miss sentinel and no
-- caller can construct a negative ordinal otherwise.
-- 🎯 WHAT THIS DOES *NOT* COVER, stated because it is the near miss: a driver that
-- threads a VALID-but-WRONG ordinal (some other module's) is undetectable here — the
-- sentinel is the only self-identifying failure — and `globalCoherenceConflict` takes no
-- ordinal at all (`cohRowsOf`, whole graph), so it is outside this guard entirely.
runFinalChecks : ModuleCtx ->
  List Decl ->
  ClassEnv ->
  ClassEnv ->
  ImplEnv ->
  ImplEnv ->
  Int ->
  Unit
runFinalChecks mctx cohDecls ownCe cycCe cohIe cycIe cur =
  ordinalSentinelGuard mctx cur
  checkCoherence mctx cohIe cur
  checkInterfaceCycles mctx cohDecls cycCe cur
  checkPhantomMethods mctx ownCe cur
  checkSuperImpls mctx cohDecls cycCe cycIe cur

-- SA-6's guard, split out so the arm is a GUARD and not a `whenL`.  ⚠️ Medaka is strict:
-- `whenL (cur < 0) (pushTypeError …)` would evaluate the push on EVERY call — the
-- documented not-a-stub trap.  A guarded function does not.
ordinalSentinelGuard : ModuleCtx -> Int -> Unit
ordinalSentinelGuard mctx cur
  | ordinalIsSentinel cur =
    pushTypeError mctx "T-INTERNAL-ORDINAL" ordinalSentinelMsg
  | otherwise = ()

-- is [cur] `declEnvsOrdOf`'s miss sentinel?  A real ordinal is an index into the list
-- `buildDeclEnvs` was handed, so it is >= 0 by construction; `0 - 1` is the only negative
-- value any producer in this file yields.
-- > ordinalIsSentinel (0 - 1)
-- True
-- > ordinalIsSentinel 0
-- False
-- > ordinalIsSentinel 3
-- False
ordinalIsSentinel : Int -> Bool
ordinalIsSentinel cur = cur < 0

checkOneIfaceCycle : ModuleCtx ->
  List Decl ->
  ClassEnv ->
  Int ->
  Ref (OrdMap Unit) ->
  CeRow ->
  Unit
checkOneIfaceCycle mctx prog ce cur done row =
  if not (omHasKey (ceRowDoneKey row) !done) then
    foreachUnit
      (pushTypeError
        (mctxAt
          (cycleReportLoc mctx.mcGraph.declEnvsRef.value.deReach prog cur row)
          mctx)
        "T-CYCLIC-SUPERINTERFACE")
      (ifaceDfsCycle ce cur done [row] row)

-- A cycle is reported at the name of the interface its walk started from when
-- the reading module [cur] declares it.  A module that only sees it reports it
-- at its import of the declaring module, or else at its first import of a
-- module that reaches the declaring one ([reach], each module's import
-- closure): the interface's span is in another file.  A module with no import
-- path to it reports it with no span.
cycleReportLoc : OrdMap (OrdMap Unit) -> List Decl -> Int -> CeRow -> Option Loc
cycleReportLoc reach prog cur row
  | ceRowOrd row == cur = ceRowLoc row
  | otherwise = match (ceRowIface row).irOrigin
    OriginModule owner => importLocFor reach prog owner
    _ => None

-- DFS from [current]; [path] is the stack of ROWS visited so far (including
-- [current] as its last element, used to reconstruct the cycle message).
-- Marks [current] as done after all its supers are explored.
ifaceDfsCycle : ClassEnv ->
  Int ->
  Ref (OrdMap Unit) ->
  List CeRow ->
  CeRow ->
  List String
ifaceDfsCycle ce cur done path current =
  let msgs = ifaceDfsCycleSupers ce cur done path (ceRowSupers current)
  done := omInsert (ceRowDoneKey current) () !done
  msgs

ifaceDfsCycleSupers : ClassEnv ->
  Int ->
  Ref (OrdMap Unit) ->
  List CeRow ->
  List Super ->
  List String
ifaceDfsCycleSupers _ _ _ _ [] = []
ifaceDfsCycleSupers ce cur done path ((Super { superHead = superName, superOrigin = so }) :: rest) =
  let msgs1 = ifaceDfsCycleOneSuper ce cur done path so superName
  msgs1 ++ ifaceDfsCycleSupers ce cur done path rest

-- check one super edge: cycle if the super's IDENTITY is on the DFS path; skip if
-- done; else recurse into the row that identity names.  A super naming no visible
-- interface abstains (see the miss-arm note at `checkInterfaceCycles`).
ifaceDfsCycleOneSuper : ClassEnv ->
  Int ->
  Ref (OrdMap Unit) ->
  List CeRow ->
  TyConOrigin ->
  String ->
  List String
ifaceDfsCycleOneSuper ce cur done path so superName =
  let key = regKeyOfTab (ifaceTabKey so superName)
  let rendered = regKeyRender key
  if containsRowKey rendered path then
    [cyclicSuperIfaceMsg (map ceRowIfaceName path ++ [superName])]
  else if omHasKey rendered !done then
    []
  else match ceLookupAt key cur ce
    None => []
    Some r => ifaceDfsCycle ce cur done (path ++ [r]) r

containsRowKey : String -> List CeRow -> Bool
containsRowKey _ [] = False
containsRowKey k (r :: rest)
  | ceRowDoneKey r == k = True
  | otherwise = containsRowKey k rest

-- map each super-param NAME through [subst] to its Ty, dropping any unmapped (so a
-- short result vs [params] signals an incomplete substitution → caller skips).
substParams : List String -> List (String, Ty) -> List Ty
substParams [] _ = []
substParams (p :: rest) subst = match lookupAssoc p subst
  Some t => t :: substParams rest subst
  None => substParams rest subst

-- does an `impl superName <head>` covering [goal] exist among [rows]?  [rows] are
-- `IE`'s rows, bound once by `checkSuperImpls`; [superKey] is the super's identity and
-- [superName] its bare spelling.
--
-- It compares the identity leg, never the buckets.  `ieInsertRow` indexes every row
-- under `oblIfaceKeys`, which mints two keys: the identity key and a bare-spelling
-- compatibility leg that #1438 still rides on.  Looking [superKey] up in
-- `ieConcrete`/`ieHeadless` would therefore answer with both same-spelled interfaces'
-- rows.  Reading `ieRows` and testing each row's own `IfaceRef` cannot reach the bare
-- bucket.
superImplExists : List ImplRow -> TabKey -> String -> List Ty -> Bool
superImplExists rows superKey superName goal =
  anyList (implRowMatchesSuper superKey superName goal) rows

-- Name first, then identity: `ifaceTabKey` allocates (it goes through `mkIdent`), and
-- this runs once per row per (impl x super) in a GC-bound stage.  Bare-name equality
-- is a necessary condition for key equality (`tabKeyOf` puts the same name into both
-- the `TkIdent` and the `TkBare` arm), so gating on it is sound; the identity compare
-- decides.
implRowMatchesSuper : TabKey -> String -> List Ty -> ImplRow -> Bool
implRowMatchesSuper superKey superName goal (ImplRow _ _ ir tys _ _ _) =
  ir.irName == superName
    && listLen tys == listLen goal
    && ifaceTabKey ir.irOrigin ir.irName == superKey
    && superHeadCovers tys goal

-- Whether the impl head [pats] covers the super goal [goal], which is the checked
-- impl's own head with its variables rigid: one substitution for the whole vector
-- (`matchOneSided`, as the min⊑ selector's `tySubsumesV` and the use site's
-- `implHeadSubst` match), so a variable [pats] repeats must bind equal types, and a
-- variable of [goal] matches only a variable of [pats].  `impl D (Pair a a)` does not
-- cover `D (Pair a b)` or `D (Pair Int Bool)`.  Effect rows are transparent on both
-- sides.  Type constructors compare by identity (`tyStep`), as at the use site.
superHeadCovers : List Ty -> List Ty -> Bool
superHeadCovers pats goal =
  isSome (matchOneSided superHeadStep eqStr tyStructEq (zipL pats goal) [])

superHeadStep : Ty -> Ty -> MStep String Ty Ty
superHeadStep pat t = tyStep pat (stripTyWrap t)

-- ── D3 / WS-2 part-2: GLOBAL (cross-module) coherence ──────────────────────
-- Per-module coherence accepts two DIFFERENT modules that
-- each define `impl C T` for the SAME instance — each module is locally coherent,
-- but jointly they are incoherent (silent dispatch ambiguity).  This pass scans
-- the joint impl set over ALL USER modules (the prelude is paired by the per-module
-- sweep, which reports with the impl's own span).
-- Each CohImpl carries the id of the module that PHYSICALLY declares it; imports do
-- NOT copy impl decls, so the joint set has exactly one entry per definition and a
-- structural (iface, head-tys) overlap already distinguishes distinct definitions —
-- no occurrence-dedup needed.  A conflict between two distinct modules is reported
-- naming BOTH (cohCrossModuleMsg via cohHardMsg's cross-module branch, or the
-- `(defined in …)` suffix `cohWhereSuffix` adds to the F-3d soft warning).
-- The joint impl set is `cohRowsOf` over the whole-graph `IE`, which leaves out the
-- prelude's rows, and the one-entry-per-definition property is `ieRows`' by
-- construction (imports copy no rows either).
--
-- the first cross-module coherence conflict of EACH CLASS (if any) as bare messages
-- — `(hard, soft)`, the same split `checkCoherence` reports, so the cross-module path
-- demotes the ⊑-incomparable class exactly as the per-module one does (F-3d).
-- Callers that thread errs as a VALUE (`checkModulesEntryFromDiags`) prepend these
-- themselves,
-- rather than relying on the typeErrors ref (cleared per-module by `freshModuleCtx`).
--
-- ⚠️ #414: this deliberately DROPS the blame-span `cohScan` returns.
-- Both consumers attach the diagnostic to the ENTRY module, but the span belongs to
-- whichever module declares the offending impl — and the `--json`/human renderers
-- key a diagnostic's file by the GROUP it is filed under, NOT by the filename
-- inside its own `Loc`.  Attaching a foreign span therefore renders a caret at that
-- line/col in the WRONG file.  Measured, with the impl 40 lines into a dependency:
--     ./main.mdk:42:7: Conflicting `impl C`. Defined in amod and bmod
-- — main.mdk is 5 lines long, so the caret block cannot even render.  That is worse
-- than the file-start default: a confidently wrong location beats an obviously
-- fabricated one only at misleading the reader.  The cross-module wording already
-- names BOTH owning modules, which is the locating information that actually helps
-- here.  Attaching a real span needs the renderers to honour `Loc`'s own filename
-- (a driver/diagnostics.mdk change, well beyond an S3 caret fix).
-- #1559 A-3.7: the input is the whole-graph `IE`, prelude carved out, not the driver's
-- per-module decl pairs.
--
-- ORDER IS THE THING THIS BITE COULD MOVE, because `cohScanInner` keeps the FIRST pair
-- per class over a `reverseL`-ed list and the wording names `e1` first.  The two orders
-- agree, term by term: the old list was `flatMap (cohImplsOfMid mid) prog` over the
-- driver's `modules` in dependency-first order; `ieRows` is built by `buildImplEnvGo`
-- over the same modules in ORDINAL order (which is that same order, offset by the
-- prelude at 0) and within a module by `implDeclFacts = flatMap implDeclFact prog`, in
-- decl order.  The one difference is the prelude, which `cohRowsOf` removes
-- BEFORE the `reverseL` below — so the filtered list's head is the first user module,
-- which is exactly what the old list's head was.
globalCoherenceConflict : ModuleCtx -> ImplEnv -> (Option String, Option String)
globalCoherenceConflict mctx env =
  match (cohScan
    CohSweepGlobal
    (reverseL (map (cohImplOfRow mctx) (cohRowsOf env)))
    [])
    CohScan hard soft => (map fst hard, map fst soft)

-- This recursion is aware (constraint-dictionary-routed) and bounded by the shared
-- `requires` measure (`reqWalkEnter`): a mono pinned to a concrete head routes RKey,
-- an in-scope constraint var routes RDict, per DICT-SEMANTICS §3 `assum`.

-- fill each constrained-fn call site's routes: one route per constraint mono.  A
-- mono pinned to a concrete head → RKey; still a constraint variable (a nested
-- constrained call) → RDict; otherwise RNone.
resolveDictApps : SiteCtx -> List PendingDictApp -> Unit
resolveDictApps sx [] = ()
resolveDictApps sx (app :: rest) =
  let sx = { sx | sxSite = app.pdaLoc }
  let routes =
    routesOfMonosTopV
      sx
      app.pdaEncl
      app.pdaScope
      app.pdaMonos
      app.pdaIfaces
      app.pdaArgVecs
  app.pdaRoutesRef := routes
  resolveDictApps sx rest

-- ── dict_pass: prepend dict parameters to constrained function definitions ──
-- For each top-level def of a name in [dictNames], prepend one `$dict_<fn>_<slot>`
-- parameter per constraint (arity from `funPredicateSlotsRef`, populated during
-- inference), matching the dicts EDictAt applies at call sites.  Multi-clause
-- functions are several DFunDef decls; each clause gets the same leading params.
-- #2189: [names] is the dict-passed set, which grows with the program, and this
-- maps over every decl, so a `contains n names` scan inside `dictPassDecl` is
-- O(decls x names).  The set is indexed once here; `dictPassDecl`/`dictPassLetBind`
-- probe it with `omHasKey`.
dictPass : ModuleCtx ->
  EvIndex ->
  String ->
  List String ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl
dictPass mctx idx mid names prog =
  let pe = PassEvidence idx (Ref omEmpty)
  map
    (dictPassDecl
      mctx
      pe
      (omFromNames names omEmpty)
      (returnPosMethodNames prog))
    (mapProg
      (e => rewriteLocalDictExpr mctx.mcGraph (rewriteBinopExpr mctx pe e))
      (grantPass mctx.mcGraph pe mid prog))

passIndex : PassEvidence -> EvIndex
passIndex (PassEvidence idx _) = idx

-- The entry published for method occurrence [ev].  A miss in both is the index's
-- miss.
passMethodOf : PassEvidence -> EvId -> PassMethod
passMethodOf (PassEvidence idx minted) ev =
  match evidenceLookup (Some idx) "method occurrence" ev
    Ok v => passMethodFacts v
    Err message => match omLookup (intToString (evOrdinal ev)) minted.value
      Some v => passMethodFacts v
      None => panic message

passMethodFacts : EvVal -> PassMethod
passMethodFacts (EvMethod iface _ tag impls meths) =
  PassMethod iface tag (impls ++ meths)
passMethodFacts _ =
  panic "evidence table: a method occurrence answered by another kind of entry"

-- ── grant passing: the authority analogue of the dictionary pass ─────────────
-- Runs before the dictionary rewrites of module [mid], so a binder's authority
-- parameters land after the dictionary parameters those rewrites prepend, and
-- each recorded use is applied to its grants while it still carries its id.
grantPass : GraphCtx -> PassEvidence -> String -> List Decl -> List Decl
grantPass gctx pe mid prog =
  let st = gctx.graphRun.grants
  let saved = st.gsPassingModule.value
  st.gsPassingModule := mid
  let result = map (grantDecl gctx pe mid) prog
  st.gsPassingModule := saved
  result

grantDecl : GraphCtx -> PassEvidence -> String -> Decl -> Decl
grantDecl gctx pe mid (DFunDef pub n pats body site bid) =
  DFunDef
    pub
    n
    (grantParamPats (topGrantIds gctx mid n) n ++ pats)
    (grantBody gctx pe body)
    site
    bid
grantDecl gctx pe mid (DLetGroup pub binds) =
  DLetGroup
    pub
    (map
      (b => match b
        LetBind n clauses site bid =>
          grantLetBind
            gctx
            pe
            (grantParamPats (topGrantIds gctx mid n) n)
            (LetBind n clauses site bid))
      binds)
grantDecl gctx pe _ (d@(DInterface { name, ifaceOrigin, methods, ... })) = DInterface { d |
  methods =
    map (grantIfaceMethod gctx pe (ifaceWordOf ifaceOrigin name)) methods,
}
grantDecl gctx pe _ (d@(DImpl { iface, implOrigin, methods, ... })) = DImpl { d |
  methods = map (grantImplMethod gctx pe (ifaceWordOf implOrigin iface)) methods,
}
grantDecl gctx pe _ (DProp pub name params body) =
  DProp pub name params (grantExpr gctx pe body)
grantDecl gctx pe _ (DTest pub name body) =
  DTest pub name (grantExpr gctx pe body)
grantDecl gctx pe mid (DAttrib attrs d) =
  DAttrib attrs (grantDecl gctx pe mid d)
-- a declaration with no expression body (data, signatures, imports, externs)
grantDecl gctx _ _ d = d

-- A method that takes grants declares them after its value arguments, so the
-- arity every backend reads off the declaration counts them.
grantIfaceMethod : GraphCtx ->
  PassEvidence ->
  String ->
  IfaceMethod ->
  IfaceMethod
grantIfaceMethod gctx pe word (IfaceMethod n ty def mloc) =
  match methodGrantOf gctx word n
    None =>
      IfaceMethod
        n
        ty
        (map
          (d => match d
            MethodDefault ps e => MethodDefault ps (grantBody gctx pe e))
          def)
        mloc
    Some mg =>
      IfaceMethod
        n
        (insertGrantArrows mg.mgArity (listLen mg.mgNames) ty)
        (map
          (d => match d
            MethodDefault ps e =>
              let (ps2, e2) =
                grantMethodParams gctx mg n ps (grantBody gctx pe e)
              MethodDefault ps2 e2)
          def)
        mloc

grantImplMethod : GraphCtx -> PassEvidence -> String -> ImplMethod -> ImplMethod
grantImplMethod gctx pe word (ImplMethod n ps e) =
  match methodGrantOf gctx word n
    None => ImplMethod n ps (grantBody gctx pe e)
    Some mg =>
      let (ps2, e2) = grantMethodParams gctx mg n ps (grantBody gctx pe e)
      ImplMethod n ps2 e2

-- A method clause's grant parameters, after its value parameters; a clause
-- written with fewer parameters than the method's arity takes the missing ones
-- first and applies its body to them.
grantMethodParams : GraphCtx ->
  MethodGrant ->
  String ->
  List Pat ->
  Expr ->
  (List Pat, Expr)
grantMethodParams gctx mg n ps body =
  let grants = grantParamPats mg.mgNames n
  let given = listLen ps
  if given >= mg.mgArity then
    (take mg.mgArity ps ++ grants ++ drop mg.mgArity ps, body)
  else
    let missing =
      map (_ => freshGrantName gctx.graphRun.grants ()) (range given mg.mgArity)
    (
      ps ++ map (x => PVar x (Loc "" 0 0 0 0) noBinderId) missing ++ grants,
      applyExprs body (map EVar missing),
    )

-- [g] `List String` arguments after the first [k] arrows of a method's type.
insertGrantArrows : Int -> Int -> Ty -> Ty
insertGrantArrows k g (TyConstrained cs t) =
  TyConstrained cs (insertGrantArrows k g t)
insertGrantArrows k g (TyEffect effs tails t)
  | k > 0 = TyEffect effs tails (insertGrantArrows k g t)
insertGrantArrows k g (TyFun a b)
  | k > 0 = TyFun a (insertGrantArrows (k - 1) g b)
insertGrantArrows _ g t = grantArrows g t

grantArrows : Int -> Ty -> Ty
grantArrows g t
  | g <= 0 = t
  | otherwise =
    TyFun
      (TyApp (tyConBuiltin "List" None) (tyConBuiltin "String" None))
      (grantArrows (g - 1) t)

grantLetBind : GraphCtx -> PassEvidence -> List Pat -> LetBind -> LetBind
grantLetBind gctx pe params (LetBind n clauses site bid) =
  LetBind
    n
    (map
      (c => match c
        FunClause ps body => FunClause (params ++ ps) (grantBody gctx pe body))
      clauses)
    site
    bid

topGrantIds : GraphCtx -> String -> String -> List Int
topGrantIds gctx mid n =
  optionOr [] (omLookup (grantTopKey mid n) gctx.graphRun.grants.gsTopIds.value)

localGrantIds : GraphCtx -> String -> List Int
localGrantIds gctx n =
  optionOr [] (omLookup n gctx.graphRun.grants.gsLocalIds.value)

grantParamName : String -> Int -> String
grantParamName n i = "$auth_\{n}_\{intToString i}"

grantParamPats : List a -> String -> List Pat
grantParamPats ids n =
  map
    (i => PVar (grantParamName n i) (Loc "" 0 0 0 0) noBinderId)
    (range 0 (listLen ids))

-- The top-down walk: a use of a file extern or a method is rebuilt with every
-- argument it takes, so it sees its whole application spine before its
-- arguments do.
grantExpr : GraphCtx -> PassEvidence -> Expr -> Expr
grantExpr gctx pe e =
  let inner = grantExprInner gctx pe e
  let st = gctx.graphRun.grants
  match st.gsValueBounds.value
    Tip => inner
    _ => match fileValueKey st.gsPassingModule.value e
      Some key =>
        let bounds = optionOr [] (omLookup key st.gsValueBounds.value)
        fold
          (result (ty, chain) => fileBoundValue gctx chain ty result)
          inner
          bounds
      None => inner

grantExprInner : GraphCtx -> PassEvidence -> Expr -> Expr
grantExprInner gctx pe (ELam pats body) = ELam pats (grantBody gctx pe body)
grantExprInner gctx pe (e@(EApp _ _)) = match grantSpine e []
  (EDictAt n ev, args) => match grantOccOf gctx ev
    Some occ => match occ.goTrailing
      Some arity =>
        saturateGrants
          gctx.graphRun.grants
          (EVar n)
          arity
          (grantTerms gctx occ)
          (map (grantExpr gctx pe) args)
      None => mapChildren (grantExpr gctx pe) e
    None => mapChildren (grantExpr gctx pe) e
  (EMethodAt n seed ev, args) => match methodGrantUse gctx pe n ev
    MethodGrants arity grants =>
      saturateGrants
        gctx.graphRun.grants
        (EMethodAt n seed ev)
        arity
        grants
        (map (grantExpr gctx pe) args)
    LeadingGrants _ grants =>
      applyExprs
        (applyExprs (EMethodAt n seed ev) grants)
        (map (grantExpr gctx pe) args)
    NoGrants => mapChildren (grantExpr gctx pe) e
  _ => mapChildren (grantExpr gctx pe) e
grantExprInner gctx _ (EDictAt n ev) = grantUse gctx n ev
grantExprInner gctx pe (EMethodAt n seed ev) = match methodGrantUse gctx pe n ev
  MethodGrants arity grants =>
    saturateGrants gctx.graphRun.grants (EMethodAt n seed ev) arity grants []
  LeadingGrants _ grants => applyExprs (EMethodAt n seed ev) grants
  NoGrants => EMethodAt n seed ev
grantExprInner gctx pe (ELet m r (PVar x xloc bid) e1 e2) =
  ELet
    m
    r
    (PVar x xloc bid)
    (grantLocalRhs gctx x (grantExpr gctx pe e1))
    (grantExpr gctx pe e2)
grantExprInner gctx pe (ELetGroup binds body) =
  ELetGroup
    (map
      (b => match b
        LetBind x clauses site bid =>
          grantLetBind
            gctx
            pe
            (grantParamPats (localGrantIds gctx x) x)
            (LetBind x clauses site bid))
      binds)
    (grantExpr gctx pe body)
grantExprInner gctx pe (EBlock stmts) = EBlock (map (grantStmt gctx pe) stmts)
-- every other node: its children, through the one traversal every pass shares
grantExprInner gctx pe e = mapChildren (grantExpr gctx pe) e

grantStmt : GraphCtx -> PassEvidence -> DoStmt -> DoStmt
grantStmt gctx pe (DoLet m r (PVar x xloc bid) e site) =
  DoLet m r (PVar x xloc bid) (grantLocalRhs gctx x (grantExpr gctx pe e)) site
grantStmt gctx pe (DoExpr e) = DoExpr (grantExpr gctx pe e)
grantStmt gctx pe (DoBind p e) = DoBind p (grantExpr gctx pe e)
grantStmt gctx pe (DoLet m r p e site) = DoLet m r p (grantExpr gctx pe e) site
grantStmt gctx pe (DoAssign x e) = DoAssign x (grantExpr gctx pe e)
grantStmt gctx pe (DoFieldAssign x fs e) =
  DoFieldAssign x fs (grantExpr gctx pe e)

-- A local that quantifies authorities takes them ahead of its own parameters.
grantLocalRhs : GraphCtx -> String -> Expr -> Expr
grantLocalRhs gctx x e = match localGrantIds gctx x
  [] => e
  ids =>
    prependLocalDicts (map (i => grantParamName x i) (range 0 (listLen ids))) e

-- An application spine's head and its arguments, through source-location
-- wrappers.
grantSpine : Expr -> List Expr -> (Expr, List Expr)
grantSpine (EApp f x) args = grantSpine f (x :: args)
grantSpine (ELoc _ e) args = grantSpine e args
-- any other node is the head
grantSpine e args = (e, args)

-- A use of a source binding: the head applied to its grants.  A grant-only use
-- of a binding that quantifies nothing is the plain variable it stood for.
grantUse : GraphCtx -> String -> EvId -> Expr
grantUse gctx n ev =
  let head = if isGrantOnlyEv gctx ev then EVar n else EDictAt n ev
  match grantOccOf gctx ev
    None => head
    Some occ => match occ.goTrailing
      Some arity =>
        saturateGrants
          gctx.graphRun.grants
          (EVar n)
          arity
          (grantTerms gctx occ)
          []
      None => applyExprs head (grantTerms gctx occ)

-- A method occurrence's grants.  One that dispatches passes the method's, after
-- the value arity its written type spells; a use that inference did not record
-- (its denotation was settled by a path that instantiates no method scheme) passes
-- the empty authority, so the method's arity still agrees with every body and the
-- use is refused rather than admitted.  One routed to the standalone its name
-- shadows passes that binding's grants, which inference recorded when it typed
-- the occurrence as the standalone; a grant-taking standalone reached without that
-- record has no grants to pass, and is a compile-time failure.  The occurrence's
-- published arity counts the grants, as the backends read it; the published table
-- is read out of the cells after the pass, so that count is written to the
-- occurrence's cell (`setOccurrenceArity`).
methodGrantUse : GraphCtx -> PassEvidence -> String -> EvId -> MethodGrantUse
methodGrantUse gctx pe n ev =
  let (PassMethod iface tag _) = passMethodOf pe ev
  let recorded = grantOccOf gctx ev
  let use = match tag
    RLocal sym _ => match standaloneOcc recorded
      Some (arity, occ) => LeadingGrants arity (grantTerms gctx occ)
      None =>
        if omHasKey
          (if sym == "" then n else sym)
          gctx.graphRun.grants.gsTakers.value then
          panic
            "grant pass: '\{n}' is routed to a standalone binding that takes authority grants, but inference did not type this use as that binding"
        else
          NoGrants
    _ => match methodGrantOf gctx iface n
      None => NoGrants
      Some mg => match recorded
        Some occ =>
          if occ.goStandalone then
            MethodGrants mg.mgArity (map (_ => bottomGrant) mg.mgNames)
          else
            MethodGrants mg.mgArity (methodTerms gctx n mg occ)
        None => MethodGrants mg.mgArity (map (_ => bottomGrant) mg.mgNames)
  match use
    MethodGrants arity grants =>
      setOccurrenceArity gctx pe ev (arity + listLen grants)
    LeadingGrants arity grants =>
      setOccurrenceArity gctx pe ev (arity + listLen grants)
    NoGrants => ()
  use

-- An occurrence in a module the drive served has no cell in this lineage: its
-- entry in the index takes the count (`setServedArity`).
setOccurrenceArity : GraphCtx -> PassEvidence -> EvId -> Int -> Unit
setOccurrenceArity gctx pe ev arity
  | evOrdinal ev < gctx.graphRun.evBase = setServedArity (passIndex pe) ev arity
  | otherwise =
    let cell = methodCellOf gctx ev
    cell.ecArity := Some arity

-- A use recorded as the standalone binding a method occurrence shadows, with its
-- value arity.
standaloneOcc : Option GrantOcc -> Option (Int, GrantOcc)
standaloneOcc (Some occ) = match (occ.goStandalone, occ.goTrailing)
  (True, Some arity) => Some (arity, occ)
  _ => None
standaloneOcc None = None

-- A recorded method use's grants, one per authority the method quantifies.
methodTerms : GraphCtx -> String -> MethodGrant -> GrantOcc -> List Expr
methodTerms gctx n mg occ =
  let terms = grantTerms gctx occ
  if listLen terms == listLen mg.mgNames then
    terms
  else
    panic
      "grant pass: a use of method '\{n}' instantiated \{intToString (listLen terms)} authorities, but the method takes \{intToString (listLen mg.mgNames)} grants"

-- The empty authority: a grant that admits no path.
bottomGrant : Expr
bottomGrant = EListLit [ELit (LString "")]

applyExprs : Expr -> List Expr -> Expr
applyExprs f args = fold (acc a => EApp acc a) f args

-- A head applied to all [arity] value arguments and then its grants.  A partial
-- or value use becomes a function of the arguments still missing; the arguments
-- it was given are bound first, so each is evaluated once, where the program
-- wrote it.
saturateGrants : GrantState -> Expr -> Int -> List Expr -> List Expr -> Expr
saturateGrants st head arity grants args =
  let given = listLen args
  if given >= arity then
    applyExprs (applyExprs head (take arity args ++ grants)) (drop arity args)
  else
    let bound = map (a => (freshGrantName st (), a)) args
    let missing = map (_ => freshGrantName st ()) (range given arity)
    let call =
      applyExprs
        head
        (map (b => EVar (fst b)) bound ++ map EVar missing ++ grants)
    fold
      (body b =>
        ELet
          noDeclLoc
          False
          (PVar (fst b) (Loc "" 0 0 0 0) noBinderId)
          (snd b)
          body)
      (ELam (map (x => PVar x (Loc "" 0 0 0 0) noBinderId) missing) call)
      (reverseL bound)

freshGrantName : GrantState -> Unit -> String
freshGrantName st _ =
  let k = st.gsFresh.value
  st.gsFresh := k + 1
  "$grant_arg_\{intToString k}"

-- Evaluate a function-valued expression once. Its bound becomes active on
-- application, and the returned function (if any) retains its own arrow rows.
fileBoundValue : GraphCtx -> List GrantBinder -> Mono -> Expr -> Expr
fileBoundValue gctx chain ty e =
  if hasFileBoundValue ty then match normalize ty
    TFun _ row result =>
      let fn = freshGrantName gctx.graphRun.grants ()
      let arg = freshGrantName gctx.graphRun.grants ()
      ELet
        noDeclLoc
        False
        (PVar fn (Loc "" 0 0 0 0) noBinderId)
        e
        (ELam
          [PVar arg (Loc "" 0 0 0 0) noBinderId]
          (fileBoundExpr
            gctx
            chain
            row
            (fileBoundValue gctx chain result (EApp (EVar fn) (EVar arg)))))
    TQual inner _ => fileBoundValue gctx chain inner e
    _ => e
  else
    e

grantBody : GraphCtx -> PassEvidence -> Expr -> Expr
grantBody gctx pe body =
  let inner = grantExpr gctx pe body
  match gctx.graphRun.grants.gsBounds.value
    Tip => inner
    boundsBySite =>
      let bounds = match fileBodyLoc body
        Some loc =>
          optionOr
            []
            (omLookup
              (fileBoundSite gctx.graphRun.grants.gsPassingModule.value loc)
              boundsBySite)
        None => []
      fold
        (result (row, chain) => fileBoundExpr gctx chain row result)
        inner
        bounds

fileBoundExpr : GraphCtx -> List GrantBinder -> EffRow -> Expr -> Expr
fileBoundExpr gctx chain row body =
  let (atoms, tails) = rowFlat row
  if isNonEmptyL tails then
    body
  else
    fold
      (result atom =>
        let label = atomLabel atom
        if narrowFileAtom atom then
          applyExprs (EVar ("$with" ++ label ++ "Bound")) [
            grantTerm gctx chain (atomAuth atom),
            ELam [PWild] result,
          ]
        else
          result)
      body
      atoms

-- The grant terms of one use, one per authority the callee quantifies.
grantTerms : GraphCtx -> GrantOcc -> List Expr
grantTerms gctx occ = match occ.goRecIds
  [] => map (grantTerm gctx occ.goChain) occ.goCells
  ids => map (i => grantIdTerm gctx occ.goChain i) ids

-- The whole domain is the empty list, the empty authority a list holding only the
-- empty element (it admits no path), and a set of elements joined with the
-- parameters of enclosing binders is their concatenation.  A variable is the
-- parameter of the innermost enclosing binder that quantifies it.  Two kinds of
-- variable have no caller to supply them, an opened existential and an instance
-- head's index (`markSourceless`), and each is the whole domain: the escape check
-- has held the declaration it reaches to its label's top.  Any other variable
-- whose binder is not found contributes the empty authority, so a lost binder is
-- a refusal at run time rather than an unconfined operation.
grantTerm : GraphCtx -> List GrantBinder -> Authority -> Expr
grantTerm gctx chain a = match authGrantShape a
  GrantTop => EListLit []
  GrantBottom => bottomGrant
  GrantParts elems vars => match grantVarParams gctx chain vars []
    None => EListLit []
    Some params =>
      let parts =
        (if isEmptyL elems then
            []
          else
            [EListLit (map (s => ELit (LString s)) elems)])
          ++ map EVar (dedup params)
      match parts
        [] => bottomGrant
        [p] => p
        p :: rest =>
          fold
            (acc param => topAbsorbs param acc)
            -- Generated after inference: the list identity supplies the operand
            -- representation that a hidden grant parameter alone cannot carry.
            (fold
              (acc q => EBinOp "++" acc q unminted)
              (EListLit [])
              (p :: rest))
            (dedup params)

-- The parameters a join's variables are, or None when one of them has no caller
-- to supply it and so makes the join the whole domain.  A variable whose binder
-- is not found contributes nothing.
grantVarParams : GraphCtx ->
  List GrantBinder ->
  List (Ref Authvar) ->
  List String ->
  Option (List String)
grantVarParams gctx _ [] acc = Some (reverseL acc)
grantVarParams gctx chain (v :: rest) acc =
  match grantParamFor gctx chain (authvarId v)
    Some p => grantVarParams gctx chain rest (p :: acc)
    None =>
      if isSourceless gctx (authvarId v) then
        None
      else
        grantVarParams gctx chain rest acc

-- A parameter holding the whole domain makes a join it is part of the whole
-- domain; concatenation alone would narrow it to the other parts.
topAbsorbs : String -> Expr -> Expr
topAbsorbs param join =
  EMatch (EVar param) [Arm (PList []) [] (EListLit []), Arm PWild [] join]

-- A recursive use forwards its enclosing binder's parameters; one whose binder is
-- not found is the empty authority, as in `grantTerm`.
grantIdTerm : GraphCtx -> List GrantBinder -> Int -> Expr
grantIdTerm gctx chain i = match grantParamFor gctx chain i
  Some p => EVar p
  None => bottomGrant

-- The parameter of the innermost enclosing binder that quantifies authority [i].
grantParamFor : GraphCtx -> List GrantBinder -> Int -> Option String
grantParamFor gctx [] _ = None
grantParamFor gctx (b :: rest) i =
  let (name, ids) = match b
    TopGrantBinder mid n => (n, topGrantIds gctx mid n)
    LocalGrantBinder n => (n, localGrantIds gctx n)
    BodyGrantBinder n bound => (n, bound)
  match elemIndex i ids
    Some k => Some (grantParamName name k)
    None => grantParamFor gctx rest i

-- Routed operators become method applications, including generic arithmetic.
-- Packed instance prerequisites move into EMethodAt's implementation-dictionary
-- routes. RNone and scalar routes preserve primitive operations, so primitive
-- Num method bodies do not recursively call their own dictionary methods.
rewriteBinopExpr : ModuleCtx -> PassEvidence -> Expr -> Expr
rewriteBinopExpr mctx pe (EBinOp op l r ev) =
  match evSiteRouteIn (passIndex pe) ev
    RNone => EBinOp op l r ev
    -- SHARED-FLOAT-RESIDUAL §3(C): an RScalar route is NOT a typeclass dispatch — it
    -- is the scalar-type tag typecheck stamped on a monomorphic binop
    -- (its primitive head on arithmetic, an allowed comparison tag on comparison).
    -- Lowering does not read the
    -- EBinOp's site id, so we carry the scalar type in a NODE by wrapping the binop
    -- in `EAnnot … (TyCon tag)`.  Eval ignores the
    -- annotation (`eval (EAnnot e _) = eval e`) and evaluates the binop dynamically
    -- (Float-correct); lowering reads the annotation to stamp CBinPrim's scalar tag so
    -- the native emitter picks that type's primitive without reading the operands'
    -- structure.  This is the dispatch route READ-OUT the design names, relocated
    -- from the (lost) ref cell to a (surviving) node.
    --
    -- #1110 (was a residual, DRAINED by the stamping PR): `tag` is a SCALAR-TYPE
    -- TAG this pass synthesises (never a head the user wrote), and this runs AFTER
    -- resolve, so nothing downstream would ever stamp it.  It takes the same
    -- treatment as `parser.mdk`'s tuple head — the reserved BUILTIN origin, not the
    -- module under elaboration, which resolve does not know and this pass would be
    -- inventing.  Its only reader is `ir/core_ir_lower.mdk`'s
    -- `lower (EAnnot (EBinOp …) (TyCon { tyConName }))`, which takes the NAME and
    -- nothing else, so the origin is unobserved either way — but `OriginBuiltin` is
    -- the TRUE identity of a scalar tag, and leaving `OriginUnresolved` on a
    -- post-resolve node would keep the §8 I6.3 sentinel alive for no reason.
    RScalar tag => EAnnot (EBinOp op l r ev) (tyConBuiltin tag None)
    route => binopMethodApp mctx pe op l r route
-- PLAN.md #11: re-tag a source integer literal to its inferred runtime rep, a 3-way
-- decision.  setNumlitFloats already
-- decided: float cell `Some f` ⇒ concrete Float ⇒ `ELit (LFloat f)`; otherwise the
-- route cell [dref] distinguishes concrete-Int (RNone, cleared) from a surviving
-- polymorphic `Num a` (a non-RNone RDictFwd/RKey route, the soundness case) — the
-- latter dispatches through the runtime Num dict via `fromInt n` (the SAME dict the
-- enclosing `Num a => …` function threads), closing the hole where `inc x = x + 1`
-- instantiated at Float crashed `VFloat + VInt`.  A selected Num impl's prerequisite
-- routes are packed in [dref] and split onto the EMethodAt impl-dict carrier here.
-- Done in the same mapProg walk that rewrites binops, so
-- eval/lower never see ENumLit and eval_arith / the emitter get matching tags.
rewriteBinopExpr mctx pe (ENumLit n ev _) = match evSiteLitIn (passIndex pe) ev
  (Some f, _) => ELit (LFloat f)
  (None, dref) => match dref
    RNone => ELit (LInt n)
    route if fixedWidthLiteralFits route n => ELit (LInt n)
    route if u64LiteralFits route n =>
      ELit (LU64 (n / 4294967296) (n % 4294967296))
    RKey word _ _ if isI64Head (literalRouteHead word) =>
      let halves = int64Halves n
      ELit (LI64 (fst halves) (snd halves))
    route =>
      let split = binopRouteSplit route
      EApp
        (EMethodAt
          "fromInt"
          ""
          (mintMethodCellWith
            mctx
            pe
            (builtinMethodIfaceWord mctx.mcGraph "fromInt")
            1
            (fst split)
            (snd split)))
        (ELit (LInt n))
-- Roadmap #18c: rewrite each *stamped* EUnOp (`-` → `negate`) into its Num
-- method application via EMethodAt, exactly like the EBinOp arm above.  A site
-- whose operand is a non-primitive instance or a dictionary carries a dispatch
-- route; Int/Float (RNone or a scalar tag) stay the literal EUnOp the eval builtin handles
-- structurally (no recursion — Int's own `negate` body uses the BINOP `0 - a`, and
-- Float's unary minus has a scalar operand).  `!` never routes (stays RNone).
rewriteBinopExpr mctx pe (EUnOp op e ev) = match evSiteRouteIn (passIndex pe) ev
  RNone => EUnOp op e ev
  -- a primitive operand's scalar tag: the builtin negation, as for an unrouted site
  RScalar _ => EUnOp op e ev
  RKey word _ _ if op == "-"
    && isI32Head (literalRouteHead word)
    && isSome (negatedI32Lit e) => ELit (LInt (optionOr 0 (negatedI32Lit e)))
  route => unopMethodApp mctx pe op e route
-- A wide literal is a `U64` or `I64` constant (`checkWideLiterals` has refused it
-- at any other type, so a program that reaches eval/emit only has it at those).
-- At `I64` the halves are the pattern of the magnitude; a `-` around it is the
-- wrapping negation that makes `-2^63` `minBound`.
rewriteBinopExpr mctx pe (EWideLit hi lo ev _) =
  match evSiteRouteIn (passIndex pe) ev
    RKey word _ _ if isI64Head (literalRouteHead word) => ELit (LI64 hi lo)
    _ => ELit (LU64 hi lo)
rewriteBinopExpr mctx _ e = e

-- `-N` at `I32` is the constant `-N`: `-2147483648` is the one literal whose
-- magnitude alone does not fit, so negating `fromInt 2147483648` would panic
-- where the literal range check (which reads the negated value) accepted it.  The
-- operand is the literal already rewritten below it: a word, or the `fromInt`
-- call an out-of-range magnitude keeps.
negatedI32Lit : Expr -> Option Int
negatedI32Lit (ELoc _ e) = negatedI32Lit e
negatedI32Lit (ELit (LInt n)) = negatedInI32 n
negatedI32Lit (EApp (EMethodAt "fromInt" _ _) (ELit (LInt n))) = negatedInI32 n
-- Every other operand is ordinary negation, which `Num I32` wraps.
negatedI32Lit _ = None

-- The range is tested on `n` before it is negated, so no `Int` negation traps.
negatedInI32 : Int -> Option Int
negatedInI32 n =
  if n >= -2147483647 && n <= 2147483648 then Some (0 - n) else None

-- A literal routed to `U64`'s `fromInt` is a `U64` constant when it is not negative;
-- a negative one keeps its `fromInt` call, which panics, exactly as
-- `fixedWidthLiteralFits` leaves an out-of-range tagged literal.
u64LiteralFits : Route -> Int -> Bool
u64LiteralFits (RKey word _ _) n = isU64Head (literalRouteHead word) && n >= 0
u64LiteralFits _ _ = False

-- A literal routed to a fixed-width head's `fromInt` is that head's word already
-- when it is in range (the heads share Int's tagged word), so it needs no call.  The
-- range is checked HERE, on the value, not assumed from the module check: an
-- out-of-range literal keeps its `fromInt` call, which panics rather than storing it.
fixedWidthLiteralFits : Route -> Int -> Bool
fixedWidthLiteralFits (RKey word _ _) n =
  let head = literalRouteHead word
  match taggedFixedRange head
    Some (lo, hi) => n >= lo && n <= hi
    None => False
fixedWidthLiteralFits _ _ = False

-- The head type a literal's `fromInt` dictionary word names: the type field of the
-- instance's canonical key (`Num|I64|`).  The readers above test it only against the
-- builtin fixed-width heads, whose type field is the head's own name.
literalRouteHead : String -> String
literalRouteHead word = match splitOnChar '|' word
  _ :: ty :: _ => ty
  _ => word

-- split the stamped RKey route into a bare-tag route (reqs dropped) + the element
-- dict routes, so the dicts ride on the EMethodAt impl-dict ref (where emitMethod /
-- eval read leading dict words) rather than the route reqs (which the RKey call
-- path ignores).  A non-RKey / empty-reqs route forwards no dicts.
binopRouteSplit : Route -> (Route, List Route)
binopRouteSplit (RKey tag reqs sups) = (RKey tag [] sups, reqs)
binopRouteSplit r = (r, [])

binopMethodApp : ModuleCtx ->
  PassEvidence ->
  String ->
  Expr ->
  Expr ->
  Route ->
  Expr
binopMethodApp mctx pe op l r route =
  let method = optionOr "eq" (binopDispatchMethod op)
  let split = binopRouteSplit route
  let call =
    EApp
      (EApp
        (EMethodAt
          method
          ""
          (mintMethodCellWith
            mctx
            pe
            (builtinMethodIfaceWord mctx.mcGraph method)
            2
            (fst split)
            (snd split)))
        l)
      r
  if op == "/=" then EApp (EVar "not") call else call

binopDispatchMethod : String -> Option String
binopDispatchMethod op = match arithDispatchMethod op
  Some method => Some method
  None => binopMethod op

-- The EUnOp analogue of binopMethodApp: one operand, no `/=`-style postfix
-- (unopMethod only ever routes `-`).  Reuses binopRouteSplit (a generic
-- Route-ripping helper — nothing about it is binop-specific).
unopMethodApp : ModuleCtx -> PassEvidence -> String -> Expr -> Route -> Expr
unopMethodApp mctx pe op e route =
  let method = optionOr "negate" (unopMethod op)
  let split = binopRouteSplit route
  EApp
    (EMethodAt
      method
      ""
      (mintMethodCellWith
        mctx
        pe
        (builtinMethodIfaceWord mctx.mcGraph method)
        1
        (fst split)
        (snd split)))
    e

dictPassDecl : ModuleCtx ->
  PassEvidence ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  List String ->
  Decl ->
  Decl
dictPassDecl mctx _ names _ (DFunDef pub n pats body site bid)
  | omHasKey n names =
    DFunDef pub n (dictParams n (dictArityOf mctx n) ++ pats) body site bid
  | otherwise = DFunDef pub n pats body site bid
-- Top-level `let rec … with …` (DLetGroup): each binding is dict-passed exactly
-- like a DFunDef — a constrained member gets `dictParams n (dictArityOf n)`
-- prepended to every clause's params, so the dict-passed call sites (which DO get
-- rewritten) line up with the definition.  (Without this, a `Num a => a -> a` group member's call site
-- supplies a leading dict the body never binds → the dict lands in the first user
-- param → arithmetic over a dict value panics `unknown op`.)
dictPassDecl mctx _ names _ (DLetGroup pub binds) =
  DLetGroup pub (map (dictPassLetBind mctx names) binds)
-- Phase 83/84 single-level + D3b-1: a parametric impl with `requires` gets one
-- leading `$dict_<method>_<slot>` param on each method (return- OR argument-
-- position) whose body actually reads an impl dict (so a terminal body like
