-- `eq Nil Nil = True` would take none — but see implDictPassMethods: the param is
-- added UNIFORMLY across all clauses of a method when ANY clause uses the dict, so
-- a multi-clause method keeps one arity).  The routes resolveSite/resolveArgStamp
-- filled on the call-site EMethodAt's impl-dicts ref line up with these params.
dictPassDecl mctx pe _ _ (d@(DImpl { iface, implOrigin, reqs, methods, ... })) = DImpl { d |
  methods =
    implDictPassMethods
      mctx
      pe
      IfaceRef { irName = iface, irOrigin = implOrigin }
      (listLen reqs)
      methods,
}
-- Phase 69.x-e: a method with method-level constraints (foldMap's `Monoid m`) gets
-- one leading `$dict_<method>_<slot>` param per constraint on its DEFAULT body, so a
-- caller can supply the dictionary the body's `empty`/… reads (routed RDict by
-- inferDefaultMethod).
dictPassDecl mctx _ _ _ (d@(DInterface { typarams, methods, ... })) =
  DInterface { d | methods = map (ifaceDictPassMethod typarams) methods }
dictPassDecl mctx pe names ret (DAttrib attrs d) =
  DAttrib attrs (dictPassDecl mctx pe names ret d)
dictPassDecl mctx _ _ _ d = d

-- DLetGroup binding dict-pass: prepend the member's dict params to every clause.
-- `dictArityOf n` is 0 for an unconstrained member (no change), matching the
-- oracle's `if k = 0 then (n, clauses)` guard.  Gated on `names` (the constrained
-- set) so an unconstrained member with a coincidental arity entry is untouched.
dictPassLetBind : ModuleCtx -> OrdMap Unit -> LetBind -> LetBind
dictPassLetBind mctx names (LetBind n clauses site bid)
  | omHasKey n names =
    LetBind n (map (prependDictClause n (dictArityOf mctx n)) clauses) site bid
  | otherwise = LetBind n clauses site bid

prependDictClause : String -> Int -> FunClause -> FunClause
prependDictClause n k (FunClause pats body) =
  FunClause (dictParams n k ++ pats) body

ifaceDictPassMethod : List String -> IfaceMethod -> IfaceMethod
ifaceDictPassMethod typarams (IfaceMethod n ty (Some (MethodDefault pats body)) mloc) =
  ifaceDictPassDefault
    n
    ty
    pats
    body
    mloc
    (listLen (methodLevelConstraintVarNames typarams ty))
ifaceDictPassMethod _ m = m

ifaceDictPassDefault : String ->
  Ty ->
  List Pat ->
  Expr ->
  Option Loc ->
  Int ->
  IfaceMethod
ifaceDictPassDefault n ty pats body mloc k
  | k > 0 =
    IfaceMethod n ty (Some (MethodDefault (dictParams n k ++ pats) body)) mloc
  | otherwise = IfaceMethod n ty (Some (MethodDefault pats body)) mloc

-- D3b-1: add the leading `$dict_<method>_<slot>` params UNIFORMLY across all
-- clauses of a method.  An impl method is many ImplMethod entries (one per
-- clause), so a per-clause `usesImplDict` test would give clauses different
-- arities (`eq Nil Nil = True` uses no dict; `eq (Cons …) (Cons …) = … eq x y …`
-- does) and break coalescing.  Compute the set of method NAMES any of whose
-- clauses reads the dict, then prepend the params to every clause of those names.
-- No rpNames gate: usesImplDict already requires an in-body RDict route to one of
-- these params, which on the non-emit path no arg-position site ever has (its
-- occurrences stay bare EVar), so return-position goldens are unaffected.
-- TYPECHECK-AUDIT S2: each method gets, in oracle slot order, its selected
-- interface declaration's METHOD-LEVEL dict params (`dictParams n k` — e.g.
-- `build`'s `Num e`) FOLLOWED BY the impl-`requires` element-dict params (at slots
-- k..k+nReq-1, only when the body reads one), then the original pats.  The final
-- pass reads k through `DImpl.implOrigin`; body inference derives the same k from
-- its selected ClassEnv row.  This is a direct mirror of
-- `dict_pats n k @ impl_pats @ pats` shape and the
-- `method_off + slot` impl-dict naming.  Eval applies
-- method dicts unconditionally first (eval.mdk), so dropping the leading method-level
-- params (the old `match reqs []=>d` early-out) mis-bound the dict into the first
-- value parameter.
implDictPassMethods : ModuleCtx ->
  PassEvidence ->
  IfaceRef ->
  Int ->
  List ImplMethod ->
  List ImplMethod
implDictPassMethods mctx pe iface nReq methods =
  let users = dedup (flatMap (clauseImplDictUser mctx pe iface nReq) methods)
  map (prependImplDictIfUser mctx iface nReq users) methods

clauseImplDictUser : ModuleCtx ->
  PassEvidence ->
  IfaceRef ->
  Int ->
  ImplMethod ->
  List String
clauseImplDictUser mctx pe iface nReq (ImplMethod n _ body)
  | usesImplDict pe n (implMethodDictArity mctx iface n) nReq body = [n]
  | otherwise = []

-- params = method-level dicts (slots 0..k-1) ++ impl-`requires` dicts (slots
-- k..k+nReq-1, only when this method's body consumes one) ++ original pats.  Skip
-- entirely only when there are neither (k = 0 and no impl-dict use), matching the
-- oracle's `if k = 0 && not uses_impl_dict then (n, pats, body)`.
prependImplDictIfUser : ModuleCtx ->
  IfaceRef ->
  Int ->
  List String ->
  ImplMethod ->
  ImplMethod
prependImplDictIfUser mctx iface nReq users (ImplMethod n pats body) =
  let k = implMethodDictArity mctx iface n
  let implPats = if contains n users then dictParamsFrom n k nReq else []
  if k == 0 && isEmptyL implPats then
    ImplMethod n pats body
  else
    ImplMethod n (dictParams n k ++ implPats ++ pats) body

-- does [body] reference an in-body return-position method already routed RDict to
-- one of THIS method's would-be impl-dict params? (the gate that distinguishes a
-- body that consumes the element dict from a terminal one that doesn't).  Impl-dict
-- slots are offset by the method's own method-level arity (S2), so probe at k..k+nReq-1.
usesImplDict : PassEvidence -> String -> Int -> Int -> Expr -> Bool
usesImplDict pe mname methodArity nReq body =
  anyMember (collectDictSites pe body) (implDictNames mname methodArity nReq)

implDictNames : String -> Int -> Int -> List String
implDictNames mname methodArity nReq =
  map (dictParamName mname) (range methodArity (methodArity + nReq))

implMethodDictArity : ModuleCtx -> IfaceRef -> String -> Int
implMethodDictArity mctx iface method =
  methodDictArityAtOrigin mctx iface.irOrigin (methodSlotKey iface method)

-- [key] is a `methodSlotKey`; [origin] is its interface's declaring module.
methodDictArityAtOrigin : ModuleCtx -> TyConOrigin -> String -> Int
methodDictArityAtOrigin mctx (OriginModule mid) key =
  match (lookupQualPayload
    mid
    key
    mctx.mcGraph.crossRun.crossModuleMethodPredicateSlotsQualRef.value)
    Some slots => listLen slots
    None => methodDictArityOf mctx key
methodDictArityAtOrigin mctx _ key = methodDictArityOf mctx key

siteRDictName : Route -> List String
siteRDictName (RDict d) = [d]
siteRDictName (RDictFwd d) = [d]
siteRDictName (RProj inner _) = routeRDictName inner
siteRDictName _ = []

siteRDictNamesL : List Route -> List String
siteRDictNamesL rs = flatMap routeRDictName rs

routeRDictName : Route -> List String
routeRDictName (RDict d) = [d]
routeRDictName (RDictFwd d) = [d]
-- Native #54/#21 residual: an element-dict RKey route can NEST an RDict forwarding
-- the enclosing impl's `requires` dict (e.g. `RKey "$tuple" [RDict $dict_debug_0,
-- RDict $dict_debug_1]` for `debug (toList m)` in a `Debug (Map k v)` body).  The
-- gate that decides whether to PREPEND those impl-dict params (usesImplDict) must
-- see the nested name, else the route references a param the clause never declares
-- → emitter panics "unbound dict witness".  Recurse into the nested reqs.
routeRDictName (RKey _ reqs sups) =
  flatMap routeRDictName reqs ++ flatMap routeRDictName sups
routeRDictName (RProj r _) = routeRDictName r
routeRDictName _ = []

-- The dict-param names the method occurrences and dictionary applications in [e]
-- route to: an `EMethodAt`'s dispatch route (RDict/RDictFwd, post-resolveSites)
-- and its impl-/method-dict route LISTS, and every `EDictAt` route list that
-- forwards RDict/RDictFwd to an impl param (a `=>`-constrained helper call that
-- threads the impl dict through, e.g. `debug xs = "[\{debugListItems xs}]"` where
-- `debugListItems` is an EDictAt).
--
-- An EMethodAt arg-position site carries its element-dict routes in the
-- impl-/method-dict lists, not its dispatch route.  A nested `requires` impl whose
-- body dispatches a method on its own element tyvar routes RDict $dict_<m>_<slot>
-- there, so both are scanned for implDictPassMethods' usesImplDict gate to prepend
-- the matching param.
collectDictSites : PassEvidence -> Expr -> List String
collectDictSites pe (EDictAt _ ev) =
  siteRDictNamesL (evDictRoutesIn (passIndex pe) ev)
collectDictSites pe (EMethodAt _ _ ev) =
  let (PassMethod _ tag dicts) = passMethodOf pe ev
  siteRDictName tag ++ siteRDictNamesL dicts
collectDictSites pe (ELoc _ e) = collectDictSites pe e
collectDictSites pe (EDoOrigin _ e) = collectDictSites pe e
collectDictSites pe (EApp f x) = collectDictSites pe f ++ collectDictSites pe x
collectDictSites pe (ELam _ b) = collectDictSites pe b
collectDictSites pe (ELet _ _ _ e1 e2) =
  collectDictSites pe e1 ++ collectDictSites pe e2
collectDictSites pe (ELetGroup binds body) =
  flatMap (letBindDictSites pe) binds ++ collectDictSites pe body
collectDictSites pe (EMatch e arms) =
  collectDictSites pe e ++ flatMap (armDictSites pe) arms
collectDictSites pe (EIf c t e) =
  collectDictSites pe c ++ collectDictSites pe t ++ collectDictSites pe e
collectDictSites pe (EBinOp _ l r _) =
  collectDictSites pe l ++ collectDictSites pe r
collectDictSites pe (EUnOp _ e _) = collectDictSites pe e
collectDictSites pe (EInfix _ l r) =
  collectDictSites pe l ++ collectDictSites pe r
collectDictSites pe (EFieldAccess e _ _) = collectDictSites pe e
collectDictSites pe (ETuple es) = flatMap (collectDictSites pe) es
collectDictSites pe (EListLit es) = flatMap (collectDictSites pe) es
collectDictSites pe (EArrayLit es) = flatMap (collectDictSites pe) es
collectDictSites pe (ERangeList a b _) =
  collectDictSites pe a ++ collectDictSites pe b
collectDictSites pe (ERangeArray a b _) =
  collectDictSites pe a ++ collectDictSites pe b
collectDictSites pe (ESlice e a b _) =
  collectDictSites pe e ++ collectDictSites pe a ++ collectDictSites pe b
collectDictSites pe (EIndex e i) =
  collectDictSites pe e ++ collectDictSites pe i
collectDictSites pe (EAnnot e _) = collectDictSites pe e
collectDictSites pe (EBlock stmts) = flatMap (doStmtDictSites pe) stmts
collectDictSites pe (ERecordCreate _ fs) = flatMap (fieldAssignDictSites pe) fs
collectDictSites pe (ERecordUpdate e fs _) =
  collectDictSites pe e ++ flatMap (fieldAssignDictSites pe) fs
collectDictSites pe (EVariantUpdate _ e fs) =
  collectDictSites pe e ++ flatMap (fieldAssignDictSites pe) fs
collectDictSites _ _ = []

letBindDictSites : PassEvidence -> LetBind -> List String
letBindDictSites pe (LetBind _ clauses _ _) =
  flatMap (funClauseDictSites pe) clauses

funClauseDictSites : PassEvidence -> FunClause -> List String
funClauseDictSites pe (FunClause _ body) = collectDictSites pe body

armDictSites : PassEvidence -> Arm -> List String
armDictSites pe (Arm _ guards body) =
  flatMap (guardDictSites pe) guards ++ collectDictSites pe body

guardDictSites : PassEvidence -> Guard -> List String
guardDictSites pe (GBool e) = collectDictSites pe e
guardDictSites pe (GBind _ e) = collectDictSites pe e

doStmtDictSites : PassEvidence -> DoStmt -> List String
doStmtDictSites pe (DoExpr e) = collectDictSites pe e
doStmtDictSites pe (DoLet _ _ _ e _) = collectDictSites pe e
doStmtDictSites pe (DoBind _ e) = collectDictSites pe e
doStmtDictSites pe (DoAssign _ e) = collectDictSites pe e
doStmtDictSites pe (DoFieldAssign _ _ e) = collectDictSites pe e

fieldAssignDictSites : PassEvidence -> FieldAssign -> List String
fieldAssignDictSites pe (FieldAssign _ e) = collectDictSites pe e

dictArityOf : ModuleCtx -> String -> Int
dictArityOf mctx n =
  listLen
    (optionOr
      []
      (lookupPredicateSlots n mctx.mcCells.funPredicateSlotsIdxRef.value))

dictParams : String -> Int -> List Pat
dictParams n k = dictParamsGo n 0 k

dictParamsGo : String -> Int -> Int -> List Pat
dictParamsGo n slot k
  | slot >= k = []
  | otherwise =
    PVar (dictParamName n slot) (Loc "" 0 0 0 0) noBinderId
      :: dictParamsGo n (slot + 1) k

-- [count] dict params for [n] starting at slot [start]: $dict_n_start ..
-- $dict_n_(start+count-1).  Used for impl-`requires` element-dict params, which
-- follow the method's own method-level params (S2 offset = methodDictArityOf).
dictParamsFrom : String -> Int -> Int -> List Pat
dictParamsFrom n start count
  | count <= 0 = []
  | otherwise =
    PVar (dictParamName n start) (Loc "" 0 0 0 0) noBinderId
      :: dictParamsFrom n (start + 1) (count - 1)

-- #80: the single per-module typecheck body, reached from the graph driver through
-- `checkModuleFullImpl`. DICT-SEMANTICS §7's single-evaluator law means one
-- elaboration decision serves check, run, and emit. `mid` and `implDecls` carry the
-- current module's identity and graph-visible impl universe; single-file callers use
-- the same function through the one-module graph projections.
--
-- The module's `ModuleCtx` is minted here, before anything else runs, and returned
-- beside the bindings: the driver continues from it.  [gctx] is the drive's graph
-- record, which the driver passes (the previous record's `mcGraph`).  [runSeed] is its
-- match oracle and warnings (`seedCheckRun`); a driver that does not seed
-- (`cmCheckWorker`, the core passes) passes the previous record's (`checkRunResidue`).
checkBodyImpl : GraphCtx ->
  CheckRunSeed ->
  ModuleSeed ->
  String ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  (ModuleBindings, List Decl, ModuleCtx)
-- multi-line RHS: the indented `:=` form is legal but not seed-parseable yet (#1744)
-- lint-disable-next-line rule-prefer-assign-op
checkBodyImpl gctx runSeed moduleSeed mid implDecls prog0 =
  let seed = moduleSeed.msSchemes
  let mctx = freshModuleCtx gctx runSeed mid
  let moduleScope =
    Scopes.freshScope
      (currentScopeStore gctx ())
      None
      mctx.mcCells.currentLevel.value
      mid
      ModuleOwner
  openScope mctx moduleScope
  recordModuleStart gctx mid
  -- #1675: this module's own `import`/`export import` decls, checked for a name the
  -- named dependency exports under two different definitions.  Here rather than in
  -- `importSeed` because the seed is built BEFORE this `freshModuleCtx` — see
  -- `reportAmbiguousImports`.  Reads only `deAmbigValues`, so a driver with no graph
  -- envelope (Flat, single-file) is a no-op.
  reportAmbiguousImports mctx prog0
  let prog = prog0
  let aliasSpellings = aliasMethodSpellings gctx prog
  -- P1 (#1446) / DICT §8 I7: the four operator-and-literal classes' identities, read
  -- off the PRELUDE's own `DInterface` decls before any body is inferred (the operator
  -- handlers consult them during inference).  See `seedBuiltinClasses`.
  seedBuiltinClasses gctx mid prog
  -- #837: stamp binding ids on the program the bodies are INFERRED from.  `prog`
  -- itself stays unstamped for the pre-inference analyses (shadows/key table/…),
  -- which do not need ids; only the inferred bodies (defs + impl/default/prop/test)
  -- carry EVarId, and schemeDefIdsRef feeds registerSchemeObligations the top-level
  -- members' ids.  Flat: a single walk (top-level frame built over the whole `prog`,
  -- so a user body referencing a prelude fn gets the prelude fn's id), then split
  -- back into core/user slices for the two-phase Flat inference.  Module: the
  -- scope alone is minted here; each binding group is MARKED and then stamped as the
  -- schedule reaches it (`processSCC`), and the tail bodies after the groups, so
  -- `progS` is the module's UNMARKED, unstamped tree and `progT` below its inferred
  -- twin.  The Flat callers marked their whole program before this call.
  let stampRes =
    let (top, ids) = stampTopScope prog
    beginModuleMarking mctx mid prog top moduleSeed
    (prog, ids)
  let progS = fst stampRes
  -- #907: index name→id as an OrdMap (was a List scanned linearly per rendered
  -- scheme in ownContext / per SCC member in registerSchemeObligations → O(decls²)).
  -- Built from the REVERSED pairs so omFromPairs' last-write-wins reproduces the old
  -- `lookupAssoc` first-match-wins on a duplicated binder name (same pattern as sigTyMapRef).
  mctx.mcCells.schemeDefIdsRef := omFromPairs (reverseL (snd stampRes)) omEmpty
  -- the full visible universe (shadows / key table /
  -- completeness / obligations): Flat = whole flattened program; Module = imported
  -- data + impl universe + this module.
  -- #154 PR-A: every consumer of `fullUniverse` is a `Flat _ =>` arm (grep confirms:
  -- buildDefinerShadows
  -- / checkImplObligations / checkCallObligations — all Flat).  #1557 A-3.5a removed
  -- `checkImplCompleteness` from that list: impl-completeness no longer takes a decl
  -- list, it reads `classEnvHere`,
  -- which IS this binding on that arm).  Medaka is STRICT, so the
  -- Module arm's `accData ++ implDecls ++ prog0` allocated an O(|accData|) list every module
  -- and discarded it unread — a dead per-module O(N) concat.  Bind `[]` on Module.
  -- registerAllData universe (#154 PR-A): the Module path no longer builds `accData ++ prog0`
  -- here — prior modules' public data lives in the persistent DATA-universe accumulators
  -- (universeCtorPop/universeRecordPop), loaded+overlaid at the `dataEnv` binding below.
  -- (#6, #1457) superDeclsRef: unified body OWNS it — Flat = coreProg ++ userProg, Module =
  -- `prog ++ implDecls`.  [implDecls] is core + every EARLIER module ONLY (foldModules never
  -- folds a module into its own universe), so binding it alone EXCLUDED this module's own
  -- `interface F t requires L t` decl from ifaceSelfAndSupers/survivorObligationEntailed and
  -- false-rejected every legal superclass-default body (#1457).  Folding `prog` in matches the
  -- graph path, whose universe includes this module itself.
  -- ⚠️ Operand order is load-bearing, BOTH ways:
  --   * cost — Medaka is strict, so `xs ++ ys` copies xs and shares ys.  [implDecls] is the
  --     growing accumulator, so it MUST be the right operand: `prog ++ implDecls` is O(|prog|)
  --     per module = O(N) overall, whereas `implDecls ++ prog` would resurrect #154 PR-C's
  --     O(modules²) per-module concat.
  --   * meaning — ifaceSupersOf/ifaceSelfAndSupers is a FIRST-MATCH scan, so `prog` first makes
  --     THIS module's own same-spelled interface decl outrank an earlier module's, which is the
  --     precedence the old single-program path had.
  let superDecls = prog ++ implDecls
  mctx.mcCells.superDeclsRef := superDecls
  -- (BREAK #3) effect domains: FLAT populates inline; MODULE relies on the driver
  -- preamble (checkModulesPreambleK / elaborateModules) populating ONCE over the whole
  -- import graph — a per-module populate would wipe another module's domains.
  checkEffectParams mctx prog
  checkLetRecDecls mctx prog
  -- #154 PR1: on the Module path, grow the persistent universe accumulators by THIS
  -- module's decls BEFORE the shadow/key reads below consult them — so they see the
  -- same universe `fullUniverse` (which appended prog0) did.
  -- untouched and rebuilds over its whole `prog` (already O(N)).
  -- #1112 A-3.4 PR2: `ieShadowCompare mid prog0` stood here, and the hard `panic`
  -- surface it put in the released compiler is GONE with it — that instrument had
  -- exactly one job, measuring the §9.5 equality before the flip committed to it,
  -- and the flip has now been made on a strictly stronger measurement (see
  -- `moduleImplUniv` just below for what was measured and how it was shown
  -- fail-capable).  `appendUniverseAccums` no longer grows an impl universe either,
  -- so there is nothing left here for `IE` to be compared against.
  -- #1499 clause (b) / S1-PRELUDE (a): `mid` is BOUND here now — `appendUniverseAccums`
  -- must know whether this pass is the PRELUDE's, because the prelude contributes to
  -- S1's INTERFACE operand but NOT to its STANDALONE one.  See its header.
  appendUniverseAccums gctx mid prog0
  -- 🚨 #1112 A-3.4 PR2 — THE `IE` READER FLIP.  A production read of stage K's `IE`
  -- (A-3.5b added a second, `ieRowsVisibleAt`; do NOT re-instate "the ONE place" here).
  -- It replaced the three `obUniv*` `CrossRun` accumulators, which are GONE rather than
  -- merely unread — two sources of truth for "what impls exist" is what design law L1
  -- removes.  The WAS/NOW migration narrative, and the whole-prefix equality MEASUREMENT
  -- that licensed deleting the `ieShadowCompare` instrument, live in
  -- `compiler/TYPECHECK-TARGET-ARCHITECTURE.md` §9.5a; what stays here are the facts a
  -- reader OF THIS LINE needs.
  --
  -- 🚨 SINCE A-3.6 (#1558) THIS IS NOT FILTERED TO THIS MODULE'S ORDINAL PREFIX.
  -- `ieSnapAt` routes through `ieCandidacyVisibleAt`, which is `True`, so this binding is
  -- the WHOLE GRAPH's impl universe regardless of `mid`'s ordinal.  This line is where
  -- A-3's C4/I2 claim is cashed: every obligation check on the multi-module path knows the
  -- same impl population in every module — *"import scoping never decides which instances
  -- exist"* (`docs/spec/DICT-SEMANTICS.md` §8 I5).  It WIDENS #1438's same-spelled-
  -- interface reach (#1482 measured that topological prefix scoping was accidentally
  -- load-bearing for it); expected and licensed, but an acceptance delta.  ⚠️ The pin that
  -- used to grade that delta, `test/must_fail_fixtures/1072-overlap-xmod-bare-head-arm-
  -- order`, IS GONE FROM THE TREE (derive: `ls test/must_fail_fixtures | grep 1072`) — see
  -- §9.5a; do not read its absence as "already drained".
  --
  -- ⚠️ `declEnvsOrdOf mid` IS STILL PASSED AND IS NOW INERT ON THIS PATH.  It is
  -- kept so the call site does not move and so re-scoping candidacy later is a
  -- one-line change; do not "simplify" it away, and do not read its presence as
  -- evidence a filter is still applied.  Its `-1` miss sentinel is likewise vacuous
  -- here — an unknown module id now gains the whole graph rather than losing
  -- everything, the opposite of the fail-CLOSED story `declEnvsOrdOf` documents for
  -- the NAME axis.
  --
  -- 🚨 BOUND ONCE, READ TWICE, AND THE "ONCE" IS LOAD-BEARING.  There are TWO Module-arm
  -- consumers — `residualUnivRef` (#1549) just below, and the end-of-body obligation
  -- `obUniv` — and A-3.4's own design was written when there was only ONE.  Do not
  -- re-derive the projection at the second site: it is a whole-prefix rebuild, so a
  -- second call doubles this unit's already-measured per-module cost for a value that
  -- cannot have changed (both `ord` and `IE` are immutable for the whole module; the
  -- accumulator these replaced was likewise grown once, above, and read at both sites).
  -- A third consumer should take this binding too, or say in writing why it needs a
  -- different ordinal.
  let moduleImplUniv =
    let envs = gctx.declEnvsRef.value
    ieUniverseAt (declEnvsOrdOf mid envs) envs.deImpls
  -- #1549: stash the impl universe the RESIDUAL REDUCER entails against
  -- (`residualPredsOf`, called from each generalizing group's close).  This is NOT a
  -- third source: it is the SAME two arm-gated sources the end-of-body obligation
  -- checkers consume — `buildImplUniverse prog` on Flat, and since A-3.4 PR2 the `IE`
  -- projection on Module (which carries this module's own impls, its ordinal being
  -- included by `declEnvVisibleAt`, exactly as the retired accumulator did after the
  -- `appendUniverseAccums` above).  Built ONCE per module rather than per group:
  -- rebuilding it inside the reducer would be O(decls) per SCC, i.e. quadratic.
  setRef mctx.mcCells.residualUnivRef moduleImplUniv
  -- (#4) shadows.  definerShadows uses the SHARED form — buildDefinerShadows over the
  -- full visible universe, scoped to THIS module's decls (prog0).  On Flat, prog0 =
  -- userProg and fullUniverse = prog, so this is exactly the old flat `buildDefinerShadows
  -- prog userProg`.  The method-name test, `isMethod`, reads `deMethods` at this module's
  -- ordinal: every interface method a module at or before it declares, whatever its
  -- export.  importerShadows exist only across a module boundary; the `Module _ _ []` arm
  -- (cmCheckWorker / core pass, implDecls = []) keeps the old empty result — `funDefs []
  -- = []` gave no imported fns there.
  -- #1354 unit A (#1353): that test is not scoped to what this module can name, so the
  -- intersection alone implements only S1's LEFT operand.  `nameableIfaceShadows` supplies
  -- the RIGHT one — the interface must be nameable in THIS module.  Applied to the RESULT,
  -- never inside either filter (the result is single-digit; `fnSet` is every fn name in
  -- the graph), and fail-open when the graph index is absent.  See `nameableIfaceShadows`.
  -- The Flat arms are untouched: a single file is one module and its own interfaces are
  -- nameable in it.
  let isMethod =
    let envs = gctx.declEnvsRef.value
    methodNameDeclaredAt (declEnvsOrdOf mid envs) envs.deMethods
  let definerShadows =
    nameableIfaceShadows gctx prog0 (definerShadowsFromSet gctx isMethod prog0)
  let importerShadows =
    if isEmptyL implDecls then
      []
    else
      nameableIfaceShadows
        gctx
        prog0
        (standaloneShadowsFromSet
          gctx
          isMethod
          (omMapValues (_ => ()) moduleSeed.msImportedValues)
          prog0)
  let sigs = sigsOf prog
  mctx.mcCells.definerShadowNamesRef := namesToSet definerShadows omEmpty
  mctx.mcCells.definerShadowSigsRef := omFromPairs (reverseL sigs) omEmpty
  -- #154 PR1 seeded a SECOND impl-existence table here — `shadowKeyTableRef`, from
  -- `buildKeyTable fullUniverse` on Flat and from the cumulative `universeKeyBucketsRef`
  -- on Module.  ARCH B-2.1-g repointed all three of its boolean existence reads onto the
  -- graph-global `bodyImplEnvRef` seeded just below (`ieImplExistsForHead`), and B-2.1-d
  -- deleted both refs.  🚨 DO NOT RE-ADD A PREFIX-KEYED EXISTENCE TABLE HERE.  The Module
  -- arm's source was a cumulative TOPOLOGICAL PREFIX while S2's impl universe is
  -- graph-global (`SHADOW-SEMANTICS.md:183-186`, `:226`), so an importer shadow whose
  -- receiver's impl sat in a topologically later module answered "no impl" and called the
  -- standalone — a located reject became exit 0 printing a `Box` pointer fed to `n + 1`,
  -- discriminated by the order of two `import` lines.  One substrate, one decision.
  -- ARCH B-2.1-a2: the SAME impl population, seated on `IE`'s shape, on BOTH arms —
  -- one ref, so the evidence reader B-2.1-b repoints has one substrate rather than an
  -- arm gate.  It landed ADDITIVE AND BEHAVIOUR-NEUTRAL, so the repoints that followed got
  -- a substrate they could trust on a path where `IE` was empty (see `buildFlatImplEnv`
  -- for the measured hazard, RUN-B-017 probe 3).
  -- ⚠️ "nothing reads `bodyImplEnvRef` yet" was true only at a2 and is now FALSE: B-2.1-b2's
  -- three selection legs, and B-2.1-g's route word plus three shadow existence reads, all
  -- read this ref.  Derive the set: `grep -n bodyImplEnvRef compiler/types/typecheck.mdk`.
  -- The Module arm is a pointer copy of the env `buildDeclEnvs` already built; it
  -- deliberately does NOT re-derive, for the reason `moduleImplUniv` gives above.
  mctx.mcCells.bodyImplEnvRef := gctx.declEnvsRef.value.deImpls
  -- (#4 + #3-restore) mode-specific pre-inference ref setup (all pure/independent of the
  -- register+globalS block below, so order-safe).  Module installs importer-shadow state and restores the cross-module dict
  -- accumulators `freshModuleCtx` just wiped.
  -- multi-line RHS: the indented `:=` form is legal but not seed-parseable yet (#1744)
  -- lint-disable-next-line rule-prefer-assign-op

  -- #1425 site 2: `mid` is BOUND here now — the three lockstep re-keys at the end of this
  -- arm need this module's identity, and the arm can no longer discard it.

  mctx.mcCells.standaloneValuesRef :=
    namesToSet (importerShadows ++ definerShadows) omEmpty
  -- #1351: the per-module copy of the identity-keyed dispatch-index universe, read by
  -- `methodDispatchIdx` through `dispatchIdxScoped`.  Its bare-name peer was retired at L5.
  mctx.mcCells.methodDispatchIdxByIdRef :=
    gctx.crossRun.universeMethodDispatchIdxByIdRef.value
  -- The list alone is seeded here and re-keyed twice below; nothing reads the
  -- name index until the final `setFunPredicateSlots` of this arm rebuilds it.
  mctx.mcCells.funPredicateSlotsRef :=
    gctx.crossRun.crossModuleFunPredicateSlotsRef.value
  -- B-2.2-f (#1113): the declared-prefix sidecar rides the IDS table — every
  -- whole-table replacement of `funConstraintsRef` owes one of these.
  mctx.mcCells.funConstraintDeclaredRef :=
    gctx.crossRun.crossModuleFunConstraintDeclaredRef.value
  -- A module alias (`import m as A`) has no `currentImportDefinersRef` row for
  -- each dotted member, so its call sites resolve through these alias-local rows.
  -- The source is nevertheless exact: `aliasConstraintEntries` selects only the
  -- `(defining module, exported name)` row admitted by that alias. Preserve the
  -- complete predicate vectors here; stripping them reduces distinct predicates
  -- such as `Tweak a Int` and `Tweak a Bool` to the ambiguous goal `Tweak a`.
  -- The graph-wide bare-name snapshot below remains vector-free because it lacks
  -- this source identity.
  let _ =
    setRef
      mctx.mcCells.funPredicateSlotsRef
      (aliasConstraintEntries
          gctx
          prog
          gctx.crossRun.crossModuleFunPredicateSlotsQualRef.value
        ++ mctx.mcCells.funPredicateSlotsRef.value)
  let _ =
    setRef
      mctx.mcCells.funConstraintDeclaredRef
      (aliasConstraintEntries
          gctx
          prog
          gctx.crossRun.crossModuleFunConstraintDeclaredQualRef.value
        ++ mctx.mcCells.funConstraintDeclaredRef.value)
  -- #1425 site 2: the three tables above were just seeded WHOLESALE from graph-wide
  -- BARE-NAME accumulators, so every name this module declares is currently answered by
  -- whichever module's same-named binding the topological order happened to put first.
  -- Re-key those names — and only those — onto this module's own `(mid, name)` rows.
  -- Three writes, in lockstep, per B-2.2-f (#1113): the declared-prefix sidecar rides the
  -- IDS table, and this is a whole-table replacement of all three.
  let _ =
    setFunPredicateSlots
      mctx
      (selfDeclArities
        mid
        prog
        gctx.crossRun.crossModuleFunPredicateSlotsQualRef.value
        mctx.mcCells.funPredicateSlotsRef.value)
  let _ =
    setRef
      mctx.mcCells.funConstraintDeclaredRef
      (selfDeclArities
        mid
        prog
        gctx.crossRun.crossModuleFunConstraintDeclaredQualRef.value
        mctx.mcCells.funConstraintDeclaredRef.value)
  -- RUN-XMOD-062: ONE derivation, two projections.  The two refs are read together
  -- (`qualConstraintKey` assembles a `(definer, origin)` key out of both), so they
  -- must not be derived by two independent walks that could admit different rows.
  let admitted = importDefinersOf gctx prog
  mctx.mcCells.currentImportDefinersRef :=
    omFromPairs (reverseL (definerRowsOf admitted)) omEmpty
  mctx.mcCells.currentImportOriginsRef :=
    omFromPairs (reverseL (originRowsOf admitted)) omEmpty
  -- #1114 (#845): this module's imported SCHEME CONTEXTS, keyed by local spelling.
  -- `reverseL` before `omFromPairs` so the FIRST entry wins a duplicate key, matching
  -- the first-match policy of the sibling tables set just above
  -- (`omFromPairs` is last-write-wins; see its own note in support/ordmap.mdk).
  let _ =
    setRef
      mctx.mcCells.importedSchemeOblsRef
      (omFromPairs
        (reverseL
          (importedSchemeOblEntries
            prog
            gctx.crossRun.crossModuleSchemeOblsQualRef.value))
        omEmpty)
  ()
  -- #2563: install THIS module's method scope — its decls and ordinal, the inputs
  -- `methodScopeHere` answers from on first read of each spelling (stage K's
  -- `deMethods` is the whole graph; nothing is copied per module).

  mctx.mcCells.methodScopeCtxRef :=
    Some (prog, declEnvsOrdOf mid gctx.declEnvsRef.value)
  -- #1386: the alias-qualified spellings (`A.mth`) this module's imports supply.
  -- Built eagerly, here, because a key that names two declarations is reported
  -- (`T-AMBIGUOUS-ALIAS-METHOD`) whether or not the module ever spells it.
  mctx.mcCells.methodAliasEntriesRef :=
    aliasQualifiedMethodEntries mctx prog omEmpty
  -- #1386: the ORIGIN name behind each of those alias-qualified keys, from the
  -- same rows, in the same module scope, on the same line as the supply they
  -- accompany — `originMethodName`'s source.
  mctx.mcCells.aliasMethodOriginsRef := omFromPairs aliasSpellings omEmpty
  -- Module arm: copy the seven persistent DATA-universe accumulators (prior modules'
  -- public data + ctor env, each minted exactly once) into the `freshModuleCtx`-wiped
  -- working refs, then register ONLY this module's `prog0` as a transient FRONT
  -- overlay — O(|prog0|) per module, O(N) total. Ordering must stay [prog0,
  -- pub_{k-1}..pub_1] to preserve lookupAssoc (first-wins) / omInsert (last-write-wins)
  -- semantics.
  let dataEnv =
    -- A-3.2b (#1512): `mid` is BOUND here now — the overlay pool below is read at this
    -- module's own ordinal, so the arm can no longer discard it.
    -- A-3.2b residual (#1512): `envs`/`cur` are bound BEFORE the reload, not
    -- after, because the reload's alias half is now a projection of `envs` at
    -- `cur`.  Both bindings are pure reads of `GraphCtx`, so hoisting them
    -- above `loadDataUniverse` changes nothing else.
    let envs = gctx.declEnvsRef.value
    let cur = declEnvsOrdOf mid envs
    loadDataUniverse mctx cur
    -- #674: OVERLAY the ctors of the types THIS module imports so a bare ctor name
    -- resolves to the module the unit imports it from, not the universe's load-order
    -- winner.  Reads the persistent universe DECLS (not the Module `accData` field —
    -- that is dead `[]` on the elaborate/emit path, #154 PR-C), so the overlay fires
    -- on the run/build gate too, not just `check`.
    --
    --     universe  <  imported-ctor overlay  <  this module's OWN `prog0`.
    -- The overlay registers AFTER the universe (that is #674's requirement — it must
    -- win the `omInsert` tie-break over the load-order winner) and BEFORE `prog0`
    -- (this module's own declarations outrank anything it imports — ordinary
    -- shadowing, and the SHADOW spec's S1 per-module scoping).
    --
    -- one: an imported decl's constructors then beat locally-declared ones, so
    -- `import json.{Json, JNull}` + a local `data Tok = JString String` was rejected
    -- `Type mismatch: Json vs Tok` — clobbered by a SIBLING constructor of `Json`
    -- that the program never imported.  It reaches the stdlib and it is not narrow:
    -- every selective constructor-naming import carries it.  Pinned by
    -- `test/engine_fixtures/ctor_scope_local_ctor_beats_stdlib_import.mdk` (the
    -- stdlib `json` shape, on all three engines) and
    -- `test/llvm_fixtures_modules/ctor_scope_local_decl_wins/` (`{Ext, Other}` plus
    -- a local decl, prelude-free).
    --
    -- cause was exactly two of them disagreeing, and a FUTURE edit re-creates that by
    -- moving ONE.  This note used to name a PAIR ("both structures agree"), and the
    -- pair it named was the one that cannot disagree — while omitting the one that can.
    --
    -- Registration order here is  universe < overlay < prog0.  Under it:
    --   * the `TcEnv` ctor scheme map (`addCtor` → `omInsert`, BARE ctor name) —
    --     LAST-write-wins → prog0.  BARE-keyed, so two modules genuinely collide here;
    --     this is #1259's table and the one the overlay exists for.
    --   * `recordByNameRef` (`registerRecordInfoKeyed` → `omInsert`, BARE ctor name) —
    --     LAST-write-wins → prog0.  #1256's table, same keying, same hazard.
    --   * `dataParamKindsRef` (`recordParamKinds`, a consed list read FIRST-match) —
    --     IDENTITY-keyed since A-2.3 (`tyTabKey o name`), so two modules' same-named
    --     types get DIFFERENT keys and registration order cannot decide between them
    --     at all.  It is order-observable only for a decl registered twice, where it
    --     agrees.  It is NOT evidence about the bare-keyed tables above.
    --     (`checkModuleFullDiags`: `seedCheckRun (prog ++ importedCtorTypeDeclsFirstWins prog …
    --     ++ accData)`), from a LIST, with `oracleMap` = `omFromPairs (reverseL …)`,
    --     i.e. FIRST-wins on that list → prog0 > overlay > universe.  Same verdict,
    --     opposite mechanism, and reached through none of the code on this line.
    --     THIS is the one a future edit can silently flip, so check it too.
    -- All four land on prog0 > overlay > universe.  Getting any two to disagree is
    -- #674's root cause.
    -- #1111 A-2.11 (#1319 unit 1): a FIFTH layer, and it is a per-NAME overlay rather
    -- than a fifth registration — `applyCtorScopeOverrides` re-points the (normally
    -- empty) set of COLLIDED constructor names at the declaration THIS module's import
    -- scope selects.  It sits ABOVE prog0 and declines for any name prog0 declares, so
    -- the ladder above is unchanged: own > import scope > import overlay > universe.
    -- A collision-free program returns this very env unchanged and unallocated.
    -- #1111 A-2.12 (#1319 unit 2): the two RECORD-table overlays are the same fifth
    -- layer one namespace-half over, and they must run HERE — after `registerAllData …
    -- prog0` has written the floor into `recordByNameRef` / `fieldOwnersRef` — for the
    -- same reason `applyCtorScopeOverrides` wraps that call.  They are statements rather
    -- than an env transform only because those two tables are per-run REFS, not `TcEnv`
    -- fields; the ladder they implement is identical.  See applyRecordScopeOverrides.
    -- `CrossRun.universeDataDecls` — a positional `List Decl` accumulated by
    -- `appendDataUniverse`, carrying no key at all — is RETIRED; the pool is the
    -- whole-graph envelope read at THIS module's ordinal through
    -- `declEnvRowVisible`/`declEnvVisibleTo`.
    --
    -- `buildDeclEnvs` indexed the row under, threaded here by the driver
    -- (`elabModuleStamp mid` on the emit path; `cmCheckWorker mid` since #1508).  It
    -- is NOT re-derived from import syntax, which is why the emit path's
    -- `private_mangle` rewriting cannot break it: mangling renames top-level
    -- bindings, never a loader module id, and the decls in the pool are the very
    -- objects the accumulator held before.  (Re-deriving a read key by re-walking
    -- `DUse` syntax is what made #1425's four-site change resolve on eval and MISS on
    -- emit — `DUse` decls are never mangled.  This key does not go through that
    -- channel.)
    -- #1112 A-3.2b (#1512) slices 2+3: the KIND and FIELD-OWNER halves of the seed
    -- `loadDataUniverse` used to copy out of two `GraphCtx.crossRun` accumulators.  Same
    -- position in the ladder (it is the UNIVERSE layer, under the overlay and under
    -- `prog0`), same content, one ordinal-aware source.  See `declEnvSeedChain` for
    -- why the reader's OWN row is excluded here and registered by the two
    -- `registerAllData` calls below instead.
    declEnvSeedDataUniverse mctx mid envs
    -- `omInsert` tables, so the LAST row wins, and the overlay's named-outranks-wildcard
    -- rule therefore needs the `UseGroup` rows LAST.  The oracle call site takes the
    -- opposite order for the opposite reason — see the partition note at
    -- `importedCtorTypeDeclsFirstWins`.  Swapping these two inverts the rule silently.
    let base =
      registerImportOverlay
        (withCtors mctx (spFloor gctx.crossRun.universeCtorPop.value))
        prog0
        (importedCtorTypeDeclsLastWins prog0 cur envs.deModules)
    let env0 = registerAllData base prog0
    applyRecordScopeOverrides mctx prog0
    applyCtorScopeOverrides prog0 env0
  recordInvocationView dataEnv
  -- #784: reject under-determined return-only effect vars on interface methods.
  -- MUST run AFTER `dataEnv` above populated `dataParamKindsRef` — the kind-aware
  -- predicate (rowArgNames) reads that table to distinguish a row-kinded ctor arg
  -- (`Async e a`, pins the effect) from a type-kinded one (`List e`, does not).
  checkUndeterminedRetEffVars mctx prog
  -- EFFECTS-SEMANTICS §6.4/§6.5: declared-kind consistency.  Same placement — the
  -- slot-kind reads consult the table `dataEnv` just populated.
  checkDeclaredKinds mctx prog
  -- One authority, one domain, for a declaration's `Authority` parameters.
  -- Same placement: an index slot's domain is read from that table.
  checkDeclAuthorityUses mctx prog
  -- #822: instance-head kind check for graded interfaces.  Same placement rationale
  -- as the line above for the HEAD-constructor half, which still reads
  -- `dataParamKindsRef` that `dataEnv` above has just populated.
  -- #1557 A-3.5c: the INTERFACE-slot half no longer reads a per-run table at all —
  -- it reads stage K's `CE` at this module's ordinal, mirroring `moduleImplUniv`'s
  -- arm-gated shape exactly. Standalone-list helpers build a single-module `CE` from
  -- `prog`, the very list `registerAllData (envFor mctx) prog` walked to fill the
  -- retired table, so the check does not go silent on a no-import `medaka check`.
  -- #1557 A-3.5a: this pair is now BOUND ONCE and read by TWO consumers — the graded
  -- impl-head check here and impl-completeness at the end of the body — hence the
  -- neutral name.  Binding once is not a style choice: `flatClassEnvOf` folds the whole
  -- decl list into a registry, so a second construction at the completeness site would
  -- pay that fold twice per flat compile, and the two copies could drift.  On Flat
  -- `fullUniverse = prog` (see its binding above), so `flatClassEnvOf prog` IS the
  -- `flatClassEnvOf fullUniverse` the completeness relocation calls for.
  let classEnvHere =
    let envs = gctx.declEnvsRef.value
    (envs.deIfaces, declEnvsOrdOf mid envs)
  checkGradedImplHeads mctx (fst classEnvHere) (snd classEnvHere) prog
  rejectCyclicAliases mctx prog
  -- #1280: `prog` reached here through a driver's stamping walk already, and
  -- `stampTyHead` is first-write-immune, so the builtins-only scope can only fill
  -- a head no driver could attribute — an `extern` written in a FLAT user file,
  -- where there is no module id and the primitive heads are all that is knowable.
  -- #2072: `userExternSchemes`, not `externSchemes` — this is the extern
  -- DECLARATION site (the program under check).  It builds the declared type
  -- verbatim; the two guards below are what hold a user extern to its row.
  let currentMethodRows = ifaceMethodSchemeRows mctx prog
  recordMethodGrants gctx currentMethodRows
  let visibleMethodRows = ifaceMethodSchemeRows mctx implDecls
  let visibleMethodRowIndex =
    methodRowsByIdentity
      (isNonEmptyL importerShadows)
      visibleMethodRows
      regEmpty
  let externS = userExternSchemes mctx (externTyOriginScope []) prog
  let globalS = legacyMethodSchemes currentMethodRows ++ externS
  -- #2074 / F1 (epic #2070): the USER-EXTERN DECLARATION guards, all gated on
  -- the same `ffiStampMode` ownership Bool — a stdlib-owned program's externs ARE
  -- the vocabulary and none of these rules owns them.  They run AFTER
  -- `rejectCyclicAliases` (`tc_decls`) so `expandAliasHeadTy` cannot recurse forever on a
  -- cyclic alias.  Order between them is not significant: diagnostics
  -- accumulate ([T-ERRORS-ACCUM]) and a signature can honestly fail more than one.
  --
  -- Four sibling loops rather than four arms inside one walk: each has its own
  -- exemption discipline (the crossable rule exempts a catalog-name
  -- redeclaration, the label and binding rules hold one to its `bind` clauses
  -- only, the shadow rule IS that exemption's admission test, and the
  -- catalog-row rule fires ONLY on a catalog name), and folding them together
  -- would force one `if` to speak for four notions of "this declaration is not
  -- mine".
  ffiCheckExternsCrossable mctx (ffiStampMode gctx mid) prog
  ffiCheckExternsLabelled mctx (ffiStampMode gctx mid) prog
  ffiCheckExternsShadow mctx (ffiStampMode gctx mid) prog
  ffiCheckExternsCatalogRow mctx (ffiStampMode gctx mid) prog
  -- (#4 cont) post-globalS mode setup.  Module: shadowMethodSchemes env layer (rebinding
  -- imported method names to the interface-method scheme) + the method-constraint cross
  -- seed (AFTER globalS's row registration, per installMethodPredicateSlots).
  let envSeed = extendVars dataEnv seed
  let shadowLayer =
    -- The rows remain local: they carry live scheme cells needed only by setup and
    -- must not become another graph-lived authority.
    let ifaceSchemes = legacyMethodSchemes visibleMethodRows
    -- #259/#2157: seed both halves from the same already-minted row selection.
    seedNumLitFromIntAnchor mctx visibleMethodRows
    -- #1351 L2 MIGRATE.  The importer-shadow layer now binds each shadowed method
    -- name to the scheme of the declaration THIS module's import scope admits
    -- (`methodScopeAt`), not to `lookupAssoc`'s decl-walk first match.
    -- Falls back to the bare-name answer on a miss — see `pickSchemesByDecl`.
    let sm =
      pickSchemesByDecl
        mctx
        importerShadows
        ifaceSchemes
        visibleMethodRowIndex
        moduleSeed.msImportedValues
    mctx.mcCells.methodPredicateSlotsRef :=
      mctx.mcCells.methodPredicateSlotsRef.value
        ++ gctx.crossRun.crossModuleMethodPredicateSlotsRef.value
    attachStandaloneSources moduleSeed.msImportedValues sm
  let envImported =
    annotateImportedMethodRows
      envSeed
      (importedMethodBindingNames gctx prog0 aliasSpellings)
      (nameableIfaceMethodSet gctx prog0)
      (namesToSet importerShadows omEmpty)
      visibleMethodRowIndex
  let envGlobal =
    extendVars (extendMethodRows envImported currentMethodRows) externS
  let env1 = extendBindings envGlobal shadowLayer
  let defs = funDefs progS
  let (topSchemes, groupedOut) =
    processTopGroups
      env1
      sigs
      defs
      (groupNames defs omEmpty)
      (namesToSet (publicValNames prog) omEmpty)
  recordTopBinderTypes gctx (omFromPairs topSchemes omEmpty) progS
  -- The tail bodies (impl, default, prop and test bodies) see the top-level
  -- bindings as the binding groups do (`processTopGroups`' result env): each
  -- binding keeps its standalone descriptor, so an occurrence of a top-level value
  -- spelled like a method resolves to the value in a tail body too.  Marking and
  -- inference read this one env.
  let tailEnv = extendTermBindings env1 topSchemes
  -- Module: the marked tree this call returns (the groups' marked clauses written
  -- back, the tail bodies marked with the module's final dict-name set) and its
  -- stamped twin, which the tail-body inference below reads.  Flat: `progS` is both.
  let progOut = match mctx.mcCells.markingRef.value
    Some mm => finishModuleMarking mm tailEnv groupedOut progS
    None => progS
  let progT = match mctx.mcCells.markingRef.value
    Some mm => stampTailDecls mm.mmTop progOut
    None => progS
  -- The module path runs a single inference pass; core is checked as its own
  -- invocation, which isolates the prelude's method bodies from a user binding
  -- that shadows an interface method (List Int vs Int).

  -- Unified impl-body inference form (Module arm, both drivers): inferUserImplBodies
  -- infers parametric heads and preserves diagnostics. allProg = implDecls
  -- (interfaces + accumulated impls) grounds the field types. See
  -- compiler/TYPECHECK-TARGET-ARCHITECTURE.md § "SA-10a. Landing log" (#2546, ARCH Q3a).

  let _ =
    inferUserImplBodies
      tailEnv
      implDecls
      (fst classEnvHere)
      (snd classEnvHere)
      progT
  let _ = inferDefaultBodiesIfEnabled tailEnv progT
  let _ = inferPropBodies tailEnv progT
  let _ = inferTestBodies tailEnv progT
  ()
  -- (#3) cross-module dict-threading SNAPSHOT — MODULE ONLY (flat SKIPS: running it would
  -- pollute the cross-module accumulators with a phantom single-file attribution).
  -- multi-line RHS: the indented `:=` form is legal but not seed-parseable yet (#1744)
  -- lint-disable-next-line rule-prefer-assign-op

  let _ = dedupPredicateSlotsTable mctx ()
  -- #1425: restore the rows the per-module view masked (see `selfNameRows`) — the view
  -- must not propagate as a graph-wide deletion into the next module's seed.
  let _ =
    setRef
      gctx.crossRun.crossModuleFunPredicateSlotsRef
      (predicateSlotTableWithoutArgs
        (mctx.mcCells.funPredicateSlotsRef.value
          ++ selfNameRows
            prog
            gctx.crossRun.crossModuleFunPredicateSlotsRef.value))
  let _ =
    setRef
      gctx.crossRun.crossModuleFunPredicateSlotsQualRef
      (attributeModuleEntries mid prog mctx.mcCells.funPredicateSlotsRef.value
        ++ gctx.crossRun.crossModuleFunPredicateSlotsQualRef.value)
  -- B-2.2-f (#1113): the sidecar's two snapshots, paired with the ids snapshots above.
  let _ =
    setRef
      gctx.crossRun.crossModuleFunConstraintDeclaredRef
      (mctx.mcCells.funConstraintDeclaredRef.value
        ++ selfNameRows
          prog
          gctx.crossRun.crossModuleFunConstraintDeclaredRef.value)
  let _ =
    setRef
      gctx.crossRun.crossModuleFunConstraintDeclaredQualRef
      (attributeModuleEntries
          mid
          prog
          mctx.mcCells.funConstraintDeclaredRef.value
        ++ gctx.crossRun.crossModuleFunConstraintDeclaredQualRef.value)
  gctx.crossRun.crossModuleMethodPredicateSlotsRef :=
    mctx.mcCells.methodPredicateSlotsRef.value
  let _ =
    setRef
      gctx.crossRun.crossModuleMethodPredicateSlotsQualRef
      (emptyMethodModulePredicateSlots mid prog
        ++ attributeMethodModulePredicateSlots
          mid
          prog
          mctx.mcCells.methodPredicateSlotsRef.value
        ++ gctx.crossRun.crossModuleMethodPredicateSlotsQualRef.value)
  -- #1114 (#845, DICT-SEMANTICS §4.2 D6(a)): snapshot THIS module's scheme contexts
  -- alongside the three arity tables above.  The arity tables carry only what
  -- `funConstraintsRef` holds, whose INFERRED half is gated on `dictEligibleSetRef`
  -- and is therefore EMPTY on the check path (see that ref's comment) — so an
  -- UNSIGNATURED constrained export was invisible to every importer at check time
  -- while `run`/`build` threaded its dict anyway.  `schemeObligationsRef` is the
  -- always-on store of the same fact and is what the SAME-module use site already
  -- reads; this makes the cross-module use site read it too, under the same
  -- source-exact (mid, name) key.
  let _ =
    setRef
      gctx.crossRun.crossModuleSchemeOblsQualRef
      (attributeModuleSchemeObls
          mid
          prog
          gctx.crossRun.crossModuleSchemeOblsQualRef.value
          mctx.mcCells.schemeObligationsRef.value
        ++ gctx.crossRun.crossModuleSchemeOblsQualRef.value)
  ()
  -- P0-17: impl missing a required method.  #1557 A-3.5a: ONE call, both modes — the
  -- arm split is gone because `classEnvHere` above already carries the mode's `CE` and
  -- its reading ordinal (Flat: a single-module `CE` over `prog`, which IS `fullUniverse`
  -- on that arm, at ordinal 0; Module: stage K's whole-graph `deIfaces` at this module's
  -- ordinal).  🚨 It must NOT read `declEnvsRef` unconditionally: that envelope is
  -- `emptyDeclEnvs` in compatibility helpers, so reading it there would make `ceRequiredAt` miss on
  -- every interface, and the miss arm is `[]` — every live rejection here would become a
  -- silent accept.  `classEnvHere`'s `Flat _` arm is what prevents that.
  checkImplCompletenessMap mctx (fst classEnvHere) (snd classEnvHere) prog
  -- (#5 / BREAK #2) obligation channels.  FLAT runs both channels + setNumlitFloats
  -- here so the per-module pass can
  -- stamp the Float-typed int literals, and a Flat consumer that read them unstamped
  -- would get Int cells where the inference said Float.  MODULE runs both channels
  -- here and leaves the Float stamp to the graph-end drain (`SSNumlitFloats`), on
  -- every driver (#2705).

  -- #1112 A-3.4 PR2: the obligation universe is now the `IE` projection bound ONCE
  -- as `moduleImplUniv` far above (see its block for the flip, the measurement, and
  -- why re-deriving it here would be a second whole-prefix rebuild for a value that
  -- cannot have changed).  The three `obUniv*` accumulators this used to read are
  -- deleted from `CrossRun`.

  let obUniv = moduleImplUniv
  -- #838 I4: unified checker, same `obUniv`.  Impl channel = (deferNonGround=True);
  -- call channel = (deferNonGround=False).
  -- #2705: BOTH channels run on EVERY driver.  A driver that infers impl
  -- bodies without checking their obligations lets a program `check` rejects
  -- reach codegen through `build`'s own elaboration.  `setNumlitFloats` is not called
  -- here on any driver any more: the Float literal stamp is `SSNumlitFloats`,
  -- first step of the graph-end drain every Module-arm driver now runs.
  let _ = recordLiveRoots mctx ()
  let _ = judgeQuiescentGoals mctx ()
  let _ = refileDeterminedRows mctx ()
  let _ =
    checkCallObligationsU mctx True obUniv mctx.mcCells.implObls.items.value
  let _ = checkCallObligationsU mctx False obUniv mctx.mcCells.obls.items.value
  let _ = settleDeferredPatLits mctx ()
  let _ =
    checkDeferredMatches mctx (reverseL mctx.mcCells.matchChecksDeferred.value)
  let _ = checkFixedWidthLiterals mctx mctx.mcCells.numlitRanges.value
  let _ = checkWideLiterals mctx mctx.mcCells.wideLitRanges.value
  ()
  mctx.mcCells.localSchemesOut :=
    mapLocalSchemes mctx mctx.mcCells.localBindRefs.value
  mctx.mcCells.seedSchemesOut := seed
  -- #154 PR-A: grow the persistent DATA-universe by THIS module's PUBLIC data, AFTER the
  -- module's inference is complete (so the copy+overlay above saw pub 1..k-1 and NEVER this
  -- module's own pub twice) — the register-time mirror of foldModules' `accData ++
  -- publicDataDecls prog` threading.  appendDataUniverse clobbers the working table refs,
  -- which are DEAD here (the next module's `freshModuleCtx` wipes them).  Flat leaves it untouched.
  -- A-3.2b residual (#1512): `mid` is BOUND here now — `appendDataUniverse`'s
  -- reload reads the alias universe at this module's own ordinal.
  appendDataUniverse mctx mid prog0
  let result = (
    ModuleBindings {
      mbSchemes = globalS ++ topSchemes,
      mbStandaloneSchemes = omFromPairs (reverseL topSchemes) omEmpty,
    },
    progOut,
    mctx,
  )
  closeScope mctx ()
  result
-- D2: check top-level `let rec` bindings for non-function members before
-- type-checking the DFunDef groups (the LetRecNonFunction guard,
-- which fires for
-- is_letrec=true groups — i.e. those coming from DLetGroup).

-- Phase 83/84 single-level: AFTER top-level inference (so the scheme output is
-- unchanged), and ONLY on the elaborate/dict path, infer each parametric impl's
-- return-position method bodies, registering the requires' element dict so the
-- inner ref routes RDict and the call site routes RKey + impl dicts.

-- Phase 69.x-e: likewise infer each interface DEFAULT body that carries a
-- method-level constraint (foldMap's default), registering the constraint var so
-- the in-body return-position ref (`empty`) routes RDict to `$dict_<method>_<slot>`.

-- Phase 4.55: type-check each prop body with
-- its declared params in scope.  This is what RESOLVES the EDictAt/EMethodAt route
-- refs the prepass marked inside a prop body — without it the routes stay empty,
-- and on the dict-passed eval path (DRIVER-COLLAPSE Phase 2 promotes the file's own
-- `=>`-constrained fns) the prop body would call a now-dict-passed `wf`/`fromList`
-- with no dict argument → under-application → `force` a partial closure → not VBool
-- → every prop "fails" (set's `fromList []` reported ill-formed).  The compiler
-- typechecker previously skipped props entirely (funDefs ignores DProp), so this
-- gap was latent until Phase 2's promotion exposed it.

-- Shape A (gap #44): ground a container literal's free result-element var THROUGH
-- the impl's method type, BEFORE the resolve* passes read the cells.

-- Error-path B4: now every method occurrence's dispatch type is fully resolved;
-- reject any whose concrete head type has no matching impl (the
-- `No impl of … for …` check).

-- Phase 4.55: infer each prop body with its declared params in scope, so the
-- prepass-marked EDictAt/EMethodAt route refs inside resolve.
-- Runs unconditionally (props are eval-only; the
-- emit/golden paths have no props): infer prop_body; unify t_bool.
-- A prop body is eval-only and is NOT dict-passed for operator dispatch: like the
-- OCaml oracle (which evals raw prop bodies against the marked env), its comparison
-- operators must stay PRIMITIVE EBinOps the eval builtin handles structurally, not
-- get stamped and rewritten to eq/lt method apps (whose dict route would then be
-- applied to a non-dict-passed comparison, panic: applied non-function).  So
-- bracket the goal channel around prop inference (`dropGoalsSince`): the routes
-- the prop body NEEDS (EDictAt for the file's promoted constrained fns, via the
-- dictionary-application and return-site goals) are still collected; only the
-- operator-rewrite goals the prop body would otherwise contribute are dropped.
inferPropBodies : TcEnv -> List Decl -> Unit
inferPropBodies env prog =
  let mark = goalsMark env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph ()
  inferPropBodiesGo env prog
  dropGoalsSince env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph mark [
    GKBinopSite, GKUnopSite, GKArithSite
  ]

inferPropBodiesGo : TcEnv -> List Decl -> Unit
inferPropBodiesGo env [] = ()
inferPropBodiesGo outer ((DProp _ name params body) :: rest) =
  -- The body's checks are located at the body (the declaration has no span),
  -- and its type at the value it returns.
  let env = envAtIfSome (exprSpanLoc body) outer
  let local = extendPropParams env params
  enterLevel env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  let parentScope = captureScope env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  let bodyScope =
    Scopes.freshScope
      (currentScopeStore env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph ())
      (Some parentScope)
      env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentLevel.value
      (Scopes.scopeFrame
        (currentScopeStore env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph ())
        parentScope).sfModuleId
      (PropOwner name)
  openScope env.teDyn.dcModule bodyScope
  let oblMark = wMark env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.implObls
  let callMark = wMark env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.obls
  let dictMark = goalsMark env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph ()
  unifyIn
    (dynAtIfSome (valueSpanLoc body) env.teDyn)
    (infer local body)
    (tconBuiltin "Bool")
  exitLevel env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  settleClosedBody
    env.teDyn.dcModule
    (tconBuiltin "Bool")
    oblMark
    callMark
    dictMark
  closeScope env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  inferPropBodiesGo outer rest
inferPropBodiesGo env (_ :: rest) = inferPropBodiesGo env rest

-- Phase 127 (restored 2026-07-11): typecheck each `test "…" = body` body,
-- requiring it to have type `Expectation` (a nullary TCon, so a plain nominal
-- unify).  Unlike props, test bodies ARE dict-passed (their `expectEqual`/… calls
-- come from `import test`), so this runs on the normal inference path with binop
-- stamping enabled (no snapshot/restore).  Without this, `test "x" = 1 + "str"`
-- and `test "x" = 42` slipped through `check` with zero diagnostics.
inferTestBodies : TcEnv -> List Decl -> Unit
inferTestBodies env [] = ()
inferTestBodies outer ((DTest _ name body) :: rest) =
  -- The body's checks are located at the body (the declaration has no span),
  -- and its type at the value it returns.
  let env = envAtIfSome (exprSpanLoc body) outer
  enterLevel env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  let parentScope = captureScope env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  let bodyScope =
    Scopes.freshScope
      (currentScopeStore env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph ())
      (Some parentScope)
      env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentLevel.value
      (Scopes.scopeFrame
        (currentScopeStore env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph ())
        parentScope).sfModuleId
      (TestOwner name)
  openScope env.teDyn.dcModule bodyScope
  let oblMark = wMark env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.implObls
  let callMark = wMark env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.obls
  let dictMark = goalsMark env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph ()
  -- #1110: `Expectation` is declared by `stdlib/test.mdk`, a USER-SPACE module —
  -- the checker fabricates this head from a literal and has no decl in view, so
  -- there is no identity to acquire.  `tconUnresolved`, not `tconBuiltin`: the
  -- language does not provide `Expectation`, and claiming §8 I6.2's
  -- program-global identity for a type some module declares would be a lie the
  -- shared carrier type cannot object to.
  unifyIn
    (dynAtIfSome (valueSpanLoc body) env.teDyn)
    (infer env body)
    (tconUnresolved "Expectation")
  exitLevel env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  settleClosedBody
    env.teDyn.dcModule
    (tconUnresolved "Expectation")
    oblMark
    callMark
    dictMark
  closeScope env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  inferTestBodies outer rest
inferTestBodies env (_ :: rest) = inferTestBodies env rest

-- A test or property body is a numeric boundary that publishes no polymorphic
-- result: nothing after it can determine its variables.  A variable below the
-- body's level (a property parameter, a value-restricted outer binding) belongs
-- to its enclosing binder and is held rigid, judged where it lives.  The body runs
-- the method-body settle sequence with an empty surviving set, then the verdict,
-- so a goal the body leaves open is judged here as a top-level binding's is.
-- [bodyTy] is the closed type the body was unified with.
settleClosedBody : ModuleCtx -> Mono -> Int -> Int -> Int -> Unit
settleClosedBody mctx bodyTy oblMark callMark dictMark =
  let level = mctx.mcCells.currentLevel.value + 1
  let addedObls = wWindow mctx.mcCells.implObls oblMark
  let bodyObls = addedObls ++ callUOblsWindow mctx callMark
  let rigidIds =
    outerRigidIds
      (Some level)
      (flatMap (uOblArgs mctx.mcGraph) bodyObls)
      omEmpty
  improveByUniqueImpl (dynFor mctx) rigidIds bodyObls
  determineByUniqueInstance mctx rigidIds bodyObls
  let withheld = finalizeNumBoundary (dynFor mctx) NumBoundary {
    nbDisposition = NumBoundaryOwnedMethodBody level,
    nbMembers = [bodyTy],
    nbSurvivingIds = omEmpty,
    nbDefaultObls = addedObls ++ calleeNumObls mctx callMark dictMark,
    nbAmbiguityObls = addedObls,
    nbGuard = NumGuard {
      ngGoals = bodyObls,
      ngRigidIds = rigidIds,
      ngOuterBelow = Some level,
    },
  }
  improveByUniqueImpl (dynFor mctx) rigidIds bodyObls
  determineByUniqueInstance mctx rigidIds bodyObls
  rejectUndeterminedVectors
    mctx
    rigidIds
    omEmpty
    addedObls
    (callUOblsWindow mctx callMark
      ++ nestedRequireGoals mctx rigidIds omEmpty bodyObls)
  rejectWithheldAmbiguity mctx rigidIds withheld bodyObls

-- bind each prop param `x : ty` as a monomorphic scheme in the env (fresh tyvars
-- for any free type variable in ty; props are normally concrete, e.g. `List Int`).
extendPropParams : TcEnv -> List PropParam -> TcEnv
extendPropParams env [] = env
extendPropParams env ((PropParam x _ ty) :: rest) =
  let scheme =
    monoScheme
      (fromAstType
        env.teDyn.dcModule
        (freshTvMap env.teDyn.dcModule (dedup (tyVarNames ty)))
        ty)
  extendPropParams (extendLocalVar env x scheme) rest

-- #760 (S1, check-vs-emit soundness): infer the USER program's impl-method bodies on
-- EVERY path, and check their obligations on every path (#2705).  A path that
-- inferred an impl body without checking its obligations, or checked without
-- inferring, lets a `deriving (Eq)`/`(Debug)` (or a hand-written impl) over a field
-- whose type lacks that instance `check` clean and `build` panic ("no impl of method
-- 'eq' for type 'Inner'").  Inferring the body records the field's `Eq Inner`
-- obligation via recordImplObligation, which the impl channel then rejects with the
-- SAME diagnostic a direct `==` already emits.
--
-- SCOPED TO THE USER decls (`prog0`), NOT the prelude (`coreProg`): re-inferring CORE's
-- own parametric impl bodies on the check path is heavier and pointless — core is
-- known-good (it builds + self-compiles), so only user impls need check-path inference.
--
-- SCOPED TO GROUND-HEADED impls (no type variable in the impl head).  A ground impl —
-- `impl Eq Outer`, the derived instance for a non-parametric type — only ever calls
-- methods on its fields' CONCRETE types, so every obligation it records is concrete:
-- checkImplObligations/checkCallObligations either finds the impl or emits the genuine
-- `No impl of Eq for Inner`.  A PARAMETRIC impl (`impl Eq (List a) requires Eq a`) instead
-- records obligations on its abstract element tyvar; those never ground on the check path
-- and would reach checkUndeterminedObligations, which reports a spurious `Ambiguous instance`
-- for any iface with >= 2 impls (it fired on EVERY program the moment core's own parametric
-- impls were inferred standalone — the prelude snapshot).  The emit path never exercised
-- that because it SKIPS the obligation gate.  Inferring only ground impls records the
-- concrete missing-instance rejects (the whole point of #760) while structurally avoiding
-- the abstract-element ambiguity.  A parametric impl over a concrete field (a rarer nesting)
-- stays deferred to `build` exactly as it was before #760 — a residual, not a regression.
--
-- DIAGNOSTICS PUSHED *DURING* body inference: #760 originally DROPPED all of them (snapshot +
-- restore typeErrors / typeErrorsSticky), because it only wanted the missing-INSTANCE rejects,
-- which are recorded as pendingImpl/CallObligations (side effects) that
-- checkImplObligations/checkCallObligations gate LATER — AFTER this returns — so dropping the
-- error accumulators did not lose a single missing-instance reject.  #777 (type mismatch) and
-- #782 (effect leak) then established that the type/effect errors the body inference itself
-- raises (e.g. an EFFECT LEAK: `putStr` in a pure-typed method body, or a body type mismatch)
-- are genuine soundness bugs that must reject symmetrically with top-level functions — so those
-- are now KEPT — and since issue 1146 they are kept because NOTHING REMOVES THEM: the
-- window that used to rebuild this list is retired (see the retirement note at the end
-- of inferUserImplBodies below).  Per-axis history follows.
-- #777 (S0, silent wrongness): a GENUINE type mismatch inside a ground impl-method
-- body (`sig _ = idInt "str"` where `idInt : Int -> Int` but `sig`'s declared return
-- is `String`) is a `unify`/`typeMismatch` error pushed DURING body inference, not an
-- obligation.  Blanket-restoring `typeErrors` here (as this did before #777) discarded
-- it, and because every driver that decides a build reaches this same body inference —
-- `check`'s directly, `build`'s through the `medaka_emitter` child's `elaborateModules` —
-- discarding it here makes `check` and `build` accept the program together: the built binary
-- then printed a wrong value at exit 0 or SEGFAULTED (an impl method returning a
-- differently-typed field/value).  We now KEEP those body clash errors so both paths
-- reject.
-- #782 (S2, ratified 2026-07-20): the effect axis is now enforced HERE too, symmetric
-- with top-level functions.  An effect leak in an impl-method body (`putStr` in a body
-- whose method signature declares no effect row) is a `T-EFFECT-LEAK`/`T-EFFECT-PARAM`
-- pushed DURING body inference, exactly like a body type mismatch.  Previously these two
-- codes were SUPPRESSED here (isSuppressedImplBodyErr) to spare the intentionally-effectful
-- `impl Speak Dog` in test/engine_fixtures/nullary_memo_with_args — but that made the
-- effect discipline the spec commits to (EFFECTS-SEMANTICS §method: an impl's latent row is
-- bounded by the signature) hold for top-level functions yet silently NOT for impl bodies.
-- The ratified fix is to STOP suppressing: the fixture's method now declares its concrete
-- `<Stdout>` row (`speak : a -> <Stdout> String`), so its body is bounded-by-signature and
-- stays valid, while a pure-signatured method that leaks an effect is now a real error.
-- Missing-instance rejects are unaffected regardless: they are recorded as
-- pendingImpl/CallObligations (side channel) and gated LATER, so they were never in this
-- window.

inferUserImplBodies : TcEnv -> List Decl -> ClassEnv -> Int -> List Decl -> Unit
inferUserImplBodies env allProg ce cur decls =
  let rpNames = returnPosMethodNames allProg
  -- GROUND heads (#760/#777): infer their bodies and KEEP the obligations they record
  -- — a ground impl only calls methods on CONCRETE field types, so every obligation is
  -- concrete and checkImplObligations either finds the impl or emits a genuine
  -- `No impl of <iface> for <field>` reject.
  let impls = locatedImpls None decls
  inferImplBodies
    env
    rpNames
    ce
    cur
    (filterList (i => implHeadGround (snd i)) impls)
  -- PARAMETRIC heads (#781, S0): a parametric impl head (`impl Sig (List a)`) is never
  -- reached by the ground filter, so a genuine non-literal type mismatch inside its
  -- method body (`sig _ = idInt "str"`, `idInt : Int -> Int` in a String-returning
  -- method) went unenforced end-to-end — `check`/`build` exit 0 and the built binary
  -- printed a wrong value.  Infer these bodies too so the `unify`/`typeMismatch` clash
  -- is surfaced (it is pushed to `typeErrors`, and kept because nothing removes it —
  -- see the retirement note at the end of this function), mirroring the
  -- ground-head fix.  BUT a parametric impl also records obligations on its ABSTRACT
  -- element tyvar (`impl Eq (List a) requires Eq a` → an `Eq a` obligation over an
  -- unground var); those never ground on the check path and would reach
  -- checkUndeterminedObligations as a SPURIOUS `Ambiguous instance` for any iface with
  -- >= 2 impls (it fired on every program the moment core's own parametric impls were
  -- inferred — the prelude snapshot).  So WINDOW the obligation channel across this
  -- pass and restore it afterward: the body-clash errors go through `typeErrors`, NOT
  -- the obligation channel, so windowing keeps the #781 reject while dropping the
  -- abstract-var false positives.
  --
  -- 🚨 #1114 (#792): THE ROLLBACK IS GROUND-PRESERVING, and it did not used to be.
  -- The two `wRestore`s below used to run bare, which threw away EVERY obligation the
  -- parametric pass recorded — including the GROUND ones, which are exactly the ones
  -- the abstract-var argument above does not cover.  `impl Foo (List a)` whose body
  -- calls `debug Bar` records a fully-ground `Debug Bar`; nothing about it is abstract,
  -- the gate would have rejected it on the spot, and the blanket rollback deleted it —
  -- so `check` exited 0 while `build` PANICKED (`no impl of method 'debug' for type
  -- 'Bar'`).  That is a `run_check_agreement` break, and the sentence this comment
  -- replaced ("stays deferred to `build` exactly as before — a residual, not a
  -- regression") named it as a known residual without naming its cost.
  --
  -- The policy is now written down: DICT-SEMANTICS §4.2 **D1** (a predicate the gate can
  -- decide where it is recorded is discharged there — no window may discard it) and
  -- **D6(b)** (a window that exists to suppress D3 false positives must filter by what is
  -- DECIDABLE, not discard wholesale).  So: window as before, then re-push exactly the
  -- obligations `uOblIsDecidableNow` accepts.  The abstract element tyvar of a parametric
  -- head is decidable by nothing, so every false positive the window was built to stop is
  -- still stopped.
  --
  -- ⚠️ The predicate is "the GATE can decide it now", NOT "it is ground" — those differ,
  -- and this site is where believing otherwise costs a verdict.  `uOblIsDecidableNow`
  -- carries the derivation and the counterexample (`Debug (Int -> Int)`); read it before
  -- touching either side.
  -- Re-pushed in `reverseL` order because `wWindow` yields newest-first (items are
  -- consed): reversing restores the original record order, which the gate reports in.
  let implOblsSnap = wSnapshot env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.implObls
  let callSnap = wSnapshot env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.obls
  inferImplBodies
    env
    rpNames
    ce
    cur
    (filterList (i => implHeadParametric (snd i)) impls)
  let keptImpl =
    filterList
      (uOblIsDecidableNow env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph)
      (wWindow env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.implObls (snd implOblsSnap))
  let keptCall =
    filterList
      (uOblIsDecidableNow env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph)
      (wWindow env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.obls (snd callSnap))
  wRestore env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.implObls implOblsSnap
  wRestore env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.obls callSnap
  wPushAll env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.implObls (reverseL keptImpl)
  wPushAll env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.obls (reverseL keptCall)
  ()

-- True for a DImpl whose head types carry NO type variable (a monomorphic receiver like
-- `Eq Outer` / `Debug (List Int)`); False for a parametric head (`Eq (List a)`) and every
-- non-impl decl (which contributes no impl body regardless).
implHeadGround : Decl -> Bool
implHeadGround (DAttrib _ d) = implHeadGround d
implHeadGround (DImpl { tys, ... }) = isEmptyL (flatMap tyVarNames tys)
implHeadGround _ = False

-- True for a DImpl whose head types carry AT LEAST ONE type variable (a parametric
-- receiver like `Eq (List a)`); False for a ground head and every non-impl decl.  The
-- exact complement of implHeadGround over DImpl decls, so the two filters partition the
-- impls without double-inferring any (and both skip non-impl decls).
implHeadParametric : Decl -> Bool
implHeadParametric (DAttrib _ d) = implHeadParametric d
implHeadParametric (DImpl { tys, ... }) = isNonEmptyL (flatMap tyVarNames tys)
implHeadParametric _ = False

-- C8b: default-body type-checking runs UNCONDITIONALLY (checks
-- ALL default bodies regardless of whether they carry method-level constraints),
-- on every driver — a driver that skipped the unconstrained defaults
-- (Ord.lt/gt/min/max, Foldable.length/isEmpty, Filterable.filter, …) would
-- silently accept a bad default body.  The constrained branch still registers dict slots (needed
-- for the emit/dict path); the unconstrained branch only type-checks — safe on
-- the plain-check path (activeDictVars mutation is harmless; reset by `freshModuleCtx`).
inferDefaultBodiesIfEnabled : TcEnv -> List Decl -> Unit
inferDefaultBodiesIfEnabled env prog = inferDefaultBodies env prog

inferDefaultBodies : TcEnv -> List Decl -> Unit
inferDefaultBodies env [] = ()
inferDefaultBodies env (d :: rest) =
  inferOneIfaceDefaults env d
  inferDefaultBodies env rest

inferOneIfaceDefaults : TcEnv -> Decl -> Unit
inferOneIfaceDefaults env (DAttrib _ d) = inferOneIfaceDefaults env d
-- Type each default body against the
-- interface's OWN method scheme (built from [typarams]+[methods]), NOT
-- `lookupVar env mname`.  On the flat single-file check path a user top-level
-- funDef can SHADOW a method name (e.g. map.mdk's `isEmpty : Map k v -> Bool`
-- shadowing Foldable's `isEmpty`); looking the name up in env would instantiate
-- that Map-typed shadow and infer the default `isEmpty t = match toList t`
-- against it, grounding the default body's container var to `Map` — so a default
-- every `Foldable` shares would be typed for ONE container.  The interface scheme is
-- shadow-free.  (Until #2769 gave `Map` a real `impl Foldable`, that grounding also
-- raised a spurious `No impl of Foldable for Map`; the mis-typing is the part that
-- does not depend on which impls happen to exist.)
-- Also extend env with these schemes so PEER-method refs in a default body
-- resolve to the interface methods (oracle's env_with_methods), not user shadows.
inferOneIfaceDefaults env (DInterface { name, typarams, typaramKinds, methods, ifaceOrigin, ... }) =
  -- #822: derived from THIS declaration, not from a name key (declGradedScope), and
  -- threaded down so the default bodies see the same Row slots the schemes were built
  -- with.  Computed ONCE per interface rather than per method.
  let dscope =
    declGradedScope env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph typarams typaramKinds methods
  let ifaceSchemes = methodSchemesPure env.teDyn.dcModule dscope methods
  let iface = IfaceRef { irName = name, irOrigin = ifaceOrigin }
  inferDefaultMethods
    (extendVars env ifaceSchemes)
    iface
    dscope
    typarams
    methods
inferOneIfaceDefaults env _ = ()

inferDefaultMethods : TcEnv ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List (String, List Kind) ->
  List String ->
  List IfaceMethod ->
  Unit
inferDefaultMethods env _ _ _ [] = ()
inferDefaultMethods env iface dscope typarams (m :: rest) =
  inferDefaultMethod env iface dscope typarams m
  inferDefaultMethods env iface dscope typarams rest

-- C8b: every interface default body is type-checked, constrained or not, by the
-- one method-body driver, against the interface's own signature for the method.
inferDefaultMethod : TcEnv ->
  IfaceRef ->
  List (String, List Kind) ->
  List String ->
  IfaceMethod ->
  Unit
inferDefaultMethod env iface dscope typarams (IfaceMethod mname mty (Some (MethodDefault pats body)) _) =
  inferMethodBody env iface DefaultBody (typarams, mty, dscope) mname pats body
inferDefaultMethod env _ _ _ _ = ()

-- ── PR3 keyed lookups (replace implMatches / implMatchesReceiver / findMatchingImplReqs /
-- implCountForIface).  Each first scans the concrete "iface|tag" bucket, then the iface's
-- headless bucket.  implMatchesU / bucketRecvMatch are EXISTENCE tests, so the
-- concrete-then-headless order is byte-identical to the old flat scan.  findMatchingImplReqsU
-- is first-MATCH and DOES depend on that order — a deliberate soundness/conformance fix,
-- documented on it below. ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

-- ── Error-path B4: missing-impl dispatch-obligation check ──────────────────
-- The `No impl of … for …` reject.  For each recorded interface-method occurrence, recover the types the
-- interface params resolved to at this site (dispatchMonosOf), and — ONLY when
-- they are all CONCRETE (a resolved head tycon, no remaining polymorphic var, so
-- a constrained-generic `Ord a =>` site whose receiver is still `a` is correctly
-- deferred to the caller) — verify the program declares a matching impl.  None →
-- `No impl of <iface> for <args>`.
-- #838 I4: the second obligation checker (checkImplObligations/checkImplObligationsU/
-- checkOneImplObligation) is RETIRED — impl obligations now route through the unified
-- checkOneCallObligation (so a rule lands ONCE).
-- #991: the `implOblToU` bridge that used to project a surviving
-- `pendingImplObligations` 5-tuple onto `UObligation` is GONE — both channels store
-- `UObligation` directly.  The projection it performed still happens at CHECK time and
-- in the same place: `uOblArgs`, via the `OpMethodOcc` arm (NOT `oblDispatchMonos`,
-- which special-cases Num → [] and would drop a numeric literal's operand).
-- Improvement, determination and defaulting at each group's close run BEFORE the gate
-- and ground the shared mono cells, so a determined multi-param goal's projected args
-- are already ground here.

-- PLAN.md #11: after HM + defaulting every source integer literal's type var is
-- ground (or a genuine `Num a` survivor).  Decide each literal's runtime rep
-- (3-way):
--   • ground Float ⇒ stamp the float cell + CLEAR the fromInt route (dref RNone) ⇒
