  let recordPop = env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph.crossRun.universeRecordPop.value
  let served = map (d => (d, overlayCachedRows ctorPop recordPop d)) overlay
  fold
    (_ p => match snd p
      None => recordDeclKinds env.teDyn.dcModule (fst p)
      Some _ => ())
    ()
    served
  let env1 =
    fold
      (e p => if isAliasDecl (fst p) then registerData e (fst p) else e)
      env
      served
  -- Cycles out before any field elaborates, as in `registerDeclsAliasesFirst`.
  rejectCyclicAliases env.teDyn.dcModule prog
  fold
    (e p => match snd p
      None => if isAliasDecl (fst p) then e else registerData e (fst p)
      Some rows => registerCachedRows e rows)
    env1
    served

-- The cached constructor schemes and record infos of [d], in variant order, when
-- every one of its constructors has a population row under its own identity; any
-- miss declines for the whole declaration.  Only `DData` has rows to serve, and
-- declining is never wrong: a declined decl is registered by `registerData`,
-- which is where a new `Decl` constructor has to be decided, so the final
-- clause covers every other constructor rather than naming each.
overlayCachedRows : SpellingPop Scheme ->
  SpellingPop RecordInfo ->
  Decl ->
  Option (List (String, Scheme), List (String, RecordInfo))
overlayCachedRows ctorPop recordPop (DData { dataCtors, dataOrigin, ... }) =
  cachedVariantRows ctorPop recordPop dataOrigin dataCtors
overlayCachedRows _ _ _ = None

cachedVariantRows : SpellingPop Scheme ->
  SpellingPop RecordInfo ->
  TyConOrigin ->
  List Variant ->
  Option (List (String, Scheme), List (String, RecordInfo))
cachedVariantRows _ _ _ [] = Some ([], [])
cachedVariantRows ctorPop recordPop o ((Variant cn payload) :: rest) = do
  ident <- mkIdent NsCtor o cn
  s <- spLookupIdent ident cn ctorPop
  recs <- cachedRecordRow recordPop ident cn payload
  later <- cachedVariantRows ctorPop recordPop o rest
  Some ((cn, s) :: fst later, recs ++ snd later)

-- A named-field variant's cached `RecordInfo`, as a zero- or one-row list; a
-- positional variant has none to look up.
cachedRecordRow : SpellingPop RecordInfo ->
  Ident ->
  String ->
  ConPayload ->
  Option (List (String, RecordInfo))
cachedRecordRow recordPop ident cn (ConNamed _ _) =
  map (ri => [(cn, ri)]) (spLookupIdent ident cn recordPop)
cachedRecordRow _ _ _ _ = Some []

registerCachedRows : TcEnv ->
  (List (String, Scheme), List (String, RecordInfo)) ->
  TcEnv
registerCachedRows env (ctors, recs) =
  fold (_ r => registerCachedRecord env.teDyn.dcModule (fst r) (snd r)) () recs
  fold (e c => addCtor e (fst c) (snd c)) env ctors

registerCachedRecord : ModuleCtx -> String -> RecordInfo -> Unit
registerCachedRecord mctx key ri =
  mctx.mcCells.recordByNameRef :=
    omInsert key ri mctx.mcCells.recordByNameRef.value
  mctx.mcCells.fieldOwnersRef :=
    addFieldOwners key (recordFieldNames ri) mctx.mcCells.fieldOwnersRef.value

-- ── dependency-ordered, SCC-merged letrec processing ──────────────────────
-- The prelude has forward references and mutual recursion throughout, so groups
-- must be type-checked in dependency order (a callee generalized before its
-- callers instantiate it polymorphically) with mutually-recursive cycles merged
-- into one letrec group (generalized together).  Mirrors the reference's
-- order_groups_by_deps + process_letrec_group (Phase 136).

-- ── Tarjan strongly-connected components (O(V+E)) ─────────────────────────
-- Replaces the former all-pairs-reachability + mutual-reachability SCC + topo
-- sort, which was O(n^3) in a module's top-level binding count and dominated
-- the multi-module typecheck (check_modules).  Emits SCCs in dependency-first
-- order (a "sink" component — no outside dependencies — finishes and is emitted
-- first), exactly what processSCCs needs.  State is held in module-level refs,
-- reset at the start of each run (processTopGroups runs sequentially per module).

-- sig-name presence set (which top-level names carry a type signature), set once
-- per module in `processTopGroups` so `memberPeelSource` does an
-- O(log n) presence check instead of an O(sigs) `lookupAssoc` scan per SCC member
-- (was O(members·sigs) over the whole compiler). Module-level ref, matching the
-- `currentFn`/`curEffect` idiom; processing is sequential per module.

sigNamesToSet : List (String, Ty) -> OrdMap Unit -> OrdMap Unit
sigNamesToSet [] m = m
sigNamesToSet ((n, _) :: rest) m = sigNamesToSet rest (omInsert n () m)

-- PERF: name → declared signature, the same `sigs` assoc list as an index.  Three
-- sites (preunifySigsEx, checkEffectEscape, checkSigConstraintOne) did
-- `lookupAssoc m sigs` — an O(N) scan of EVERY top-level signature, run per member
-- of every group, so O(N²) over a large file.  Companion to `sigNameSetRef`, seeded
-- from the same `sigs` in processTopGroups.
--
-- Built from the REVERSED list: `omFromPairs` is last-write-wins, while the
-- `lookupAssoc` it replaces was first-match-wins, so reversing preserves which
-- signature a duplicated name resolves to.

processTopGroups : TcEnv ->
  List (String, Ty) ->
  List (String, (List Pat, Expr)) ->
  List String ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  (List (String, Scheme), OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr)))
processTopGroups env sigs defs names exported =
  env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.sigNameSetRef := sigNamesToSet sigs omEmpty
  env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.sigTyMapRef := omFromPairs (reverseL sigs) omEmpty
  let grouped = groupClauses defs
  let ordered = tarjanSCCs names (depGraphMap names grouped)
  let result = processSCCs env sigs grouped ordered
  resolvePendingJoins env.teDyn 0
  let failures =
    EffectSolver.closeRootAuthorities
      env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.effectSummaries
      env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.rigidAuthvarsRef.value
      (exportedRootCells exported (fst result))
      (widenOpenedFor env.teDyn.dcModule)
  -- read again after the close: a cell the root solved no longer appears
  let unsolved = rootCellsOf exported (fst result)
  let unsolvedIds = fold (acc (_, ids) => IdMap.union acc ids) Tip unsolved
  reportEffectSummaryFailures
    env.teDyn.dcModule
    (filterList (f => not (failureMentions unsolvedIds f)) failures)
  let _ =
    fold
      (seen u => reportUnsolvedExport env.teDyn.dcModule grouped seen u)
      Tip
      unsolved
  result

-- The authority cells an exported binding's published type holds unquantified:
-- a binding the value restriction keeps monomorphic leaves its type's cells to
-- the module root.
exportedRootCells : OrdMap Unit -> List (String, Scheme) -> Map Int Unit
exportedRootCells exported schemes =
  fold (acc (_, ids) => IdMap.union acc ids) Tip (rootCellsOf exported schemes)

rootCellsOf : OrdMap Unit ->
  List (String, Scheme) ->
  List (String, Map Int Unit)
rootCellsOf exported schemes =
  flatMap
    ((name, scheme) =>
      if omHasKey name exported then match unquantifiedAuthIds scheme
        Tip => []
        ids => [(name, ids)]
      else
        [])
    schemes

failureMentions : Map Int Unit -> SummaryFailure ObligationSite -> Bool
failureMentions Tip _ = False
failureMentions ids failure = match failure.esfAuthority
  Some (lo, hi) =>
    anyList (c => IdMap.has (authvarId c) ids) (authVars lo ++ authVars hi)
  None => False

-- An exported binding whose published type (or residual context) still holds
-- a cell after the root solved: nothing in its module bounds it below, and an
-- importer cannot supply it later.  Each cell is reported once, at the first
-- exported binding that holds it; the obligations over it are this failure,
-- not separate ones.  Located at the binding's first located expression.
reportUnsolvedExport : ModuleCtx ->
  OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr)) ->
  Map Int Unit ->
  (String, Map Int Unit) ->
  Map Int Unit
reportUnsolvedExport mctx grouped seen (name, ids) =
  if IdMap.foldlWithKey (acc id _ => acc && IdMap.has id seen) True ids then
    seen
  else
    let loc = match clausesOf name grouped
      (_, body) :: _ => firstExprLoc body
      [] => None
    pushTypeErrorAt
      mctx
      "T-EXPORT-UNSOLVED-AUTHORITY"
      loc
      "exported binding `\{name}` has an authority in its type that nothing in this module determines; give `\{name}`, or the value it uses, a type signature that names the authority"
    IdMap.union seen ids
-- process each SCC as a letrec group in topological order.  The clause map is
-- threaded through and returned: a Module-arm group's clauses come back MARKED
-- (`processSCC`), and `checkBodyImpl` writes them back into the module's tree.
processSCCs : TcEnv ->
  List (String, Ty) ->
  OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr)) ->
  List (List String) ->
  (List (String, Scheme), OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr)))
processSCCs env _ grouped [] = ([], grouped)
processSCCs env sigs grouped (scc :: rest) =
  let (env2, schemes, grouped2) = processSCC env sigs grouped scc
  let (restSchemes, grouped3) = processSCCs env2 sigs grouped2 rest
  (schemes ++ restSchemes, grouped3)

-- The Num obligations of variables that reach a boundary only through a
-- constrained callee's instantiation (a where helper generalized as
-- `Num r => a -> r`, used as `debug (two ())`).  They are on the call and
-- dictionary-application windows, not the boundary's own (#23); a top-level
-- group and a method body default them like any other candidate.
calleeNumObls : ModuleCtx -> Int -> Int -> List UObligation
calleeNumObls mctx callN0 dictN0 =
  numCallObls mctx.mcGraph (callUOblsWindow mctx callN0)
    ++ numDictObls mctx.mcGraph (dictAppsSince mctx.mcGraph dictN0)

-- #23 support: synthesize impl-obligation-shaped Num entries from a group's
-- pendingCallObligations / pendingDictApps deltas.  The Num constraint of an
-- ambiguous var reaching a group ONLY through a constrained-callee instantiation
-- (`main = println (app2 (==))`) is recorded on those refs, never on
-- pendingImplObligations, so group-level Num defaulting (defaultGroupNumWith /
-- groundNumVarsWith, which both reads candidate ids AND finds the live var to ground
-- from impl-shaped entries) never saw it — leaving an ungrounded var whose Num dict
-- route resolves RNone → a NULL dict word → build-time SIGTRAP (run is correct).
-- Only field 0 (iface) and field 3 (the live operand mono) are read downstream;
-- the rest mirror inferNumLitBare's placeholder shape.
-- Num is 1-param, so its obligation vector is a singleton; a wider predicate can
-- never be "Num" and is filtered out anyway.
numCallObls : GraphCtx -> List UObligation -> List UObligation
numCallObls gctx [] = []
numCallObls gctx (o :: rest) = match (o.pred.iface.irName, uOblArgs gctx o)
  ("Num", [mono]) =>
    mkMethodOccObl
        (builtinIfaceRef gctx BNum)
        ["a"]
        (TyVar "a")
        mono
        []
        PNumLit
        o.loc
        o.uoScope
      :: numCallObls gctx rest
  _ => numCallObls gctx rest

numDictObls : GraphCtx -> List PendingDictApp -> List UObligation
-- #1155: the loc comes from the ENTRY's own snapshot.  This runs at a generalized
-- group close, well after inference left the call site, where the record's `mcLoc`
-- names no construct of the entry.
-- Behaviour-neutral by inspection rather than by hope: these synthetic entries feed
-- ONLY the Num-defaulting search (`NumBoundaryOwnedScc` →
-- `numConstrainedIds`/`groundNumVarsWith` → `numObligIds`/`liveNumVarGo`), and every one
-- of those readers destructures the 5th element as `_`.  Nothing renders it today;
-- the point is that the tuple stops carrying a span it knows to be wrong.
numDictObls gctx [] = []
-- B-4b-iii: SPELLING consumer of the widened route carrier — the `"Num"` test is a
-- name test against the prelude spelling, unchanged, so `.irName` is projected here.
numDictObls gctx (app :: rest) =
  flatMap
      (p =>
        if fst p == "Num" then
          [
            mkMethodOccObl
              (builtinIfaceRef gctx BNum)
              ["a"]
              (TyVar "a")
              (snd p)
              []
              PNumLit
              app.pdaLoc
              app.pdaScope,
          ]
        else
          [])
      (zipL (map (i => i.irName) app.pdaIfaces) app.pdaMonos)
    ++ numDictObls gctx rest

processSCC : TcEnv ->
  List (String, Ty) ->
  OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr)) ->
  List String ->
  (TcEnv, List (String, Scheme), OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr)))
processSCC outer sigs grouped0 members =
  -- The group's own checks (generalization, defaulting, its signatures'
  -- coverage) are located at its members' clause bodies.
  let env = envAtIfSome (membersSpanLoc grouped0 members) outer
  -- Marking on the schedule (ARCH §E): a Module-arm group is marked HERE, after
  -- every group it depends on has generalized, with the dict-name set as it stands;
  -- inference reads the stamped twin of the marked clauses.  Flat (`None`): the
  -- caller marked and stamped the whole program, the map is used as given.
  let marking = env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.markingRef.value
  let grouped = match marking
    Some mm => markGroupClauses mm env members grouped0
    None => grouped0
  let groupedStamped = match marking
    Some mm => stampGroupClauses mm members grouped
    None => grouped
  enterLevel env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  beginEffectSummaryScope env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  let oblN0 = wMark env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.implObls
  let callN0 = wMark env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.obls
  let dictN0 = goalsMark env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph ()
  let placeholders = map (m => (m, freshVar env.teDyn.dcModule ())) members
  let scopedMembers =
    scopeMembers
      env.teDyn.dcModule
      (captureScope env.teDyn.dcModule ())
      groupedStamped
      placeholders
  let (regs, sigTvMaps) = preunifySigsEx env.teDyn.dcModule sigs scopedMembers
  let savedRigidEffects = env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.rigidEffvarsRef.value
  let savedRigidAuths = env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.rigidAuthvarsRef.value
  env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.rigidEffvarsRef :=
    fold
      (roots member =>
        IdMap.foldlWithKey
          (acc id _ => IdMap.set id () acc)
          roots
          member.smDeclaredRoots.value)
      savedRigidEffects
      scopedMembers
  env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.rigidAuthvarsRef :=
    fold
      (roots member =>
        IdMap.foldlWithKey
          (acc id _ => IdMap.set id () acc)
          roots
          member.smDeclaredAuths.value)
      savedRigidAuths
      scopedMembers
  let env2 = extendBindings env (map scopedMemberBinding scopedMembers)
  -- P0-19 (constrained-receiver arm): publish THIS group's `=>`-constraint vars for
  -- the duration of body inference, so a definer-shadow method occurrence on one of
  -- them (`neq x y = not (eq x y)` under `neq : Eq a => …`) is seen as a DISPATCH and
  -- not monomorphised to the shadowing standalone's declared domain.
  -- `gcMonos` answers a SPELLING question (`dictVarSatisfiesIface`
  -- compares interface NAMES), so U1b (#1482) projects back to the name here rather than
  -- widening a second ref for a reader that would only throw the identity away.
  let groupCtx = GroupCtx {
    gcMonos = flatMap (r => flatMap ifaceMonoName (regIfaceMonosOf r)) regs,
    gcPendingEscapes = Ref [],
  }
  let groupEnv = { env2 | teDyn = { env2.teDyn | dcGroup = Some groupCtx } }
  -- #837: the schemeObligationsRef snapshot/restore window is RETIRED.  It existed
  -- because registerLocalScheme entries were NAME-KEYED and body-scoped: a prelude
  -- where-helper named `g` (core's `find`) leaked obligations onto an unrelated
  -- top-level `g` in a later body (a phantom `Num a =>` on types/numlit_bidir's
  -- signed fn).  Registration/lookup now key by (name, binding-id), so a top-level
  -- `g`'s use keys (g, its-id) and can never match a where-helper `g`'s (g, 0) entry.
  inferMembers groupEnv sigs groupedStamped scopedMembers
  fold
    (_ member => checkRecursiveValue env.teDyn member.smOwned)
    ()
    scopedMembers
  resolvePendingJoins env.teDyn env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentLevel.value
  let residuals =
    finishEffectSummaryScopeKeeping
      env.teDyn.dcModule
      (quantifiableAuthorities env2 groupedStamped scopedMembers)
      (fold (acc member => memberEffectRoots member acc) Tip scopedMembers)
      (fold
        (acc member =>
          borrowedEffectCells env.teDyn.dcModule member.smOwned.bsValue acc)
        Tip
        scopedMembers)
  env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.rigidEffvarsRef := savedRigidEffects
  env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.rigidAuthvarsRef := savedRigidAuths
  checkSigsTooGeneral env.teDyn.dcModule sigTvMaps
  checkSigsFixedByExpansive env2 groupedStamped scopedMembers sigTvMaps
  registerConstraintRegs env.teDyn.dcModule regs
  flushPendingEscapes env.teDyn.dcModule (Some groupCtx)
  exitLevel env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  -- PLAN.md #11 (locked §0.2): GROUP-LEVEL + per-binding Num defaulting.  Ground
  -- every ambiguous Num-only var to Int before this group generalizes.  A live var
  -- carried by a declared signature stays caller-determined across both passes;
  -- an argument-reachable var also stays polymorphic.  Body-only vars (`n = tag [1,2,3]`) still ground.  Scoped to
  -- THIS group's newly-added obligations (prepended at the front) so an earlier
  -- group's already-generalized var is never touched.
  let protectedSigIds = sccProtectedSignatureIds sigTvMaps
  let addedObls = wWindow env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.implObls oblN0
  let groupObls = addedObls ++ callUOblsWindow env.teDyn.dcModule callN0
  -- Determination holds rigid exactly the variables this group does not own: the
  -- declared ones and those in an argument position of a member's type, which the
  -- caller supplies.  A result-position or body-local variable is the group's.
  let unownedIds =
    omFromNames
      (map intToString (flatMap monoArgUnboundIds (map snd placeholders)))
      protectedSigIds
  improveByUniqueImpl env.teDyn protectedSigIds addedObls
  improveByUniqueImpl
    env.teDyn
    protectedSigIds
    (callUOblsWindow env.teDyn.dcModule callN0)
  determineByUniqueInstance env.teDyn.dcModule unownedIds groupObls
  -- #23: also ground an ambiguous Num var that reaches this group ONLY through a
  -- constrained-callee instantiation (its Num obligation lives on the call/dict deltas,
  -- not pendingImplObligations).  See numCallObls/numDictObls.  The synthetic entries
  -- feed ONLY the Num-defaulting search; addedObls alone still drives the
  -- ambiguous-constraint/scheme-obligation registration below.
  let defaultObls = addedObls ++ calleeNumObls env.teDyn.dcModule callN0 dictN0
  let sccGuard = NumGuard {
    ngGoals = groupObls,
    ngRigidIds = protectedSigIds,
    ngOuterBelow = None,
  }
  let withheld = finalizeNumBoundary
    env.teDyn
    NumBoundary {
      nbDisposition =
        NumBoundaryOwnedScc (env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentLevel.value + 1),
      nbMembers = map snd placeholders,
      nbSurvivingIds =
        tiedSurvivors
          env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph
          (map snd placeholders)
          sccGuard
          protectedSigIds,
      nbDefaultObls = defaultObls,
      nbAmbiguityObls = addedObls,
      nbGuard = sccGuard,
    }  -- RETPOS soundness
  -- Defaulting is a substitution like any other, so the goals it changed are
  -- improved and determined once more.
  improveByUniqueImpl env.teDyn protectedSigIds groupObls
  determineByUniqueInstance env.teDyn.dcModule unownedIds groupObls
  checkSigVarGoals
    env.teDyn.dcModule
    DeclaredBySignature
    protectedSigIds
    sigTvMaps
    groupObls
  let schemes =
    sccSchemes
      env2
      sigs
      groupedStamped
      (isLetrecGroup members)
      residuals
      0
      scopedMembers
  let scopedSchemes = alignScopedSchemes scopedMembers schemes
  checkSigsOverExpansive env2 groupedStamped sigTvMaps
  -- #23 two-hop forward: also record constraints FORWARDED from a constrained
  -- callee (living on the call delta, never in addedObls) into schemeObligationsRef,
  -- so a caller of this group re-instantiates them and its own group can ground the
  -- shared ambiguous var.
  -- The CALL delta is passed RAW (it already carries each predicate's joint `List
  -- Mono`); registerSchemeObligations maps it with forwardedVecObls so a multi-param
  -- predicate survives whole.  #838 I5: a constrained callee's DICT slot is forwarded
  -- through THIS same call delta — inferDictAtFound records it as a 1-ary PCallSlot
  -- obligation (recordCallObligations, beside pushDictApp), so the old `allDictObls`
  -- re-derivation off the dict delta was a redundant duplicate (deduped away) and is
  -- retired; addedObls now carries only the real pendingImplObligations delta.
  let callOblsDelta = callOblsWindow env.teDyn.dcModule callN0
  registerSchemeObligations
    env.teDyn.dcModule
    env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.schemeDefIdsRef.value
    sigTvMaps
    callOblsDelta
    addedObls
    schemes
  let liveIds = liveMemberIds env.teDyn.dcModule (map snd placeholders)
  rejectUndeterminedVectors
    env.teDyn.dcModule
    unownedIds
    liveIds
    addedObls
    (callUOblsWindow env.teDyn.dcModule callN0
      ++ nestedRequireGoals env.teDyn.dcModule unownedIds liveIds groupObls)
  rejectWithheldAmbiguity env.teDyn.dcModule unownedIds withheld groupObls
  -- SIGNATURE CONSTRAINT SOUNDNESS: a signed member whose body induces an
  -- interface constraint on one of its own quantified vars that its declared `=>`
  -- context (superclass-closed) does NOT cover severs the constraint for callers
  -- → wrong-dictionary dispatch (a silent wrong answer).  Reject at the def-site.
  -- Runs on every path; the census over compiler+stdlib+sqlite was 0 new failures.
  checkSigConstraintCoverage
    env.teDyn.dcModule
    regs
    sigs
    sigTvMaps
    callOblsDelta
    addedObls
    schemes
  registerInferredConstraints
    env.teDyn.dcModule
    sigs
    callOblsDelta
    addedObls
    scopedSchemes
  -- From here on every instance-head matcher holds this group's declared variables
  -- rigid; the group's own generalization above reads them as free variables, so a
  -- goal `checkSigVarGoals` rejected is not reported a second time.
  declareRigidVars env.teDyn.dcModule (omKeys protectedSigIds)
  -- The group's own occurrences of the members it just promoted (see
  -- `markRecursiveOccurrences`); Flat marks nothing here.
  let groupedOut = match marking
    Some mm =>
      markRecursiveOccurrences
        env.teDyn.dcModule
        mm
        placeholders
        scopedMembers
        grouped
    None => grouped
  match marking
    Some _ =>
      recordTopGrants
        env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph
        env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentModuleRef.value
        schemes
        groupedOut
    None => ()
  (extendTermBindings outer schemes, schemes, groupedOut)

scopedMemberBinding : ScopedMember -> (String, EnvBinding)
scopedMemberBinding member =
  let binding =
    optionOr
      (ordinaryEnvBinding
        (Forall
          []
          []
          []
          []
          (memberForce member)
          member.smOwned.bsRecursiveValue))
      member.smRecursive.value
  (
    member.smName,
    bindingWithStandalone binding (LocalStandalone, binding.ebValue),
  )

scopeMembers : ModuleCtx ->
  ScopeId ->
  OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr)) ->
  List (String, Mono) ->
  List ScopedMember
scopeMembers mctx _ _ [] = []
scopeMembers mctx parent grouped ((name, mono) :: rest) =
  let sid =
    Scopes.freshScope
      (currentScopeStore mctx.mcGraph ())
      (Some parent)
      mctx.mcCells.currentLevel.value
      (Scopes.scopeFrame (currentScopeStore mctx.mcGraph ()) parent).sfModuleId
      (BindingOwner name)
  -- This is the evaluator's topGroupValue distinction: a singleton nullary
  -- clause is a thunk, including a thunk whose result happens to be a function.
  let clauses = clausesOf name grouped
  let arity = match clauses
    (pats, _) :: _ => listLen pats
    [] => 0
  let owned = newBindingSummary arity (freshVar mctx) (freshEffectSummary mctx)
  let force = match clauses
    [([], _)] => Some owned.bsForce
    _ => None
  ScopedMember {
      smName = name,
      smMono = mono,
      smOwned = owned,
      smDeclaredRoots = Ref Tip,
      smDeclaredAuths = Ref Tip,
      smSigned = Ref False,
      smRecursive = Ref None,
      smForce = force,
      smForceBound = Ref None,
      smScope = sid,
    }
    :: scopeMembers mctx parent grouped rest

alignScopedSchemes : List ScopedMember ->
  List (String, Scheme) ->
  List ScopedScheme
alignScopedSchemes [] [] = []
alignScopedSchemes (member :: members) ((name, scheme) :: schemes)
  | member.smName == name =
    ScopedScheme {
        ssName = name,
        ssScheme = scheme,
        ssScope = member.smScope,
      }
      :: alignScopedSchemes members schemes
  | otherwise = panic "scope/member scheme alignment mismatch"
alignScopedSchemes _ _ = panic "scope/member scheme arity mismatch"

-- Extended Pass A: same as preunifySigs but also returns the tyvar maps (for
-- the signature-too-general check after body inference).  Returns a pair:
-- (constraintRegs, sigTvMaps) where sigTvMaps is [(name, sig_ast, tvs)] for
-- each signed member.
-- #1161 (F-3a-ii): each reg is now a TRIPLE — (name, slot-parallel (iface, mono) pairs,
-- slot-parallel predicate argument VECTORS).  The first two components are unchanged;
-- the third is carried alongside, never instead of, so nothing downstream that sizes or
-- orders dict slots can move.
preunifySigsEx : ModuleCtx ->
  List (String, Ty) ->
  List ScopedMember ->
  (List ConstraintReg, List (String, Ty, List (String, Mono)))
preunifySigsEx mctx _ [] = ([], [])
preunifySigsEx mctx sigs (member :: rest) =
  let m = member.smName
  let v = member.smMono
  let (restRegs, restTvs) = preunifySigsEx mctx sigs rest
  match omLookup m mctx.mcCells.sigTyMapRef.value
    Some ty =>
      member.smSigned := True
      let (signedMono, tvs, forceBound) = instantiateSigTracked mctx ty
      member.smDeclaredRoots :=
        effectRowRoots
          (optionOr pureRow forceBound)
          (effectRoots signedMono Tip)
      member.smDeclaredAuths :=
        authRowRoots (optionOr pureRow forceBound) (authRoots signedMono Tip)
      member.smForceBound := forceBound
      let (declaredScheme, declaredTvs) = sigToSchemeTvs mctx ty
      let (Forall ids eids aids _ declaredForce declaredValue) = declaredScheme
      let slots =
        declaredPredicateSlots
          (constraintVarIfaceMonos (sigConstraints ty) declaredTvs)
          (constraintVarArgMonos
            mctx
            (sigConstraints ty)
            (sigConstraintArgTys ty)
            declaredTvs)
      member.smRecursive := Some EnvBinding {
        ebValue = ValueScheme {
          vsScheme =
            Forall
              ids
              eids
              aids
              []
              (match forceBound
                Some _ => declaredForce
                None => optionOr pureRow member.smForce)
              declaredValue,
          vsDeclared = Some CDeclared {
            cdSlots = predicateSlotCSlots slots,
            cdPrefix =
              CDPLen (listLen (dedupSlotVecs (map predicateSlotView slots))),
            cdArgs = predicateSlotArgs slots,
          },
        },
        ebMethodRow = None,
        ebStandalone = None,
      }
      bindFrom (dynFor mctx) v signedMono
      let regs = [
        ConstraintReg {
          crName = m,
          crScope = member.smScope,
          crIfaceMonos = constraintVarIfaceMonos (sigConstraints ty) tvs,
          crArgVecs =
            constraintVarArgMonos
              mctx
              (sigConstraints ty)
              (sigConstraintArgTys ty)
              tvs,
        },
      ]
      (regs ++ restRegs, (m, ty, tvs) :: restTvs)
    None =>
      unify mctx v member.smOwned.bsValue
      (restRegs, restTvs)

-- Pass B: infer each member's clauses, unifying with its placeholder.
-- Phase 73 (bidirectional, signature-driven parameter typing): a member WITH a
-- signature peels its declared arrow types onto the clause parameter patterns
-- BEFORE inferring the body, so the body sees concrete parameter types (a
-- receiver-directed field access `f p = p.x` or a `String`-indexed `s.[0]`
-- resolves from the signature alone).  [peel] is Some(placeholder) for a signed
-- member, None otherwise; the placeholder already holds the sig instantiation
-- (preunifySigsEx unified it), and its shared tyvars accumulate unifications
-- across clauses exactly as the oracle's `sig_t` does.  Purely additive: the
-- per-clause `unify v arrow` below imposes the same equalities anyway.
inferMembers : TcEnv ->
  List (String, Ty) ->
  OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr)) ->
  List ScopedMember ->
  Unit
inferMembers env _ _ [] = ()
inferMembers outer sigs grouped (member :: rest) =
  let m = member.smName
  -- A member's own checks (its signature against its value, its forcing
  -- bound, its effect escape) are located at its clauses' bodies.
  let env = envAtIfSome (membersSpanLoc grouped [m]) outer
  let v = member.smMono
  openScope env.teDyn.dcModule member.smScope
  env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentFn := m
  let peel = memberPeelSource env.teDyn.dcModule sigs m v
  let effs = inferMemberClauses env peel member.smOwned (clausesOf m grouped)
  -- The signature is checked against the value the clauses return.
  if member.smSigned.value then
    unifyInto
      (dynAtIfSome (joinLocs (clauseSpans valueSpanLoc grouped [m])) env.teDyn)
      True
      member.smMono
      member.smOwned.bsValue
  match member.smForceBound.value
    Some bound =>
      fold
        (_ cl => recordFileBound env.teDyn.dcModule (snd cl) bound)
        ()
        (clausesOf m grouped)
      rowInto
        env.teDyn
        True
        (effrowNorm bound)
        (effrowNorm (optionOr pureRow member.smForce))
    None => ()
  env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.currentFn := ""
  closeScope env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  -- A value signature constrains the returned value, not the cost of forcing
  -- its initializer. That cost travels on the binding and is checked at uses.
  match member.smForce
    None => checkEffectEscape env.teDyn sigs m effs
    Some _ => ()
  inferMembers outer sigs grouped rest

-- The span of the named members' clause bodies (`exprSpanLoc`), joined.
membersSpanLoc : OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr)) -> List String -> Option Loc
membersSpanLoc grouped names = joinLocs (clauseSpans exprSpanLoc grouped names)

-- [span] of each clause body of the named members.
clauseSpans : (Expr -> Option Loc) ->
  OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr)) ->
  List String ->
  List Loc
clauseSpans span grouped names =
  flatMap
    (m =>
      flatMap
        (cl => option [] (l => [l]) (span (snd cl)))
        (clausesOf m grouped))
    names

-- The span of the expression whose value [e] is: a `let … in`, which has no
-- span of its own, returns its body's value, and a block returns its last
-- statement's.
valueSpanLoc : Expr -> Option Loc
valueSpanLoc (ELoc l _) = Some l
valueSpanLoc (ELet _ _ _ _ body) = valueSpanLoc body
valueSpanLoc (ELetGroup _ body) = valueSpanLoc body
valueSpanLoc (EBlock stmts) = match last stmts
  Some (DoExpr e) => valueSpanLoc e
  _ => exprSpanLoc (EBlock stmts)
valueSpanLoc e = exprSpanLoc e

-- the peel source for a member: Some placeholder if it has a signature (peel the
-- declared arrow domains onto the clause params), None otherwise
memberPeelSource : ModuleCtx ->
  List (String, Ty) ->
  String ->
  Mono ->
  Option Mono
memberPeelSource mctx sigs m v =
  map (_ => v) (omLookup m mctx.mcCells.sigNameSetRef.value)

-- zip-unify the equal-length prefix of param types and peeled sig domains; a
-- shorter [qs] (partial sig) pushes nothing past its end
-- Domains constrain the recursive placeholder as each clause is inferred.
-- Produced results join once after all alternatives are known: the first
-- clause must not fix a returned callback's row for its siblings.
inferMemberClauses : TcEnv ->
  Option Mono ->
  BindingSummary ->
  List (List Pat, Expr) ->
  List Atom
inferMemberClauses env _ _ [] = []
inferMemberClauses env peel owned clauses =
  let (values, effects) = inferClauseValues env peel owned clauses
  publishProducedResults env.teDyn owned values
  effrowLabels (collectRows (joinCellOf env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph) effects)

inferClauseValues : TcEnv ->
  Option Mono ->
  BindingSummary ->
  List (List Pat, Expr) ->
  (List (Option Loc, Mono), List EffRow)
inferClauseValues env _ _ [] = ([], [])
inferClauseValues env peel owned (cl :: rest) =
  let ce = inferClauseEff env peel cl
  -- A clause that does not fit the member's type is reported at the value it
  -- returns.
  let value = valueSpanLoc (snd cl)
  unifySourceDomains
    (dynAtIfSome value env.teDyn)
    (listLen (fst cl))
    owned.bsValue
    (fst ce)
  recordEffectBody env.teDyn.dcModule owned.bsBody (snd ce)
  let (values, effects) = inferClauseValues env peel owned rest
  ((value, fst ce) :: values, snd ce :: effects)

-- infer one clause, returning its arrow type AND the concrete effect labels its
-- body performs (captured in a fresh collection, then the ambient restored —
-- building a closure performs nothing).  Mirrors inferLam but exposes the effect.
-- Phase 73: when [peel] is Some(sig source) and the clause has params, peel the
-- signature's arrow domains and zip-unify them onto the clause param types BEFORE
-- inferring the body (bidirectional checking mode).
inferClauseEff : TcEnv -> Option Mono -> (List Pat, Expr) -> (Mono, EffRow)
inferClauseEff outer peel (pats, body) =
  -- The clause is located at its body: patterns carry no source Loc, so an
  -- over-applied-constructor / arity pattern error lands on this clause, and a
  -- body the parser leaves unwrapped (an application, an operator) is still
  -- located.  See the twin note in inferLam.
  let env = envAtIfSome (exprSpanLoc body) outer
  let lits = takePatLits env.teDyn.dcModule ()
  let pr = inferPats env pats
  peelOntoParams env.teDyn peel (fst pr) pats
  let scope =
    openExistentialScope
      env.teDyn.dcModule
      (takeOpenedExistentials env.teDyn.dcModule ())
  settlePatLits env.teDyn lits
  match peel
    Some src => recordClauseFileBound env.teDyn.dcModule body (listLen pats) src
    None => ()
  -- #2109: a signed clause's body is inferred AGAINST the signature's result
  -- type (result-first), so a fresh construction at a non-covariant slot meets
  -- the declaration while its own slot is still a metavariable.  See
  -- `inferExpected`.  An unsigned clause is byte-identical to before.
  let (bodyTy, bodyEff) = captureEffects
    env.teDyn.dcModule.mcCells.curEffect
    (joinCellOf env.teDyn.dcModule.mcGraph)
    (_ => match peel
      Some src => match resultAfterArrows (listLen pats) src
        Some expected =>
          let bodyEnv = extendLocalVars env (snd pr)
          checkedInto
            bodyEnv
            body
            expected
            (inferExpected bodyEnv body expected)
        None => infer (extendLocalVars env (snd pr)) body
      None => infer (extendLocalVars env (snd pr)) body)
  closeExistentialScope env.teDyn.dcModule scope bodyTy (exprLoc body)
  (arrowsWithLastEffect (fst pr) bodyEff bodyTy, bodyEff)

-- Phase 73 peel: for a signed clause with params, zip-unify the peeled sig
-- domains onto the inferred param types.  No-op for an unsigned member, a value
-- binding (no params), or a sig with no remaining arrows.
peelOntoParams : DynCtx -> Option Mono -> List Mono -> List Pat -> Unit
peelOntoParams dyn None _ _ = ()
peelOntoParams dyn (Some _) _ [] = ()
peelOntoParams dyn (Some src) patTypes pats =
  zipBindFrom dyn patTypes (peelArrows (listLen pats) src)

-- A local binding carries no signature of its own.
localRole : Bool -> BindingRole
localRole True = RoleQuantifies
localRole False = RoleMonomorphic

-- Runs in a carry of [prev], the caller's record, in its graph record with a fresh
-- graph run.
methodReturnProbeStamp : ModuleCtx ->
  MethodSchemeRow ->
  MethodSchemeRow ->
  List Decl ->
  (String, String, String)
methodReturnProbeStamp prev ownedRow foreignRow impls =
  let gctx = GraphCtx { prev.mcGraph | graphRun = freshGraphRun () }
  let mctx = carryModuleCtx gctx prev
  let scope = methodReturnProbeScope mctx "return-owner-stamper"
  let request = methodReturnProbeRequest mctx ownedRow
  methodReturnProbeSpelling mctx foreignRow
  let env = buildFlatImplEnv impls
  mctx.mcCells.bodyImplEnvRef := env
  let tagRef = Ref RNone
  let implRef = Ref []
  let resultMono = stripArrows request.mrrOccurrence
  resolveExactReturnSite
    (siteFor mctx)
    omEmpty
    "make"
    tagRef
    implRef
    resultMono
    request
    ""
    None
    scope
  let goals = optionOr [] (methodReturnArgs gctx request)
  let ownedKey =
    match ieSelectRowByIface (siteFor mctx) env ownedRow.msrIface goals
      Some selected => rowRouteKey selected
      None => ""
  let foreignKey =
    match ieSelectRowByIface (siteFor mctx) env foreignRow.msrIface goals
      Some selected => rowRouteKey selected
      None => ""
  (methodReturnProbeRouteKey tagRef.value, ownedKey, foreignKey)

-- The request is created before the spelling table is pointed at Foreign.  The checker
-- must still reject a graph containing only Foreign's impl, its positive control must
-- accept Owner's impl, and the stamper must select Owner's distinct route.
methodReturnOwnershipProbe : Unit -> (List String, List String, Bool, Bool)
methodReturnOwnershipProbe _ =
  let ownedGraph = probeGraphCtx ()
  let ownedDecl =
    methodReturnProbeIface
      "return-owner"
      "Owner"
      (TyFun (tyConBuiltin "Unit" None) (TyVar "a"))
  let foreignDecl =
    methodReturnProbeIface
      "return-foreign"
      "Foreign"
      (TyFun (tyConBuiltin "Unit" None) (TyVar "a"))
  let ownedCtx = initialModuleCtx ownedGraph
  let ownedRow = firstMethodRow (ifaceMethodSchemeRows ownedCtx [ownedDecl])
  let foreignGraph = GraphCtx { ownedGraph | graphRun = freshGraphRun () }
  let foreignCtx = carryModuleCtx foreignGraph ownedCtx
  let foreignRow =
    firstMethodRow (ifaceMethodSchemeRows foreignCtx [foreignDecl])
  let ownedImpl = methodReturnProbeImpl "return-owner" "Owner"
  let foreignImpl = methodReturnProbeImpl "return-foreign" "Foreign"
  let (rejected, rejectedCtx) =
    methodReturnProbeCodes foreignCtx ownedRow [foreignImpl]
  let (accepted, acceptedCtx) =
    methodReturnProbeCodes rejectedCtx ownedRow [foreignImpl, ownedImpl]
  let (actualKey, ownedKey, foreignKey) = methodReturnProbeStamp
    acceptedCtx
    ownedRow
    foreignRow
    [foreignImpl, ownedImpl]
  let observed = (
    rejected,
    accepted,
    actualKey == ownedKey,
    actualKey /= foreignKey,
  )
  observed

-- > methodReturnOwnershipProbe ()
-- (["T-NO-IMPL"], [], True, True)

regIfaceMonosOf : ConstraintReg -> List (IfaceRef, List Mono)
regIfaceMonosOf reg = reg.crIfaceMonos

-- U1b (#1482): project a reg's (interface occurrence, mono) pair back to the SPELLING
-- for `gcMonos`, whose only reader (`dictVarSatisfiesIface`) compares
-- interface NAMES.
-- ⚠️ S-dict-arity-contract: a reg entry is now ONE PREDICATE carrying ALL its bare-tyvar
-- monos, so this fans back out to one (name, mono) pair per variable.  Collapsing the
-- SLOT must not collapse the READ-ONLY census this and `declaredPairOne` feed: they
-- answer "is this variable declared at this interface", not "how many dicts", and
-- dropping `b` from `Ix a b =>` would make a body use at `b` UNCOVERED — an
-- over-rejection of a program that type-checks today.
ifaceMonoName : (IfaceRef, List Mono) -> List (String, Mono)
ifaceMonoName (ir, monos) = map (mono => (ir.irName, mono)) monos

-- Render accumulated type errors as `TYPE ERROR: <msg>` lines (in order of
-- occurrence — typeErrors accumulates newest-first, so reverse).
typeErrorLines : List String -> List String
typeErrorLines [] = []
typeErrorLines (e :: rest) = "TYPE ERROR: " ++ e :: typeErrorLines rest

-- #415 item 1: the seeding PREAMBLE every runtime-seeded entry point runs before its
-- typecheck pass — the head half of the sandwich whose tail is `runFinalChecks`.
-- [oracleDecls] is the decl set the ctor oracle is built from: the ONE axis the callers
-- legitimately differ on (the flat paths pass `prog`; checkModuleFullDiags passes
-- `prog ++ accData` own-module-FIRST — see the P0-9 note there, that order is load-bearing).
-- The module's mint (`checkBodyImpl`) installs the seed: this oracle and an empty
-- warnings list.
seedCheckRun : List Decl -> CheckRunSeed
seedCheckRun oracleDecls = CheckRunSeed {
  crsOracle = buildOracle oracleDecls,
  crsWarnings = [],
}

-- #415 item 1: seed-and-run for the three FLAT runtime-seeded entry points
-- (the `checkOne*` wrappers). They
-- used to repeat this body verbatim under a "Mirrors checkToLinesWithRuntime's
-- side-effects EXACTLY" comment — a mirror obligation enforced only by that comment.
-- They now differ ONLY in what they HARVEST from the accumulators afterwards, so the
-- seeding+coherence they share has exactly one body and cannot drift.
-- ⚠️ trap #5, same as runFinalChecks: coherence sees the driver-staged USER decls only,
-- NEVER `prog`.  A user impl deliberately overrides a seeded prelude impl, so feeding
-- the seeded set to checkCoherence false-positives on the stdlib itself.
-- ── type-aware non-exhaustive-match check (the `check_match` driver) ────────
-- Run the full typecheck pass over [prog] (runtime externs seeded, NO prelude —
-- mirrors the reference's check_program_no_prelude oracle) and return one
-- `Warning: non-exhaustive match …` line per `match` that isn't exhaustive.
-- The oracle is built from the program's own data decls + the syntactic builtins
-- (same set check_match's env-backed oracle has in the no-prelude path).  Diffs
-- against `dev/diagdump.exe --check-match` (the harness sorts).
-- ── diagnostics entry point (compiler/driver/diagnostics.mdk bridge) ────────────
-- Run the full typecheck pass (runtime-seeded) over [prog] and return the
-- accumulated errors and non-exhaustive-match warnings as `TcDiag`s — each
-- carrying its own code, span (B.10.2b / S4), message, and optional help/fix —
-- so diagnostics.mdk maps them straight to structured `Diag` values.
-- ── multi-module typecheck (bootstrap front-end) ───────────────────────────
-- Threads per-module exports in dependency order.  The prelude (core) is checked
-- ONCE and ALL its schemes + ctors seed every module (it's implicitly visible);
-- each compiler module then contributes only its PUBLIC value schemes — private
-- helpers stay module-local, so same-named helpers across modules never collide
-- (the per-module-frame property, without a frame) — plus its public ctors.
-- Returns each module's OWN value schemes, in load order.

-- typecheck one program with seeded value schemes + accumulated data decls, as
-- the prelude's core pass.  Re-registers prior modules' public data declarations
-- (`accData ++ prog`) so imported constructors AND named-field-variant record
-- info (e.g. ast's DInterface) resolve.  The program's own impls are its impl
-- universe, as the tree arm's core pass (`elabModuleStamp`) has them: an impl
-- body's occurrence then routes through the impl's `requires` given on both arms.
-- Returns the module's own value schemes.  [prev] is the record current before the
-- pass, whose oracle and warnings the unseeded pass carries.
checkModuleFull : ModuleCtx ->
  List (String, Scheme) ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  (ModuleBindings, List Decl, ModuleCtx)
checkModuleFull prev seedVars accData prog =
  checkModuleFullImpl
    prev.mcGraph
    (checkRunResidue prev)
    ""
    (plainModuleSeed seedVars)
    accData
    prog
    prog

-- E5: like checkModuleFull but takes [implDecls] (core + every EARLIER module — NOT this
-- module: foldModules only grows the accumulator for LATER modules, so a module is never in
-- its own [implDecls]; a caller that needs this module's own decls too must fold [prog] in
-- itself, as the `superDecls` binding in checkBodyImpl does for #1457) as the impl-body
-- inference universe.  It ALSO infers THIS module's parametric impl
-- bodies, so their
-- ARG-position ELEMENT dispatch (`eq`/`compare`/… on the impl head tyvar) reaches
-- inferMethodAt and lands in pendingArgStamps, which elabModuleStamp's
-- resolveArgStamps then stamps RDict (via the requires dict registered by
-- registerImplRequires).  The stage-K ClassEnv gives body inference the interface
-- declarations, while [implDecls] lets a body dispatch against an earlier module's impl.
-- [gctx] and [runSeed] are the drive's graph record and the module's check-run seed,
-- passed to its mint (see `checkBodyImpl`), and the module's record is returned beside
-- its bindings.
checkModuleFullImpl : GraphCtx ->
  CheckRunSeed ->
  String ->
  ModuleSeed ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  (ModuleBindings, List Decl, ModuleCtx)
checkModuleFullImpl gctx runSeed mid seedVars _accData implDecls prog =
  let (schemes, marked, mctx) =
    checkBodyImpl gctx runSeed seedVars mid implDecls prog
  -- #2705 (M2 phase 2): solving is not optional.  Every module a Module-arm driver
  -- checks — `check`, `run`, `build`, the LSP alike — cuts its stamping context
  -- here, at the point its stampers used to run, for the one graph-end drain
  -- (`drainStampQueue`, DICT §6.2 T4).  A driver that queues and never drains
  -- leaves the queue for the next driver entry, so every Module-arm driver ends
  -- with a drain (`driveGraphK`'s, or `checkGraphFinish` on a memo path).
  enqueueStampCtx mctx mid implDecls
  (schemes, marked, mctx)
-- C5: compute this module's standalone-shadow set BEFORE inference, so the
-- inferMethodAt arg-position record can gate on it (`freshModuleCtx` cleared it via
-- pendingRLocalSites, but standaloneValuesRef is set fresh here per module).
--
-- Two flavours of standalone-shadow, BOTH needing RLocal recording so a method
-- call on a no-impl receiver routes to the standalone instead of mis-dispatching:
--   • IMPORTER shadow (`importerShadows`): a name imported from a sibling that is
--     also an interface method (box importing map's `toList`).  Its scheme must be
--     REBOUND to the interface-method scheme (`shadowMethodSchemes`) so the call
--     site types polymorphically; RLocal then redirects the no-impl receiver back.
--   • DEFINER shadow (`definerShadows`): a name THIS module defines as a top-level
--     funDef that ALSO names an interface method (map-as-root's own `toList` /
--     `isEmpty`).  The MARK pass (`buildStandaloneShadowsGraph`) rewrites these to
--     `EMethodAt`, so without a matching RLocal record the route falls back to the
--     result-type `RKey` (e.g. `toList`'s `List` result), dispatching the method on
--     the WRONG impl (List's `toList = identity`) → `debug`/`display` recurse on the
--     unchanged receiver forever (Map Debug/Eq/Ord impl bodies call standalone
--     `toList`).  These must be RECORDED for RLocal but must NOT be rebound to the
--     method scheme — their local standalone scheme (`Map k v -> …`) is what the
--     impl body types against.

-- E6: re-install the cross-module constraint accumulator that `freshModuleCtx` just
-- wiped, so this module's `=>`-constrained call sites into EARLIER modules resolve.
-- Post-ARGSTAMP-UNIFY (Phase 4): eval and emit both thread dicts, so this runs
-- UNCONDITIONALLY on every path (single elaboration mode).

-- `methodEntryHere` answers from stage K's whole-graph `deMethods` (core, earlier
-- modules and this prog), so resolveSite's ifaceParamMonos can recover a multi-param
-- interface's full param monos (the element grounding `e` for `FromEntries c e`).
-- An empty table on the module path would make ifaceParamMonos return None → a
-- Set/Map-literal return-position `fromEntries` route drops its `Ord` element dict →
-- null dict → SIGSEGV.

-- C5: a standalone-shadow method name (box's `toList`/`isEmpty`) is bound in
-- seedVars to its imported MONOMORPHIC standalone scheme (`Box k v -> …`), which
-- would shadow the polymorphic interface-method scheme and mis-type a genuine
-- method call (`isEmpty [1,2,3]` unifying List with Box).  Re-bind those names to
-- the graph-wide METHOD scheme so the call site types against the method; RLocal then redirects only the no-impl receiver back to the standalone
-- at eval: the EApp method-head arm types against the
-- method scheme even when a standalone value holds the name.
-- DEFINER shadows are EXCLUDED here: the module's OWN funDef (map-root's `toList`)
-- must type against its local standalone scheme (`Map k v -> List (k, v)`), not the
-- imported method scheme — the impl bodies call it ON a Map.  Only IMPORTER shadows
-- (imported-from-sibling method names) get the method-scheme rebind.

-- E5: infer this module's parametric impl bodies (gated, emit path only), seeing
-- [implDecls] for interface method types + cross-module impl dispatch.  The sites
-- it records stay in pendingArgStamps/pendingSites for elabModuleStamp to resolve.

-- C8(b): also infer THIS module's interface DEFAULT bodies (gated identically to
-- the single-file path's inferDefaultBodiesIfEnabled) so a default body's type
-- error is caught on every path.

-- Phase 4.55: infer this
-- module's prop bodies so their prepass-marked EDictAt/EMethodAt routes resolve.
-- The multi-module test path (runPropsMulti) evaluates the ELABORATED prop body
-- against the dict-passed env, so the body's calls into the file's own promoted
-- `=>`-constrained fns (set's `wellFormed`/`fromList`) need their dict-arg routes
-- filled here — otherwise the call under-applies the dict-passed callee → not VBool
-- → every prop "fails".  funDefs ignores DProp, so without this the module path
-- never typed props at all.

-- E6: fold THIS module's freshly-registered fn-constraints into the cross-module
-- accumulator so a LATER module's call site finds them after its own reset.
-- Post-ARGSTAMP-UNIFY (Phase 4): unconditional on every path (single elaboration mode).

-- Shape A (gap #44): ground a container literal's free result-element var THROUGH
-- the unique impl's method type, so this module's pending sites/arg-stamps resolve
-- against the GROUNDED element (Set Int, not Set _a).  [implDecls] is the full impl
-- universe (core ++ earlier modules ++ prog), so the Set/Map impls are visible.

-- public top-level value names (the pub flag may sit on the sig, def, or extern).
-- C8(a): a PUBLIC interface ALSO exports its method names so an importer can see
-- their schemes — methods of an
-- `is_pub = true` interface are appended to the exported value schemes.
publicValNames : List Decl -> List String
publicValNames [] = []
publicValNames ((DAttrib _ d) :: rest) =
  publicValNames [d] ++ publicValNames rest
publicValNames ((DFunDef True n _ _ _ _) :: rest) = n :: publicValNames rest
publicValNames ((DTypeSig True n _ _) :: rest) = n :: publicValNames rest
publicValNames ((DExtern (ExternDecl { edPub = True, edName = n, ... })) :: rest) =
  n :: publicValNames rest
publicValNames ((DInterface { pub = True, methods, ... }) :: rest) =
  ifaceMethodNames methods ++ publicValNames rest
publicValNames (_ :: rest) = publicValNames rest

-- ⚠️ #1557 A-3.5a REMOVED THE COMPLETENESS LINE from this fold, with the
-- `universeIfaceRequiredRef` cell and its `insertIfaceRequired` writer.  The ordering
-- guarantee of this fold, which `checkBodyImpl`'s Module arm calls BEFORE the shadow
-- reads so that this module's own decls are visible at the read, is no longer what
-- impl-completeness depends on: it reads stage K's `CE`, whose rows
-- carry their declaring module's ordinal, and `declEnvVisibleAt cur o` (`o <= cur`)
-- admits the reader's OWN row — the same 0..cur-inclusive prefix the accumulator held
-- here.  Do not re-add a completeness accumulator to restore an ordering property that
-- has moved onto the ordinal predicate.
appendUniverseAccums : GraphCtx -> String -> List Decl -> Unit
appendUniverseAccums gctx mid prog =
  -- 🚨 SHADOW-SEMANTICS S1-PRELUDE (a), RULED 2026-08-10 (#1375 item 2, #1499 clause (b)):
  -- The prelude is not S1's left (standalone) operand.  The asymmetry with the shadow
  -- builders' interface-method test, `methodNameDeclaredAt`, which counts the prelude's
  -- interfaces at ordinal 0, is deliberate and is S1-PRELUDE's own
  -- (`SHADOW-SEMANTICS.md:225`): S1's INTERFACE operand is the wider "nameable in M",
  -- which INCLUDES the prelude, while its STANDALONE operand is pinned by the
  -- definer/importer kind partition — and a standalone reaching M only as an implicit
  -- prelude export is NEITHER kind, so it creates no shadow in M.
  -- This ref's ONE reader is the `importerShadows` binding in `checkBodyImpl`
  -- (`standaloneShadowsFromSet`'s `fnSet`), i.e. exactly that left operand; folding the
  -- prelude's own funDefs in admitted every prelude standalone as an IMPORTER shadow —
  -- the reading S1-PRELUDE names and REJECTS by consequence — so a user interface method
  -- colliding with `isEven`/`count` fell back to the prelude function at any receiver head
  -- carrying no impl, ACCEPTING at exit 0 where the ruling requires a located reject
  -- (`test/shadow_fixtures/x1_prelude_standalone_not_left_operand.mdk`, x2, matrix rows
  -- 46-48).  ⚠️ SUBTRACTING the prelude's names at the READ site instead would be WRONG:
  -- a name the prelude AND a real user module both define IS imported into M by the user
  -- module and DOES create a shadow there.  Not folding is what expresses "contributes
  -- nothing"; the union still carries the name via whichever user module defines it.
  if isPreludeMid mid then
    ()
  else
    gctx.crossRun.universeFunNamesRef :=
      namesToSet
        (map fst (funDefs prog))
        gctx.crossRun.universeFunNamesRef.value
  -- #154 PR-B: grow the dispatch-index accumulator by THIS module's interface indices.
  -- APPEND (universe first) so the accumulated list stays in the same core-first order the
  -- old `argDispatchIndices (accAll ++ prog)` flatMap produced.  #1351 L5 (CONTRACT) deleted
  -- the bare-name accumulator that used to be grown alongside this one: its only reader was
  -- `dispatchIdxScoped`'s fall-back arm, and the reader is now identity-keyed only, so a
  -- prior-module entry this module never names cannot be queried by spelling at all.
  gctx.crossRun.universeMethodDispatchIdxByIdRef :=
    gctx.crossRun.universeMethodDispatchIdxByIdRef.value
      ++ argDispatchIndicesById prog
  -- #1112 A-3.4 PR2: the #154 PR3 leg that grew the three `obUniv*` obligation-universe
  -- accumulators here is GONE.  Its consumer — the Module arm's `obUniv` — now projects
  -- stage K's `IE` at the reader's ordinal instead (`ieUniverseAt`), so this fold was
  -- building a second copy of a table nothing reads.  Note what that makes this function:
  -- it no longer answers "what impls exist" at all; every remaining line here is an
  -- interface/method/name-side accumulator.  Do not re-add an impl accumulator — the whole
  -- point of the flip is that `IE` is the one answer, and a second one is design law L1's
  -- divergence.
  ()

-- Takes this module's whole decl list, not a pre-filtered one.  The polarity
-- fixpoint runs over all of it (#2112), and filtering at the CALL SITE is what once let
-- the opaque-kind half go missing.
--
-- `fieldOwnersRef` arrives holding the K seed PLUS everything this module registered
-- during inference, and `registerAllDataScoped … pubDecls` below registers this module's
-- PUBLIC records a SECOND time.  `addFieldOwners` conses without dedupe, so every own
-- public record is DOUBLE-listed in `fieldOwnersRef` from that line until the next
-- `freshModuleCtx`.  Unobservable today only because nothing reads the multimap in between
-- (the two population walkers read `env2` and `recordByNameRef`).  A doubled owner key is
-- the shape `declEnvSeedChain`'s own-row note exists to prevent.  `fieldOwnerNames`
-- `sortUniqS`es on read, so the doubling does not move an answer; a new reader of
-- `fieldOwnersRef` after this point must de-duplicate first or restore a reset.
-- (`dataParamKindsRef` gets the same
-- doubling; it is inert there because `lookupTab` is first-match over identity-bearing
-- keys whose two copies are equal.)
appendDataUniverse : ModuleCtx -> String -> List Decl -> Unit
appendDataUniverse mctx mid prog0 =
  let pubDecls = publicDataDecls prog0
  -- The alias half of the reload is a stage-K projection, so it takes THIS module's
  -- ordinal, strictly BELOW-this-module (`aliasUniverseAt`'s `<`): the registration
  -- below is what puts this module's own aliases, public and private, in front.
  loadDataUniverse mctx (declEnvsOrdOf mid mctx.mcGraph.declEnvsRef.value)
  -- #2112: the polarity fixpoint sees the WHOLE module (`prog0`), the universe
  -- receives only the public keys — see `registerAllDataScoped`.
  let env2 =
    registerAllDataScoped
      (withCtors mctx (spFloor mctx.mcGraph.crossRun.universeCtorPop.value))
      (publicDataScopeDecls prog0)
      prog0
  -- Both walkers read the payloads this registration just made back out of `env2` and
  -- `recordByNameRef`, so each population row holds the very object its floor holds.
  mctx.mcGraph.crossRun.universeCtorPop :=
    insertCtorPop env2 pubDecls mctx.mcGraph.crossRun.universeCtorPop.value
  mctx.mcGraph.crossRun.universeRecordPop :=
    insertRecordPop mctx pubDecls mctx.mcGraph.crossRun.universeRecordPop.value
  mctx.mcCells.ownPopsRef :=
    (insertCtorPop env2 pubDecls spEmpty, insertRecordPop mctx pubDecls spEmpty)

-- What `appendDataUniverse` registers to elaborate a module's public data: the
-- public declarations plus every alias the module declares, private ones
-- included.  A public field may name a private alias, and the scheme it
-- elaborates to here is the one every importer reads back, so it expands under
-- the declaring module's aliases.  The private aliases reach only the working
-- alias table, which the next module's arm reloads; the populations take
-- `pubDecls` alone.
publicDataScopeDecls : List Decl -> List Decl
publicDataScopeDecls prog0 =
  filterList (d => publicDataDecl d || isAliasDecl d) prog0

-- L3 (xmod-identity #1351 spine, RUN-XMOD-022/026): the graph-level fact "this
-- compile's decls carry at least one top-level funDef with its own module's
-- mangle prefix" — the DENOTATION the new GraphCtx flag below actually
-- records (F12).  NOT literally "a mangler ran": a hand-written `m__foo` in
-- module `m` on the un-mangled (check/run) path also satisfies it, harmlessly
-- (see that flag's callers).  Reuses `isMangledFor` (F6) rather than a second
-- prefix test, and `funDefs` rather than a second decl walk.
-- Monomorphic, explicit-recursion, short-circuits on the first hit — do NOT
-- delegate to prelude `any`/`elem` here (AGENTS.md: costed +56% self-compile
-- on this file's hot helpers).
--
-- 🚨 RUN-XMOD-045 CORRECTION (post-landing, slice-breaker finding): on EVERY
-- emit path this flag is CONSTANT TRUE, not merely "true when some module
-- shadows an interface method."  `private_mangle.mdk:14-16` states the
-- mangler's actual scope: "EVERY top-level FUNCTION binding (in core + every
-- module) is renamed to a module-qualified unique symbol," unconditionally,
-- BEFORE `elaborateModules` (and therefore this function) ever runs.  So
-- `core`'s own funDefs already carry the `core__` prefix by the time this
-- walks them, and the very first unit checked (`("core", coreDecls)`, see
-- both call sites below) already satisfies `unitCarriesMangledFunDefs` —
-- MEASURED: a feature-free `main = println 1` build emits ~70 distinct
-- `@mdk_core__*`/`@mdk_<mid>__*` symbols in its own IR with zero user
-- modules, zero shadows, zero interfaces.  The ORIGINAL packet's inertness
-- argument (F8: "a non-empty route symbol implies this flag is True") is
-- still literally correct but was read as "this flag is sometimes False,"
-- which is false — it is NEVER False on the emit path, so F8's implication
-- is vacuously satisfied rather than doing narrowing work.  The precondition
-- F8's phrasing hid: BOTH writers (this flag AND the route-symbol conjunct
-- in `importerShadowOnEmitPath`) are stamped by the SAME compile, and on
-- that compile this flag is always True the moment mangling has run at all —
-- see `importerShadowOnEmitPath`'s own header for the consequence.
--
-- 🚨 THIS FACT CURRENTLY HAS NO DISCRIMINATING CONSUMER — L4's conjunct is
-- constant-True on emit and its partner (`occurrenceCarriesMangledShadowSym`)
-- is always-empty off emit.  It is explicit documentation of an implicit
-- invariant, not a live condition.  Do not migrate a reader onto it
-- expecting it to select.  KEPT (not reverted) by owner ruling because it is
-- provably zero-risk and reads better than the anonymous test it replaced —
-- see `importerShadowOnEmitPath`.
graphCarriesMangledFunDefs : List (String, List Decl) -> Bool
graphCarriesMangledFunDefs [] = False
graphCarriesMangledFunDefs ((mid, decls) :: rest) =
  if unitCarriesMangledFunDefs mid (funDefs decls) then
    True
  else
    graphCarriesMangledFunDefs rest

unitCarriesMangledFunDefs : String -> List (String, (List Pat, Expr)) -> Bool
unitCarriesMangledFunDefs mid [] = False
unitCarriesMangledFunDefs mid ((n, _) :: rest) =
  if isMangledFor mid n then True else unitCarriesMangledFunDefs mid rest

-- WS-1a fix: every impl in scope, EXPORT OR NOT.  Instances are GLOBAL (coherence
-- + dispatch leak across module boundaries regardless of `export`), so the
-- superinterface existence query (checkSuperImpls/superImplExists) must see an
-- imported module's `impl Semigroup T` even when it isn't `export`-marked — else
-- `impl Monoid T` in an importer is falsely rejected for a "missing" super impl.
pickSchemes : List String -> OrdMap Scheme -> List (String, Scheme)
pickSchemes [] _ = []
pickSchemes (n :: ns) table = match omLookup n table
  Some s => (n, s) :: pickSchemes ns table
  None => pickSchemes ns table

-- Candidate spellings come from the same three binding sources the environment sees:
-- nameable bare methods (including the implicit core row), selective-import local
-- names, and module-alias-qualified names.  `lookupBinding` below remains the final
-- no-new-name gate, while this bounded list avoids walking every ordinary seed binding.
importedMethodBindingNames : GraphCtx ->
  List Decl ->
  List (String, String) ->
  List String
importedMethodBindingNames gctx prog aliases =
  flatMap snd (nameableIfaceRows gctx prog)
    ++ importedMemberBindingNames prog
    ++ map fst aliases

plainModuleSeed : List (String, Scheme) -> ModuleSeed
plainModuleSeed schemes = ModuleSeed {
  msSchemes = schemes,
  msImportedValues = omEmpty,
  msImportedNames = omEmpty,
  msImportedExterns = omEmpty,
}

-- The ordinary winner and standalone alternative travel together through
-- import selection, aliases, re-exports, and graph memoization.
tagModuleExports : OrdMap Scheme ->
  List (String, Scheme) ->
  List (String, ExportBinding)
tagModuleExports standalones schemes =
  map
    ((name, scheme) => (
      name,
      ExportBinding {
        xbScheme = scheme,
        xbStandalone = omLookup name standalones,
        xbExtern = False,
      },
    ))
    schemes

publicModuleExports : List Decl ->
  ModuleBindings ->
  List (String, ExportBinding)
publicModuleExports prog bindings =
  let standalones =
    omFromPairs
      (flatMap
        (name => match omLookup name bindings.mbStandaloneSchemes
          Some scheme => [(name, scheme)]
          None => [])
        (pubTopFnNames prog))
      omEmpty
  let externs =
    omFromNames (map fst (directExternSigs (externDecls prog))) omEmpty
  map
    ((name, binding) => (
      name,
      ExportBinding { binding | xbExtern = omHasKey name externs },
    ))
    (tagModuleExports
      standalones
      (pickSchemes
        (publicValNames prog)
        (omFromPairs (reverseL bindings.mbSchemes) omEmpty)))

-- The first row for a name wins, unless a second import supplies a different
-- declaration of the same name: then the occurrence is the ambiguity the
-- resolver reports as R-AMBIGUOUS-OCCURRENCE (`ambiguousSet`, keyed by
-- declaration through `importValueDecls`, whichever module each import names;
-- a local definition, which it exempts, shadows the seed here anyway).
-- Choosing either supplier would type the use against a definition the program
-- never named, and the cascade would change with the order the imports were
-- written.
importedBindingWinners : ModuleCtx ->
  List (String, (Option String, ExportBinding)) ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  List (String, ExportBinding)
importedBindingWinners mctx [] _ _ = []
importedBindingWinners mctx ((name, (_, binding)) :: rest) seen ambiguous =
  if omHasKey name seen then
    importedBindingWinners mctx rest seen ambiguous
  else
    let chosen =
      if omHasKey name ambiguous then
        ambiguousImportBinding mctx ()
      else
        binding
    (name, chosen)
      :: importedBindingWinners mctx rest (omInsert name () seen) ambiguous

ambiguousImports : List (String, (Option String, a)) -> OrdMap Unit
ambiguousImports rows = ambiguousImportsGo rows omEmpty omEmpty

ambiguousImportsGo : List (String, (Option String, a)) ->
  OrdMap String ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  OrdMap Unit
ambiguousImportsGo [] _ acc = acc
ambiguousImportsGo ((_, (None, _)) :: rest) firstMid acc =
  ambiguousImportsGo rest firstMid acc
ambiguousImportsGo ((name, (Some mid, _)) :: rest) firstMid acc =
  match omLookup name firstMid
    None => ambiguousImportsGo rest (omInsert name mid firstMid) acc
    Some seen => ambiguousImportsGo rest firstMid (if seen == mid then
      acc
    else
      omInsert name () acc)

-- An ambiguous name types as a fresh, poisoned variable at every occurrence
-- (`freshSubst` recognises the reserved quantifier), so the resolver's
-- rejection stays the only diagnostic on the drivers that keep typechecking
-- after a resolve error (`check --json`, the LSP).
ambiguousImportBinding : ModuleCtx -> Unit -> ExportBinding
ambiguousImportBinding mctx _ =
  let cell =
    Ref (Unbound ambiguousImportTyvarId mctx.mcCells.currentLevel.value)
  ExportBinding {
    xbScheme = Forall [ambiguousImportTyvarId] [] [] [] pureRow (TVar cell),
    xbStandalone = None,
    xbExtern = False,
  }

moduleImportSeed : ModuleCtx ->
  List (String, Scheme) ->
  List (String, (Option String, ExportBinding)) ->
  ModuleSeed
moduleImportSeed mctx base imported =
  let selected =
    importedBindingWinners mctx imported omEmpty (ambiguousImports imported)
  ModuleSeed {
    msSchemes =
      base ++ map ((name, binding) => (name, binding.xbScheme)) selected,
    msImportedValues =
      omFromPairs
        (flatMap
          ((name, binding) => match binding.xbStandalone
            Some scheme => [(name, scheme)]
            None => [])
          selected)
        omEmpty,
    msImportedNames = omFromNames (map fst selected) omEmpty,
    msImportedExterns =
      omFromNames
        (flatMap
          ((name, binding) => if binding.xbExtern then [name] else [])
          selected)
        omEmpty,
  }

-- `import m as A` binds EVERY value m exports under `A.name` — so it enumerates the
-- dependency's schemes rather than a fixed member list.
--
-- Same golden/mangled split as above: on the emit path the reference is already
-- `<definer>__name`, so the key must stay mangled; on the golden path the reference is
-- the flat `A.name` that desugar produced, so bind it under that.
--
-- #1337/#1427/#1472: the mangle test asks the LOADED MODULE-ID SET, not just the module
-- the importer spelled.  A key reached through `export import` is mangled for its
-- DEFINER, not for the re-exporter `m` that the importer named — so a spelled-mid-only
-- prefix test answered False for it and re-bound `lib_plain__g` as `A.lib_plain__g`,
-- while types/private_mangle (which chases re-exports to the definer) had already
-- rewritten the body's reference to the bare `lib_plain__g`.  The lookup then missed:
-- for a constrained callee that reaches inferDictAt's panic and `build` fails outright
-- (#1427); for an unconstrained one the enclosing prelude call's dict route resolves to
-- nothing, the emitter writes a null dict operand, and the BINARY segfaults (#1472).
--
-- Conservatism (the property this rests on): a BARE key — one no loaded module exports
-- under that exact name with that module's own mangle prefix — is still re-bound under
-- the alias.  That population is exactly the interface METHODS (publicValNames admits
-- them; private_mangle's rename map, built from unitDefNames/pubFnNames, never renames
-- them), which is the occurrence-carrier question #1276/#1386 own — deliberately NOT
-- moved here.  The only keys whose binding changes are those a DIFFERENT loaded module
-- actually exports under its mangled name, i.e. precisely the re-exported ones, i.e.
-- precisely the defect.
--
-- 🚨 THE TEST IS AN IDENTITY TEST, NOT A STRING-SHAPE TEST (RUN-XMOD-039 F2), and it
-- must stay one.  A first version asked only "does `k` carry SOME loaded module's mangle
-- prefix?" — a pure spelling question — and that regressed a program base accepted: with
-- a module `lib.plain` loaded, an unrelated module's ordinary exported binding literally
-- named `lib_plain__g` was misread as already-mangled and rejected `Unbound variable:
-- O.lib_plain__g` at exit 1.  That surface is UNBOUNDED AND GROWS WITH THE MODULE GRAPH
-- (every module `a.b` makes `a_b__x` a landmine), and a sprint whose thesis is "identity
-- must not be derived from spelling" cannot decide identity by spelling, even in a guard.
-- ⚠️ So do NOT repair a future false positive here by TIGHTENING THE PREFIX PATTERN — a
-- narrower heuristic has a smaller unbounded surface, not a bounded one.  The conjunct
-- below is what bounds it: `k` must be a name the candidate module ACTUALLY EXPORTS, so
-- a false positive now requires two modules to genuinely export the same symbol rather
-- than one identifier to merely look like a mangled one.
aliasSchemes : List (String, List (String, a)) ->
  String ->
  List (String, a) ->
  List (String, a)
aliasSchemes deps alias depSchemes =
  map (aliasSchemeEntry deps alias) depSchemes

aliasSchemeEntry : List (String, List (String, a)) ->
  String ->
  (String, a) ->
  (String, a)
aliasSchemeEntry deps alias (k, s) =
  if isMangledExportOfAny deps k then (k, s) else (qualifiedLocal alias k, s)

-- does `k` carry the `<sanitized mid>__` prefix the mangler would have given it?
isMangledFor : String -> String -> Bool
isMangledFor mid k =
  let pre = mangledName mid ""
  let lp = stringLength pre
  lp <= stringLength k && stringSlice 0 lp k == pre

-- is `k` a symbol some loaded module ACTUALLY EXPORTS under that module's own mangled
-- name?  Both halves are load-bearing and the ORDER is deliberate: the cheap spelling
-- test gates the assoc lookup, so the scan below runs only for the rare key that already
-- looks mangled.  Short-circuiting and monomorphic on purpose (a dict-passed `any` over
-- a closure is the measured anti-pattern here).
--
-- 🚨 THE HONEST RESIDUAL, RECORDED SO THE NEXT READER DOES NOT HAVE TO RE-DERIVE IT
-- (RUN-XMOD-042).  This is "SHAPE **AND** ACTUALLY-EXPORTED", **not** pure identity, and
-- the distinction matters if you are auditing it against the sprint's own thesis that
-- identity must not be derived from spelling.  `isMangledFor` is still a string test; it
-- has simply stopped being the *whole* decision.  What the `isSome (lookupAssoc k pubV)`
-- conjunct buys is that the surface becomes BOUNDED BY THE PROGRAM'S REAL EXPORT SET: a
-- false positive now needs a GENUINE SYMBOL COLLISION -- module `m` must actually export
-- something named exactly `k`, where `k` also carries `m`'s mangle prefix -- instead of
-- merely a similar-LOOKING name.  Before the conjunct, the surface grew with the module
-- graph (every module `a.b` made `a_b__x` a landmine, which is what regressed `core__foo`
-- and `lib_plain__g`); now it does not grow with the graph at all.
--
-- ⚠️ WHY NOT DROP THE SHAPE HALF AND MAKE IT PURE IDENTITY?  Because that is measurably
-- WRONG here, not merely purer: a re-exported interface METHOD key is also a key of its
-- declaring module's `pubV`, so "is `k` a key of some other loaded module?" alone answers
-- True for methods and would re-bind them -- moving the bare-key population that
-- #1276/#1386 own and that this slice must not touch.  The shape half is precisely what
-- holds methods out (a bare method name carries no `<mid>__` prefix).  So the two halves
-- are not redundant and neither may be removed on tidiness grounds.
--
-- ⚠️ The residual's true root is one level down and is NOT fixed here: private_mangle's
-- `(module, name) -> symbol` encoding is not injective -- a module `lib.plain` and a
-- module literally named `lib_plain` both yield `lib_plain__g`.  That is the common root
-- of both regressions above and is bigger than this function; do not try to repair it by
-- editing this test.
isMangledExportOfAny : List (String, List (String, a)) -> String -> Bool
isMangledExportOfAny [] _ = False
isMangledExportOfAny ((m, pubV) :: rest) k =
  isMangledFor m k && isSome (lookupAssoc k pubV) || isMangledExportOfAny rest k

-- the (key, scheme) pairs a single `import` form brings into scope, resolving each
-- member to its (possibly mangled) key in the dependency's schemes.  `deps` is the
-- loaded dependency environment — module id PLUS that module's public schemes, because
-- the alias arm's test needs the exported NAMES, not just the ids (see aliasSchemes).
-- The non-alias arms ignore it — their resolution is definer-agnostic by construction
-- (a `__<name>` SUFFIX test, and the wildcard form performs no mangle test at all).
--
-- Passing `depEnv` WHOLE is also what supplies the spelled `depId` itself: both callers
-- reach this only through a successful `lookupAssoc depId depEnv`, so the spelled module
-- is in the list by construction and needs no separate term.
--
-- 🚨 `"core"` IS DELIBERATELY **NOT** IN `mids`, AND MUST NOT BE ADDED BACK
-- (RUN-XMOD-039).  It was, briefly.  The argument for it reads well — `reexportSeed`'s
-- own comment records core as the one source NOT in depEnv, and private_mangle *does*
-- mangle core's exports to `core__<name>` — but it was DERIVED, never witnessed: a
-- `export import core.{…}` reached through an alias is green on every verb with or
-- without the term, because core's names are seeded via `baseSeed` and resolve before
-- the alias binding is ever consulted.  Meanwhile the term has a MEASURED cost: it made
-- `mangledName "core" "" == "core__"` a live prefix, so an ordinary user binding named
-- `core__foo` reached through an alias import was misread as already-mangled and left
-- un-rebound — `Unbound variable: O.core__foo`, exit 1, on a program that compiled and
-- printed correctly before.  Zero measured benefit, measured cost.
importFormSchemes : List (String, List (String, a)) ->
  UsePath ->
  List (String, a) ->
  List (String, a)
importFormSchemes deps (UseAlias _ alias) depSchemes =
  aliasSchemes deps alias depSchemes
importFormSchemes _ path depSchemes = importFormRows path depSchemes

-- ── import aliasing: re-key the dict-arity / dict-iface tables ───────────────────
-- Both tables (funConstraintsRef, funConstraintIfacesRef) are keyed by the name a CALL
-- SITE writes.  An alias makes that name differ from the definition's, so without this
-- an aliased constrained callee gets zero dict routes and under-applies.  Generic over
-- the payload so the arity table (List Int) and the iface table (List String) share it.
--
-- [qual] is the (definerMid, name)-keyed table, which is what makes this PRECISE: an
-- entry is copied only when its DEFINER is the very module the alias names.
-- #1114 (#845): THIS module's imported bindings' SCHEME CONTEXTS, keyed by the local
-- spelling the importer writes.  Structurally the sibling of `aliasConstraintEntries`
-- below — same `DUse` walk, same "copy an entry only when its DEFINER is the very module
-- this import names" precision, and the payload is likewise taken from the
-- `(definerMid, name)`-keyed qual table.
--
-- TWO deliberate differences from `aliasConstraintEntries`, both because that function
-- serves the DICT-ARITY tables on the emit path and this one serves the CHECK-time
-- obligation channel:
--   * it has a `UseWild` arm.  `aliasConstraintEntries` needs none — on the emit path a
--     wildcard-imported name keeps its own spelling and `funConstraintsRef` is re-seeded
--     from the bare `crossModuleFunConstraintsRef` accumulator, which already covers it.
--     The check path has no such bare re-seed (that ref is the emit path's), so without
--     this arm `import m.*` would be the one spelling that still dropped the obligation.
--   * it emits the UNALIASED member of a `UseGroup` too (`useMemberLocal`, not
--     `useMemberAlias`), because plain `import m.{f}` is the common spelling and is
--     exactly what #845 pins.
--
-- ⚠️ Kept SEPARATE from `aliasConstraintEntries` rather than generalizing it. Adding a
-- `UseWild` arm there would change what `funConstraintsRef` holds on the emit path, i.e.
-- dict-passing arity — a different judgment, with a different blast radius, reached from
-- here only by the coincidence that both read the same qual-table shape.
importedSchemeOblEntries : List Decl ->
  List ((String, String), List VecObl) ->
  List (String, List VecObl)
importedSchemeOblEntries [] _ = []
importedSchemeOblEntries ((DAttrib _ d) :: rest) qual =
  importedSchemeOblEntries [d] qual ++ importedSchemeOblEntries rest qual
importedSchemeOblEntries ((DUse _ path _) :: rest) qual =
  schemeOblEntriesFor (importTableMid path) path qual
    ++ importedSchemeOblEntries rest qual
importedSchemeOblEntries (_ :: rest) qual = importedSchemeOblEntries rest qual

-- ── import aliasing of an interface/impl METHOD ─────────────────────────────────
-- A method is GLOBAL-BY-NAME.  Impl coalescing, dispatch routing, the emitter's method
-- tables and the METHOD-side dict-arity tables are every one of them keyed by the
-- method's own name, and there is exactly ONE cell per name — a method is deliberately
-- NOT a per-module binding (eval.mdk's globalCells / coalesceImpls).  So an alias of a
-- method is not a new binding at all: it is a second SPELLING of the same method.
--
-- No alias spelling is resolved here, module or member.  The alias spelling is what
-- makes the occurrence decidable.  Erasing `A.area` makes it the same name as an
-- unrelated imported standalone `area`, and the standalone shadow wins (#1386 Repro B);
-- erasing a member alias `import m.{area as computeArea}` makes `computeArea` and a bare
-- `area` one name, so the import's method captures an `area` that resolve bound to
-- another declaration (#3708).  Inference gets the spelling supplied to it
-- (`aliasQualifiedMethodEntries`, `moduleMarkCtx`, `originMethodName`) and
-- `resolveAliasMethodSpellings` puts the occurrence back under its origin name once
-- inference is done, so every stage after elaboration still sees an ordinary method
-- reference and needs no alias awareness.
--
-- That is also precisely why the METHOD-side predicate carrier and its qualified
-- scoped projection need no alias re-keying the
-- way funConstraintsRef did: by the time they are built, no aliased method name survives.
-- The standalone `=>`-constrained functions are the opposite case — they ARE per-module
-- bindings that keep their local name, which is why they needed the re-keying.
--
-- What this pass does rewrite is a module alias's `DUse`: it keeps its own non-method
-- values and an `import m.{…m's methods…}` is appended beside it, so the origin name is
