-- in scope for the occurrence `resolveAliasMethodSpellings` resolves it to.  A member
-- alias's `DUse` is rewritten to its origin name by that same restore, after inference.
-- Beside the rewritten modules it returns each module's admissions, which the drive's
-- mint installs (`GraphCtx.graphAdmittedMethodsRef`, read by `admittedIn`).
renameAliasedMethods : List Decl ->
  List (String, List Decl) ->
  (OrdMap (List (String, String)), List (String, List Decl))
renameAliasedMethods coreDecls modules =
  let coreEntry = ("core", declMethodNames coreDecls)
  let methodsPerMid = coreEntry :: methodsPerMidGo [coreEntry] modules
  let admitted =
    omFromPairs
      (map
        ((mid, prog) => (mid, synthesizedAdmissions methodsPerMid prog))
        modules)
      omEmpty
  (admitted, map (renameAliasedMethodsIn methodsPerMid) modules)

admittedIn : GraphCtx -> String -> List (String, String)
admittedIn gctx mid =
  optionOr [] (omLookup mid gctx.graphAdmittedMethodsRef.value)

-- The method names `deAliasMethodImports` admits WITHOUT a binding the resolver
-- counted: every method of an alias-imported module.  `importSeed` reads this so
-- such a row never makes a bare name look supplied twice.
synthesizedAdmissions : List (String, List String) ->
  List Decl ->
  List (String, String)
synthesizedAdmissions _ [] = []
synthesizedAdmissions mm ((DAttrib _ d) :: rest) =
  synthesizedAdmissions mm (d :: rest)
synthesizedAdmissions mm ((DUse _ path _) :: rest) =
  let mid = useModId path
  let here = match lookupAssoc mid mm
    None => []
    Some methods => match path
      UseAlias _ _ => map (n => (mid, n)) methods
      _ => []
  here ++ synthesizedAdmissions mm rest
synthesizedAdmissions mm (_ :: rest) = synthesizedAdmissions mm rest

-- A module's method set is what it DECLARES *plus what it RE-EXPORTS*, folded in
-- dependency-first (loader) order so a re-export resolves against its source's
-- already-computed set (and a >1-hop chain still resolves).
--
-- The `++ reexportedMethodNames` half closes a run≠build divergence that predates
-- core re-exports and is NOT core-specific: with a module's set limited to its own
-- `declMethodNames`, a module that re-exports a method did not list it, so at an
-- importer's `import reExporter.{method as alias}` neither half of the rewrite fired
-- — the alias was not dropped from the DUse (b) and references were not renamed to the
-- origin (a).  `run` still worked (eval's import frame binds the alias to the origin's
-- cell), but a method is global-by-name with no per-module symbol, so EMIT had nothing
-- to bind `alias` to and died with `unbound variable '<alias>'`.  Observed on a pure
-- user-module chain (b defines `area`; c re-exports it; main imports `area as surface`
-- → run prints 16, build fails), and on `import list.{filter as f}` once
-- `export import core.{filter}` began re-exporting at all.
methodsPerMidGo : List (String, List String) ->
  List (String, List Decl) ->
  List (String, List String)
methodsPerMidGo _ [] = []
methodsPerMidGo acc ((mid, decls) :: rest) =
  let entry =
    (mid, dedup (declMethodNames decls ++ reexportedMethodNames acc decls))
  entry :: methodsPerMidGo (entry :: acc) rest

-- method names a module re-exports via `export import src.{…}` (`DUse True`), taken
-- from `acc` — the dependency's already-folded method set.
reexportedMethodNames : List (String, List String) -> List Decl -> List String
reexportedMethodNames acc decls = flatMap (reexportedMethodsOf acc) decls

reexportedMethodsOf : List (String, List String) -> Decl -> List String
reexportedMethodsOf acc (DAttrib _ d) = reexportedMethodsOf acc d
reexportedMethodsOf acc (DUse True path _) =
  match lookupAssoc (useModId path) acc
    None => []
    Some srcMethods => match importedBindings path
      -- `export import src.*` re-exports every one of src's methods
      None => srcMethods
      Some bs => filterList (n => contains n srcMethods) (map fst bs)
reexportedMethodsOf _ _ = []

-- Only a MODULE alias is rewritten before inference (`deAliasMethodImports`).  A
-- member alias reaches inference as written, so `import m.{mth as loc}` binds `loc`
-- and not `mth`; `resolveAliasMethodSpellings` restores the origin name afterwards.
-- The pass is a no-op on a module whose imports name no method.
renameAliasedMethodsIn : List (String, List String) ->
  (String, List Decl) ->
  (String, List Decl)
renameAliasedMethodsIn methodsPerMid (mid, prog) =
  (mid, flatMap (deAliasMethodImports methodsPerMid) prog)

-- `import m as A` is kept (its non-method values are still `A.f`) and gains a sibling
-- `import m.{…m's methods…}`, the origin name `resolveAliasMethodSpellings` resolves
-- `A.area` to once inference is done.  The rewrite is recorded in
-- `graphAdmittedMethodsRef` (`synthesizedAdmissions`), because the resolver never saw
-- it.  The added import keeps the alias import's path and location, which is how the
-- method scope ladder tells it from a written one (`writtenImportsOf`).
deAliasMethodImports : List (String, List String) -> Decl -> List Decl
deAliasMethodImports mm (DAttrib attrs d) =
  map (DAttrib attrs) (deAliasMethodImports mm d)
deAliasMethodImports mm (d@(DUse pub path loc)) =
  match lookupAssoc (useModId path) mm
    None => [d]
    Some methods => match path
      UseAlias quals _ => match methodMembersOf methods loc
        [] => [d]
        mems => [d, DUse pub (UseGroup quals mems) loc]
      _ => [d]
deAliasMethodImports _ d = [d]

methodMembersOf : List String -> Loc -> List UseMember
methodMembersOf methods loc = map (n => UseMember n False loc None) methods

-- [qualified] holds the `A.mth` spellings: nothing but the method can be spelled that
-- way, so every occurrence moves.  [members] holds the member-alias locals no own
-- top-level value takes (`memberAliasCands`), which a local binder can still spell;
-- only a MARKED occurrence is the import's, since the marker leaves a locally-bound
-- name unmarked (`rewriteArgScoped`).
renameMethodVar : List (String, String) -> List (String, String) -> Expr -> Expr
renameMethodVar qualified _ (e@(EVar x)) = match lookupAssoc x qualified
  Some origin => EVar origin
  None => e
renameMethodVar qualified _ (e@(EVarId x _)) = match lookupAssoc x qualified
  Some origin => EVar origin
  None => e
-- A marked occurrence: `resolveAliasMethodSpellings` runs after inference, on a tree
-- the schedule has already marked.  Only the NAME moves — the route cell carries the
-- dispatch decision inference reached under the alias spelling.
renameMethodVar qualified members (e@(EMethodAt x sym ev)) =
  match lookupAssoc x qualified
    Some origin => EMethodAt origin sym ev
    None => match lookupAssoc x members
      Some origin => EMethodAt origin sym ev
      None => e
renameMethodVar _ _ e = e

-- ── #1386: the alias-qualified spelling, resolved AFTER inference ───────────────
-- `A.mth`, and a member alias `loc` from `import m.{mth as loc}`, reach inference
-- spelled as written, because that spelling is what makes the occurrence decidable:
-- rewriting either to a bare `mth` up front merges it with whatever else a bare `mth`
-- names in this module (`renameAliasedMethods`' header, #1386 Repro B, #3708).  Every
-- reader inference needs is supplied under that spelling — the obligation table, the
-- mark sets, the dispatch index — so the distinction survives exactly as long as it
-- decides something.
--
-- It must not survive further.  Everything DOWNSTREAM of elaboration keys a method by
-- its origin name and only its origin name: eval's coalesced method cells and its
-- per-(method, tag) `requires` counts (`methodReqCountRef`, whose miss would turn a
-- dispatch into the inherited-default path), the Core-IR interpreter's twin, and the
-- emitter's method tables.  Resolving the spelling here leaves all of them the tree
-- they get today, so the fix is a VERDICT change and nothing else.
resolveAliasMethodSpellings : GraphCtx ->
  (String, List Decl) ->
  (String, List Decl)
resolveAliasMethodSpellings gctx (mid, prog) =
  let qualified = map aliasRowSpelling (useKeyCands (moduleAliasKeys gctx) prog)
  let members = map aliasRowSpelling (memberAliasCands gctx prog)
  match (qualified, members)
    ([], []) => (mid, prog)
    _ => (
      mid,
      mapProg
        (renameMethodVar qualified members)
        (map (deAliasMethodMembers members) prog),
    )

-- `import m.{mth as loc}` → `import m.{mth}`, once every `loc` occurrence carries `mth`:
-- downstream of elaboration a method is bound by its origin name only.  Only a
-- `DUse` names import members, so every other decl passes through unchanged.
deAliasMethodMembers : List (String, String) -> Decl -> Decl
deAliasMethodMembers rows (DAttrib attrs d) =
  DAttrib attrs (deAliasMethodMembers rows d)
deAliasMethodMembers rows (DUse pub (UseGroup quals ms) loc) =
  DUse pub (UseGroup quals (map (deAliasMethodMember rows) ms)) loc
deAliasMethodMembers _ d = d

deAliasMethodMember : List (String, String) -> UseMember -> UseMember
deAliasMethodMember rows (m@(UseMember n allCtors loc (Some local)))
  | containsPair (local, n) rows = UseMember n allCtors loc None
  | otherwise = m
deAliasMethodMember _ m = m

-- every interface/impl method name a decl list declares (interface methods with or
-- without a default, plus impl method names).
declMethodNames : List Decl -> List String
declMethodNames decls = dedup (flatMap declMethodNamesOf decls)

declMethodNamesOf : Decl -> List String
declMethodNamesOf (DAttrib _ d) = declMethodNamesOf d
declMethodNamesOf (DInterface { methods, ... }) = ifaceMethodNames methods
declMethodNamesOf (DImpl { methods, ... }) = map implMethodName methods
declMethodNamesOf _ = []

-- build THIS module's import-scoped seed: walk its DUse decls, and for each one
-- pick the imported names out of the named dependency's public schemes (held in
-- depEnv, keyed by the dotted module id that useModId yields == the loader's
-- mid).  `core` DUse decls are skipped — core is always seeded via baseSeed.
-- ── #1675: reject an import that admits a name with more than one denotation ──────
-- The hub `export import lib.pa.{g}` + `export import lib.pb.{g}` exports ONE spelling
-- `g` standing for TWO definitions.  Downstream, `resolveMemberRows`' `lookupAssoc`
-- took the first of them and every verb exited 0, so which function ran was decided by
-- the ORDER OF TWO `export import` LINES — a semantically null edit moving the printed
-- value from `2` to `10`.  This is the reject.
--
-- ⚠️ THE MECHANISM IS THE EXACT-KEY ARM, NOT THE `__<name>` SUFFIX FALLBACK, and the
-- distinction decides where the check can live.  #1675's body cites the suffix `filter`
-- ("cited, not instrumented", per its own pin's claim) — but `types/private_mangle`
-- runs ONLY in the emit drivers, so on `check`/`run` the hub's rows are keyed by the
-- BARE name, `lookupAssoc origin` HITS, and the fallback is never reached.  A guard
-- written on "the filter returned more than one candidate" is green on the whole repro.
-- The ambiguity is a property of the DEPENDENCY'S EXPORT TABLE, which is where
-- `deAmbigValues` records it, on both paths at once.
--
-- Reported at the IMPORT DECL (that is where the location points, and where the fix
-- belongs), but keyed on an OCCURRENCE: a name is rejected only if this module actually
-- WRITES it, in the spelling the form binds it under — bare for `import m.*` and for a
-- selective `{g}`, alias-qualified (`A.g`) for `import m as A`.  A hub may re-export a
-- hundred names under two denotations; an importer that never mentions any of them has
-- no ambiguity to resolve and must not be rejected.  This is the USE-SITE model taken
-- literally (#1070's reject-at-declaration stays superseded; the hub itself is still
-- legal).  It also keeps the verdict from depending on which definer came first: the
-- moment the name IS written, the import is rejected rather than silently resolved.
--
-- ⚠️ CORRECTED (sprint-review F2, from #1675's own landed behavior): the first cut
-- rejected at ADMISSION — `import lib.hub.*` / `import lib.hub as H` failed even when
-- the importer never mentioned the colliding name, while the selective form correctly
-- did not.  The precedent cited for that, `T-AMBIGUOUS-ALIAS-METHOD`, is a DIFFERENT
-- namespace: methods are dispatched by argument type, where "admitted into scope" and
-- "used" are hard to pull apart because having the method callable is often the point.
-- Whether the method side wants the same narrowing is a separate question, deliberately
-- not answered here.
--
-- ⚠️ THE CHAIN IS NOT WEAKENED by narrowing to an occurrence.  `reexportDefiners` takes
-- a wildcard `export import`'s rows WHOLESALE, so a module that re-exports an ambiguous
-- hub without mentioning the name carries the ambiguity into its OWN export table, and
-- the first module downstream that does write the name is rejected there.  Nothing is
-- laundered clean by passing through a silent hop.
--
-- Called from `checkBodyImpl`, after its module mint, and not from `importSeed`.
-- `importSeed` is where the member resolution lives and was the first home for this, but
-- the seed is computed in `foldModules` BEFORE the module's worker runs, and
-- `checkBodyImpl` opens with `freshModuleCtx` — which clears `typeErrors`.  MEASURED on
-- that version: `run` exited 1 with the unlocated "detected during elaboration … see
-- issue #1812" fallback (the sticky flag survives the reset, the diagnostic does not)
-- and `check`/`check --json` were both still SILENT at exit 0 on the whole repro.  A
-- diagnostic pushed while a seed is being built cannot be reported.  Everything this
-- needs is on the module's own `DUse` decls plus the graph table, so nothing is lost by
-- moving it inside the window; `checkBodyImpl` is the ONE body all four drivers share
-- (`checkModuleFullImpl` and `elabModuleStamp` both route through it), which is what
-- keeps `check` and the run/build elaboration pass answering alike.
reportAmbiguousImports : ModuleCtx -> List Decl -> Unit
reportAmbiguousImports mctx prog0 =
  reportAmbiguousImportsIn mctx (moduleRefNameSet prog0) prog0

-- every name this module's own decl bodies REFERENCE, as a set.  Parallels `groupRefs`'
-- collector (`freeEVars`, which skips locally bound names; `allEVars` here keeps every
-- occurrence) one level up, at the decl layer: the top-level clause bodies plus
-- the impl/default/prop/test bodies, which is every place a user program can spell
-- an imported value.  Alias-qualified references arrive here already flattened into a
-- single dotted `EVar "A.g"` by desugar's `rewriteAliasQual` (via `qualifiedLocal`), so
-- the alias spelling is a plain string lookup and needs no separate walk.
--
-- `allEVars` has no `EMethodRef` arm and does not need one: no production verb ever
-- constructs that node (it does carry `EMethodAt`/`EDictAt`, the shapes the elaborate
-- driver's dict pre-pass actually mints).  Independently of shape, the rows being filtered
-- come from `ambiguousExportRows` → `modulePubDefiners` → `pubTopFnNames`, i.e.
-- `declTopFnNames` ∩ exports — so an interface method name can never be in `amb` at all.
moduleRefNameSet : List Decl -> OrdMap Unit
moduleRefNameSet decls = namesToSet (flatMap declRefNames decls) omEmpty

-- `core` is never in `depEnv` (it is the implicit prelude — `reexportSeed`'s comment
-- carries the full reason), so it is passed separately as `coreV`, and it contributes
-- ONE thing: the keys an ALIAS introduces.  A plain `import core.{f}` still seeds
-- nothing, because `f` is already in `baseSeed` under that very spelling and seeding it
-- twice only adds a duplicate assoc entry — but `import core as C` and
-- `import core.{f as g}` ask for `C.f` / `g`, which `baseSeed` does not hold under any
-- spelling.  `resolve.mdk`'s `coreAliasNames` binds exactly the same two forms, and the
-- two must agree: a key bound in scope with no scheme here is a `T-UNBOUND` at the use
-- site, which is what #95 measured for six years.
-- Each row a use-path BINDS carries the declaration it denotes
-- (`importSupplierKey`), the same identity the resolver's value ambiguity check
-- keys on (`importValueDecls`), so `moduleImportSeed` can refuse to pick a winner
-- by import order for a name the resolver has already rejected, and still
-- accept one declaration reached through two imports. A row the form admits
-- without binding its name (a bare method row admitted for dispatch, a mangled
-- twin) carries no supplier, and core is exempt there as it is in the resolver.
-- The key is looked up by local name, so one member list binding a local twice
-- (`import m.{a as b, b}`) gives both rows one key and the first row wins here;
-- the resolver rejects that occurrence by declaration all the same.
importSeed : GraphCtx ->
  List (String, a) ->
  List (String, String) ->
  List Decl ->
  List (String, List (String, a)) ->
  List (String, (Option String, a))
importSeed gctx _ _ [] _ = []
importSeed gctx coreV admitted ((DAttrib _ d) :: rest) depEnv =
  importSeed gctx coreV admitted (d :: rest) depEnv
importSeed gctx coreV admitted ((DUse _ path _) :: rest) depEnv =
  let depId = useModId path
  if depId == "core" then
    map (suppliedBy None) (coreAliasSchemes path coreV)
      ++ importSeed gctx coreV admitted rest depEnv
  else match lookupAssoc depId depEnv
    None => importSeed gctx coreV admitted rest depEnv
    Some depSchemes =>
      let bound = boundNames path
      let decls =
        omFromPairs
          (reverseL (importFormRows path (graphPubDefiners gctx depId)))
          omEmpty
      let methods =
        identKeysByName
          omEmpty
          (importFormRows
            path
            (match omLookup depId (methodExportsIndex gctx ())
              Some rows => rows
              None => []))
      map
          (row =>
            suppliedBy
              (if bindsName bound (fst row)
                && not (containsPair (depId, fst row) admitted) then
                Some (importSupplierKey depId decls methods (fst row))
              else
                None)
              row)
          (importFormSchemes depEnv path depSchemes)
        ++ importSeed gctx coreV admitted rest depEnv
importSeed gctx coreV admitted (_ :: rest) depEnv =
  importSeed gctx coreV admitted rest depEnv

-- The identity one import's binding of `name` is compared by: the declaration
-- it denotes.  A standalone value is `(defining module, name there)` from
-- `graphPubDefiners`, first row winning as it does there; an interface method
-- is the set of method declarations the import carries under that name
-- (`meExports`).  A driver without an import graph knows neither, so the
-- binding falls back to the importing module's id.  The three key shapes are
-- two, a multiple of four, and one netstring long, so no two can coincide.
importSupplierKey : String ->
  OrdMap (String, String) ->
  OrdMap (List String) ->
  String ->
  String
importSupplierKey depId decls methods name = match omLookup name decls
  Some (defMid, origin) => "\{lenKey defMid}\{lenKey origin}"
  None => match omLookup name methods
    Some keys => joinWith "" (sortUniqS keys)
    None => lenKey depId

identKeysByName : OrdMap (List String) ->
  List (String, Ident) ->
  OrdMap (List String)
identKeysByName acc [] = acc
identKeysByName acc ((n, ident) :: rest) =
  let seen = match omLookup n acc
    Some keys => keys
    None => []
  identKeysByName (omInsert n (identKey ident :: seen) acc) rest

suppliedBy : Option String -> (String, a) -> (String, (Option String, a))
suppliedBy mid (name, row) = (name, (mid, row))

containsPair : (String, String) -> List (String, String) -> Bool
containsPair _ [] = False
containsPair (a, b) ((x, y) :: rest) =
  a == x && b == y || containsPair (a, b) rest

-- The names an import form binds, as the resolver counts them
-- (`importedNamesMM`): a member list binds its locals, a single dotted name its
-- last component, an alias nothing bare, and a wildcard (`None`) every name it
-- reaches.
boundNames : UsePath -> Option (OrdMap Unit)
boundNames (UseGroup _ ms) = Some (omFromNames (map useMemberLocal ms) omEmpty)
boundNames (UseName ns) =
  Some (omFromNames (if listLen ns > 1 then [lastComponent ns] else []) omEmpty)
boundNames (UseWild _) = None
boundNames (UseAlias _ _) = Some omEmpty

bindsName : Option (OrdMap Unit) -> String -> Bool
bindsName None _ = True
bindsName (Some names) name = omHasKey name names

-- the schemes a `core` use-path binds under a spelling the prelude did not supply.
coreAliasSchemes : UsePath -> List (String, a) -> List (String, a)
coreAliasSchemes (UseAlias _ a) coreV = map (coreQualScheme a) coreV
coreAliasSchemes (UseGroup _ ms) coreV = flatMap (coreRenameScheme coreV) ms
coreAliasSchemes _ _ = []

coreQualScheme : String -> (String, a) -> (String, a)
coreQualScheme a (k, s) = (qualifiedLocal a k, s)

coreRenameScheme : List (String, a) -> UseMember -> List (String, a)
coreRenameScheme coreV m = match useMemberAlias m
  None => []
  Some local => match lookupAssoc (useMemberOrigin m) coreV
    None => []
    Some s => [(local, s)]

-- WS-2/D2: THIS module's imported value name → import-source module id, from its DUse
-- decls.  Mirrors importSeed's walk but records (localName, depId) for EXPLICIT imports
-- only (importedBindings = Some bindings); a wildcard `import mod.*` (None) is skipped —
-- it can't enumerate names here, so those names fall back to the bare arity table at the
-- call site.  `core` is skipped (core fns route via the prelude dict machinery, never the
-- cross-module qual tables).  depId == useModId == the loader mid == the qual
-- tables' definer key for a DIRECT import; a re-exported fn's depId is the intermediate
-- (≠ definer), so its qual lookup misses and it too falls back to bare (correct).
--
-- Keyed by the LOCAL name, because that is the name the CALL SITE writes: under a member
-- alias (`import m.{a as b}`) the call site says `b`, so `b` is what must map to m.
--
-- A whole-module alias (`import m as A`) contributes nothing, for the same reason a
-- wildcard doesn't: its locals are one-per-export and this walk has no depEnv to
-- enumerate them.  Those call sites take the same documented bare-table fallback as
-- every wildcard import does today.  The dict ARGS themselves are unaffected — they are
-- stamped from the callee's SCHEME, which importSeed binds under the alias local — so
-- this costs only the cross-module arity DISAMBIGUATION, and only when two modules
-- export same-named constrained fns of differing dict arity.
-- ── #674 / #1111 A-2.6: import-scoped constructor overlay ──────────────────
-- The `data`/`newtype` decls (from the surrounding universe `pool`) whose
-- CONSTRUCTORS this module binds by name, read from its own DUse decls.  They
-- OVERLAY the whole-universe ctor tables (the typecheck scheme table, the
-- record-info table AND the exhaust oracle) so a bare ctor / record name resolves
-- to the SPECIFIC module this unit imports it from — instead of the universe's
-- arbitrary load-order winner, the #674 root cause where the check side
-- (last-loaded-wins) and the native mangler (first-import-wins) DISAGREED.
--
-- A `UseGroup` member contributes its owning decl when EITHER
--   (a) it carries the `(..)` flag and names the decl's TYPE (`import m.{T(..)}`) —
--       the original #674 rule; or
--   (b) it NAMES ONE OF THE DECL'S CONSTRUCTORS (`import m.{T, C}` — and, because a
--       record's sole variant carries the type's own name, `import m.{Cfg}` for a
--       `data Cfg = { … }`).  #1111 A-2.6: (b) is the half that drains #1259 (the
--       ctor-scheme env) and #1256 (the record-info table).
--
-- ⚠️ Rule (b) is a CONSTRUCTOR-name test, not a "not a type name" test, and the
-- difference is observable.  A member spelled like a TYPE contributes nothing only when
-- no decl of `mid` happens to have a constructor of that spelling; if one does, the
-- member matches by rule (b) and that SIBLING decl is overlaid.  Measured: `pmod` with
-- `data Wrap = T Int`, `import pmod.{T, pf}`, and a local `data Loc = T String` —
-- pinned as `test/llvm_fixtures_modules/ctor_scope_type_only_sibling_decl/`.
-- (An earlier revision of this note claimed such a member "contributes NOTHING"; it was
-- measured false and the paragraph is rewritten rather than re-pointed.)
--
-- That contribution is harmless BECAUSE of the layering at the registration site
-- (`dataEnv`, `Module` arm): the overlay sits BELOW this module's own `prog0`, so a
-- sibling decl riding along can never clobber a locally-declared constructor.  What it
-- can still do is out-rank a ctor the unit names from a DIFFERENT module in an EARLIER
-- import clause, decided by source order — the residual this note used to claim was
-- prevented outright.  It is the pre-existing `(..)` hazard (#674's remainder) now also
-- reachable via (b), and it is order-dependent on `main` too.
--
-- 🚨 IT IS **#1284**, and that number is the point of this paragraph.  The note used to
-- end "it is tracked, not fixed here" while NOTHING tracked it — #1283 is the RE-EXPORT
-- spelling, #733 item 1a is marked FIXED and item 1c is wildcards only.  A declared-
-- but-unfiled residual is indistinguishable from an unnoticed one.  Pinned self-
-- drainingly by `test/must_fail_fixtures/1284-a26-overlay-sibling-ctor-beats-named-
-- import/`, whose CONTROL is the discriminator that dates it: the NON-sibling case is
-- rejected on `main` and accepted here, so A-2.6 repairs that one and leaves exactly
-- the sibling one.
--
-- 🚨 The pool lookup is IDENTITY-scoped, not bare-name.  The pool is the WHOLE
-- universe, so two modules declaring the same TYPE name (#1256's two `Cfg`s) made the
-- old bare-name first-match a LOAD-ORDER coin flip inside the very overlay that exists
-- to defeat load order.  The pool is appended in LOAD order and searched FIRST-match
-- while the tables it overlays are `omInsert` LAST-write-wins, so the two orders are
-- OPPOSITE: an unscoped lookup picks right only when the wanted module is loaded
-- FIRST, and `test/eval_typed_modules_fixtures/ctor_scope_load_order/` is the measured
-- counterexample (stubbing `declOwnedBy` to `True` regresses it to `7.0`, an answer
-- pristine `main` gets right).  `declOwnedBy` compares the decl's own identity against
-- `OriginModule <this import's module id>`; `useModId` yields exactly the loader
-- mid that `stampDeclOrigins` stamped with (see `aliasDictNamesOfPath`'s note, which
-- states the same equality for the qual tables).
--
-- ⚠️ PERF (issue #154) — THE REAL BOUND, stated for the WORK and not just the RESULT.
-- The RESULT is bounded by IMPORT COUNT x PER-MODULE PUBLIC DECL COUNT: at most one
-- overlay decl per UseGroup member, and — since `wildOverlayDecls` — the wildcard-named
-- module's whole published row per `UseWild`.  It is still a per-module VIEW (the row is
-- the envelope's own memoized `demPubDecls`, not a copy), never a per-module rebuild of
-- the global universe.  A module importing no constructors AND no wildcard overlays
-- NOTHING and stays byte-identical.  A bare `import mod` (UseName) still contributes no
-- overlay: the bare form binds no ctors at all, so no ctor occurrence in the reader can
-- mean that module's declaration by that import.  A wildcard `import mod.*` DOES
-- contribute, as of `wildOverlayDecls` below — it cannot name its owning type, but it
-- does not need to: every decl the module publishes is in scope by construction, and
-- leaving it to the universe-fallback made import-clause ORDER decide which declaration
-- a ctor occurrence meant, in both the spurious-warning and the lost-warning direction.
--
-- The WORK is NOT import-count bounded, and saying it is has already shipped a
-- regression.  `pool` is the WHOLE accumulated universe and it is SCANNED — so the cost
-- is O(members x |pool|) per module, i.e. O(modules x universe) across a run, the same
-- shape `main` has paid since #674 for its `(..)` members.  What keeps that acceptable
-- is entirely the CONSTANT, and the constant has exactly two load-bearing parts, both
-- enforced downstream and both measured:
--   * ONE traversal per member, not three (see `findOverlayDecl`/`overlayScan`); and
--   * ZERO allocation per visited decl (see `overlayNote` — name tests before the
--     identity mint).
-- Break either and the perf gate's `modules` shape goes superlinear: this comment
-- previously asserted the universe-independence outright, the first cut of A-2.6 broke
-- both parts, and the gate read typecheck TIME r2=3.24 (hard threshold 3.0) with net
-- allocation 306/744/2013 MB against `main`'s 242/491/1010.  A cheaper bound is
-- available if it is ever needed — index `pool` by owning module id, which would make
-- the owned passes O(log n) — but it does not exist today, so do not cite one.
--
-- 🚨 A-3.2b (#1512, absorbing #1319 unit 4): THE POOL IS NO LONGER A MATERIALISED
-- ACCUMULATOR.  It used to be `CrossRun.universeDataDecls` — a bare `List Decl`
-- grown by `appendDataUniverse` one module at a time, with NO record of which module
-- contributed what and no key at all beyond list position.  It is now the whole-graph
-- envelope (`DeclEnvs.deModules`, stage K) read at the READER'S OWN ORDINAL through
-- `declEnvRowVisible`, i.e. through `declEnvVisibleTo`'s two conjuncts.  `cur` is
-- `declEnvsOrdOf mid` for the module being checked — a LOADER-derived identity, not a
-- spelling re-derived from import syntax, which is what makes it survive the emit path
-- (see the call site in `checkBodyImpl`).
--
-- ⚠️ THE POPULATION IS NOT BYTE-IDENTICAL TO THE OLD ACCUMULATOR, and the difference
-- is exactly one row: the READER'S OWN module.  The accumulator held only STRICTLY
-- EARLIER modules' public decls (`appendDataUniverse` runs at the END of a module's
-- own pass); `declEnvVisibleTo` admits the reader's own row too, privately, because
-- `entryOrd == cur` short-circuits the publicity conjunct.  That is the ruled
-- predicate and it is deliberately not special-cased away here.  Its reach is
-- bounded: `ownedType`/`ownedCtor` are scoped by `declOwnedBy mid` where `mid` comes
-- from a `DUse` path, and no module imports itself, so an own-module decl can only
-- ever fill the `bareType` fallback — LAST in a FIRST-wins walk, so it can only add a
-- candidate where every earlier row supplied none, never displace one.
-- 🚨 THE RESULT IS PARTITIONED: NAMED (`UseGroup`) ROWS AND WILDCARD (`UseWild`) ROWS
-- ARE TWO SEPARATE HALVES, and which half a consumer must see FIRST depends on that
-- consumer's own tie-break direction.  This is not a style choice; a single flat
-- source-ordered list shipped an S1.
--
-- WHY.  Before `wildOverlayDecls`, only `UseGroup` contributed, and every row was ONE
-- precisely-named decl.  A wildcard row is the module's WHOLE published set, so once
-- `UseWild` was enrolled the flat `flatMap` over the unit's decls in SOURCE ORDER made
-- import-clause order decide same-named-type collisions BETWEEN the two spellings: with
-- `import zzcol.*` written above `import aacol.{Red, Blue}`, a non-exhaustive match over
-- `aacol.Col` was reported as `Missing case: 'Green'` — a constructor of `zzcol.Col`,
-- the wrong type entirely — and the real missing case went unreported, so the program
-- then died at runtime on the case nobody warned about.  Swapping the two clauses fixed
-- it.  Measured on af6e0414 (broken) vs c7c879b7 (correct in BOTH orders).
--
-- THE RULE, and it is the ordinary scoping one: AN EXPLICITLY NAMED MEMBER OUTRANKS A
-- WILDCARD.  "You named this type" beats "you imported everything and it happened to be
-- in there", whichever clause is written first.
--
-- 🚨 THE TWO CONSUMERS TIE-BREAK IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, so they take opposite orders.
-- Enumerated, because a future edit that routes one of them through the other's wrapper
-- silently inverts the rule for that consumer with no diagnostic anywhere:
--   * `registerAllData` (the `dataEnv` overlay) folds the list LEFT and its bare-keyed
--     tables are `omInsert`, i.e. LAST-WRITE-WINS  -> named rows must come LAST
--     -> `importedCtorTypeDeclsLastWins`.
--   * `seedCheckRun` (the exhaustiveness ctor ORACLE) builds `oracleMap` =
--     `omFromPairs (reverseL …)`, i.e. FIRST-WINS   -> named rows must come FIRST
--     -> `importedCtorTypeDeclsFirstWins`.
-- Same rule, both sites; only the list order differs.  The big note at the `dataEnv`
-- call site enumerates the full set of order-observable structures — this pair is the
-- overlay's own contribution to it.
--
-- ⚠️ WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY DOES **NOT** DECIDE: named-vs-named.  Two `UseGroup` clauses
-- each naming a same-spelled type from a different module are still resolved by
-- import-clause order, exactly as before this partition — within each half the walk is
-- the same `flatMap` over `unitDecls` in source order, and neither consumer's tie-break
-- direction moved.  That case is a SEPARATE, PRE-EXISTING defect (it reproduces on
-- c7c879b7, before the wildcard arm existed) and fixing it needs the overlay keyed by
-- RESOLVED DECLARATION IDENTITY rather than by bare type name — #1319/#1185 territory,
-- not an ordering change.  Do not "while you are here" it: an ordering answer for
-- named-vs-named would freeze a guess into the oracle.
--
-- ⚠️ PERF: the unit's decl list is walked TWICE (once per half) instead of once, but the
-- POOL — the expensive part, see `THE REAL BOUND` above — is scanned exactly as many
-- times as before: each clause yields its rows in whichever half claims it and `[]` in
-- the other, so the total member/wildcard lookups are unchanged.  The extra cost is one
-- linear pass over `unitDecls`, which is import-clause bounded, not universe bounded.
importedCtorTypeDeclsFirstWins : List Decl ->
  Int ->
  List DeclEnvModule ->
  List Decl
importedCtorTypeDeclsFirstWins unitDecls cur rows =
  overlayHalf False unitDecls cur rows ++ overlayHalf True unitDecls cur rows

importedCtorTypeDeclsLastWins : List Decl ->
  Int ->
  List DeclEnvModule ->
  List Decl
importedCtorTypeDeclsLastWins unitDecls cur rows =
  overlayHalf True unitDecls cur rows ++ overlayHalf False unitDecls cur rows

-- One half of the partition, in the unit's own source order.  `wildHalf` selects which:
-- True = `UseWild` rows only, False = `UseGroup` rows only.
overlayHalf : Bool -> List Decl -> Int -> List DeclEnvModule -> List Decl
overlayHalf wildHalf unitDecls cur rows =
  flatMap (importOverlayDecls wildHalf cur rows) unitDecls

importOverlayDecls : Bool -> Int -> List DeclEnvModule -> Decl -> List Decl
importOverlayDecls wildHalf cur rows (DAttrib _ d) =
  importOverlayDecls wildHalf cur rows d
importOverlayDecls wildHalf cur rows (DUse _ (p@(UseGroup _ ms)) _) =
  if wildHalf then [] else flatMap (memberOverlayDecl cur rows (useModId p)) ms
importOverlayDecls wildHalf cur rows (DUse _ (p@(UseWild _)) _) =
  if wildHalf then wildOverlayDecls cur rows (useModId p) else []
importOverlayDecls _ _ _ _ = []

-- The exhaustiveness oracle's import rows beyond `importedCtorTypeDeclsFirstWins`:
-- every decl a module ALIAS import's module publishes, and the declarations of the
-- constructors a wildcard or alias import reaches through that module's own
-- `export import`.  The oracle reads constructors by bare name (resolve strips `A.`
-- before inference), so without these rows a same-spelled constructor of a module
-- loaded earlier answers for them (#1185).  They follow both halves of
-- `importedCtorTypeDeclsFirstWins` because a bare occurrence means an unaliased
-- import's constructor.  Kept out of `importOverlayDecls`, whose other reader is the
-- `dataEnv` overlay.  A selective `import m.{…}` is already one of those rows, and no
-- decl other than a `DUse` imports anything, so `oracleImportDeclsOf` adds nothing for
-- either.
oracleImportDecls : GraphCtx ->
  List Decl ->
  Int ->
  List DeclEnvModule ->
  List Decl
oracleImportDecls gctx unitDecls cur rows =
  flatMap (oracleImportDeclsOf gctx cur rows) unitDecls

oracleImportDeclsOf : GraphCtx -> Int -> List DeclEnvModule -> Decl -> List Decl
oracleImportDeclsOf gctx cur rows (DAttrib _ d) =
  oracleImportDeclsOf gctx cur rows d
oracleImportDeclsOf gctx cur rows (DUse _ (p@(UseAlias _ _)) _) =
  let dep = useModId p
  wildOverlayDecls cur rows dep ++ reexportedCtorDecls gctx cur rows dep
oracleImportDeclsOf gctx cur rows (DUse _ (p@(UseWild _)) _) =
  reexportedCtorDecls gctx cur rows (useModId p)
oracleImportDeclsOf gctx _ _ _ = []

-- The decls declaring the constructors `dep` re-exports from other modules, found
-- through the graph's constructor export index, whose rows carry each constructor's
-- declaring identity across any chain of `export import`.  One decl per (declaring
-- module, type), however many of its constructors are re-exported.
reexportedCtorDecls : GraphCtx ->
  Int ->
  List DeclEnvModule ->
  String ->
  List Decl
reexportedCtorDecls gctx cur rows dep =
  match omLookup dep (ctorExportsIndex gctx ())
    None => []
    Some es =>
      flatMap
        (k => reexportedTypeDecl cur rows (fst k) (snd k))
        (dedupBy (k => "\{fst k}.\{snd k}") (flatMap (reexportedOwner dep) es))

-- (declaring module, owning type) of an export row declared outside `dep`.
reexportedOwner : String -> (String, String, Ident) -> List (String, String)
reexportedOwner dep (_, owner, Ident _ io _) =
  identOriginFold [] (m => if m == dep then [] else [(m, owner)]) io

reexportedTypeDecl : Int -> List DeclEnvModule -> String -> String -> List Decl
reexportedTypeDecl _ [] _ _ = []
reexportedTypeDecl cur (m :: rest) declarer tyName =
  if m.demId == declarer then
    filterList (declIsOwnedType declarer tyName) (declEnvRowVisible cur m)
  else
    reexportedTypeDecl cur rest declarer tyName

-- Only a `data` or `newtype` declaration declares constructors, so no other decl owns
-- a type whose constructors a re-export reaches.
declIsOwnedType : String -> String -> Decl -> Bool
declIsOwnedType mid tyName (DAttrib _ d) = declIsOwnedType mid tyName d
declIsOwnedType mid tyName (DData { dataName = tn, dataOrigin = o }) =
  tn == tyName && declOwnedBy mid tn o
declIsOwnedType mid tyName (DNewtype { newtypeName = tn, newtypeOrigin = o }) =
  tn == tyName && declOwnedBy mid tn o
declIsOwnedType _ _ _ = False

-- A wildcard import's overlay: EVERY decl the named module publishes, as the reader at
-- ordinal `cur` may see it.  A wildcard names no member, so there is nothing to look up
-- by name — the whole published row IS the answer, and one row is all a module id can
-- have (`deOrdIndex` keys rows by `demId`), hence the stop at the first match.
--
-- 🚨 `declEnvRowVisible`, NEVER `m.demDecls`.  The visible projection is what confines
-- this to `publicDataDecl`s — public `DData`/`DInterface`/`DImpl`/`DTypeAlias` — and
-- `DNewtype`'s ABSENCE from that predicate is deliberate (see `publicDataDecl`): reading
-- `demDecls` here would leak a wildcard-imported module's PRIVATE and NEWTYPE
-- constructors across the module boundary, draining #1311/#1305 in the loud→silent
-- direction, i.e. a severity INCREASE.  A wildcard-imported `newtype`'s ctors are
-- consequently NOT overlaid; that is the ruled behaviour, not an oversight.
--
-- The private branch of `declEnvRowVisible` (`entryOrd == cur`, the reader's own row) is
-- UNREACHABLE from here for the reason the pool note above already gives: `mid` comes
-- from a `DUse` path, and no module imports itself.
--
-- ⚠️ PERF: this returns the row's OWN memoized `demPubDecls` list — no filtered copy is
-- materialised, per `declEnvRowVisible`'s zero-allocation contract.  It does move the
-- RESULT bound: see the `THE REAL BOUND` note above.
wildOverlayDecls : Int -> List DeclEnvModule -> String -> List Decl
wildOverlayDecls _ [] _ = []
wildOverlayDecls cur (m :: rest) mid =
  if m.demId == mid then
    declEnvRowVisible cur m
  else
    wildOverlayDecls cur rest mid

-- One member's overlay decl.  The bare-name fallback is kept for the `(..)` spelling
-- ALONE, so no overlay that fired before #1111 A-2.6 is lost where the identity cannot
-- match — a RE-EXPORTED type's decl names the ORIGINAL module, not the re-exporter
-- this import path names.  The (b) spellings are new, so they get no fallback: an
-- unscoped guess there would be the load-order coin flip this unit is removing.
-- (The fallback is not a second pass over `pool` — `overlayScan` collects it in the
-- same walk as the two identity-scoped candidates; see `findOverlayDecl`.)
memberOverlayDecl : Int ->
  List DeclEnvModule ->
  String ->
  UseMember ->
  List Decl
memberOverlayDecl cur rows mid (UseMember n ctors _ _) =
  match findOverlayDecl mid n ctors cur rows
    Some d => [d]
    None => []

-- The pool decl DECLARED BY `mid` that this member names.
--
-- 🚨 TWO PASSES, not one first-match, and the order between them is the point.  A
-- module may declare BOTH a type `T` and, in an earlier decl, a constructor spelled
-- `T` (`data Wrap = T Int` above `data T = A | B`).  For `import m.{T(..)}` the member
-- means the TYPE — `(..)` is what makes it a type spelling — so the type-name match
-- must be tried over the WHOLE pool before any constructor-name match is considered.
--
-- ⚠️ A single first-match pass that accepted `variantNamed n vs || ctors && tn == n`
-- shipped and was wrong: `import m.{T(..)}` selected `Wrap` (whose ctor is `T`), so
-- `T`'s own `A`/`B` were never overlaid and a universe collision on `A` won instead —
-- `Type mismatch: T vs Other`.  `declOwnedBy` had removed the CROSS-module first-match
-- hazard; this WITHIN-module one is what `variantNamed` newly made reachable.  Pinned
-- by `test/llvm_fixtures_modules/ctor_scope_ctors_prefer_type_name/`.
--
-- The constructor pass is still the fallback for `(..)`, not dead: `import m.{C(..)}`
-- where `C` is a constructor and not a type name of `m` keeps its pre-A-2.6 meaning.
--
-- 🚨 THE THREE PASSES SHARE ONE TRAVERSAL, and that is a MEASURED PERF CONTRACT.
-- `pool` is the WHOLE accumulated universe and this runs once per UseGroup member of
-- every module, so each independent pass over it is an O(modules x universe) term.
-- The first cut of A-2.6 ran three (type-owned, then ctor-owned, then the bare
-- fallback) where `main` ran ONE, and that alone put the perf gate's `modules` shape
-- at typecheck TIME r2=3.24 — over the hard 3.0 threshold.  `overlayScan` collects all
-- three candidates in a SINGLE walk (their predicates are independent, so first-wins
-- per candidate is unchanged) and stops the instant the DECIDING candidate is found,
-- which is the early exit the three-pass form had.  See `overlayScan`.
findOverlayDecl : String ->
  String ->
  Bool ->
  Int ->
  List DeclEnvModule ->
  Option Decl
findOverlayDecl mid n ctors cur rows =
  match overlayScanRows mid n ctors cur (None, None, None) rows
    (ownedType, ownedCtor, bareType) =>
      if ctors then
        orElseOpt (orElseOpt ownedType ownedCtor) bareType
      else
        ownedCtor

-- ONE walk of the pool, THREE first-wins candidates, in the precedence order
-- `findOverlayDecl` applies:
--
--   ownedType — first decl DECLARED BY `mid` whose TYPE name is `n`   (the `(..)` rule)
--   ownedCtor — first decl DECLARED BY `mid` with a CONSTRUCTOR named `n`  (rule (b))
--   bareType  — first decl of ANY owner whose TYPE name is `n`  (the `(..)` fallback,
--               `dataDeclForType`'s old job: a RE-EXPORTED type's decl names the
--               ORIGINAL module, so no identity-scoped pass can ever match it)
--
-- Each is recorded independently and FIRST-wins, which is exactly what three separate
-- first-match passes computed; a decl can legitimately fill two of them at once (a
-- record's sole variant carries the type's own name), so they are collected with
-- INDEPENDENT tests and never with an `else`.
--
-- ⚠️ THE EARLY EXIT IS `ctors`-DEPENDENT AND MUST STAY THAT WAY.  With `(..)` the
-- deciding candidate is `ownedType` (it outranks both others), so finding it ends the
-- walk; WITHOUT `(..)` only `ownedCtor` is ever read, so exiting on `ownedType` would
-- abandon the walk before the answer was found.  Exiting on "all three filled" is
-- likewise wrong for the second case.
-- A-3.2b (#1512): the OUTER half of the same one-traversal walk, over the envelope's
-- per-module rows in ORDINAL order — which is the identical decl order the old
-- accumulator was appended in (`appendDataUniverse` ran once per module, dependency
-- first), so every FIRST-wins candidate below sees the same sequence it saw before.
--
-- 🚨 THE EARLY EXIT MUST BE CHECKED AT BOTH LEVELS.  `overlayScan` stops mid-row on
-- the deciding candidate; without the identical test here the walk would continue into
-- every LATER row having already decided, which is the O(modules x universe) term this
-- whole neighbourhood is written to avoid.  `declEnvRowVisible` allocates nothing, so
-- a skipped row costs one comparison.
overlayScanRows : String ->
  String ->
  Bool ->
  Int ->
  (Option Decl, Option Decl, Option Decl) ->
  List DeclEnvModule ->
  (Option Decl, Option Decl, Option Decl)
overlayScanRows _ _ _ _ acc [] = acc
overlayScanRows mid n ctors cur acc (m :: rest) =
  let acc2 = overlayScan mid n ctors acc (declEnvRowVisible cur m)
  if overlayDecided ctors acc2 then
    acc2
  else
    overlayScanRows mid n ctors cur acc2 rest

overlayScan : String ->
  String ->
  Bool ->
  (Option Decl, Option Decl, Option Decl) ->
  List Decl ->
  (Option Decl, Option Decl, Option Decl)
overlayScan _ _ _ acc [] = acc
overlayScan mid n ctors acc (d :: rest) =
  let acc2 = overlayScanOne mid n acc d
  if overlayDecided ctors acc2 then acc2 else overlayScan mid n ctors acc2 rest

overlayDecided : Bool -> (Option Decl, Option Decl, Option Decl) -> Bool
overlayDecided ctors (ownedType, ownedCtor, _) =
  if ctors then isSome ownedType else isSome ownedCtor

overlayScanOne : String ->
  String ->
  (Option Decl, Option Decl, Option Decl) ->
  Decl ->
  (Option Decl, Option Decl, Option Decl)
overlayScanOne mid n acc (DAttrib _ d) = overlayScanOne mid n acc d
overlayScanOne mid n acc (d@(DData { dataName = tn, dataOrigin = o })) =
  overlayNote mid n tn o d acc
overlayScanOne mid n acc (d@(DNewtype { newtypeName = tn, newtypeOrigin = o })) =
  overlayNote mid n tn o d acc
overlayScanOne _ _ acc _ = acc

-- 🚨 NAME TESTS FIRST, IDENTITY SECOND — a MEASURED perf contract, not style.
-- `tn == n` / `declCtorNamed` are string compares over fields already in hand and
-- ALLOCATE NOTHING; `declOwnedBy` MINTS an identity on both sides (`OriginModule`,
-- `IdentModule`, the `map` closure, the `Ident`, the `Some` — five objects per call).
-- This runs ONCE PER POOL DECL, i.e. over the whole universe per member per module, so
-- minting unconditionally is O(modules x universe) ALLOCATION — `compiler/AGENTS.md`'s
-- named exception ("when the KEY PROJECTION allocates"), and it re-created the #154
-- quadratic that `modules` was promoted out of `KNOWN_SUPERLINEAR` for.  Measured on
-- the gate's own `modules` shape (N=100/200/400, K=8, one worktree, one emitter,
-- interleaved): mint-first 306/744/2013 MB net (r2=2.71) vs name-first 242/491/1010 MB
-- (r2=2.06), which is `main`'s figure to 0.1 MB.  A name test matches at most the
-- handful of pool decls sharing that spelling, so the mint is O(1) per member.
--
-- The unchanged `acc` is returned BY IDENTITY when neither name matches — the common
-- case — so the walk allocates nothing at all until it actually finds something.
overlayNote : String ->
  String ->
  String ->
  TyConOrigin ->
  Decl ->
  (Option Decl, Option Decl, Option Decl) ->
  (Option Decl, Option Decl, Option Decl)
overlayNote mid n tn o d acc = match acc
  (ownedType, ownedCtor, bareType) =>
    let hitType = tn == n
    let hitCtor = declCtorNamed n d
    if hitType || hitCtor then
      let owned = declOwnedBy mid tn o
      (
        if hitType && owned then orElseOpt ownedType (Some d) else ownedType,
        if hitCtor && owned then orElseOpt ownedCtor (Some d) else ownedCtor,
        if hitType then orElseOpt bareType (Some d) else bareType,
      )
    else
      acc

-- Does this decl's DECLARATION identity name module `mid`?  Both sides go through
-- `mkIdent`, so an ABSENT identity matches NOTHING — not even another absence.  That
-- polarity is deliberate and is A-2.3's, not A-2.10's: this answers a LOOKUP, where a
-- miss is recoverable (the universe fallback stands, i.e. today's behaviour) and a
-- false hit would silently overlay the wrong module's constructors.  It is why `mid`
-- being `""` (the I6.3 "origin not recorded" sentinel, which `identOriginOf` refuses)
-- cannot pair with an `OriginUnresolved` decl.
declOwnedBy : String -> String -> TyConOrigin -> Bool
declOwnedBy mid tyName o = match mkIdent NsType (OriginModule mid) tyName
  Some want => mkIdent NsType o tyName == Some want
  None => False

-- ── the local-spelling → DEFINER map, for EVERY import form ─────────────────────
-- This is the ONE representation the dict-arity identity seam resolves through:
-- `qualConstraintKey` turns a name into a `(definer, origin)` key with it, and
-- `hasImportDefiner` reads the same rows to decide that a qual MISS means "genuinely
-- unconstrained in its source module" rather than "look in the source-blind bare
-- table".  Every reader of that decision — `declaredConstraintFor`,
-- `declaredConstraintIds`, the pinned-var guard — takes its answer from here, and
-- none of them knows which import FORM produced a row.  So the forms are normalized
-- here, once, and a form whose rows are missing is not a gap in one arm: it is a
-- silent fall-through to bare-name first-match for that whole spelling.
--
-- 🚨 `import m.*` USED TO CONTRIBUTE NOTHING, and that hole is #1425's F1.
-- `importedBindings` answers `None` for `UseWild` because a wildcard's member list
-- cannot be read off the `DUse` decl alone — it is every public top-level binding the
-- DEPENDENCY declares — so this walk simply skipped it and every wildcard-imported
-- name fell to the bare table.  While the bare table happened to be wrong on BOTH
-- sides of a same-name collision (a foreign constrained row sized the define AND the
-- call), the two errors cancelled and the spelling looked correct.  `selfDeclArities`
-- then repaired the DEFINE side by identity; the call side, still on the bare table,
-- began applying a dict its callee no longer abstracts —
-- `E-NOT-A-FUNCTION: applied non-function: <dict:>` on nine ordinary 3-line stdlib
-- programs, in BOTH import orders, behind a `check` that exits 0.  The defect did not
-- move because the repair was wrong; it moved because the repair was applied at one
-- arm of a seam whose other arm had no rows at all.
--
-- The graph is what supplies the missing member list, and it is already built and
-- already keyed by module id: `declEnvsRef.deModules`.  On the Flat/loader-less paths
-- that envelope is EMPTY, so the wildcard rows are empty and this is byte-identically
-- today's behaviour — the same fail-closed-on-absent-identity discipline
-- `selfDeclArities` takes for `mid == ""`.
--
-- ORDER AND SHADOWING.  Named-form rows come FIRST (every reader is first-match), and a
-- wildcard row is dropped when the name is already spoken for — by a named import of
-- this module, or by this module's OWN top-level declaration, which shadows the
-- wildcard binding and whose arity `selfDeclArities` answers from its own qual row.
--
-- 🚨 THE SUPPLY SIDE DOES NOT ENUMERATE (RUN-XMOD-062).  It used to, twice over — one
-- walk for the named forms, one for the wildcard form, each deciding for itself what a
-- dependency "makes available".  Both walks answered that with the names a dependency
-- DECLARES, so a name it RE-EXPORTS (`export import u.{pick}` / `export import u.*`,
-- at any depth) got no row and fell to the source-blind bare table — the same
-- `E-NOT-A-FUNCTION: applied non-function: <dict:>` on a well-typed program, one hop
-- further out.  That was the THIRD enumeration in this seam to miss a member.  The rows
-- are now DERIVED: `graphPubDefiners` answers "what does module m export, and who
-- DEFINED each of those names" (declared publics, plus re-exports resolved through the
-- same predicate, transitively), and `importFormRows` — the one admission predicate,
-- shared with `importFormSchemes` — answers "which of those does this import form
-- admit, under which local key".  A form or a re-export shape this seam has never seen
-- is covered by construction, not by a case.
--
-- Also, the payload is now a PAIR: `(definer module, origin name at the definer)`,
-- because an IMPORTER can rename a re-exported member (`import r1.{pick as pk}` — an
-- ordinary import with an as-alias on a name that happens to be re-exported).  A
-- RE-EXPORT hop itself cannot rename: `export import u.{pick as pk}` is a hard parse
-- error (`parser.mdk:2379`), so that is not the motivating shape.  The qual tables are
-- keyed `(definer, ORIGINAL exported name)`, so carrying only the definer would key them
-- with the local spelling, MISS, and — via `hasImportDefiner` — read that miss as
-- "genuinely unconstrained", silently dropping the callee's dict.  Both halves of the
-- key come out of one derivation; they cannot disagree.
importDefinersOf : GraphCtx -> List Decl -> List (String, (String, String))
importDefinersOf gctx prog =
  let named = useAdmittedRows gctx False prog
  let taken = namesToSet (map fst named ++ declTopFnNames prog) omEmpty
  named
    ++ filterList
      (e => not (omHasKey (fst e) taken))
      (useAdmittedRows gctx True prog)

-- one precedence TIER of the walk above — [wild] selects the wildcard-form rows or the
-- named-form rows.  This is a precedence split, not a re-enumeration of the forms:
-- WHICH names a form admits is `importFormRows`' answer in both tiers.
useAdmittedRows : GraphCtx ->
  Bool ->
  List Decl ->
  List (String, (String, String))
useAdmittedRows gctx _ [] = []
useAdmittedRows gctx wild ((DAttrib _ d) :: rest) =
  useAdmittedRows gctx wild [d] ++ useAdmittedRows gctx wild rest
useAdmittedRows gctx wild ((DUse _ path _) :: rest) =
  useDefinerRows gctx wild path ++ useAdmittedRows gctx wild rest
useAdmittedRows gctx wild (_ :: rest) = useAdmittedRows gctx wild rest

-- `core` is skipped: the implicit prelude is never an explicit provenance (every reader
-- of these rows relies on that — see `declaredConstraintFor`).
useDefinerRows : GraphCtx -> Bool -> UsePath -> List (String, (String, String))
useDefinerRows gctx wild path =
  let depId = useModId path
  if depId == "core" then
    []
  else match importedBindings path
    None => if wild then graphPubDefiners gctx depId else []
    Some bindings =>
      if wild then
        []
      else
        flatMap (memberDefinerRow depId (graphPubDefiners gctx depId)) bindings

-- resolve ONE named member against the dependency's export table.  The fallback is the
-- load-bearing part: on the Flat / loader-less drivers `deModules` is EMPTY, so the
-- table is silent about every dependency, and a named import must keep contributing its
-- row (attributed to the SPELLED module, which is what it contributed before this
-- derivation existed) rather than vanish.  The wildcard form has no such fallback — it
-- cannot enumerate without the graph — which is the same fail-closed-on-absent-identity
-- discipline `selfDeclArities` takes for `mid == ""`.
memberDefinerRow : String ->
  List (String, (String, String)) ->
  (String, String) ->
  List (String, (String, String))
memberDefinerRow depId pubs (origin, local) =
  match resolveMemberRows (origin, local) pubs
    [] => [(local, (depId, origin))]
    rows => rows

-- #739 fix follow-up: local-import-name → ORIGINAL exported name.  `importedBindings`
-- yields (origin, local) pairs, so an aliased member `{x as y}` gives (y ↦ x) and a plain
-- `{f}` gives (f ↦ f).  qualConstraintFor keys the (source, name) qual tables by the ORIGIN,
-- not the surface alias — the tables are attributed under the DEFINING name — so a constrained
-- aliased import (`hash_map.{set as hmSet}`) resolves its `Hash`/`Eq` dict instead of being
-- misclassified as unconstrained and short-circuited (which DROPPED the dict → dispatch panic).
--
-- RUN-XMOD-062: this is now a PROJECTION of `importDefinersOf`'s rows rather than its own
-- `DUse` walk.  Two walks over the import forms could disagree about which rows exist —
-- and a `(definer, origin)` key assembled from two disagreeing walks is exactly the
-- silent misroute this seam pays for.  `definerRowsOf` is its sibling projection; both
-- take the SAME rows, computed once at the single write site.
originRowsOf : List (String, (String, String)) -> List (String, String)
originRowsOf rows = map (e => (fst e, snd (snd e))) rows

definerRowsOf : List (String, (String, String)) -> List (String, String)
definerRowsOf rows = map (e => (fst e, fst (snd e))) rows

-- the (key, scheme) pairs a module RE-EXPORTS via `export import` (`DUse True`).
-- Mirrors resolve's re-export set (resolve.pubUsePaths filters the same `DUse True`)
-- into the typecheck seed: walk the export-flagged DUse decls and, for each, pick the
-- re-exported member names out of the SOURCE dependency's public schemes already in
-- depEnv — the exact member resolution importSeed uses (importFormSchemes /
-- resolveMemberRows), so it works on both golden and mangled emit paths.  Schemes
-- come from depEnv by IDENTITY (the definer's original schemes, never re-generalized),
-- which preserves the original-definer constraint ids (D2 diamond-safety).  ONLY
-- `DUse True` is threaded, so a plain `import` never leaks the importer's names
-- downstream.  Transitivity is automatic: pubV accumulates these and is carried
-- forward as depEnv, so a second `export import` hop re-resolves against the enriched
-- pubV.  Methods need no special case — the source module's pubV already holds the
-- method scheme (publicValNames includes DInterface method names).
--
-- `core` is the one source that is NOT in depEnv: it is the implicit prelude, so its
-- schemes go into `baseSeed`, not into the per-module dep chain.  It is therefore
-- passed separately as `coreV` — without it, `lookupAssoc "core" depEnv` missed and
-- `export import core.{filter}` re-exported nothing (in silence, and forever).
-- `coreV` is consulted ONLY here, on `DUse True`: `importSeed` keeps taking the plain
-- depEnv, so a plain `import core.{…}` still seeds nothing (its names are already in
-- baseSeed — seeding them twice would only add duplicate assoc entries).
reexportSeed : List (String, a) ->
  List Decl ->
  List (String, List (String, a)) ->
  List (String, a)
reexportSeed _ [] _ = []
reexportSeed coreV ((DAttrib _ d) :: rest) depEnv =
  reexportSeed coreV [d] depEnv ++ reexportSeed coreV rest depEnv
reexportSeed coreV ((DUse True path _) :: rest) depEnv =
  let depId = useModId path
  let src = if depId == "core" then Some coreV else lookupAssoc depId depEnv
  match src
    None => reexportSeed coreV rest depEnv
    Some depSchemes =>
      importFormSchemes depEnv path depSchemes ++ reexportSeed coreV rest depEnv
reexportSeed coreV (_ :: rest) depEnv = reexportSeed coreV rest depEnv

foldModules : Accumulate ->
  (ModuleCtx -> String -> ModuleSeed -> List Decl -> List Decl -> List Decl -> (ModuleBindings, e, ModuleCtx)) ->
  Option (ModuleServe e) ->
  (Bool -> String -> e -> acc -> acc) ->
  acc ->
  List (String, Scheme) ->
  List (String, ExportBinding) ->
  List (String, List (String, ExportBinding)) ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  ModuleCtx ->
  List (String, List Decl) ->
  (acc, Option (ModuleServe e), ModuleCtx)
foldModules acc worker serve collect base baseSeed coreV depEnv accData accAll prev modules =
  let (done, served, last) =
    workModules
      acc
      worker
      serve
      baseSeed
      coreV
      depEnv
      accData
      accAll
      []
      prev
      modules
  (collectModules collect base done, served, last)

-- `foldModules`' loop: runs the worker over [modules] head-first, threading the
-- accumulators, the record and the serve policy, and returns each module's payload,
-- newest first.  The recursive call is a tail call: a frame waiting on the rest would
-- keep its module's record reachable until the graph end.
workModules : Accumulate ->
  (ModuleCtx -> String -> ModuleSeed -> List Decl -> List Decl -> List Decl -> (ModuleBindings, e, ModuleCtx)) ->
  Option (ModuleServe e) ->
  List (String, Scheme) ->
  List (String, ExportBinding) ->
  List (String, List (String, ExportBinding)) ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  List (String, e) ->
  ModuleCtx ->
  List (String, List Decl) ->
  (List (String, e), Option (ModuleServe e), ModuleCtx)
workModules _ _ serve _ _ _ _ _ done prev [] = (done, serve, prev)
workModules _ worker serve baseSeed coreV depEnv accData accAll done prev [(mid, prog)] =
  let seed = moduleSeedFor prev baseSeed coreV mid prog depEnv
  let (_, extra, next) = worker prev mid seed accData accAll prog
  ((mid, extra) :: done, serve, next)
workModules acc worker serve baseSeed coreV depEnv accData accAll done prev ((mid, prog) :: rest) =
  let step = map (policy => policy.msStep mid prog prev) serve
  let (own, done2, serve2, next) = match step
    Some (ServeHit own extra policy) =>
      (own, (mid, extra) :: done, Some policy, prev)
    _ =>
      let seed = moduleSeedFor prev baseSeed coreV mid prog depEnv
      let (schemes, extra, next) = worker prev mid seed accData accAll prog
      let own = publicModuleExports prog schemes
      match step
        Some (ServeCheck after) =>
          let (done3, policy) = after next own ((mid, extra) :: done)
          (own, done3, Some policy, next)
        _ => (own, (mid, extra) :: done, serve, next)
  workModules
    acc
    worker
    serve2
    baseSeed
    coreV
    ((mid, own ++ reexportSeed coreV prog depEnv) :: depEnv)
    (match acc
      AccumulateBoth => accData ++ publicDataDecls prog
      AccumulateNone => accData)
    (match acc
      AccumulateBoth => accAll ++ prog
      AccumulateNone => accAll)
    done2
    next
    rest

-- The import-scoped seed [mid] is checked from: [baseSeed] and what [prog]'s imports
-- select from [depEnv].
moduleSeedFor : ModuleCtx ->
  List (String, Scheme) ->
  List (String, ExportBinding) ->
  String ->
  List Decl ->
  List (String, List (String, ExportBinding)) ->
  ModuleSeed
moduleSeedFor prev baseSeed coreV mid prog depEnv =
  moduleImportSeed
    prev
    baseSeed
    (importSeed prev.mcGraph coreV (admittedIn prev.mcGraph mid) prog depEnv)

-- The right fold of `collect` over the payloads [done] (newest first): the last module
-- first, the only one `collect` sees as last, onto [base].
collectModules : (Bool -> String -> e -> acc -> acc) ->
  acc ->
  List (String, e) ->
  acc
collectModules _ base [] = base
collectModules collect base ((mid, extra) :: older) =
  fold (acc (m, x) => collect False m x acc) (collect True mid extra base) older

-- The core pass, through the prelude interface (`types/prelude_interface.mdk`).
-- Under the caller's prelude key a hit is the cached interface whose section lists
-- this drive's IO join.  A miss checks core, drains it, freezes the result, caches
-- it when keyed, and continues from that frozen value as a hit does, so the record
-- past core is one shape however the drive came by it: core's evidence, binder rows,
-- scope frames and goals stay in the run core was checked in, and its schemes reach
-- inference as fresh cells.
-- The interface's extern catalog is the one [runtimeDecls] alone build, not the
-- process's union, which holds whatever runtimes earlier drives declared.
-- Returns the bindings inference reads, the prelude's published rows and the module
-- record to continue from, whose `mcGraph` is the graph record.
checkCoreMemoized : ModuleCtx ->
  Option (Int, Int) ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  List (String, Scheme) ->
  (ModuleBindings, List (String, PubScheme), ModuleCtx)
checkCoreMemoized prev key runtimeDecls coreDecls runtimeSeed =
  let gctx = prev.mcGraph
  let join = gctx.config.value.tcIoJoin
  let cached = match key
    Some k => preludeCacheHit k join
    None => None
  match cached
    Some pi => continueFromInterface gctx gctx.graphRun pi
    None =>
      -- #2705: core is marked inside the pass, with the unsplit set
      -- (`moduleMarkCtx`'s core arm), in the run the continuation below leaves.
      let (coreSchemes, _, coreCtx) =
        checkModuleFull prev runtimeSeed [] coreDecls
      -- #2705: drain core's stamping context before the freeze, so core is solved
      -- once per process rather than once per analyze.  This treats core as closed
      -- at its own end.  The prelude has no diagnostics list for a hole to land in.
      match checkGraphFinish coreCtx
        [] => ()
        f :: _ => panic "evidence hole in the prelude: \{tcMsg f.dfDiag}"
      -- #673/#837: the published rows carry core's own obligations, keyed by bare
      -- name; the thaw derives `coreSchemeObligationsRef` from them.
      let pi =
        freezeInterface
          gctx.crossRun
          gctx.graphRun
          (externSigsToMap runtimeDecls omEmpty)
          (publishCore (coreOwnContexts coreCtx) coreSchemes.mbSchemes)
          (omMapValues (_ => ()) coreSchemes.mbStandaloneSchemes)
          coreCtx.mcCells.invocationViewRef.value
      match key
        Some k => seedPreludeInterface k [([join], pi)]
        None => ()
      continueFromInterface gctx (graphLineageRun (internersOf gctx).lineage) pi

-- The record a drive continues from past the core pass: [gctx] with [pi] thawed
-- into it.  [run] is a graph run core was not checked in; it takes the interface's
-- id counters and existential cells and nothing else of core's.  Core's module
-- record is not carried: the diagnostics worker seeds each module from its own
-- decls (`seedCheckRun`), and `cmCheckWorker` seeds its first module from this
-- blank record, an empty oracle (the one core was checked from) and no warning.
-- The interface's externs join the drive's catalog, whose own rows lose to them on
-- a collision, so a hit leaves the catalog a miss would and never shrinks it.
continueFromInterface : GraphCtx ->
  GraphRun ->
  PreludeInterface ->
  (ModuleBindings, List (String, PubScheme), ModuleCtx)
continueFromInterface gctx run pi =
  let (bindings, corePub, cross, seed) = thawInterface gctx pi
  run.tyvarCounter := seed.grsTyvarNext
  run.effvarCounter := seed.grsEffvarNext
  run.ctorExistentialsRef := seed.grsCtorExistentials
  run.anyExistentialsRef := seed.grsAnyExistentials
  let restored = GraphCtx { gctx |
    crossRun = cross,
    graphRun = run,
    builtinExternNamesRef =
      Ref (IdMap.union pi.piExternNames gctx.builtinExternNamesRef.value),
  }
  let mctx = initialModuleCtx restored
  mctx.mcCells.invocationViewRef := readInvocationView pi.piInvocationView
  (bindings, corePub, mctx)

preludePreambleMemoRef : Ref (Option (((Int, Int), String), PreludePreamble))
preludePreambleMemoRef = Ref None

preludePreambleOf : GraphCtx -> List Decl -> DeclEnvModule -> PreludePreamble
preludePreambleOf gctx coreDecls coreRow = PreludePreamble {
  ppEnvAcc = declEnvAccOf gctx [coreRow] emptyDeclEnvAcc,
  ppMangledFunDefs = unitCarriesMangledFunDefs "core" (funDefs coreDecls),
  ppMarkFacts = preludeMarkFactsOf coreDecls,
}

preludePreambleFor : GraphCtx ->
  Option (Int, Int) ->
  List Decl ->
  DeclEnvModule ->
  PreludePreamble
preludePreambleFor gctx None coreDecls coreRow =
  preludePreambleOf gctx coreDecls coreRow
preludePreambleFor gctx (Some k) coreDecls coreRow =
  match !preludePreambleMemoRef
    Some entry =>
      if fst entry == (k, gctx.config.value.tcIoJoinProfile) then
        snd entry
      else
        preludePreambleStore gctx k coreDecls coreRow
    None => preludePreambleStore gctx k coreDecls coreRow

-- One entry only (the prelude does not change under a process); a different
-- prelude simply misses and replaces it.
preludePreambleStore : GraphCtx ->
  (Int, Int) ->
  List Decl ->
  DeclEnvModule ->
  PreludePreamble
preludePreambleStore gctx k coreDecls coreRow =
  let p = preludePreambleOf gctx coreDecls coreRow
  preludePreambleMemoRef := Some ((k, gctx.config.value.tcIoJoinProfile), p)
  p

-- The drive's configuration: the IO join of the selected profile's grants (after the
-- effect domains it reads), the profile's name, and the stdlib ownership.
export
tcConfigOf : List (String, Param) -> DriveInputs -> TcConfig
tcConfigOf domains inputs = TcConfig {
  tcIoJoin = ioJoinAtoms domains inputs.diIoJoinGrants,
  tcIoJoinProfile = inputs.diProfileName,
  tcStdlibOwned = inputs.diStdlibOwned,
  tcFlatEntryIsStdlib = inputs.diFlatEntryIsStdlib,
  tcKey =
    "\{inputs.diProfileName}\n\{inputs.diFlatEntryIsStdlib}\n\{joinWith "," (omKeys inputs.diStdlibOwned)}",
}

-- [admitted]: the per-module method admissions `renameAliasedMethods` computed for
-- the drive's graph, or `omEmpty` on a drive that does not rename.  The last
-- component is the record the core pass leaves current, which the drive's first
-- module starts from.
graphPreamble : DriveInputs ->
  OrdMap (List (String, String)) ->
  GraphOut ->
  Option (Int, Int) ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  List (String, List Decl) ->
  (List (String, Scheme), ModuleBindings, Option (List (String, PubScheme)), OrdMap (List VecObl), List Decl, MarkSets, ModuleCtx)
graphPreamble inputs admitted sel preludeKey runtimeDecls coreDecls modules =
  -- S-emit-interleave-leak (#2049), TREES only: THE EMIT DRIVER OWNS ITS OWN
  -- (empty) ctor oracle.  A module checked without a `CheckRunSeed` carries the
  -- previous module record's `matchOracle`, and the tree arm's core pass is one
  -- (the seed is `seedCheckRun`'s, reached from `checkModuleFullDiags`
  -- only).  So every `oGetCtors`
  -- reader the tree arm reaches — `ctorSiblingWithholdingName`, `matchCol0Type` —
  -- would read whatever the LAST CHECK RUN IN THIS PROCESS left behind.
  --
  -- That residue used to be unreachable by accident rather than absent: `typeCtors`
  -- is keyed by DECLARATION IDENTITY (`tabKeyOf NsType <dataOrigin> <tyname>`), the
  -- flat entries build it from UNSTAMPED decls (`TkBare` rows), and this arm's
  -- readers mint `TkIdent` for a module-stamped head — so every lookup MISSED and
  -- every reader fell through its fail-open `None` arm.  A `Module`-arm re-check
  -- interleaved between two elaborations (the emit path's async-wrap re-check)
  -- writes rows under the entry module's OWN identity, i.e. under exactly the key
  -- these readers mint — so the lookups start HITTING, against rows built from the
  -- UN-MANGLED tree while the drive walks the MANGLED one.  MEASURED:
  -- `ctorSiblingWithholdingName` then reads the un-mangled ctor `A` as a sibling of
  -- the mangled survivor and false-rejects `a.k` with `Field 'k' is not declared by
  -- every constructor of 'A'`; `Display` cannot ground, the `println` route stays
  -- RNone, and the emitter writes a NULL dict word (`i64 0`) — SILENTLY on
  -- `runEmitWith`'s own path (`compiler/entries/entry_support.mdk`), which never
  -- reads `hadTypeErrors` after the call.  Clean exit 0, SIGSEGV at runtime.
  --
  -- The module record starts from `initialModuleCtx` of the minted graph record,
  -- whose oracle is empty, so no reader can see a previous run's residue, no matter
  -- which arm (or none) ran before.  It is what the core pass below runs against; each
  -- user module then overwrites it from its own decls (`checkModuleFullDiags` →
  -- `seedCheckRun`).
  --
  -- A process holding the prelude's elaborated trees (`types/prelude_elab.mdk`)
  -- starts every lineage past the evidence ordinals those trees carry, so no drive
  -- of it mints one again, whichever arm it takes.  Local binder names need no such
  -- raise: they carry their module's id.
  match heldPreludeEvCounter ()
    Some k =>
      let lineage = interners.value.lineage
      lineage.lnEvCounter := max lineage.lnEvCounter.value k
    None => ()
  let gctx = mintGraphCtx inputs admitted
  let initial = initialModuleCtx gctx
  -- #80/#201: populate effect domains ONCE over the WHOLE import graph (builtins +
  -- every `effect …` decl in core or any module), BEFORE the per-module foldModules
  -- loop, so a module using an effect declared in ANOTHER module sees its domain.
  -- `freshModuleCtx` no longer re-seeds, so this survives every per-module reset below.
  -- Must precede the core checkModuleFull (it runs checkEffectParams, reading these).
  --
  -- It must also precede the declaration ENVELOPE below, and that ordering is the
  -- newer half of the constraint: the envelope's atom-guarantee seed
  -- (`declEnvRowAtomsEntries` → `dtopFor`) READS this table, so an envelope built
  -- first degrades every parameterized label to its ⊤ and over-rejects an honest
  -- relay into an abstractly-exported wrapper.
  --
  -- #1112 A-3.1: the units here are what `deAllDecls` flattens (`declEnvDeclsOf`),
  -- in the same order; `populateEffectDomainsGraph` walks them without building
  -- that concatenation a second time.
  populateEffectDomainsGraph gctx coreDecls modules
  -- What `IO` joins, from the grants of the profile the verb selected, after the
  -- domains the atoms take their tops from.  `run` checks against `runProfile` of
  -- that profile, whose host-label grants are the selected profile's own.
  gctx.config := tcConfigOf gctx.effectDomains.value inputs
  -- the prelude's own contribution to every derivation below, from the memo when
  -- the caller supplied a prelude key -- see `PreludePreamble`.  The row is built
  -- HERE, not inside the memo, because it carries THIS analyze's decls.
  let coreRow = declEnvModule gctx 0 "core" coreDecls
  let modRows = declEnvModulesFrom gctx 1 modules
  let prelude = preludePreambleFor gctx preludeKey coreDecls coreRow
  -- L3 (xmod-identity #1351 spine): the graph-level mangled-funDefs fact, under the
  -- two-part safety property stated on `meExports` (F3: unconditional
  -- whole-value overwrite at the Module-mode driver entry + no reset point after it
  -- is what keeps compile N's flag from leaking into compile N+1).  The two terms
  -- are the `("core", coreDecls) :: modules` unit list split on its head, which
  -- `graphCarriesMangledFunDefs` folds with `||`.
  gctx.mangledFunDefsPresentRef :=
    prelude.ppMangledFunDefs || graphCarriesMangledFunDefs modules
  -- #1112 A-3.1: the whole-graph declaration envelope, under the same two-part
  -- property as the line above (nothing resets it within the drive, and the
  -- Module-mode driver entry writes it unconditionally).  See `buildDeclEnvs`.  It
  -- carries the method namespace (`deMethods`) and the constructor export index
  -- (`deData.deCtorExports`), so it is written before any module — the core pass
  -- included — reads a method's scope or a constructor's import witness.
  let declEnvs = buildDeclEnvs gctx prelude.ppEnvAcc coreRow modRows
  gctx.declEnvsRef := declEnvs
  -- #1280: `coreDecls` arrives here ALREADY STAMPED (the caller's
  -- `stampGraphTyOrigins` line), but the scope is derived from its type
  -- NAMES, not its origins, so it is the same map either way.
  -- An extern's signature may index a prelude head by an authority
  -- (`netSend : Socket h -> … <Net h> …`), and a name in an index slot is an
  -- authority binder only by the head's declared kind.
  let runtimeSeed = withDeclParamKinds initial coreDecls (u =>
    externSchemes initial (runtimeExternTyOriginScope coreDecls) runtimeDecls)
  seedAbstractRecordTypes gctx coreDecls modules
  -- #2705: BOTH arms MARK (solving is not optional), with the same sets, and each
  -- module is marked on the schedule inside `checkBodyImpl` — after any memo
  -- restore of `GraphCtx.graphRun`, never before, which is what keeps a minted cell indexing
  -- the table it was minted into.  `markSetsOf` publishes the sets to
  -- `checkBodyImpl` and writes `mangledShadowMapRef`/`argDispatchIdxByIdRef`.
  -- The split of the mark set (`msMarkRpNames` vs `msMarkSharedNames`) and every
  -- input that can become an `EMethodAt` are enumerated in `moduleMarkCtx`; the
  -- return-position/non-nameable axis it scopes is expressed by
  -- `test/shadow_fixtures/d24_definer_return_pos_not_nameable/`.
  let ms =
    markSetsOf gctx prelude.ppMarkFacts coreDecls modules declEnvs.deAllDecls
  -- Both arms PROMOTE: an unsignatured user fn whose body dispatches a method gets
  -- an inferred constraint and joins the dict-name set, so its occurrences route
  -- through its own dictionary parameter on every verb.  The completeness judgment
  -- reads those routes, and a check driver that left such a body unpromoted would
  -- see `RNone` where the tree arm sees `RDict`.  The eligible set is written and
  -- the harvest cleared at the entry of every drive, which `maybeInferConstraint`
  -- reads.
  setDictEligible gctx (moduleUserFnNames modules)
  gctx.promotionHarvestRef := []
  -- The core pass.  The diags arm continues from the prelude interface, cached
  -- under the caller's prelude key (see `checkCoreMemoized`, which drains core's
  -- stamping context before it freezes).  The tree arm needs core's dict-passed
  -- decls as well, which an interface does not hold: it continues from the
  -- interface only when the process also holds the prelude's shipped trees for
  -- the drive's key (`treeArmHit`), and otherwise runs the pass outright and
  -- drains only at graph end.
  -- The prelude's published rows come back here only when this pass closed core
  -- (the diags arm, and the tree arm's hit); otherwise the tree arm publishes them
  -- after its graph-end drain.  Both arms return core's own contexts as a value.
  -- The tree arm's snapshot is never written to
  -- `CrossRun.coreSchemeObligationsRef`, which inference reads.
  let (coreSchemes, corePub, coreContexts, coreTree, coreCtx) = match sel
    GOutDiags =>
      let (bindings, published, coreCtx) =
        checkCoreMemoized initial preludeKey runtimeDecls coreDecls runtimeSeed
      -- The graph record the drive continues from, with the interface thawed into
      -- it.  Nothing holds `initial` past this point.
      noteInterners coreCtx.mcGraph
      (
        bindings,
        Some published,
        coreCtx.mcGraph.crossRun.coreSchemeObligationsRef.value,
        [],
        coreCtx,
      )
    GOutTrees => match treeArmHit inputs coreDecls gctx
      Some (pe, pi) =>
        let (bindings, published, coreCtx) =
          continueFromInterface gctx gctx.graphRun pi
        noteInterners coreCtx.mcGraph
        (
          bindings,
          Some published,
          coreCtx.mcGraph.crossRun.coreSchemeObligationsRef.value,
          pe.peDecls,
          coreCtx,
        )
      None =>
        let (bindings, tree, coreCtx) =
          elabModuleStamp initial "" runtimeSeed [] coreDecls coreDecls
        (bindings, None, coreOwnContexts coreCtx, tree, coreCtx)
  (runtimeSeed, coreSchemes, corePub, coreContexts, coreTree, ms, coreCtx)

-- The prelude's shipped trees for a tree-arm drive (`types/prelude_elab.mdk`), moved
-- onto the binders of [coreDecls], the drive's own desugar of core: held for the
-- drive's prelude key.
treeArmElab : DriveInputs -> List Decl -> Option PreludeElab
treeArmElab inputs coreDecls = match inputs.diPreludeKey
  Some k => preludeElabFor k coreDecls
  None => None

-- Those trees with the interface of the same key cached for the drive's IO join:
-- a drive takes both or neither.
treeArmHit : DriveInputs ->
  List Decl ->
  GraphCtx ->
  Option (PreludeElab, PreludeInterface)
treeArmHit inputs coreDecls gctx = do
  k <- inputs.diPreludeKey
